name: Seasonal Youth Apprenticeship
org: 1001 Colors (Cincinnati public art and youth workforce development)
pay_detail: $13 an hour
duration: 8 weeks, June to July; 20 to 30 hours a week, Monday to Friday about 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
deadline_text: The 2026 Application and Interview Weekend has passed. The page says 2027 details will be posted by late 2026.
who_can_apply: Must be 14 to 21 years old at the start of employment. No prior professional experience is required.
how_to_apply: Complete the in-person application and interview during the scheduled Application and Interview Weekend.
notes: The organization's Gallery Fellowship (ages 16 to 24) and 10-month Mural Studio job are separate programs. The old ArtWorks web address now redirects to 1001colors.org. Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.

name: ACCEL Middle College (East Side Union / Evergreen Valley College)
org: East Side Union High School District
pay_detail: No cost listed on the page (public school program)
duration: 2 years
deadline_text: Recruitment meetings are held in the evening; dates not posted on the page I read.
who_can_apply: Sophomores (80 to 90 credits) and juniors (140 to 150 credits by January) with a 2.0 GPA or higher, good attendance, Algebra I or Integrated Math I done, and currently in Geometry or higher.
how_to_apply: Register for the Evergreen Valley College placement test at (408) 274-7900 x6636, attend a recruitment and info meeting to get the application, then mail it or hand-deliver it to the Roble Building mailroom at Evergreen Valley College.
notes: Page lists no age rule and no 2026-27 meeting dates; call the coordinator (Kathleen Leal, (408) 274-7900 x6881) for the schedule. Must also be taking biology, chemistry and physics and English 2 (sophomores) or English 3 (juniors).

name: Youth Innovation Program (WIOA In-School Youth)
grades: Currently in high school or college
pay_detail: Not stated. The youth page mentions paid and unpaid work experience but gives no wage.
deadline_text: Ongoing
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21, currently in high school or college. Alameda County program. No income or residency rule is listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Contact a regional provider: Eden Area ROP in Hayward, (510) 293-2900, or Tri-Valley ROP in Livermore, (925) 487-4153. Main ACWDB line: (510) 259-3842.
notes: Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 use the Future Force program instead: La Familia (Eden Area) (925) 935-2643, Ohlone College (Tri Cities) (510) 742-2323, International Rescue Committee (North Cities) (510) 857-6884. The county page names only two providers, Eden ROP (Hayward) and Tri-Valley ROP (Livermore), and says to contact the one near you.

name: After School Matters (paid apprenticeships and assistantships)
pay_detail: Paid stipend based on program level and frequency. Dollar amounts vary by program and are not stated on the apply page.
duration: Spring: late Feb to mid May. Summer: late June to early Aug. Fall 2026: Sept 28 to Dec 12.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 application opened Aug 26 and programs started Sept 28; no closing date stated and spaces are limited. Spring 2027 applications open in January; summer 2027 in April (per the session timeline).
who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Chicago and attend a Chicago high school. Most programs are ages 14 to 18 (14 by Sept 28, 2026 for the fall session). Outreach Assistantships need age 16+.
how_to_apply: Apply online (up to six programs, ranked). Save your Application ID for the Teen Dashboard. Most programs require an interview; offers must be accepted within 72 hours. A parent/guardian consent form is required after you accept.
notes: One program per session. A Social Security number or ITIN is not required for every program; teens without one should contact ASM. Applying again each session needs a new application. The fall page says the application is open, but programs began Sept 28, so confirm spots remain. Work permit rules for under-16 not stated on ASM pages.

name: Discovery Station volunteer, Udvar-Hazy Center
org: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: At least 8 hours per month for one year
deadline_text: No application window stated; new openings are posted through the year.
who_can_apply: Must be 16 or older for Discovery Station and Astronomy volunteering (18 for most other roles). Commit to at least 8 hours a month for one year, preferably in 3-hour shifts.
how_to_apply: Click 'Apply Now' on the volunteer page, create an account in the museum's volunteer system, complete the orientation and online training, and sign a Program Volunteer Agreement.
notes: The Astronomy Education volunteer role (also 16+) was marked 'not recruiting at the moment'. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

name: California Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary)
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of California
city: California (session location not stated on the site)
grades: 11th grade (the site says each delegate is an 11th grader during the 2025-26 school year)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the pages read. The site says there are opportunities for scholarship consideration, including the Samsung American Legion Scholarship.
duration: One week. The 2026 session (83rd) ran June 22-27, 2026.
deadline_text: 2026 session: June 22-27, 2026. 2027 dates and application deadlines are not posted on the site.
who_can_apply: Girls in 11th grade who are selected and sponsored by a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit. Each high school may have only one delegate. If a school has no sponsoring Unit, a student can apply as a Department (statewide) alternate applicant. Age rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor or contact a local American Legion Auxiliary Unit (the site has a spreadsheet to find one). Each Unit picks a delegate and two alternates. Students at schools with no sponsoring Unit can use the START HERE online application as Department alternate applicants.
notes: Separate from the coed American Legion California Boys State (Boys & Girls State) program, which has its own card on this site. The FAQ says a student may apply to either American Legion CA Boys State or American Legion Auxiliary CA Girls State, but not both. Selection criteria, grade-school rules beyond the 11th grade note, and cost are not stated on the pages read.

name: Alameda County Community Food Bank: Volunteer
duration: Shifts
deadline_text: No deadline. Pick a shift on the volunteer calendar.
who_can_apply: Ages 10 and up. Teens 15 to 17 may volunteer on their own. Under 15 needs an adult (1 adult for every 5 youth).
how_to_apply: Book shifts on the volunteer calendar or email volunteer@accfb.org, phone 510-635-3663 ext. 308.
notes: 7900 Edgewater Dr, Oakland. Wear closed-toe shoes that cover your whole foot. BART to Coliseum, then AC Transit 98.

name: Alameda County Library Teen Volunteers (Fremont, Newark, Union City)
city: Fremont, Newark and Union City, CA
deadline_text: Ongoing.
who_can_apply: Ages and requirements vary by role and are shown on the portal. Not stated on the page I read.
how_to_apply: Browse and apply on the library's Better Impact volunteer portal. Phone 510-745-1500. The application link is on the official page.
notes: The teen page is thin. Ask the Fremont Main Library which roles take teens.

name: Alameda Free Library Teen Advisory Group (TAG)
pay_detail: Community service hours only
duration: 1st Tuesday of the month, 4:30 to 5:30 pm
deadline_text: Rolling
who_can_apply: Teens. The TAG page does not state an age or grade. Other teen volunteer roles on the same page use grades 7 to 12 or ages 12 to 17.
how_to_apply: Complete the online TAG registration form on the library page. Questions: refdesk@alamedaca.gov or (510) 747-7777.
notes: Meets at the Main Library in the Stafford Room. The page states no age rule, so ask the library if you are younger than 12 or older than 17. See also Alameda Free Library Teen Volunteers (Book Reviewers and Coding with LEGO) for volunteer roles such as book reviews and LEGO coding.

name: Alameda Free Library Teen Volunteers (Book Reviewers and Coding with LEGO)
pay_detail: Community service hours only
deadline_text: Rolling
who_can_apply: Teen Book Reviewers: grades 7 to 12. Coding with LEGO: ages 12 to 17.
how_to_apply: LEGO program: email Fernanda Nunez at fnunez@alamedaca.gov. Book reviews: use the Teen Book Reviews page. Questions: refdesk@alamedaca.gov or 510-747-7777.
notes: Book reviews are limited to one a month. No coding experience needed for LEGO. See also Alameda Free Library Teen Advisory Group (TAG) for the advisory role, where teens suggest ideas for library events and projects.

name: Alameda Youth Career and Job Fair
org: City of Alameda and Alameda Unified School District
pay_detail: Free event
duration: One afternoon
deadline_text: The 10th annual fair was Wednesday, April 1, 2026, 1 to 5 pm. No 2027 date is posted.
who_can_apply: Local youth, especially students in Alameda Unified School District career technical education programs.
how_to_apply: No sign-up is listed; admission is free. Contacts: Jennifer Padilla (City) 510-747-6852; Amanda Vigil (AUSD) 510-337-7091.
notes: Held at Encinal Jr/Sr High, 210 Central Ave, Alameda. It is an annual fair, but the 2027 date has not been posted.

name: Alexandria Library Teen Volunteers and Teen Advisory Group
pay_detail: Unpaid. Service hours can be earned.
duration: No required hours listed
deadline_text: No deadline listed.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18 can apply to volunteer. The Teen Advisory Group is for ages 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application online. Go to a Teen Volunteer Orientation. The dates are on the library events page. Use an email that is not from your school. You can write to volunteer@alexlibraryva.org.
notes: The page was last updated in March 2025. Confirm the age range and orientation dates by email. Volunteers cannot lead story times.

name: Alexandria Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
org: City of Alexandria Workforce Development Center
pay_detail: Paid; rate and weekly hours not stated on the program page (a city video page says 20 to 30 hours per week)
duration: 6 weeks (June 22 to July 31 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Dec 15 and closed Feb 14, 2026. 2027 dates not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21, in middle or high school, who live in the City of Alexandria. You must be allowed to work in the U.S. Your household must get SNAP, Medicaid, TANF or free or reduced lunch. Or its income must be at or below 130% of the poverty line. Students with an IEP can also qualify.
how_to_apply: Send the Smartsheet youth application one time, with all your papers. You need proof of an Alexandria address, proof you can work, proof of income or benefits, and a photo ID. Some students with benefits need only three papers.
notes: Forms that are not complete, or sent more than once, can slow or hurt your application. Questions: DCHSSummerYouth@alexandriava.gov or 703-746-5940 (4850 Mark Center Drive, Floor 6). The page does not mention work permits.

name: Teen Volunteers, Internships and Teen Advisory Board
org: Alive Center (Naperville, Aurora and Hanover Park)
city: Naperville, Aurora and Hanover Park, IL
grades: High school teens for the Teen Advisory Board
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens get service hours for volunteering. Internships are non-paid.
duration: Teen volunteer hours are not stated. Internships run fall, spring and summer.
deadline_text: Teen Advisory Board: new high school members are picked each April. Volunteering and internships have no deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Teens can volunteer. The internship page gives no age or school rule and lists colleges, so ask if high schoolers can intern.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. Then meet a staff member for an interview and training. Interns use a different form. Teen Advisory Board members use their own form.
notes: Alive says it runs free drop-in hours after school and over the summer, plus teen-led clubs. Locations named on the site are Naperville, Aurora and Hanover Park. The internship page lists college affiliated schools, so ask about high school interns.

name: Palefsky Collision Project (Alliance Theatre)
pay_detail: Free to all participants. No stipend mentioned.
duration: 3 weeks, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily (June 29 to July 17 in 2026, with performances July 17 and 18)
deadline_text: The interview and application window runs from January to mid-April each year; the Summer 2026 window is closed. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising 11th graders, 12th graders and post-secondary students. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Apply during the window; the process includes an interview. The page encourages students to attend a performance and check back next year. Contact: collision.project@alliancetheatre.org or 404-733-4700.
notes: Free thanks to the Palefsky family. Exact dates were not printed on the application page, only the January to mid-April range. The Alliance also lists a year-long Teen Ensemble, but its current page was not read so it is not listed.

name: Volunteer and School Service Hours (ages 16 and up, plus at-home projects)
city: South Elgin, Bloomingdale, Geneva, Algonquin, IL
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is a $35 volunteer membership fee for all opportunities.
duration: Dog and cat care: at least 40 hours over 6 months, with weekly or every-other-week shifts. Animal care roles ask for at least six months.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. When read, Wildlife applications were closed and Clinic Support was full. Check back for future opportunities.
who_can_apply: In-person volunteer roles are for ages 16 and up. At-home projects are a good option for anyone under 16. Vet clinic support is 18 and up. School service roles need an agreement signed by a parent and a teacher.
how_to_apply: Register on the volunteer page for the role you want. You also complete virtual Safety and Protocols training and pay the $35 membership fee. For school hours, sign up on the School Service page.
notes: Animal care roles ask for at least six months. The page says Shelter Support is not eligible for court-ordered service hours. Sites include South Elgin, Bloomingdale Petco, Algonquin Petco and Geneva Petco. Others are the St. Charles office and Elburn Forest Preserve.

name: Young Artist Competition (Ann Arbor Symphony Orchestra)
pay_detail: $50 application fee (email jpepper@a2so.org if the fee is a problem). Prizes: $500 grand prize, $250 runner-up.
duration: Final round Nov 7, 2026. Winner plays Feb 23, 2027.
deadline_text: 2026 application closed Sept 25, 2026 at 10 AM. Final round is Nov 7, 2026. Next year dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 who go to school in Michigan and play a string, wind, brass or percussion instrument (harp too). Pianists are not considered.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form on the A2SO site. Send a one take YouTube video of you playing one part of a solo piece with an accompanist.
notes: This is a contest, not a job. The page is for the 2026 contest. Expect similar timing next year, from August to late September.

name: Ann Arbor District Library Volunteer Program (teens and adults)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Ongoing; you commit to the shifts you sign up for
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Apply any time with the online form, then attend a volunteer orientation.
who_can_apply: Anyone 14 or older. Ages 14 to 17 need a signed permission slip from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. After review you are contacted with details on signing up for a required volunteer orientation, then you pick shifts.
notes: Library does not offer court-ordered community service. Older library posts mention a summer teen volunteer program, but the current page only describes the year-round program. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

name: BioMed Focus (Michigan Medicine summer research)
pay_detail: $4,000 for taking part
duration: 8 weeks, June 14 to Aug 6, 2027. You must be on campus at least 35 of the 40 days.
deadline_text: The BioMed Focus 2027 interest form opens Monday, Oct 12, 2026. No closing date is posted.
who_can_apply: You must live in Michigan and go to a Michigan high school. You must be close enough to travel to Ann Arbor. Rising juniors and seniors are best. Most students come from partner schools: Ypsilanti Community, Lincoln and Belleville. There is no GPA minimum.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online interest form. One letter of recommendation is required. The page does not describe the later steps.
notes: The page shows an Interest Form Closed button even though it says the form opens Oct 12, so check the page for the current status. Commuter program, so you live at home.

name: Food Gatherers Volunteer Shifts (warehouse and Community Kitchen)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Single shifts; you can volunteer as often as you like
deadline_text: Shifts open for sign-up 3 months ahead and fill quickly.
who_can_apply: Age 14 or older to volunteer alone at the warehouse or Community Kitchen. Younger kids can come with an adult. The warehouse takes ages 8 and up. The kitchen takes ages 12 and up.
how_to_apply: Create a user account with Individual Registration and sign up for shifts in advance; no walk-ins. If you need school hours signed or an observer will attend, call the volunteer coordinator first.
notes: Not teen-specific, but a steady way for teens 14 and up to earn volunteer hours. Warehouse work involves moderate lifting. Groups of four or more use a separate group form. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

name: Teen Leadership Program (Growing Hope urban farm)
pay_detail: $14 an hour, plus free weekly produce bags in the growing season.
duration: Summer 2027: June 15 to Aug 6, Monday to Thursday, 9 AM to 2:30 PM. After school: Sept to May, Tue/Wed/Thu, 4 to 6 PM.
deadline_text: Summer 2027 applications open March 1, 2027. A closing date is not posted.
who_can_apply: High-school-aged youth who live in Ypsilanti and the surrounding townships. For the summer, you must have finished 9th grade and cannot miss more than 4 days. The school-year program is for teens who finished the summer program in good standing.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Youth and Schools page when applications open. Questions: Jenny Pritchett, jenny@growinghope.net.
notes: Michigan requires a work permit for workers under 18. From Oct 2, 2026 permits come through the state Youth Employment Permit Portal.

name: Volunteer at Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum and Leslie Science & Nature Center
org: Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum and Leslie Science & Nature Center (Discover Science and Nature)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer roles.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No dates or deadlines are posted.
who_can_apply: The page says community volunteers include high school and college students, corporate partners and retirees. It does not state a minimum age. Ask before you apply.
how_to_apply: For the Hands-On Museum, email volunteer@aahom.org. For wildlife volunteering at Leslie Science & Nature Center, fill out the application linked on the page. Or email volunteer@lesliesnc.org.
notes: The page is short. It gives no age rule, hours, training or start dates, so email first. The Hands-On Museum's old address (aahom.org/volunteer) now sends you to this page. The Leslie wildlife application link goes to a file named Adult_Volunteer_Application.pdf, so ask Leslie before a teen applies for wildlife work.

name: Junior Volunteer Program at Humane Society of Huron Valley
pay_detail: $205 program fee for the 6 session training (training, T-shirt, supplies). Limited scholarships for families with financial need.
duration: 6 training sessions, then a 2 to 4 hour per month volunteer commitment
deadline_text: Registration for the November sessions (Nov 2 to 19) opens Mon Oct 19 at 8am; for the December sessions (Nov 30 to Dec 17) it opens Mon Nov 16 at 8am. Sessions are offered monthly and fill quickly.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 to 17 (must be 12 before registering). Those about to turn 18 within 6 months may prefer the adult orientation.
how_to_apply: Online registration only, which opens about 30 days before each session. You must attend all six classes; there are no make-ups, refunds or transfers. A waitlist is available.
notes: Demand is higher than space, so you may wait months. After training you volunteer without a parent present. Inactive for 6 months or more means retaking the training. Shelter is at 3100 Cherry Hill Rd, Ann Arbor. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

name: Young Filmmakers Camp (Michigan Theater and State Theatre)
org: Marquee Arts (Michigan Theater and State Theatre)
pay_detail: 2026 prices: $576.25 for session 1, $901.25 for session 2, $576.25 for session 3, or $1,901.25 for all sessions.
duration: 2026 dates: June 29 to July 3, July 6 to 10 and 13 to 15, and July 20 to 24
deadline_text: 2026 registration closed Friday, June 19, 2026 at 5 PM. 2027 dates and prices are not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17. Beginners are welcome.
how_to_apply: Register online on the Film Camp page. Questions: Holly Behrend, hbehrend@marquee-arts.org.
notes: This camp costs money. Check the page in spring for 2027 dates.

name: #MI-Internship Prep (4-week free course)
pay_detail: The course is free. Eligible participants can earn cash incentives for finishing it. Amount not stated.
duration: 4 weeks per cohort
deadline_text: Cohorts run throughout the year. No dates are posted on the page.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24. You live in Hillsdale, Jackson, Lenawee, Livingston or Washtenaw County.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the page and choose your county.
notes: This prepares you for internships. It is a course, not a job. The same agency runs SummerWorks, a paid summer program, for Washtenaw County.

name: Neutral Zone free teen programs and youth-led projects
pay_detail: Free. Donations are welcome.
duration: Weekly programs all school year
deadline_text: School year 2026-27 programs run weekdays. Drop-in is Monday to Friday, 2 to 6 PM. No deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: Any teen of high school age. It is best to sign up ahead, but you can sign up when you come.
how_to_apply: Fill out the teen sign up form on the website or sign up when you come. Questions: Hananiah Wiggins, hananiah@neutral-zone.org, (734) 214-9995.
notes: This is a free teen center, not a paid job. Future Corps for high schoolers meets the first Monday of each month, 4 to 6 PM, and helps with first-job support. Neutral Zone is at 310 E Washington St, Ann Arbor.

name: Leadership Institute (Ozone House)
pay_detail: All Ozone House services are free.
duration: One week, offered twice a year at the Drop-In Center
deadline_text: Dates are not posted. The page says it is offered twice a year.
who_can_apply: High-risk youth ages 13 to 18 in Washtenaw County.
how_to_apply: Not stated for this program. Call Ozone House at (734) 662-2222 any time, day or night. Text 'Ozone' to that number or use online chat Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM.
notes: The page also lists a monthly Career Panel for youth 13 to 20. It is the third Thursday at 5 PM at the Ypsilanti Drop-In Center, and food is served. A Peer Outreach Worker team for youth 15 to 19 was coming back in winter. WorkZone paid internships are for ages 18 to 20.

name: Ann Arbor lifeguard certification course and pool jobs
org: City of Ann Arbor Parks and Recreation (Mack Indoor Pool)
pay_detail: Course fee $200, fully refunded if you pass, apply, are hired and start work at a city pool. Pay for pool jobs is not stated on the pages read.
duration: Weekend course: Friday evening, Saturday and Sunday
deadline_text: Registration for the course opens Jan 21, 2027. Session 1 starts Friday, April 16, 2027 (Friday 5 to 10 p.m., then Saturday and Sunday 11 a.m. to 7:30 p.m.). Registration closes 7 days before the course starts. Seasonal job postings for 2027 are not up yet.
who_can_apply: The course is open to ages 15 and up. The page says you are prepared to be a lifeguard when you turn 16. Fifteen year olds who finish the course can join the city's Lifeguard in Training Volunteer Program.
how_to_apply: Register for the course by calling 734-794-6237 or at Mack Indoor Pool (715 Brooks St., inside Ann Arbor Open School). Pool jobs are applied for online through the city's job board when posted.
notes: The lifeguard certification page says 15 year olds can join the Lifeguard in Training Volunteer Program. The recertification section says 15 year olds can be eligible for a city lifeguard job. These two statements differ. Ask the pool at 734-794-6237 what age you can be hired. Michigan says minors must get a work permit before starting a job unless exempt. The permit comes through a Michigan school. See the state youth employment page. You get no refund of the course fee if you fail the course.

name: Volunteer in the Parks (City of Ann Arbor)
org: City of Ann Arbor Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: One-day to long-term. Group projects run April to October.
deadline_text: No deadline. Event dates are on the online volunteer calendar.
who_can_apply: The page says individuals and groups of all ages can volunteer. No minimum age is stated.
how_to_apply: Individuals use the online volunteer calendar and sign-up. Groups submit the Group Volunteer Inquiry form. Email a2parksevents@a2gov.org or call 734.794.6627.
notes: Ask staff whether a teen needs a parent signature. The page does not say.

name: Summer Day Camp counselors and Counselors in Training (Peace Neighborhood Center)
pay_detail: Not stated
duration: Summer Youth Services runs eight weeks
deadline_text: Dates and application steps are not posted on the page.
who_can_apply: Rising 9th graders for Counselors in Training. High school students for counselor roles.
how_to_apply: Not stated. Call Peace Neighborhood Center at (734) 662-3564. 1111 N. Maple Rd., Ann Arbor.
notes: Ask whether the job is paid before you apply. The page also lists College and Career Prep for high school students, Monday to Thursday during the school year.

name: Ann Arbor Summer Festival volunteer (Top of the Park)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Completed shifts earn perks such as access to special hospitality areas, and select benefits include tickets to some performances and prize giveaways.
duration: Single shifts at the festival
deadline_text: The page says sign-up opens April 1 (for the 2026 season). Festival dates are not on this page. 2027 sign-up is not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 and up for most roles. Survey Squad is 16 and up. Ushers must be 18. The page says 12 and 13 year olds may volunteer with an adult volunteer. Volunteers work under the supervision of festival staff.
how_to_apply: Pick a volunteer role and a night on the A2SF volunteer sign-up page. Questions: call 734-994-5999.
notes: Seasonal: shifts are in the summer festival only. Usher spots for 2026 were closed. Check the page in spring for 2027 sign-up.

name: SummerWorks (Washtenaw County Summer Youth Employment Program)
org: SummerWorks: Michigan Works! Southeast, Washtenaw County OCED, University of Michigan Poverty Solutions and partners
pay_detail: Internships pay $15 or $17 per hour depending on whether you have finished high school or an equivalent (employer FAQ). About 20 to 25 hours a week.
duration: Program runs April to August; internship is 10 weeks between June and August
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Jan 15 and were due Mar 22, 2026; internship period June 15 to Aug 21, 2026. The site says 2027 applications open in mid-January and are usually open late January to late March. 2027 closing date is not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 when programming begins (you must turn 16 by June 1 of the program year) AND you live in, or attend school in, Washtenaw County. Participants may take part for up to three years.
how_to_apply: Online application (opens January): your contact info, parent or guardian contact, approximate household income, possible summer conflicts, and one reference who is not a relative. Accepted minors need a parent or guardian signature.
notes: A paid internship is not guaranteed: the site says a subset of participants is selected, though staff aim to match everyone. After acceptance you need I-9 identification documents and a bank account in your name for pay (this is for payroll, not a fee). Professional development is Tuesday or Wednesday evenings online, then Fridays 10am to 2pm in person from June. Michigan requires a work permit for minors under 18 to work; as of Oct 2, 2026 permits are issued through the state's Youth Employment Permit Portal, not schools. Contact: mail@summerworks.info.

name: Trinity Health Ann Arbor Teen Volunteer Program
org: Trinity Health Michigan, Ann Arbor and Livingston
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Year-round roles with some seasonal placements (a summer teen cohort exists)
deadline_text: No application dates posted. The 2026 Ann Arbor summer teen orientation was June 24, 2026, 11am to 4pm; no later orientation is listed.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the Ann Arbor and Livingston volunteer page (the link goes to the hospital's volunteer system at stjoemercyann.vsysweb.com). Then an interview, paperwork, health screening and a required orientation.
notes: Requirements listed for volunteers: interview, two TB skin tests, proof of varicella and MMR immunity, Tdap, this year's flu shot, health clearance form, one non-relative reference, and orientation; background checks apply to volunteers 18 and over. Also on the same page: The Farm at Trinity Health takes volunteers age 15 and up (no background check under 18). The Apply Now link is http, not https, so it is not in the apply_url field. Volunteer office phone is on the page. Michigan's youth employment page (Youth Employment Standards Act) says the law covers employers of anyone under 18 including volunteers, so ask the program whether a work permit is needed.

name: Washtenaw County Youth Commission
org: Washtenaw County Youth Commission (run through the Neutral Zone)
pay_detail: Not stated
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: Application timeline not posted. The page says to contact Britt Baron at britt@neutral-zone.org.
who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 18. The commission has 21 members: 2 from each county district and 3 at-large.
how_to_apply: Email britt@neutral-zone.org. Ask when you can apply.

deadline_text: Windows each year: fall Jul 1-31, spring Dec 1-31, summer Mar 1-31. The fall window has closed; the next one is spring, Dec 1-31 (the page gives these windows without a year).
who_can_apply: Teens 13 to 17 (no younger than 13 and no older than 17 by Aug 1 for fall, Dec 1 for spring, or May 1 for summer). Must pass a background check (fingerprinting for ages 15+ who lived outside Texas in the last seven years) and attend a mandatory orientation.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application posted on the Teen Volunteer Program page during the window. There may be an interview with the volunteer coordinator; you get three business days to accept an offer. Not every applicant gets a placement.
notes: Placement depends on the library branch and supervisor, and the library gets more applicants than placements. Contact: APL.Volunteers@austintexas.gov. Limit of two absences per season.

name: Caminos Teen Leadership Program
org: Emma S. Barrientos Mexican American Cultural Center (City of Austin)
pay_detail: $22.05 per hour, about 6 to 10 hours per week
duration: 10 months, mid-to-late August through early June; most Saturdays 10:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. plus Wednesday evenings
deadline_text: Applications for the Class of 2027 are closed. The center will announce when applications reopen for the Class of 2028 on Instagram @atxcaminos.
who_can_apply: High school students living in Central Texas, ages 16 to 18 (or turning 16 in the year they apply), interested in creative careers and Latinx issues, and able to work legally in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Submit a personal application, a portfolio and teacher recommendations, then do one-on-one and panel interviews. Questions: caminos@austintexas.gov.
notes: About 10 to 12 teens per cohort. Competitive. Dates for the next application window are not posted.

name: Lifeguard training and hiring
org: Austin Parks and Recreation Department, Aquatic Division
pay_detail: Starting at $22.05 per hour (March 2026 posting)
duration: Seasonal; training happens before the swim season
deadline_text: Spring 2026 hiring open hours were Mar 31, Apr 16 and Apr 28 (4 to 8 p.m.) at 2818 San Gabriel St. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Lifeguard training and hiring starts at age 15 with no upper age limit. You need a physical Social Security card and Texas-issued ID for the in-person paperwork.
how_to_apply: Step 1: fill out the online lifeguard job application. Step 2: visit the Aquatic Office in person at 2818 San Gabriel St. with your Social Security card, Texas ID and any hiring paperwork emailed to you. Questions: 512-974-9330.
notes: The 2026 posting also offered a $200 stipend for guards trained and working 40 hours before July 4, 2026. One library list says age 16+; the Parks page (dated March 20, 2026) says 15. Texas hour limits apply to 15 year olds.

name: Teen Summer Volunteer Program, St. David's Medical Center
org: St. David's HealthCare, St. David's Medical Center
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 7 to 8 weeks, usually first week of June to end of July, two 4 hour shifts a week
deadline_text: The page says applications open March 15 and close April 15 at 11:59 pm, once a year. The year is not stated.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18. You must be 15 by June 1 and free for the whole program.
how_to_apply: Send the online volunteer application. If you are accepted, you get orientation and training details later. Email sdmc.volunteers@stdavids.com. Or call 512-544-4491.
notes: Records are required for 2 MMR doses, 2 chickenpox doses or history, Tdap within 10 years, a TB test within 90 days and a flu shot. Homeschooled teens may apply year round. Up to 2 service day absences may be requested ahead of time.

name: Teen Summer Volunteer Program, St. David's North Austin Medical Center
org: St. David's HealthCare, North Austin Medical Center
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 7 to 8 weeks, usually first week of June to end of July. Weekly hours are not stated.
deadline_text: The page says applications run March 1 to March 31 and late materials are not accepted. The year is not stated.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. You must be 16 by June 1 and available the whole program.
how_to_apply: Send the online application. Then you get an email asking for a teen and parent agreement, two letters of support, short essay answers and shot records. Teens who are picked get an invite to interview. Orientation is by invite. Email namc.volunteers@hcahealthcare.com or call 512-901-1223.
notes: St. David's Medical Center in central Austin has a separate teen program with different ages (15 to 18) and dates. Apply to the campus whose rules you meet.

name: VolunTeen Program
pay_detail: Volunteer service. Cost and pay are not stated on the page I could read.
duration: 60 hours of training plus 40 hours of service
deadline_text: Dates and application window are not stated on the page I could read.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. Other rules are not stated on the page I could read.
how_to_apply: Thinkery's VolunTeens web address forwards to an online volunteer application (Volgistics). That form needs JavaScript, so I could not read it. Check it for the current steps.
notes: Thinkery also runs a teen Counselor in Training program for summer camps. Its page was not found (404), so it is not listed here. Check the dates, cost and application window before you apply.

name: Urban Roots High School Leadership Programs
pay_detail: Described as paid youth internships. The amount is not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: Applications are closed. The page says to watch for future opportunities. No dates are posted.
who_can_apply: The page does not state ages, grades or school or home rules. It says applications are closed and to watch for future chances.
how_to_apply: No application is open now. Contact Urban Roots at info@urbanrootsatx.org or 512-750-8019 to ask when the next one opens.
notes: Details on this page are thin. The page does not name a Summer Farm Program. Ask about ages, pay and season before counting on it. The same page lists free elementary day camps (2nd to 5th grade) and a free middle school Food Lab, which are not for high schoolers.

name: Youth Career Services
pay_detail: Work experience is part of the services. Paid work experience is named only for the SEAL program (students with disabilities ages 16 to 22). Pay amounts are not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline listed. Start any time.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24 (out of school youth services target ages 16 to 24). The page says low income youth. For training scholarships and case managed help, the main page lists U.S. work authorization, living in Austin or Travis County, and one more need related to work, income or school.
how_to_apply: Click Get Started on the Youth Services page. It leads to the Jumpstart Your Career registration form and a career info session. You can also use the contact page or call your local career center.
notes: The Jumpstart form asks for the last four digits of a Social Security number. It uses them to check your info on WorkInTexas.com. Summer jobs through SEAL need year round part in WIOA. No income limit is listed.

name: Austin Youth Council
org: City of Austin Economic Development (Youth Initiatives)
pay_detail: Pay is not mentioned on the page.
duration: Monthly meetings and service events. Term length is not stated on the page.
deadline_text: Applications are closed. The page says 2027 to 2028 applications are expected to open in Spring 2027.
who_can_apply: High school students who live in the City of Austin or its Extraterritorial Jurisdiction (ETJ). Students who only attend school in Austin are not eligible. No citizenship rule. A 2.5 GPA or higher is preferred, but applicants are read as a whole.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page for the application in Spring 2027. Send questions to the program coordinator. Her email is abrianna.citta01@austintexas.gov.
notes: Members may attend national conferences each year, including one in Washington, D.C. The page does not say who pays for travel.

name: Austin Youth Development (AYD)
org: Austin Public Health, City of Austin
pay_detail: Pay, hours and length are not listed on the page.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No application dates are listed.
who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 22 who live in the Austin and Travis County area. You need a reliable ride. You must be able to get a driver's license within 90 days. You must have a high school diploma or GED, or be working toward one.
how_to_apply: Complete the online interest form linked on the page. Call 512-972-4785 or email AYD@austintexas.gov.
notes: The page says youth work for the City while building skills toward education and career goals. It does not say what the work is, or give pay, hours, length or application dates. Call before applying. Office: 1416 Montopolis Drive, Austin.

name: Youth Forest Council
org: City of Austin, Austin Climate Action and Resilience (Urban Forest Program)
pay_detail: $22.05 per hour, about 10 to 15 hours per month
duration: One year, June to May; one full council meeting a month
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026-27 cohort were due March 15, 2026. The page says applications open again in January 2027.
who_can_apply: Young people ages 16 to 20 who live in the City of Austin or its extraterritorial jurisdiction and are eligible to work legally in the U.S. No academic requirements.
how_to_apply: Online application (about 1.5 hours), short-answer questions, and one reference who completes a recommendation form. Accepted members become City of Austin employees and must verify work eligibility.
notes: Meetings are held at locations around Austin and transportation help may be available.

name: Bard on the Beach Volunteer Program
org: Bard on the Beach Shakespeare Festival
pay_detail: Unpaid. Every 25 hours earns ticket codes and access to dress rehearsals.
duration: Mid-May to mid-September, shifts of 2 to 5 hours
deadline_text: Applications are closed until early 2027.
who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. Can give at least 25 hours between mid-May and mid-September. Basic English.
how_to_apply: Apply when the page reopens. Then you do a 30 minute interview. Orientation is in early April. Training runs April to June.
notes: The day it reopens is not posted. Contact the Volunteer Coordinator through the page.

name: BART Summer Internship (high school)
pay_detail: $20 per hour (high school, 2026)
duration: June 22 to July 31, 2026, 10 to 20 hours a week
deadline_text: 2026 program ran June 22 to July 31, 2026. Direct applications are not accepted. 2027 not posted.
who_can_apply: At least 16 years old, and enrolled in high school or college (or enrolled within the past 12 months). A community group must sponsor your placement.
how_to_apply: You cannot apply to BART directly. Ask a community organization or your school to sponsor you and have them email workforcedevelopment@bart.gov.
notes: Sponsor organizations fund the placements. Build a relationship with a community group and ask them to contact workforcedevelopment@bart.gov.

name: Berkeley High CTE Pathways
fields: health; law-government; arts-media; tech-cs; engineering; trades
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.
deadline_text: Choose pathway classes during course selection.
who_can_apply: Berkeley High students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe enrollment. Contact CTE Manager Wyn Skeels, WynSkeels@berkeley.net, (510) 644-8727, or your counselor.
notes: Pathway classes meet the a-g rules for getting into college. Middle schoolers get a STEM exploration track.

name: Berkeley Humane Volunteer (teens 12 and up)
deadline_text: Rolling. Internships are 18+ only.
who_can_apply: Age 12 or older. Ages 12 to 15 must have a parent or guardian with them 1 to 1. Age 16 and up can volunteer alone with a release form.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a General Volunteer Orientation online, read the manual, attend orientation. Contact volunteer@berkeleyhumane.org, (510) 845-7735.
notes: Internships need 18 or older (10 to 20 plus hours a week for 3 months or more).

name: Berkeley Pre-College Scholars (Summer Sessions)
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $15,987 (8 weeks, June 22 to Aug 14) or $14,687 (6 weeks, July 6 to Aug 14). There is also an application fee. One media scholarship was offered in 2026.
duration: 6 or 8 weeks
deadline_text: 2026 application ran Feb 2 to Mar 17, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Finished 10th or 11th grade, 3.0 GPA, 16 by June 21 (2026 rule).
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Pre-College Scholars site. The 2026 window opened Feb 2, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
notes: Very expensive. Aid is limited. Also needs a 3.0 GPA and good standing at your school.

name: Berkeley Public Library Teen Volunteer and Youth Worker
pay_detail: Volunteering is unpaid. Youth Worker jobs are paid (rate not posted; no benefits).
duration: Youth Worker up to 15 hours a week
deadline_text: Library page says YouthWorks accepts applications in March and October only. YouthWorks lists a Winter 2027 interest form due Oct 30, 2026.
who_can_apply: Teen volunteer: fill out the application. No age is stated. Youth Worker: ages 14 to 25. No experience is needed. A work permit is required if under 18.
how_to_apply: Volunteers: complete the Teen Volunteer Application form. Paid work: go through Berkeley YouthWorks (2180 Milvia St, 510-981-4970); see the YouthWorks page for the current interest form.
notes: The library page also lists other groups that take teen volunteers. Berkeley YouthWorks may require Berkeley residency.

name: Teen Council
org: Berkeley Repertory Theatre, School of Theatre
pay_detail: Transportation stipend. Free admission to teen programs and shows, and free food at events.
deadline_text: A new group is chosen at the start of each school year. No 2026 to 2027 dates are posted; join the mailing list for news.
who_can_apply: Bay Area high school students. A new group starts at the beginning of each school year.
how_to_apply: Join the Teen Council mailing list on the Teen Council page, or email teencouncil@berkeleyrep.org.
notes: No grade or age rule is listed beyond high school. Competitive: only 10 to 15 spots.

name: Berkeley YouthWorks
pay_detail: Wage not posted. Ready to Work workshop stipend if you attend at least 7 of 8 sessions.
duration: Winter 2027 placements run January to March 2027
deadline_text: Interest form for Winter 2027 is due October 30, 2026. Summer 2027 information is expected February 2027. Fall 2026 is full through November 2026.
who_can_apply: Berkeley residents (proof of residency at onboarding). Priority for youth facing barriers, such as foster care or legal system involvement, English learners, young parents, and students with IEPs or 504 plans. The page states no age rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online YouthWorks interest form. Chosen candidates get an email for a 15 to 20 minute interview. Contact: youthworks@berkeleyca.gov, (510) 981-4970.
notes: An interest form does not guarantee a placement. Berkeley Public Library lists the Youth Worker age as 14 to 25. Berkeley residents only.

name: Beyond Emancipation (B:E) employment coaching for foster youth
pay_detail: No pay to the youth is stated. The cost of services to the youth is not stated on the pages read.
deadline_text: Ongoing. No application window is stated on the pages read.
who_can_apply: Current and former foster youth in Alameda County, per the homepage (it says it serves over 500 each year). The age range and intake steps are not stated on the pages read.
how_to_apply: Call 510.980.9010 or email info@beyondemancipation.org (both from the site footer). Staff connect youth to coaching, training and job resources.
notes: Corrected on 2026-10-07. The site loaded this time (the earlier certificate error is gone). The homepage and employment page say who is served and what coaching covers, but do not state an age range, costs or an intake process, so those are left null or not stated. This is a coaching service rather than a paid job, so the type is the closest available. The employment page lists outside job boards and training partners (Civicorps, Oakland Private Industry Council, EASTBAY Works), which are separate organizations. The jobs page is for B:E staff openings, not youth jobs. Call before relying on it.

name: Industry Clubs (Boys & Girls Clubs of North Central Illinois)
org: Boys & Girls Clubs of North Central Illinois
city: Elgin / South Elgin area and other Fox Valley clubs, IL
pay_detail: Described as paid; the amount is not stated.
duration: 8 to 10 week sessions
deadline_text: No dates posted on the page. Fill out the interest form to hear about the next session.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. The page does not say which clubhouse hosts each Industry Club or whether you must be a member first.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Industry Clubs interest form on the page, or email membership@bgcncil.org or call the South Elgin office at (847) 608-5017. Teen membership (middle and high school) is free and signs up through MyClubHub (bgcncil.org/join/).
notes: The organization runs Elgin and South Elgin clubhouses (administrative office at 735 Martin Dr, South Elgin) plus Aurora, Batavia and a Schaumburg Teen Center, but the Industry Clubs page does not say where each session meets. Ask before you sign up. Elgin clubhouses follow the School District U-46 calendar.

name: Keystone Club and Youth of the Year
org: Boys & Girls Clubs of North Central Illinois
city: Elgin, South Elgin, Aurora, Streamwood, Hanover Park and Schaumburg, IL
pay_detail: Teen membership is free. Winners of Youth of the Year are eligible for Club scholarships.
duration: Youth of the Year sessions start in January
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Youth of the Year sessions start each January. Applications are processed in the order received.
who_can_apply: Keystone Club is for ages 14 to 18. Youth of the Year is for ages 10 to 18. You must be a Club member. Teen membership (middle and high school) is free, and you must meet the local residency or school district rules.
how_to_apply: Create an account in MyClubHub, pick your clubhouse and fill out the membership application. Staff will email next steps and a start date. Contact for Youth of the Year: cmaxwell@bgcelgin.org.
notes: Age limits can differ by clubhouse. The Industry Clubs (paid career programs for teens) are a separate listing. A Schaumburg Teen Center page exists but only shows a calendar.

name: Junior Staff (Boys & Girls Clubs of Oakland)
pay_detail: The page says 'Paid positions and income.' The pay rate and hours are not stated.
deadline_text: Not stated on the page.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who have been Club members for 2 or more years and meet academic requirements. The page does not list the academic requirements.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Ask staff at your Clubhouse. The site lists a 3300 High Street address.
notes: The same Teens page lists Keystone Clubs (ages 14 to 18) and Youth of the Year (ages 16 to 18, a $20,000 scholarship opportunity, not a job). They are not separate cards because the page gives no joining steps. Staff openings are posted on LinkedIn (the careers page does not list them). Season, pay rate, hours and deadlines are not stated, so confirm with the Club before a teen applies. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

name: Black Girls Code Workshops
pay_detail: Workshop cost and pay are not stated on the home page. The Code Along videos on YouTube are free. The page does not say anyone is paid.
duration: Workshop length varies
deadline_text: See the events page for current workshops.
who_can_apply: Girls ages 7 to 18 for workshops. A separate College and Careers Community serves ages 18 plus.
how_to_apply: Check the community events page for current workshops: community.wearebgc.org/events.
notes: The home page did not name a Bay Area chapter, prices or workshop dates. Check the events page for what is open now. Code Along videos are free on YouTube. Home page shows no workshop price, so the card is not in the paid group.

name: Student Volunteers (Historic Smithfield)
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: Museum season April to December; July camp; some roles year-round
deadline_text: No deadline. Open season April to December.
who_can_apply: The page seeks volunteers and student volunteers. It lists no minimum age or youth rules.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Contact form on the volunteer page. You can also email info@historicsmithfield.org. Or call 540-231-3947.
notes: No age rule is posted, so ask whether teens under 16 or 18 need a parent. Shifts are Wednesday to Saturday daytime for tours and the store.

name: Junior Volunteer Program (LewisGale Hospital Montgomery)
pay_detail: Unpaid. A free meal in the cafeteria for a 3-hour shift.
duration: 3 to 9 hours a week in the school year. More shifts allowed in summer and school breaks with parent permission.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Qualified applicants are called for an interview as spots open.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. You need a parent signature and your shot record. You also need a note of support from a teacher, school counselor or an adult who is not family.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application. Send the other forms. They are a disclosure and release form, a signed parent consent form, your shot record and a note of support.
notes: The page also lists a signed disclosure and release form and parental consent form. You must keep your scheduled shifts. Hospital address: 3700 South Main Street, Blacksburg.

name: Montgomery County 4-H clubs (including Teens for a Better Tomorrow)
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the clubs page. Ask the Extension office.
duration: Clubs meet 9 to 12 months a year. Home school clubs meet Oct to early May.
deadline_text: No deadline is posted. Clubs fill first come, first served.
who_can_apply: Community and project clubs are for ages 9 through 18. The home school Senior club is ages 14 to 19. Clubs have size limits and fill first come, first served, and they depend on volunteer leaders.
how_to_apply: Email one of the Extension 4-H staff on the page. They are Kendra Young kkyoung@vt.edu, Lesa Miller lvmiller@vt.edu and Margarita Palomino mrpalomi@vt.edu. Or call the Montgomery County Extension office at 540-382-5790. Staff pass your request to the club leaders.
notes: The clubs page does not give an age rule or meeting time for the Teens for a Better Tomorrow club, so ask staff. This is a youth club, not a paid job.

name: Summer Bridge: Women in STEM (Radford University)
org: Radford University, Artis College of Science and Technology
pay_detail: $1,600 covers tuition, room and board. Competitive scholarships can cover the full cost, and earlier applicants are more likely to get one.
duration: One week, residential (dates not shown on the page)
deadline_text: No dates or deadline are shown on the page. It links to a 2026 application.
who_can_apply: Rising high school sophomores, juniors and seniors from Virginia or other states. It is not just for girls. Any student who is interested can apply.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Upload a typed essay of 400 words about why you like science, math or IT. Get one letter from a counselor, teacher or adult leader. Contact David Horton, rhorton@radford.edu, or 540-831-5958.
notes: Radford is about 15 miles from Blacksburg. Families get students to and from campus. You share a room with one other student.

name: Summer Enrichment Experience (SEE Camp)
org: Edward Via College of Osteopathic Medicine (VCOM), Virginia campus
pay_detail: Free. Meals, lodging and activities are included. No pay.
duration: One week (two sessions in 2026: weeks of June 21 and July 5)
deadline_text: 2026 registration ran Feb 6 to Mar 6, with acceptances Mar 15 and week commitment due Apr 1. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors with a minimum 3.5 GPA. The page lists no location rule.
how_to_apply: Register online during the winter window. The page gave no apply link when read, so use the contact on the page: Louann Morrow, lomorrow@vcom.edu.
notes: Next-cycle dates are not posted; expect a similar early-year window. Camp has a strict dress code (closed-toe shoes, no shorts or hats) and no phones in the anatomy lab.

name: Virginia 4-H State Congress
pay_detail: 2026 prices: $310 for full time registration, $70 for the one-day competition. Each unit gets one first-time delegate scholarship for half the cost ($155).
duration: 4 days (2026: June 16 to 19)
deadline_text: 2026 Congress was June 16 to 19, 2026. The page gives two different 2026 registration windows: March 6 to May 10, 2026, and March 13 to May 15, 2026 on 4-H Online. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Enrolled senior 4-H members in Virginia. The page says the event is for 4-H youth ages 14 to 18. You must be signed up as a member through 4-H Online.
how_to_apply: Join 4-H first. Your county 4-H office can help. Then register through your family profile in 4-H Online. Your county 4-H agent handles unit delegations.
notes: You must already be a 4-H member. Part of the page still shows last year's details, so check the newest page. Statewide event that happens to be in Blacksburg, so it may also be listed as a Virginia-wide card.

name: Volunteer Montgomery (volunteers under 18)
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: No required hours
deadline_text: No deadline.
who_can_apply: Anyone who lives in Montgomery County can join. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian must come to every activity. They must also fill out a sign up form. No minimum age is listed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer sign up form linked on the FAQ page. Call 540-382-5775 or email hayesaw@montgomerycountyva.gov. Hours are Mon to Fri, 8:30 to 5.
notes: Teens need an adult with them, so it works best for families or a parent who volunteers too. A volunteer inactive for more than 12 months may be removed from the roll.

name: BLAST: Building Leaders for Advancing Science and Technology (Virginia Tech session)
org: Virginia Space Grant Consortium with Virginia Tech and partner universities
pay_detail: Free for all participants. Meals are provided during the session.
duration: 3 days, in college dorms
deadline_text: Applications open December 1 and close February 1 (the page lists this window with 2027 session dates). 2027 sessions: William & Mary June 20 to 23, UVA June 27 to 30, Radford July 18 to 21, Virginia Tech July 21 to 24, Old Dominion July 25 to 28. Acceptance notices go out at the end of April.
who_can_apply: Current 8th or 9th grade students at a Virginia middle, high, home-school or private school. You must be a Virginia resident and a U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident, with at least a C+/B- average (2.7 GPA) and a desire to explore STEM. The program is meant for students without STEM experience.
how_to_apply: Use the online application on the BLAST page. Pick one session. A recommender and a school counselor must also submit forms online before the deadline.
notes: This is a state program with sessions at five universities, so it may also be listed as a Virginia-wide card. The page says applicants must be a current 8th or 9th grader in one place. It describes rising 9th and 10th graders in another place. That means the same thing, since you apply in the school year before. The Feb 1 close date comes from the 'December 1 to February 1' window. The page does not tie it to a year.

name: CyberSpark cybersecurity camp (Virginia Tech)
org: Virginia Tech College of Engineering, DoD Senior Military College Cyber Institute
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page.
duration: 5 days
deadline_text: 2026 camps: July 6 to 10 in Blacksburg and July 27 to 31 in Arlington, VA. Applications closed March 24, 2026 and decisions were emailed April 17, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising 8th and 9th grade students. Any student who might like cybersecurity is welcome. You do not need any previous experience.
how_to_apply: Use the application link on the CyberSpark page. Phone: 540-231-4312.
notes: Mostly for younger teens (rising 8th and 9th graders). Cost and whether it is a day camp or overnight are not stated, so ask the program. Camp, not a job.

name: Explore Architecture (formerly Inside Design)
pay_detail: 2026 tuition: Blacksburg session $1,250 (materials not included, about $100 estimated); virtual session $250. Needs-based scholarships are offered through the registration form.
duration: One week (2026 Blacksburg session June 21 to 27)
deadline_text: 2026 registration opened Dec 1 and closed May 15 or when full. The page says the program is being rebooted; 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Everyone in grades 9 to 12. No prior design courses needed.
how_to_apply: Use the registration links on the program page for the Blacksburg or virtual session. No refunds after the May 15 close. Questions: Chris Pritchett, cpritche@vt.edu.
notes: Page shows 2026 information. Expect registration to open around Dec 1 again, but this is a past pattern and not confirmed. Overnight campers stay in suite-style dorms with an RA.

name: Geosciences High School Summer Camp
org: Virginia Tech Department of Geosciences with the Fralin Life Sciences Institute
pay_detail: $120 for the week (2026). Two scholarships are available each week for families with financial need.
duration: One week, 9am to 4pm (2026: June 1 to 5), day camp, no overnight
deadline_text: 2026 camp ran June 1 to 5. No registration deadline and no 2027 dates posted.
who_can_apply: Campers ages 15 to 18. The page lists no school or residency rules. Limit of 16 campers.
how_to_apply: Sign up with the link on the STEM Summer Camp page. For a scholarship, email the contact on the page. That is kdivitto@vt.edu or the Fralin education director.
notes: The same page lists camps for younger ages; only the Geosciences camp for ages 15 to 18 is for teens. The page shows 2026 details, so confirm before planning for 2027.

name: Pamplin's Inspiring Possibilities (PIP) Academy
org: Virginia Tech Pamplin College of Business
pay_detail: Free. The page says cost of attendance is covered except travel to and from Blacksburg. No pay.
duration: 10 days, residential (page dates: Thursday July 9 to Saturday July 18)
deadline_text: Application deadline not shown on the page. The page shows the 2026 session; the next one for seniors in 2027-28 is not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students who start their senior year in 2026-27. You need a GPA of 3.5 out of 4.0 or the same in another scale. You need to have done or be doing pre-calculus. You also write a short note about why you are interested.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the PIP page and submit a statement of interest. Questions: PCOBrecruiting@vt.edu.
notes: Only for rising seniors, so a teen has one chance to apply. Travel to Blacksburg is on the family.

name: Pathways for Future Engineers (Virginia Tech)
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program pages. Ask pathways@vt.edu.
duration: Two-week summer program plus campus visits during the school year
deadline_text: The pages link a 2026 summer program and a 2026 application. No 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Virginia residents entering grade 10, 11 or 12. You must be a first generation college student. That means neither parent graduated from a four year college in the U.S. or abroad.
how_to_apply: Send in the Pathways application linked on the program page. Contact Perry Martin at pathways@vt.edu with questions.
notes: Only for Virginia residents who would be first generation college students. The pages do not say whether the summer program is free. The eligibility text on the page mentions students entering grades in the fall of 2025, so it may be out of date. Check the application link before you plan.

name: VT Summer Strings
org: Virginia Tech School of Performing Arts (VT String Project)
pay_detail: $450 covers meals, dorm housing, T-shirt, music and supplies
duration: 3 days, residential (June 12-14 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 camp was June 12-14, 2026. 2027 dates and registration not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th graders with at least two years of lessons on violin, viola, cello or double bass.
how_to_apply: Registration information is not posted yet (the 2026 page said it was coming soon). Questions: stringproject@vt.edu.
notes: Dates are last year's. The page said registration information was coming soon.

name: Talent Search (Virginia Tech)
pay_detail: Free. No pay.
duration: Ongoing through school years
deadline_text: No deadline posted.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 12 at listed schools. They include Blacksburg High, Auburn High, Christiansburg High and Eastern Montgomery High. It mostly serves students who are first in their family to go to college and have lower family income. Any student who needs college prep help may join.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the Talent Search page if you attend a listed school. A Spanish application PDF is also posted.
notes: Not a job. It is a free college access program. Out-of-school and adult learners have a separate application.

name: UPWARDS Summer Camp: semiconductors and microelectronics (Virginia Tech)
org: Virginia Tech UPWARDS program and Center for Engineering Excellence and Discovery (CEED)
pay_detail: $2,500 for two weeks. It covers room, board and program costs. You pay your own travel and personal items. Scholarships are available based on financial need. Cancel 30 or more days before camp for a 50% refund.
duration: 2 weeks, residential
deadline_text: No dates for the next camp are posted on the pages read. The apply page still refers to the 2025 application.
who_can_apply: Rising 11th and 12th grade students, per the Virginia Tech engineering pre-college list. The camp pages read do not give more rules.
how_to_apply: There are two parts. One is a student application. It has activities, short essays of 120 words or less each, and a transcript. The transcript does not need to be official. The other is a parent form. It has consent and a financial statement used for scholarships. The application is shared with the C-Tech2 camp. You can choose either camp or both.
notes: Costs money and is a camp, not a job. The pages read are partly out of date (they mention the 2025 application), so check the newest page and confirm dates with the program. The Virginia Tech C-Tech2 camp has its own card in this guide.

name: Volunteering at the Bloomington Animal Shelter
org: City of Bloomington Animal Care and Control
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: 2-hour weekly shift for a minimum of 6 months
deadline_text: The page (updated September 24, 2026) says the waitlist is open. You join the waitlist now and get the application link later.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15 must be with a legal guardian at all times. Ages 16 and older can volunteer on their own. Everyone must pass screening.
how_to_apply: Join the waitlist through the Bloomington Volunteer Network. Use the green button on the page. That is not the application. The volunteer director will email you a link to it later.
notes: Book Buddies (K to 6th grade, all ages welcome with an adult) needs no application. Shelter hours for Book Buddies are listed on the page.

name: Youth Tree Tenders
pay_detail: $15 per hour
duration: Part time, Monday to Friday 9am to 1pm (20 hours a week). Two 4-week sessions: June and July (2026 dates).
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran Monday March 2 to Friday May 8. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Anyone 15 or older who can do hard physical work. That means digging, carrying mulch buckets and pulling water tanks. You must show up on time. Grant rules also ask that you treat all people fairly, no matter their gender, who they love or their race.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online form linked from the job page. Questions: hello@canopybloomington.org.
notes: The page does not say which year the March and May dates belong to, but the weekday dates match 2026. Check the page again in early 2027. Work permit rules for Indiana minors were not checked.

name: Summer Art Camp: Teen Art Week
org: Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art, Indiana University
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the page
duration: 1 week, noon to 3 p.m. Monday to Friday (July 27 to 31 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 teen week is full. The page says registration for each camp opens on the museum calendar; 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a class. Use the events calendar at the Eskenazi Museum.
notes: The 2026 camp was full. Younger weeks are for ages 7 to 12. Contact the museum for cost.

name: Construction Volunteer and Student Chapters
org: Habitat for Humanity of Monroe County
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Lunch is provided for construction site volunteers.
duration: Ongoing; many volunteers come weekly, monthly or for special events
deadline_text: No deadline. Contact Habitat to sign up for a build day.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. You must be 18 to use power tools. Student chapters exist at Bloomington High School North and South.
how_to_apply: Email ec@monroecountyhabitat.org to sign up for a build day. You can also use the contact form on the volunteer page.
notes: Wear closed-toe shoes and clothes you do not mind getting dirty. Groups such as schools can sign up together. ReStore roles are listed but the page does not state a separate age for them.

name: Acting for the Camera (IU summer program)
org: Department of Theatre and Drama and The Media School, Indiana University Bloomington
pay_detail: $950, which includes lodging, meals, instruction, equipment use and supplies (2026 price).
duration: 1 week
deadline_text: 2026 session ran July 20 to 24, 2026. Students were told by April 26, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students. The page does not state exact grades or ages. Highly selective, about 15 to 20 students.
how_to_apply: Record a monologue of up to 90 seconds. Upload it to YouTube or Vimeo as unlisted. Then fill out the online application with the video link. The program can give you a monologue if you need one.
notes: You must live on campus. The application page is at cinemaacademy.indiana.edu/summer-sessions/afc.html. Check the exact age rules there.

name: Camp S.O.U.L. (Students Obtaining Unique musical Levels)
org: African American Arts Institute, Indiana University Bloomington
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page
duration: 6 days (June 13 to 18, 2027)
deadline_text: Camp is June 13 to 18, 2027 on the IU Bloomington campus. The page has an Apply now link but does not state an application deadline.
who_can_apply: Gifted high school students, such as singers, players and spoken word artists. Students are picked. Age and grade limits are not listed.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the camp page (an online form). Students are selected.
notes: Contact campsoul@iu.edu or the director, Ignoisco Miles. His email is imiles@iu.edu and his phone is 812-855-0816. Ask about cost and how to audition before you apply.

name: IU Cinema Academy
org: The Media School, Indiana University Bloomington
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the pages read. Three kinds of scholarships are offered.
duration: 1 week for most sessions; the Advanced Filmmakers Academy is 2 weeks
deadline_text: 2026 sessions ran July 6 to 24. The Media School lists 2027 sessions for June and July (various weeks). No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 18. The page has a star by this, so check the session page for exceptions.
how_to_apply: Fill in the form. It is on the Cinema Academy summer sessions page.
notes: There is also a one-week Online Filmmaking Bootcamp. The Media School also holds a free one-day teen workshop on Saturday Nov 14, 2026 (Cinema, Game Dev and Journalism tracks).

name: Factor Future Educator Program (IU School of Education)
org: School of Education, Indiana University Bloomington
pay_detail: Free. Food and lodging are covered.
duration: 1 week (July 11 to 17, 2027)
deadline_text: Program is July 11 to 17, 2027. The page says applications will open in February 2027. No closing date is posted.
who_can_apply: Current Indiana high school juniors on a college-prep path. That means the Indiana GPS Diploma or GPS Diploma Plus. You need a 3.0 or higher cumulative GPA. You should like teaching, counseling or student services.
how_to_apply: The online application opens in February 2027. Use the link on the page to ask for more info and get updates.
notes: The page does not state the exact day it opens or closes. Only people who live in Indiana can join.

name: IU Game Development Camp (in person)
org: The Media School, Indiana University Bloomington
pay_detail: Overnight $850, day camp $500. Scholarships are available.
duration: 5 days
deadline_text: 2027 session dates are listed as coming soon on the camp page. No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Students ages 12 to 18. The minimum age varies by camp, so check the page for each session. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Sign up online on the camp website. The scholarship form is separate.
notes: Overnight tuition includes dorm lodging. Day camp is an option for local students. Tuition includes meals, a t-shirt, a thumb drive and a water bottle. Media School also lists June and July 2027 weeks.

name: High School Journalism Institute (HSJI)
org: The Media School, Indiana University Bloomington
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the pages read. Scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: High school students. Beginners and experienced students are both welcome. Age limits are not stated.
how_to_apply: Register online and choose one workshop per session. You can sign up for one or both sessions. Full workshops may have a waitlist.
notes: Run since 1946. Check the site for cost and dorm details before you plan.

name: Jim Holland Research Initiative in STEM Education (RISE)
org: Department of Biology, Indiana University Bloomington
pay_detail: $600 stipend after you finish the program. Accepted students also pay a $125 non-refundable registration fee.
duration: 2 weeks (June 21 to July 3 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. 2027 dates are not posted yet. In 2026, accepted students were told in late April.
who_can_apply: High school juniors with a GPA of at least 3.2, not counting extra credit. You are taking or have taken science and math. You want a science career. Students from the other Holland programs go first.
how_to_apply: Apply online. A parent or guardian must say they know. A counselor checks your classes and grades. You also need letters from a science teacher and a math teacher.
notes: Housed in a campus dorm. In 2026, accepted students were told the week of April 20. Contact holland@iu.edu, 812-855-5179.

name: Jim Holland Summer Enrichment Program in Biology (SEP)
org: Department of Biology, Indiana University Bloomington
pay_detail: $125 non-refundable registration fee, charged only to accepted students
duration: About 1 week (July 19 to 24 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. 2027 dates are not posted yet. In 2026, accepted students were told in late April.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 8, 9 or 10. You need a GPA of at least 3.0, not counting extra credit. You are taking or have taken science and math.
how_to_apply: Apply online. A parent or guardian must say they know. A counselor checks your classes and grades. You also need letters from a science teacher and a math teacher.
notes: Housed in a campus dorm. Contact Kody Beaver, holland@iu.edu, 812-855-5179.

name: Jim Holland Summer Science Research Program (SSRP)
org: Department of Biology, Indiana University Bloomington
pay_detail: $125 non-refundable registration fee for accepted students
duration: About 1 week (July 12 to 19 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. 2027 dates are not posted yet. In 2026, accepted students were told in late April.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9, 10 or 11. You need a GPA of at least 3.2, not counting extra credit. You are taking or have taken science and math. You want a science career.
how_to_apply: Apply online. A parent or guardian must say they know. A counselor checks your classes and grades. You also need letters from a science teacher and a math teacher.
notes: Housed in a campus dorm. You contact your assigned mentor before the program. Expect to work some evenings. Contact Kody Beaver, holland@iu.edu, 812-855-5179.

name: Hoosier Debate Camp
org: Indiana Debate Team, Indiana University Bloomington
pay_detail: 2026 prices: housing and meals $950 ($150 deposit plus $800 tuition); commuter with meals $750; commuter without meals $500. Scholarships awarded on a rolling basis after May 15.

who_can_apply: Students of all backgrounds and experience levels. The IU O'Neill School page says middle and high school students. Exact ages are not stated.
how_to_apply: Register and pay the deposit through the camp sign up page (IU Conferences payment page). Financial aid form is separate.
notes: Labs may be cancelled if too few students sign up, and you would be offered another lab. Camp size is limited. The camp says it is cheaper than many other university camps.

name: HSJI One-Day Journalism Workshop (Journalism: Oh, the Places You Could Go!)
org: High School Journalism Institute, The Media School, Indiana University Bloomington
pay_detail: Free. Lunch is provided.

who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 18. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the registration form on the workshop page. A liability form and details are emailed before the workshop.
notes: Drop-off and pick-up are at the Franklin Hall commons atrium (601 E Kirkwood Ave). This is separate from the summer HSJI program.

name: Jacobs Composition Academy (online)
org: Jacobs Academy, Jacobs School of Music, Indiana University Bloomington
pay_detail: Track 1 (private lessons plus group class) $800. Track 2 (group class only) $550. A $50 non-refundable deposit is credited to tuition.
duration: 12 weeks, entirely on Zoom
deadline_text: Spring 2027 semester: registration and payment close January 11, classes start January 18, concerts April 1 to 16. The page says Spring 2027 registration begins in mid November.
who_can_apply: People 14 and older (the page also welcomes adults). Parents of kids under 14 can email musicsp@iu.edu. You do not need an audition or past experience.
how_to_apply: Complete the online registration form and pay the deposit and tuition. Questions go to musicsp@iu.edu.
notes: There is also a summer intensive linked from the page. Group class is Tuesdays 8:30 to 9:30 p.m. Eastern.

name: Jacobs Dance Summer Intensives (Ballet and Contemporary)
org: Indiana University Jacobs School of Music, Jacobs Academy
pay_detail: Tuition $1,000 per one-week session ($2,000 for two, $3,000 for three) plus $100 registration fee credited to tuition. Optional housing with meals $550 per session; commuter meal plan $115 per session.
duration: 1 to 3 weeks: June 6-12, June 13-19 (ballet) and June 20-26 (contemporary), 2027
deadline_text: Registration for summer 2027 opens mid-December 2026. Prescreen and registration due February 8, 2027; acceptance notice February 19; payment due March 1.
who_can_apply: Ballet intensive: ages 13 to 18, admitted by a filmed prescreen of a classical variation. Contemporary intensive: ages 14 to 18, must have completed grade 8, no screening.
how_to_apply: Online registration form and $100 fee; ballet applicants upload a private YouTube link to a classical variation. Do not pay tuition until accepted. Then submit the Participant Agreement Form.
notes: Intense schedule (Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM). The student pays; this is not a job.

name: Summer Brass Academy (Jacobs School of Music)
org: Jacobs Academy, Jacobs School of Music, Indiana University Bloomington
pay_detail: Tuition $750 plus a $100 registration fee credited to tuition. Optional youth housing with meals is $500 (2026 prices).
duration: 1 week (June 21 to 27 in 2026)
