who_can_apply: High school age (pre-college) and undergraduate brass players. The page gives no exact age range. You send a placement recording for ensemble placement.
how_to_apply: Sign up online and pay the $100 fee and tuition. Also upload a placement recording to the Jacobs audition portal.
notes: Confirm 2027 dates and prices.

name: Jacobs Summer Jazz Workshop
org: Jacobs Academy, Jacobs School of Music, Indiana University Bloomington
grades: Entering 8th grade through the summer after high school
pay_detail: Tuition $775 plus a $100 registration fee credited to tuition. Optional housing with meals is $500 (2026 prices). Need-based aid and merit awards exist.
duration: 1 week

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18 on brass, woodwinds, voice, strings or rhythm instruments. No audition to get in, but you send a placement recording.
how_to_apply: Sign up online and pay the $100 fee and tuition. Then upload a placement recording that has not been edited. YouTube links are fine. Use the Jacobs audition portal.
notes: Check the 2027 dates and prices before you plan.

name: IU Summer Music Clinic
org: Indiana University Jacobs School of Music, Jacobs Academy
pay_detail: 2026: residential tuition $1,120 (housing and meals); commuter tuition $815 (lunch and dinner); $100 non-refundable registration fee credited to tuition. Need-based financial aid is available.
duration: One week (June 14 to 20 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 session June 14-20, 2026: registration and payment due May 8, 2026; financial aid application due April 13, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Intermediate to advanced string, wind and percussion students in grades 8 to 12. Jazz band requires an audition on the first day.
how_to_apply: Online registration form plus the $100 registration fee, tuition by the payment deadline, then a Participant Agreement Form. Contact: musicsp@iu.edu.
notes: Costs and dates are from the 2026 session page. The student pays; this is not a job. The Jacobs Academy also lists other pre-college summer programs.

name: Summer Piano Academy (Jacobs School of Music)
org: Jacobs Academy, Jacobs School of Music, Indiana University Bloomington
pay_detail: Tuition $2,400 plus a $100 deposit credited to tuition (2026 prices). Housing and meal plans cost extra. Financial aid and scholarships exist.
duration: 2 weeks (June 27 to July 11 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 application, audition and financial aid forms were due March 2, 2026, with acceptance notices March 13. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Serious pianists ages 12 to 19. You must be able to practice several hours a day. You should play music that is early advanced to advanced. The director can admit exceptional students under 12. You must audition with a recording.
how_to_apply: Pay the $100 fee in the online sign-up form. Then upload a list of the music you play and two different pieces you play from memory. Send them as recordings to the Jacobs audition portal. Pay tuition only after you are accepted.
notes: The director is Dr. Elizabeth Yao (elizyao@iu.edu). Check the 2027 dates and prices.

name: Summer Saxophone Academy (Jacobs School of Music)
org: Jacobs Academy, Jacobs School of Music, Indiana University Bloomington
pay_detail: Tuition $900 plus a $100 registration fee credited to tuition. Optional housing with meals is $500 (2026 prices). Need-based aid exists.

deadline_text: 2026 registration, payment and placement recording were due May 15, 2026. Financial aid deadline was April 13, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 18. You send a placement recording so you can be placed in studios and groups.
how_to_apply: Finish the online sign-up and pay the $100 fee and tuition. Then upload a recording for placement in the Jacobs audition portal.
notes: Confirm 2027 dates and prices.

name: Summer String Academy (Jacobs School of Music)

duration: 4 weeks (June 20 to July 18 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 application and audition were due February 9, 2026, with acceptance notices February 20 and tuition due March 2. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Serious string players ages 12 to 18. You must audition by recording.
how_to_apply: Pay the $100 fee in the online sign-up form. Then upload two different pieces as recordings to the Jacobs audition portal. YouTube links are fine. Pay tuition only after you are accepted.
notes: Directed by Prof. Mimi Zweig (zweig@iu.edu). Confirm 2027 dates and prices.

name: Kelley Sprint Case Competition

who_can_apply: The city says it connects volunteers of all ages. Each posting sets its own rules, so check the listing for age limits.
how_to_apply: Search for chances at BloomingtonVolunteerNetwork.org. Make an account and sign up. Call the coordinator at 812-349-3433.
notes: You need an account on the volunteer network site. Parks volunteer pages on the city site list events, camps and clean-ups but do not state ages.

name: Teen Volunteer
org: WonderLab Museum of Science, Health, and Technology
grades: Entering grade 7 or higher in the fall of the next school year
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. Perks: free admission, 20 percent off in the gift store
duration: Ongoing; flexible hours
deadline_text: Apply any time. Volunteer orientation sessions in 2026 were listed through Tuesday, November 10, 2026 (prior registration required).
who_can_apply: Teens entering at least 7th grade in the fall of the next school year. Teens apply with the Teen Volunteer Application; adults 18 and over use a separate form.
how_to_apply: Submit the Teen Volunteer Application (online form linked on the Become a Volunteer page), then register for a volunteer orientation. Contact: Volunteer Manager, 812-337-1337 ext. 221.
notes: Middle and high school volunteers work alongside college students and adults. Some roles (parties, outreach) need prior museum experience and training. Outreach events require your own transportation.

name: WonderCamp High School Summer Intern
org: WonderLab Museum of Science, Health, and Technology
grades: Entering grade 9 per the Become a Volunteer page. The internship page says entering grades 9-12 or home-school equivalent. Graduating seniors may also apply.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer internship (the page describes it as volunteering your time)
duration: Summer camp weeks; training also required the Saturday before each camp week
deadline_text: Applications for summer 2026 are closed. The page says to check back for summer 2027. Dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens entering 9th through 12th grade, or the home-school equivalent. Graduating seniors may also apply. Required training is held at University Elementary School.
how_to_apply: Apply with the Teen Volunteer Application on WonderLab's Become a Volunteer page, choosing the WonderCamp internship; special training sessions are listed on the application form. Contact: 812-337-1337 ext. 221.
notes: Unpaid. The Become a Volunteer page says WonderCamp interns must be entering grade 9 in the fall of the next school year, while the internship page says entering grades 9 to 12; use the stricter reading (grade 9 or older) unless WonderLab says otherwise.

name: Aspire: Five-Week Music Performance Intensive
org: Berklee College of Music Summer Programs
pay_detail: Listed tuition $5,430, or $5,230 if you save before Jan 31. Housing $4,200. Scholarships exist (see the Scholarships link on the summer page).
duration: 5 weeks (listed dates July 9 to August 13; year not shown on the page)
deadline_text: The page lists a Jan 31 early-pay discount date. The application deadline is not stated on the page read.
who_can_apply: Students age 15 and up, based on the age filter on the Berklee summer page. Check the program page for any playing experience needed.
how_to_apply: Use the Admissions and How to Enroll links on the Berklee summer programs page.
notes: Costs money. The year of the listed dates is not shown, so confirm dates, prices and any audition steps on the program page.

name: Summer Youth Jobs Program
pay_detail: Paid internship; hourly rate not stated
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Thursday, 32 hours a week
deadline_text: Application season starts in March and slots usually fill by mid-April.
who_can_apply: Boston Public School high school students who need more support go first. You must be referred. You cannot apply on your own.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's Private Industry Council (PIC) contact. You can also ask a partner group: ABCD, Boys and Girls Club of Boston, Roxbury Tenants at Harvard, Sociedad Latina or METCO. They send students in.
notes: You cannot apply directly. Talk to your school's PIC career specialist or one of the partner organizations.

name: Junior Summer Volunteer Program (JSVP)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 8 weeks (2026: June 29 to Aug 21)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: BPS students could apply Jan 21; all students Mar 6; it closed Mar 9 after 100 applications. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students entering their junior or senior year who can commit to the full 8 weeks. Boston Public School students got the first application window. Preference goes to Boston residents.
how_to_apply: Apply online when it opens in winter. The program talks only with you. It does not talk with family or teachers. Questions: juniorsummervolunteerprogram@bmc.org.
notes: In 2026 the form closed March 9 after 100 applications. That was three days after it opened to all students. The page says the program takes 70 students.

name: Ready to Work (Boys & Girls Clubs of Boston)
pay_detail: The page says the internships are paid but gives no pay rate. The Clubs report about 500 teen jobs and internships a year.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the page.
who_can_apply: Teen members of Boys & Girls Clubs of Boston, which serves ages 6 to 18 at clubs in Boston and Chelsea. The page gives no age rule for the workforce program itself.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how teens are placed. Find your nearest Club on the Find Your Club page and ask about the Ready to Work program and the Club's Employment Specialist. General contact page: bgcb.org/contact-us.
notes: Confirm first: ages, hours and how to apply are not on the page. Under Massachusetts law (M.G.L. c.149 s.86) a child employed needs a work permit from the superintendent of schools, so ask the Club how permits are handled. The Clubs' home page said membership fees were waived for the 2025 to 2026 school year; ask about this year's fee. Teen centers: Mildred C. Hailey Teen Center (Jamaica Plain) and Josh Kraft Mattapan Teen Center. See permit.html?state=ma for the exact permit and steps.

name: Teen Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid
duration: Fall (September to December) and spring (January to June) cycles; five skill workshops on Monday afternoons at 4 p.m. on Zoom
deadline_text: The page says the program runs year-round, in a fall cycle (September to December) and a spring cycle (January to June). No application deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: Teens in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Email volunteer@bpl.org or call 617-859-2304 to ask about openings and apply.
notes: Sites: Brighton, Central Library, Teen Central, Codman Square, East Boston, Grove Hall, Hyde Park, Mattapan, Roslindale, Shaw-Roxbury and West Roxbury. Workshops include resume building, privacy training and know your rights in the workplace.

name: Academic Immersion (AIM)
pay_detail: 2026 total was $5,991 for commuters and $7,875 for residential students. 2027 rates post Dec 17.
duration: 3 weeks. 2027 dates (pending approval): June 27 to July 16 or July 18 to Aug 6
deadline_text: Applications for Summer 2027 open Dec 17, 2026. Close date not posted. The page says to check back Dec 17 for 2027 details.
who_can_apply: Students who start their junior or senior year in fall 2027. Students from other countries can apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Academic Immersion page. See the How to Apply page after Dec 17.
notes: Costs money. The 2027 price is not posted yet. The course page does not say whether it gives college credit.

name: High School Honors
pay_detail: Summer 2026 total was $7,245 (commuter, 8 credits) or $11,565 (residential, 8 credits), plus a $75 application fee. Summer 2027 costs post December 17, 2026. Limited financial aid (need and merit).
duration: 6 weeks; 2027 dates pending approval: June 27 to August 6, 2027
deadline_text: Applications open on December 17. The page does not list a final deadline.
who_can_apply: Students entering their junior or senior year of high school in fall 2027. Juniors need to be in Honors and/or AP courses.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with transcript, a 500 to 750 word personal statement and one academic teacher recommendation. The student must apply, not a parent or counselor.
notes: Expensive. 2027 dates are pending approval and may change. Standardized test scores are optional for summer 2027. Contact: summerhs@bu.edu.

name: RISE Internship/Practicum
pay_detail: 2026 total was $6,415 for commuters and $10,735 for residential students; $75 application fee. 2027 rates post Dec 17. Limited financial aid.
duration: 6 weeks (2027: June 27 to Aug 6)
deadline_text: Applications for Summer 2027 open Dec 17, 2026. Close date not posted.
who_can_apply: Students currently in their junior year of high school. The page says RISE is for a "domestic student" and does not define that term. Strong grades (the page says most competitive applicants are A- to A) and a STEM recommendation.
how_to_apply: You apply online yourself. Send your transcript and three short essays. Send one letter from a STEM teacher, counselor or research boss. For internships, also name three BU teachers you want to work with.
notes: Costs money. Test scores are optional for 2027. Placement in a requested lab is not guaranteed.

name: Summer Challenge
pay_detail: 2026 total was $3,989 for commuters and $5,245 for residential students; $75 application fee. 2027 rates post Dec 17.
duration: 2 weeks. Dates listed (pending approval): Session 1 June 20 to July 2, Session 2 July 11 to 23, Session 3 July 25 to Aug 6
deadline_text: Applications for Summer 2027 open Dec 17, 2026. Close date not posted.
who_can_apply: Students who start sophomore, junior or senior year in fall 2027. BU looks at your grades, courses and a personal essay. Students from other countries can apply.
how_to_apply: You apply online yourself. Send a transcript that starts in 9th grade. Write a personal essay of 500 to 750 words. Pay the $75 fee.
notes: Costs money. The calendar says dates are pending approval.

name: Mayor's Summer Youth Employment Program (MSYEP)
org: City of Cambridge Department of Human Service Programs
pay_detail: Paid minimum wage by the City; the page says $15.00 per hour for Summer 2025 (the page has not been updated with a 2026 rate)
duration: 6 weeks, 20 hours a week
deadline_text: Information about the 2027 program will be posted in early spring 2027. Hiring paperwork starts in mid-April.
who_can_apply: Cambridge residents who are 14 through the summer after finishing high school and eligible to work in the U.S. Priority goes to students eligible for free or reduced lunch and lower-income families.
how_to_apply: Apply online through Trax, the Department of Human Service Programs enrollment system. All applications go on a waitlist for review, which does not mean the program is full. Staff then schedule hiring paperwork (original ID and Social Security card needed).
notes: Questions: youthemployment@cambridgema.gov. The page does not mention a work permit; Massachusetts requires one for workers under 18 (M.G.L. c.149 s.86; Boston youth worker rights page written with the state Attorney General's Office). Participants may not miss more than 5 program days. There is no fixed maximum age on the page; eligibility ends after the summer following high school graduation.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadets, Boston Cadet Squadron
org: Civil Air Patrol, Boston Cadet Squadron (MA-002)
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.
duration: The squadron meets Saturdays from 4 to 6:30 p.m. at the Barnes Army Reserve Center, 495 Summer St., Boston, MA 02210.
deadline_text: No deadline. Contact the wing any time.
who_can_apply: Cadets ages 12 to 18. The Massachusetts Wing site lists Become a Cadet as ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: The squadron page does not describe a visit process. Use the Contact Us and Join CAP pages on the Massachusetts Wing site. The wing phone is 781-225-6540 and its email is hq@mawg.cap.gov (these are the wing's, not the squadron's).
notes: The Massachusetts Wing also lists a Hanscom squadron (MA-043). The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.

name: School-Year ZooTeens (Winter Teen Conservation Outreach Internship)
org: Zoo New England, Franklin Park Zoo
pay_detail: Unpaid internship
duration: 30 hours of weekend and February vacation week shifts, plus workshops
deadline_text: Applications for the Winter Teen Conservation Outreach Internship are due December 9, 2026 at 5:00 p.m.
who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 19 years old at the start of the internship, with a sincere interest in wildlife, education and environmental justice. About 6 to 8 interns are accepted.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application by December 9. Some applicants are invited to an in-person group interview. Email Ana Shapiro, Youth Programs Manager, at ashapiro@zoonewengland.org (no phone calls).
notes: Unpaid, so the work permit question is left open. Spring and summer teen internships are also planned; the page links a calendar of internship periods. The fall internship application is closed.

name: Summer ZooTeen Program
org: Zoo New England, Franklin Park Zoo
pay_detail: Paid roles (Boston and Cambridge residents only) and volunteer roles; hourly rate not stated
duration: Not stated on the program page
deadline_text: No application dates are posted on the program page. Check the zoo's Jobs and Volunteering pages or email the Youth Programs Manager.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 18. Paid ZooTeen roles are only for teens who live in Boston and Cambridge; volunteer roles are also offered.
how_to_apply: The program page does not give application steps. The school-year ZooTeen page lists the Youth Programs Manager, Ana Shapiro, at ashapiro@zoonewengland.org for questions, and an interest form for application updates.
notes: Work permit flag applies to the paid roles only (state rule: M.G.L. c.149 s.86 and the Boston youth worker rights page, written with the Attorney General's Office); volunteers do not need one. Dates and pay were not on the page, so confirm with the zoo.

name: futureBOS youth jobs (SuccessLink)
org: City of Boston Office of Youth Employment and Opportunity
pay_detail: Youth jobs (ages 14 to 18) are paid $15 an hour; leader jobs (19 to 24) $20 an hour. Professional development programs pay a stipend.
duration: Summer 2026 ran June 23 to August 29. School-year jobs are limited to up to 8 hours a week for youth; summer up to 25 hours a week.
deadline_text: School-year 2026-27 opportunities are open now and more are added through spring. Summer 2026 applications were rolling and closed; summer 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Youth jobs are for ages 14 to 18 (leader jobs for 19 to 24). Must be 14 by the start of the job, have finished 6th grade, and be legally permitted to work in the U.S. Most opportunities are limited to full-time Boston residents; some have extra requirements.
how_to_apply: Browse the futureBOS catalog, apply to at least three jobs, then get an offer and finish onboarding (work permit if under 18, proof of identity and work authorization, proof of school enrollment). City of Boston agency jobs can be onboarded in one visit to the YEO office at 1483 Tremont Street.
notes: Questions: futurebos@boston.gov or 617-635-4202. Under-18 workers need a Massachusetts work permit for the specific job (a doctor must sign for ages 14 and 15); the city page explains the steps. The $15 rate is quoted from the city FAQ. The state minimum wage statute (M.G.L. c.151 s.1) says a wage of less than $15.00 per hour is presumed oppressive and unreasonable; the current 2026 minimum wage page from the state Department of Labor Standards could not be read (403), so confirm the rate in your job offer. The work permit rule is M.G.L. c.149 s.86.

name: Secondary School Program
pay_detail: 2027 cost $4,180 to $15,980 depending on format and length, plus a $75 application fee. Financial aid is available.
duration: 4 weeks (June 14 to July 8 or July 12 to August 5, 2027) or 7 weeks (June 21 to August 6, 2027)
deadline_text: Application opens December 1, 2026. Early application and priority financial aid deadline January 13, 2027. Regular deadline February 10, 2027. Late deadline March 31, 2027.
who_can_apply: High school students who will graduate and enter college in 2027, 2028 or 2029. You must be at least 16 by June 13, 2027. You must not turn 19 before July 31, 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply online at Harvard Summer School when the application opens December 1, 2026. Financial aid is requested during the application.
notes: Expensive and selective. Residential financial aid is limited to U.S. citizens and permanent residents.

name: ICA Teens Programs (Teen Arts Council, Fast Forward, Photography Collective, Teen Exhibitions)
org: Institute of Contemporary Art, Boston (ICA Teens)
pay_detail: Participants receive compensation. The amount is not stated on the page.
duration: 2026 to 27 school year groups meet after school (4 to 7 p.m.; Teen Arts Council and Teen Exhibitions start at 4:30). Examples: Teen Arts Council Thursdays, Sept 10 to May 20; Fast Forward Wednesdays and Fridays, Oct 21 to May 5.
deadline_text: The page shows the 2026 to 27 schedules but no application dates or deadlines. Ask the ICA whether spots are still open.
who_can_apply: Teens of all skill levels and interests. The page does not give an age range, grades or a residency rule. Admission to the ICA is free for anyone 18 and under.
how_to_apply: Email teens@icaboston.org to get involved. The Teen Arts Council and Teen Exhibitions pages mention an application, but the programs page does not explain how to submit it. Phone: 617-478-3100.
notes: Confirm first. Ages, pay amount and deadlines are not on the pages we could read. Boston Public School students from participating high schools can earn school credit for taking part. Other ICA teen programs had no dates set. They are the Teen Digital Cooperative, and the music and photo break intensives. Paid work for people under 18 in Massachusetts needs a work permit (employment permit). See permit.html?state=ma for the exact permit and steps.

name: Mass General Brigham Youth Program
pay_detail: Paid internships in 11th and 12th grade and paid summer jobs (hourly rate not stated)
duration: Multi-year: exploration in 10th grade, paid internships in 11th and 12th grade
deadline_text: The page says applications open in the spring and selections are finalized in the summer. The 2026 link was due to appear in spring 2026; no 2027 date is posted. Summer jobs are recruited through the Boston Private Industry Council (PIC).
who_can_apply: Sophomores at the Edward M. Kennedy Academy for Health Careers, Revere High School, Chelsea High School or any Boston public school. A 3.0 GPA is required to apply.
how_to_apply: Ask your school guidance counselor (or PIC career specialist) in the fall and watch the program page for the spring application link. For summer jobs, contact your school's PIC career specialist.
notes: Combines the old Mass General Youth Scholars and Brigham Student Success Jobs programs. Sites include Mass General Hospital, Brigham and Women's, Faulkner Hospital and Mass Eye and Ear. Paid jobs under 18 need a Massachusetts work permit (state rule: M.G.L. c.149 s.86 and the Boston youth worker rights page; not on the MGB page).

name: Teen Arts Council
pay_detail: $15 per hour
duration: Thursdays 4 to 6:30 p.m., October 15, 2026 to May 27, 2027 (2026-27 cycle), plus two of three Sunday events
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026-27 Teen Arts Council are closed. The next cycle's dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 10, 11 or 12 who are City of Boston residents or attend Boston Public Schools, and who can attend Thursday sessions 4 to 6:30 p.m. all year.
how_to_apply: Check the MFA Teen Programs page for the next application. This cycle's application is closed.
notes: Paid job, so teens under 18 need a Massachusetts work permit (not mentioned on the MFA page; see M.G.L. c.149 s.86 and the Boston youth worker rights page). The MFA also offers Teen Studio Art Classes for ages 12 to 17.

name: Beaver Works Summer Institute (BWSI)
grades: Designed for students entering their senior year of high school
pay_detail: Free for families with income and assets under $200,000 (housing is not covered for in person programs). Families above that pay $3,000. No stipend is mentioned.
duration: Four week program in July. The online prerequisite course opens February 1.
deadline_text: The page says "BWSI 2027 Online Prerequisites are Now Open!" Self registration for the online course is open now. Approvals come in late January, the online course opens February 1, the summer application is sent in March, nominations are accepted through March 31, and the teacher or mentor recommendation is due April 2. The page does not give a final date for the summer application.
who_can_apply: Students who live or attend high school in the United States and finish the online course and the separate summer application. You must be in the US for the July program. The page lists no age or citizenship rule.
how_to_apply: Sign yourself up through the Formstack link on the Summer Program Application page. No nomination is needed. Or have a teacher or mentor nominate you. Later you need three essays of 500 words or less each. You need a teacher or mentor recommendation. You need parent or guardian information with an electronic signature. You also need to finish the online prerequisite course. Contact: bwsi-admin@mit.edu.
notes: Competitive. The cost wording on the page leaves the $200,000 to $200,001 range unclear, so ask BWSI if you are near that line. The online course is free and stays open to independent learners.

name: MITES Saturdays
org: MIT (MITES, Introduction to Technology, Engineering and Science)
pay_detail: Free of charge. Students pay only their own transportation to MIT (Lawrence students get free transport).
duration: 8 Saturdays in spring and 8 in fall, 10:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., for up to about five and a half years
deadline_text: The application deadline is not stated on the program pages read. Check the Apply page.
who_can_apply: Public school students from Boston, Cambridge or Lawrence, MA in 7th, 8th, 9th or 10th grade who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents (green card). Exceptions are not made.
how_to_apply: Create a profile in the MITES application portal and submit the MITES Saturdays application (separate from the Summer and Semester application).
notes: Students are expected to keep A and B grades; no minimum GPA to apply. The program encourages applicants who are underrepresented in STEM or from lower-income families or the first in their family to attend college.

name: MITES Summer
org: MIT (MITES, Introduction to Technology, Engineering and Science)
grades: 11th grade at time of application (rising seniors)
pay_detail: Free of charge. Students pay only for transportation; travel scholarships are available for MITES Summer.
duration: Six weeks, late June through early August, weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
deadline_text: The application deadline is not stated on the pages read. Check the Apply page.
who_can_apply: High school juniors who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents with a current green card. You can be from anywhere in the country, at a public, private or homeschool.
how_to_apply: Create a profile in the MITES application portal. MITES Summer and MITES Semester (a six-month STEM experience for rising seniors) share one application. Short-answer responses and recommendations from recent teachers are needed.
notes: Competitive and focused on students from underserved or under-resourced backgrounds. Residential on campus.

name: MIT PRIMES (math and bioinformatics research)
grades: High school sophomores and juniors (home schooled students count)
pay_detail: Free to join. Pay is not mentioned on the page.
duration: A year long after school program. The start date is not stated.
deadline_text: Applications are due 11:59 p.m. Eastern on November 2, 2026. Letters of recommendation are due November 6, 2026. Decisions come by early January 2027.
who_can_apply: High school sophomores and juniors who live in the United States. Students from Greater Boston can meet on campus. Other students can apply to PRIMES-USA. It meets with mentors online. Local and non-local students use the same portal.
how_to_apply: Use the online application portal linked on the MIT PRIMES how to apply page. It has an online questionnaire. It asks for two or three recommenders. Math teachers or camp counselors are ideal. It asks for a personal statement of up to 2 pages. It asks for lists of math books, courses, camps and computing skills. It also asks for solutions to the PRIMES 2027 Math Problem Set. Apply if you solve at least 70 percent. Upload solutions as one PDF with your name only in the file name.
notes: Competitive and heavy on math. There is also PRIMES Circle, a spring math enrichment program. It is for students within commuting distance of Boston. It has its own apply page at https://math.mit.edu/research/highschool/primes/circle/apply-circle.html, which was not read. Phone: (617) 253-4381.

name: Summer and Academic Year Youth Internships (Museum of Science)
grades: Enrolled in high school or an equivalent program
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the museum pages.
duration: The summer program is 7 weeks. The academic year program runs during the school year. Hours are not stated.
deadline_text: No openings were posted when checked on Oct 9, 2026. The museum says summer internships are usually recruited in February or March and fall ones in June or July, but timing can change. Deadlines are listed in each posting.
who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 19. You must be in high school or an equivalent program.
how_to_apply: Watch the museum's internship job board. Use View Internships on the Museum of Science internships page. Apply to the youth internship posting when it opens.
notes: The museum pages do not say if the internships are paid, so ask before you apply. Massachusetts law (M.G.L. c.149 s.86) says a child needs a work permit from the superintendent of schools to be employed. The museum also has Youth Volunteers, ages 14 to 19 and in high school. The volunteer page gives no application steps beyond a general interest form. See permit.html?state=ma for the exact permit and steps.

name: Summer Teen Internship Program
pay_detail: All teen internships are paid positions (rate not stated)
duration: One week of training and six weeks of work
deadline_text: The summer 2026 application is closed. The page says to check back next March for the summer 2027 application.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 and older. Most internships are open to residents of Boston and Cambridge.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the application opens (expected next March). Interns also attend a weekly professional development course and an ocean advocacy course. Questions: teens@neaq.org.
notes: Paid job, so teens under 18 need a Massachusetts work permit (the aquarium page does not mention it; M.G.L. c.149 s.86 and the Boston youth worker rights page, written with the state Attorney General's Office, cover the permit rule). The aquarium also runs ClimaTeens (ages 13 and up, 2026-27 applications due October 18, 2026).

name: Accelerate Pre-College Programs, Boston campus (Northeastern)
pay_detail: Summer 2027 tuition is $6,995 and includes tuition, course materials, housing, meals and social activities. Need based financial aid is available, and a non-refundable deposit of 20 percent of tuition (after aid and discounts) holds your spot. Priority round applicants get a $500 discount.
duration: Twelve days, move in on Sunday and move out the following Friday. Summer 2027 session dates were not posted on the pages read.
deadline_text: The page says Summer 2027 applications open in early December. Priority deadline January 15, regular February 28 and late March 15, each at 11:59 p.m. Eastern. The page does not print the year with these three dates. Deposit deadlines are February 18 (priority), April 1 (regular) and April 15 (late), and full tuition is due May 1.
who_can_apply: High school rising juniors and seniors from the US and around the world. (The 17 or older rule on the page applies only to the London program.)
how_to_apply: Send in the online application. Add an unofficial high school transcript or report card. Add a personal statement of up to 250 words. A teacher or counselor reference is optional. You ask for financial aid inside the application.
notes: Expensive. The program page says the Summer 2027 offerings were still being finalized and will be posted later this fall. For a free Northeastern option for Massachusetts juniors see the Young Scholars Program card.

name: Young Scholars Program (YSP)
grades: Entering 12th grade in the fall (current juniors)
pay_detail: Free program. No stipend is mentioned on the page.
duration: About six weeks. 2027 dates: June 22 to July 31, 2027, Monday to Thursday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., in person on the Northeastern campus.
deadline_text: Applications open Dec 14, 2026 and close March 1, 2027 at 5 p.m. Teacher recommendations are due March 8 or 9 (the page lists both dates).
who_can_apply: Current juniors. You must be a permanent Massachusetts resident. That means you live and go to school in MA all year. You must live within commuting distance of campus. You must be a US citizen or permanent resident, with no exceptions.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Online Student Application. It takes 60 to 90 minutes. You cannot save it or restart it. So write the essay answers ahead of time. You also need two teacher recommendations. A STEM teacher is best. Enter the recommenders' email addresses in the application.
notes: Free, but only for Massachusetts residents who are US citizens or permanent residents. Late applications are not accepted. Read the program FAQ before emailing the coordinator. The same page also has a line saying applications are due March 2nd, 2026, which conflicts with the March 1, 2027 close date. Confirm the 2027 date with the program before you plan around it.

name: Youth Conservation Corps, National Parks of Boston
org: National Park Service, Boston National Historical Park
pay_detail: $16.00 per hour
duration: 2026 schedule: Monday June 29 to Friday August 21, about 30 to 35 hours a week, 9 AM to 4 PM
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed April 26, 2026 at 11:59 PM (rolling until then). 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Must be 15 on or before the first day and not turn 19 during the program. U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident. You must live locally. You should enjoy working with kids who are 7 to 12 years old.
how_to_apply: In 2026: download the YCC application form from the park page, add 1 or 2 references, scan it and email it to npb_youthprograms@nps.gov. Applications for 2026 are closed.
notes: Paid. Mon to Fri. No housing. Work includes safety duties with young campers and training on public land management. This is a federal job, so ask the park how the Massachusetts permit rule applies. Watch the park page in early 2027. Paid work for people under 18 in Massachusetts needs a work permit (employment permit). See permit.html?state=ma for the exact permit and steps.

name: Boys & Girls Clubs of Metro Atlanta (club membership)
org: Boys & Girls Clubs of Metro Atlanta
city: Metro Atlanta, GA (26 Clubs in 9 counties)
pay_detail: Annual membership fee. The join page lists no dollar amount. It says the fee is lower than other youth groups, is waived for youth with Amerigroup insurance, and that no child is turned away for inability to pay.
duration: Membership year (the 2026 after school registration announcement is on the home page)
deadline_text: The home page says 2026 after school registration is open. No end date read.
who_can_apply: Children and teens ages 6 to 18 may apply at each location. Each Club has its own enrollment.

name: Librarians of Tomorrow
pay_detail: Stipend (amount not stated), plus volunteer service hours.
duration: Nov 2026 to June 2027, 3-6 hours a week, 100 hours total
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application deadline was October 3, 2026. Expect the next call in fall 2027 (last-year pattern).
who_can_apply: Students in grades 10-12 at a NYC high school, with a parent's signed consent, available 3 to 6 hours a week outside school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application or mail a print application to the Librarians of Tomorrow Internship Program, 10 Grand Army Plaza, Brooklyn, NY 11238. Questions: LOT@bklynlibrary.org or 718-230-2406.
notes: Library teen page lists ages 15-18; the program page requires grades 10-12 in NYC. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.

name: StoryTeen
pay_detail: Stipend (amount not stated), plus volunteer service hours.
duration: Nov 2026 to May 2027, 3-5 hours a week, 100 hours total
deadline_text: Applications for 2026-27 were open through October 3, 2026. Expect the next call in fall 2027 (last-year pattern).
who_can_apply: Students in grades 10-12 at a NYC high school, with a parent's signed consent, available 3 to 5 hours a week outside school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Selected applicants are contacted for an interview. Questions: storyteen@bklynlibrary.org.
notes: Funded through the NYC Council's City's First Readers initiative. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.

name: Teen Night Out Branch Council
pay_detail: Stipend (amount not stated), plus volunteer service hours.
duration: Weekly meetings Oct 2026 to June 2027, 75 hours of service
deadline_text: Applications for 2026-27 were open through October 3, 2026. Expect the next call in fall 2027 (last-year pattern).
who_can_apply: Teens ages 16-19, with a parent's signed consent for 75 hours of intern service outside school, available to meet weekly.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. All applicants get an email after. Some are invited to interview.
notes: The page does not say which library branches host councils. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.

name: Teaching Intern and Summer Volunteer
pay_detail: Pay not stated. Ask the program.
duration: 6-week summer program
deadline_text: Not posted.
who_can_apply: The site says it recruits college and high school students as teaching interns. No age or grade rule is posted. Middle school students can also join as program students.
how_to_apply: Use the Teaching Intern application link on breakthroughsac.org (online account login). Questions: BSAC@BreakthroughSac.org or 916-234-3905.
notes: Age minimum, pay and dates are not posted on the site, so call or email before applying. Training is two weeks (80 hours) on site.

name: Canadian Cadets (Sea, Army and Air Cadets)
org: Department of National Defence (Government of Canada)
city: Local corps and squadrons across British Columbia
pay_detail: The pages read do not state a cost. The program page calls it a funded program. Ask the local unit about any fees.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Register online and the unit staff contact you.
who_can_apply: Young people who are at least 12 and have not reached 19. Have your health card ready when you register.
how_to_apply: Choose Sea, Army or Air Cadets. Find a unit near you in the Corps and Squadron Directory. Register with the Online Registration Tool. Have your health card and your parents' contact details ready. Then unit staff contact you to check ID and welcome you.
notes: This is a Canada-wide program. The units in British Columbia come from the national directory. The British Columbia work rule is not verified for this card. A youth program, not a paid job.

name: Foundry Work & Education Program (FWEP)
pay_detail: Free. This is job and school support, not a paid job. Foundry says all its services are free and confidential.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No dates. Foundry says no referral is needed to use its services.
who_can_apply: British Columbia youth ages 15 to 24 who want to work, go to school or start a training program and face barriers to doing so. You must be legally entitled to work in BC. You should not already be working, in school or in training, or be working less than 15 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Sign yourself up with the online Foundry Work & Education form linked on the Foundry services page. Or find a Foundry centre near you.
notes: Foundry also gives free and confidential mental health and wellness services for youth ages 12 to 24. WorkBC also lists this program. The British Columbia work rule is not verified for this card.

name: SkilledTradesBC Youth Trades Programs (Discover, Explore, Train and Work in Trades)
org: SkilledTradesBC, with the Ministry of Education and Child Care
city: Across British Columbia (through your high school)
grades: High school students (grade and age rules are not stated on the pages read)
pay_detail: Youth Work in Trades training is paid, but no wage is stated. The youth programs page says tuition for these programs is covered. SkilledTradesBC and the Ministry fund technical training done in high school.
duration: From 1 high school course to a year-long program, depending on the program and trade
deadline_text: No application deadline is stated on the pages read. Talk to your school for dates.
who_can_apply: Students in high school. The pages read give no grade or age rule. Check the Youth Train in Trades Guide and your school for rules.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school's career educator or work experience coordinator. Train in Trades uses a program guide and a registration form. Work in Trades signs you up as an apprentice with an employer sponsor. It uses a Youth Apprentice and Sponsor Registration Form.
notes: The British Columbia work permit rule for these jobs is not verified. Other ways to find an apprenticeship listed on the site include job boards, WorkBC centres and hiring fairs. Youth Explore the Trades lets you sample several trades.

name: Skills Canada BC Competitions (regionals and provincials)
city: Regional events around British Columbia, provincials in Abbotsford
grades: Jr. Skills Projects are for grades 6 to 9. Other competitions are labelled Sec. (secondary) or PS (post-secondary).
pay_detail: No fees are listed on the pages read.
duration: Regionals in February to March 2027, provincials on April 14, 2027
deadline_text: Regionals run February to March 2027 in communities around the province, exact dates not posted yet. Provincials: April 14, 2027 at Abbotsford Tradex. Nationals: May 27 and 28, 2027 in Calgary. Registration deadlines are not listed.
who_can_apply: Students who are active at a school or college. Your teacher, instructor or career coordinator must sign you up. The exact rules are in the provincial rules document.
how_to_apply: Talk to your teacher, instructor or career coordinator. They sign you up through the Skills Canada BC registration page. It needs a password. You get it from the organization or your regional coordinator.
notes: Students cannot sign themselves up. Regional registration goes through a teacher login. The provincial rule document at skillscanada.bc.ca/competitions/rules-and-regulations/ lists exact eligibility. The British Columbia work rule is not verified for this card.

name: King Conservation Science Explorers (middle school)
pay_detail: Not stated. No cost is listed on the page.
duration: Saturdays in October and November (fall) or April and May (spring)
deadline_text: Applications open twice a year: September 1 to October 1 and March 1 to April 1. The fall 2026 window has closed. Years for future windows are not printed on the page.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 8. Letters of recommendation are not needed but are welcome.
how_to_apply: Fill out the yearly application during an open window. You share your interests and recent wins. You also share your goals for college and a career.
notes: For younger teens. Eighth graders are encouraged to apply to King Scholars at the high school level. Cost is not stated on the page.

name: King Conservation Science Scholars
pay_detail: Unpaid. Perks include zoo access like a basic membership, ten free admission passes, and discounts. Scholars commit to at least 80 hours a year.
duration: Year-round. At least 80 engagement hours each year.
deadline_text: Applications open twice a year. Fall: September 1 to October 1 (onboarding early to mid November). Spring: March 1 to April 1 (onboarding early to mid May). The fall 2026 window has closed. Years for future windows are not printed on the page.
who_can_apply: Students enrolled in grade 9, 10, 11 or 12 when they apply. Spring applicants must be in grades 9 to 11. A parent or guardian must attend onboarding.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the fall or spring window. Check the King Scholars page for the application and how to prepare.
notes: The Brookfield Zoo volunteer page says its regular volunteer forms are for adults. It says this program is its chance for high school students. Grade 8 graduates can join KCLA Transitions. Grade 12 students are not accepted in spring. Scholars who take part a lot can apply for seasonal jobs.

name: Brookhaven Police Cadet Program
pay_detail: Volunteer program. Cost is not listed.
duration: Weekly meetings, Thursdays 7 to 9 pm
deadline_text: No deadline is listed.
who_can_apply: Residents of Brookhaven or nearby areas, ages 14 to 18 or 19. The page says both, so confirm. You need passing grades and a clean background check. You cannot have criminal convictions or Juvenile Court referrals.
how_to_apply: Download the Cadet Application Packet and the Cadet Agreement Waiver (both PDFs) from the page. The page does not describe the steps after you turn them in.
notes: Meets at Brookhaven Police Department, 1793 Briarwood Road. The page lists ages 14 to 18 in one place and 14 to 19 in another. There is a community service requirement. Contact Officer Hawkins through the page or call 404-637-0600. Not a paid job.

name: Brookhaven Police Teen Academy
pay_detail: Free
duration: 5 days, 9 am to 3 pm (July 20 to 24 on the page, year not printed)
deadline_text: The page lists July 20 to 24 but does not print a year or a deadline. Treat it as the yearly pattern and check for the next dates.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 19 who live in or around Brookhaven. No grade is listed. Seats are limited.
how_to_apply: Reserve a spot with the online form on the program page, or contact the department. The page says early sign-up is encouraged.
notes: Held at Brookhaven Police Department, 1793 Briarwood Rd, Brookhaven, GA 30329. Call Officer Angela Hawkins at 678-296-1904. You can also call the Community Engagement Unit. The number is 404-637-0600, Option 8. This is unpaid, so no work permit.

name: Volunteer program
pay_detail: Unpaid. After 25 hours of service volunteers can get a complimentary museum membership.
duration: At least 6 hours per month
deadline_text: The page says applications for the volunteer program are open. No deadline is stated.
who_can_apply: Anyone at least 16 years old who can volunteer at least six hours a month and is excited about Texas history and welcoming visitors.
how_to_apply: Submit the online volunteer application. If it is approved you are contacted for an interview, then attend a New Volunteer Orientation.
notes: Only 16 and older. Younger teens should look at the Austin Public Library youth volunteer program (ages 13 to 17).

name: Burke Composite Squadron, Civil Air Patrol cadets
org: Civil Air Patrol, Virginia Wing (Burke Composite Squadron)
pay_detail: Annual cadet dues are $45 for Virginia in CAP's dues table, which also says national dues went up $10 for FY27. Uniform costs are not stated on the pages read.
duration: Weekly meetings, Thursday nights 6:30 to 9:00
deadline_text: No deadline. You can join any time. Email the squadron to ask about visiting a meeting.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18 (the Virginia Wing page says to be at least 12 and not yet 19, and a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident). The squadron has both teen and adult members.
how_to_apply: Email va-130info@vawg.cap.gov or call (703) 239-4530 to ask about a meeting. The Virginia Wing steps are to visit with your parents. Then go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the cadet application.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Meetings are at Irving Middle School, 8100 Old Keene Mill, Springfield, VA 22152, but the location can change for school events, and in August they meet elsewhere. Meetings are cancelled on the same days Fairfax County Schools cancels. The squadron page says it won a 2021 Virginia Wing Squadron of Merit award.

name: Volunteer Program at Burnaby Hospital
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: One 3-hour shift a week for at least 8 months
deadline_text: No deadline stated. The page says some areas may have no openings.
who_can_apply: Age 16 or older (18 for the Emergency triage role). Must give 3 hours a week for 8 months.
how_to_apply: Apply online. It takes about 30 minutes. If you are picked, you get an interview. You also need a police record check and references. Then you go to orientation and training.
notes: Call Volunteer Resources at 604-412-6130. The page was last updated on Jan 22, 2025.

name: Become a Lifeguard and Swim Instructor
org: City of Burnaby Parks, Recreation and Culture
pay_detail: Course fees not stated on the page read. The page says lifeguard jobs have great pay and flexible hours but gives no rate.
duration: Several courses in a series
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Register for courses online or at a pool front desk.
who_can_apply: Age minimums by course. Bronze Medallion is 13 or older. You must swim 400 m in under 12 minutes. Bronze Cross is 13 or older. First Aid is 14 or older. Lifeguard and instructor courses are 15 or older.
how_to_apply: Check the age and skills table. Then sign up for courses with the City (WebReg). You can also ask at a rec center with an indoor pool. Email questions to the address on the page.
notes: The page says extra certificates help but are not required to be a lifeguard with the City. This covers the instructor and fitness leader certificates. Pay and job age rules are not stated. The page says courses can earn high school credits.

name: Burnaby Village Museum Volunteer Program
org: City of Burnaby, Burnaby Village Museum
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: At least 1 year and 35 hours of service per year
deadline_text: Intakes: February (spring/summer) and September (fall/winter) for costumed interpretation, school programs and events. Camps: February and April. Collections and sewing: ongoing.
who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. If you are under 18, a parent must say yes. You need good English, health coverage, 2 references and the right to volunteer in Canada. You must be able to walk the 10 acre site.
how_to_apply: Pick a job on the museum volunteer page. Then apply online.
notes: The page lists the intake months but not the year, so confirm the next date. The City of Burnaby volunteer page also lists Camps and playgrounds volunteering for youth 14 and older.

name: American Legion California Boys State (Boys & Girls State)
grades: Finished 11th grade, with at least one semester of high school left
pay_detail: Registration fee listed as $550 per delegate on the Key Dates page (the page does not label the year). Ask your sponsoring Post who pays.
duration: One week in June at Sacramento State. The site counts down to June 19, 2027.
deadline_text: 2027 selection dates are not posted. The Key Dates page (year not labeled) shows delegate selection Jan 15 to Apr 1 and all registrations due Apr 1. Posts usually interview late Jan to late March.
who_can_apply: High school students who completed junior year and have a semester left. There is no application. Your school recommends you. A local American Legion Post interviews and sponsors you. Girls State (below) is a separate program.
how_to_apply: Tell your counselor in junior year you are interested, or contact a local American Legion Post (use Find-A-Post on calegion.org). The Post chooses delegates; the delegate then registers online.
notes: Two separate programs. This one has been coed since 2023. California Girls State (American Legion Auxiliary, cagirlsstate.org) is its own program. It ran June 22 to 27, 2026 for 11th graders sponsored by a local Auxiliary Unit, one delegate per school. You can apply to only one. An old note about a 2020 article and a Sanger phone was out of date.

name: California Highway Patrol Explorer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cost to you: 2026 competition fees were $150 per explorer, $125 per advisor and $75 per spectator.
duration: Not stated for post membership. The 2026 competition ran April 24 to 26, 2026.
deadline_text: No post sign-up dates are stated. The 2026 competition registration opened December 2025 and full payment was due February 23, 2026. Both have passed.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 21, per the 2026 Explorer competition packet. This is the competition age rule. Post membership rules such as GPA or background checks are not stated on the pages read.
how_to_apply: Email CHPExplorers@chp.ca.gov or call (916) 843-3210 (both listed in the 2026 packet) to ask how to join a post near you.
notes: Both official pages were read on 2026-10-07. The program page covers the statewide competition and does not say how to join a post. The 2026 packet is the source for the 15 to 21 age rule, which it states for the competition. Whether a post near you has room, and any background check or GPA rule, must be asked of CHP. The CHP East Sacramento post page returns 403 to automated reads, so use the email or phone above. See also CHP Explorer Post (East Sacramento) for a local post. Ages differ by source: the 2026 competition packet says 15 to 21, while the CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers.

name: California Division of Apprenticeship Standards: how apprenticeship works and minimum ages
org: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Apprenticeship Standards
pay_detail: DAS describes apprenticeship as earn-and-learn. Wages depend on the program; DAS has a tool to look up apprenticeship wages.
deadline_text: Each program sets its own application window.
who_can_apply: California law says an apprentice must be at least 16 (Labor Code 3077, in the state child labor guide). Each registered program sets its own minimum age, education and tests, shown in the DAS search, and may set a higher age.
how_to_apply: Use the Apprenticeship Search on the DAS site, check each program's minimum age and requirements, and apply the way the listing says.
notes: The DAS homepage states no age rule. The 16 minimum comes from the 2013 DLSE child labor guide, which also says apprentices need a school-issued work permit. DAS's How to Become an Apprentice page says search results list each program's minimum age. DAS runs a youth apprenticeship grant and reports 5,776 registered pre-apprentices on its homepage.

name: Youth Employment Opportunity Program (YEOP)
city: California (YEOP specialists at local EDD offices)
pay_detail: No pay. The page does not say whether services cost anything.
duration: Ongoing
deadline_text: No application dates. Contact a YEOP specialist any time.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 15 to 25 who need extra help to finish school or find work. Examples listed are offense history as a minor and teen parent. Others are foster care or no stable housing, and gang involvement or risk. Minority group, low income, and disability or reading difficulty are also listed. You may still qualify if you do not match these.
how_to_apply: The page has no separate enrollment steps. Use the YEOP Contact Information page. It helps you reach a YEOP specialist in your area. Or contact your local America's Job Center of California.
notes: The page says clearly: this is not a job placement program. It is help and coaching toward school and work.

name: EDD Employment Services for Youth (America's Job Centers of California)
city: California (local America's Job Center of California offices)
pay_detail: The services are free (the page says Job Centers connect employers with job seekers at no cost). Work experience can be paid or unpaid; no pay rate is given.
duration: Ongoing, set by each local center
deadline_text: No application dates. Visit or contact your local center any time.
who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 24 who meet certain requirements. The EDD page does not list the requirements. It points to the Youth Employment Opportunity Program page and fact sheet for criteria.
how_to_apply: Find your local America's Job Center of California with the EDD Office Locator (edd.ca.gov/en/Office_Locator/). The page also suggests building a resume in CalJOBS and visiting the center to ask about internships, apprenticeships and training.
notes: The EDD page does not say the youth services are free. It says Job Centers connect employers with job seekers at no cost. Eligibility criteria are not on the EDD page read; it links to the YEOP services and eligibility criteria. Teens under 18 who take a paid job in California need a work permit from their school (CDE page).

name: California State Parks Volunteers in Parks (youth)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Varies by park
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: Under 18 needs written parent or guardian permission. Specific age minimums vary by park.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the State Parks volunteer portal or print a paper application and mail it to the park you want. Questions: Volunteer.inparksprogram@parks.ca.gov or (916) 653-9069. The application link is on the official page.
notes: A criminal background check may be required. Park-level age minimums were not on the page, so ask the park. Student volunteer or intern roles are mentioned only as a general possibility at local parks. No Junior Ranger details were on this page.

name: California Volunteers Youth Service Corps
org: California Volunteers (Office of the Governor), run through partner cities and counties
city: California (23 partner cities, counties and tribes)
regions: los-angeles; oakland; sacramento; san-francisco; san-jose; orange-county; inland-empire; san-diego
pay_detail: At least minimum wage; the rate varies by location (page wording).
duration: Not stated on the state page; set by each local program
deadline_text: The state page does not say whether applications are open. Each partner city or county runs its own application.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 30 on the first day of service. You must meet at least one of: foster care, justice involved, mental health or substance abuse system, low income, hard time finding work, or unemployed and/or out of school.
how_to_apply: Pick your local program from the partner list on the state page and apply through its link. Or use the state interest form. State office: info@californiavolunteers.ca.gov (say Youth Service Corps) or (916) 323-7646.
notes: Partner list on the page: Anaheim, Antioch, Bakersfield, Chula Vista, Fresno, Irvine, La Puente, Long Beach, Los Angeles, Oakland, Rancho Cucamonga, Riverside, Sacramento, San Francisco, San Diego, San Jose, Santa Cruz, South Gate, Stockton, Marin County, Monterey County, Mechoopda Band of Chico Rancheria and Ramona Band of Cahuilla. California requires a work permit for minors in paid jobs (CDE page), so under 18 you will need one. The state page does not say whether each city requires you to live there, so check the local program.

name: California Work Experience Education (Exploratory, General, Career Technical)
pay_detail: Exploratory is unpaid. General and Career Technical WEE combine paid work with a class.
deadline_text: Ask your counselor or the school's work experience coordinator.
who_can_apply: Your school district must run an approved WEE program. Exploratory WEE students can be as young as 12 and do not need a work permit. General WEE usually needs a work permit. Career Technical WEE needs a job related to a career technical class you take.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor or CTE/work experience coordinator whether your district has a WEE program and what class goes with it.
notes: The 2013 state child labor guide says students must be 16 to enroll in WEE, with exceptions in the Education Code (14 and 15 year olds can get permits in some cases). The CDE page says Exploratory can start at 12. Programs exist only where the district chose to run one. Use the three current names above.

name: Next-Gen Manufacturing Academy (High School Summer Academy)
pay_detail: $25 per person. Parking permit and daily lunch included.
duration: Held each July, daily 9:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., at Cal Poly Pomona Building 17
deadline_text: Page says applications open in January and close in April each year. Exact 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors interested in engineering, robotics or AI. Bonita Unified School District students get priority.
how_to_apply: Email the RASIM Center at rasim@cpp.edu to sign up during the January to April window.
notes: The page's sample schedule is labeled Summer 2027 but gives no exact dates. Confirm by email.

name: California 4-H Youth Development
pay_detail: Not confirmed. Fees depend on the county program.
duration: Club year
deadline_text: Join through a county 4-H program.
who_can_apply: Kids and teens join through a county 4-H program. Check your county page for age rules and fees.
how_to_apply: Find your county 4-H office from ucanr.edu/sites/ca4H.
notes: The 4-H site blocked automated access on 2026-10-07 (403 and a bot check), so age rules and fees could not be read. Ages, fees and teen roles must be confirmed with your county 4-H office. Re-checked on 2026-10-09: the 4-H page returned HTTP 403 again, so it could not be read and the card stays snippet-only.

name: California Cadet Corps (school based leadership program)
org: California Cadet Corps, California Military Department
grades: Grades 4 to 12 per the program site; the state military page says grades 6 to 12
pay_detail: Free. The program site says it is fully funded by the state with no cost to families or host schools. Cadets earn up to ten elective credits per year.
duration: Ongoing school year program
deadline_text: No dates. Enrollment follows your school's schedule.
who_can_apply: Students at a school that runs a California Cadet Corps unit. Participation is voluntary. The pages read do not say how a student enrolls beyond being at a host school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school whether it has a Cadet Corps unit. The program site says schools that want to start one should email Recruiting@cacadets.org. The site's Contact Us page is cacadets.org/about/contact.
notes: Pages read did not include a school finder, so the best first step is to ask your school office or email the program. The program site says more than 7,000 students are in over 100 schools.

name: California FBLA (Future Business Leaders of America)
city: California (through school chapters in six geographic sections)
grades: Not stated on the pages read
pay_detail: Not a job. The join page lists no dues amounts.
duration: Ongoing through the school year
deadline_text: No join deadline on the page.
who_can_apply: Students at a California school with an FBLA chapter. The FAQ says FBLA is open to students enrolled in a Career and Technical Education (CTE) business program.
how_to_apply: Ask whether your school has a chapter: email hello@cafbla.org or call (714) 824-4489. If not, fill out the FBLA Interest Form so staff can help your school affiliate; that needs your school administration.
notes: You join through a school chapter, so you need a business pathway or class at your school. If your school has no business program, the FAQ says starting one has to be started with school administration.

name: California FFA and Supervised Agricultural Experience (SAE)
org: California FFA and National FFA Organization
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the pages read. Ask your ag teacher what your chapter charges.
duration: School year; SAE can be year-round
deadline_text: Join through your ag teacher.
who_can_apply: Join through a school that has an agricultural education program; chapters are chartered in schools with ag classes. California reports over 103,000 members. Age and grade rules were not on the pages I read.
how_to_apply: Take an agriculture class at a school with an FFA chapter.
notes: Not every school has an FFA chapter. Ask your counselor or ag teacher. Age and grade limits and dues were not on the California or National FFA pages I read.

name: California Partnership Academies (CPA)
pay_detail: The CDE page does not say whether internships pay or give school credit. Ask the school.
duration: 3 years
deadline_text: The CDE page lists no student application dates. Each school sets its own.
who_can_apply: Students at schools that host an academy. Each academy has its own way to apply. Look on the school's website for 'Partnership Academy'.
how_to_apply: Ask your counselor if your school has an academy. The CDE page links a directory of academies (a spreadsheet updated September 2026). The page does not say how students apply.
notes: Read the CDE page on 2026-10-09. It confirms a three-year program for grades 10 to 12, structured as a school-within-a-school, with academics plus career technical education, business partnerships, mentoring and internships. It posts only school and district grant dates, not student application dates, and does not say whether students from other districts may transfer in. Academies are run by individual schools, so ask your counselor. Fremont Unified says some CTE courses sit inside Partnership Academies.

name: Caltech Summer Research Connection (Pasadena Unified high school students)
org: Caltech Center for Teaching, Learning, and Outreach
pay_detail: The page does not say whether interns are paid or what it costs. Ask the program contact.
duration: 6 weeks
deadline_text: No deadline listed. The page says spots are limited and usually fill by early spring. It mentions summer 2026 with no schedule.
who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled in a Pasadena Unified School District (PUSD) high school. Grade and age rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: The page has no form. Use the email link for the program contact (Mitch Aiken) on the Summer Research Connection page.
notes: Only for PUSD students. Contact early in the school year because spots fill by early spring.

name: Camp Ignite
org: Camp Ignite Society (with Metro Vancouver fire departments)
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the page read. Run by a not-for-profit that aims to keep it affordable.
duration: Three full days, Aug 7 to 9, 2026 (the page also has a four-day, three-night description, so confirm)
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed. 2026 camp was Aug 7 to 9. Next year not posted.
who_can_apply: Girls who are in grade 12 or will enter it in 2026 and live in British Columbia (2026 camp).
how_to_apply: Watch campignite.com for the next form. Email info@campignite.com. Do not email to ask how your form is going.
notes: Camp page is inconsistent: it says three days and also four days three nights. Confirm details on the next posting. Other Ignite camps run on Vancouver Island and in the Kootenays.

name: Capital Area NextGen Youth Services
org: Capital Area Workforce Development Board (NCWorks Career Centers)

how_to_apply: Create an account on the After School Matters website and apply there. Use an email you check often. Interviews follow.
notes: Meetings are on Saturdays with a few extra dates. No meetings over CPS spring break. Two absences per semester may be allowed if told in advance. The page does not say whether the board is paid. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

name: Nature Buds Internship
org: Lincoln Park Zoo with After School Matters
pay_detail: Stipend of $17.05 per hour through After School Matters (2026 page)
duration: June to August, Monday to Thursday, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026 application opened the week of April 27 on the After School Matters site. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: You must live in the city of Chicago and go to a Chicago high school. You must be at least 16 by June 1. You must be able to come to all program dates.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the After School Matters website and apply there. Rank "Lincoln Park Zoo - Nature Buds" as your top pick.
notes: Outdoor work. Shifts are four days a week. Pay rate is from the 2026 page and may change. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

name: Malott Family Research Apprenticeship Program
grades: Entering grades 11 to 12, or freshman year of college
pay_detail: Paid, 7 weeks. The page does not state the hourly rate.
duration: 7 weeks, Monday to Friday (June 22 to Aug 7 in 2026), plus a Saturday orientation
deadline_text: 2026 application ran Feb 1 to Mar 9. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Must live in the city of Chicago, be entering grades 11 to 12 (or a college freshman) in the fall, be 16 to 18 by the June start, and be legally allowed to work in the U.S. with proof of identity. No research experience needed.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the zoo SlideRoom link on the program page. The zoo invites strong applicants to a half-day group interview in March.
notes: Introductory research program, so teens with no lab or field experience are welcome. Apprentices do not work directly with animals. You need a way to get to the zoo each day. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

name: Malott Family Zoo Intern Program
grades: Entering grades 10 to 12, or freshman year of college
pay_detail: Paid, 7 weeks. The page does not state the hourly rate.

deadline_text: 2026 application ran Feb 1 to Mar 9. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: You must live in the city of Chicago. You must be going into grades 10 to 12 (or be a college freshman) in the fall. You must be 16 to 18 by the June orientation date. You must be allowed to work in the U.S. and have proof of identity.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the zoo SlideRoom link on the program page. Invited applicants go to a half-day group interview at the zoo in March. The zoo also held two Zoom info sessions in late Feb and early March in 2026.
notes: Interns do not work directly with animals. You need a reliable way to get to the zoo each day. You can apply to several zoo teen programs at once. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules. Contact is listed on the program page.

name: Zoo Teens events
pay_detail: Free
duration: Single events on select days through the year
deadline_text: Events listed for Saturday Oct 31 (Roll for Wildlife, Prism Games, Logan Square) and Saturday Nov 7 (Plants and Prints, Lincoln Park Zoo). The page does not state the year. Register on the page.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18 from across the Chicago area. Parents are not allowed at the events.
how_to_apply: Register for each event with the Register Now button on the Zoo Teens page.
notes: Going to an event adds you to the list for news about the zoo's internships and other teen programs. Parking is at 2400 N. Cannon Drive for events at the zoo.

name: Marwen Art@Work summer internship
pay_detail: 2026: $16.20 per hour, 14.5 hours a week for 5 weeks, about $1,174.50 before taxes (may change)
duration: 5 weeks, July to August; 12 hours a week at the site and 2.5 hours at Marwen
deadline_text: Applications for Summer 2027 open in spring 2027. For 2026 they were due April 11, 2026.
who_can_apply: Chicago residents ages 16 to 18 by July 1 of the program year. You have taken at least one Marwen course. You can commit to the full schedule. You have a Social Security number or an employment tax ID.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the spring window opens. Selected teens get a 30-minute Zoom interview with Marwen staff in May.
notes: You must have taken a Marwen course first. Marwen classes are no-cost for Chicago students in grades 6 to 12 who face barriers to arts programs. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

name: Teen Creative Agency (TCA)
pay_detail: Up to $1,600 a year
duration: Weekly sessions during the program year; exact months not stated
deadline_text: Applications for TCA open next spring (spring 2027). Exact dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Chicago teens. The page says ages 14 to 19 in one place and 15 to 19 in another, so confirm the age rule with the museum.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply to TCA form (Airtable) on the MCA Teens page when it opens. Questions: Ahmad Bracey, abracey@mcachicago.org, 312-397-4020.
notes: Free museum entry for anyone 18 and under. Teens can also send projects to 21Minus each winter. It is free for ages 21 and under. The page does not say if a work permit is needed. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16. It refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

name: CPS Student Advisory Council (Mikva Challenge)
grades: Citywide Youth Councils are for current 9th to 11th graders
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the program pages. Ask Mikva Challenge.

how_to_apply: Recruitment for 2027 starts in the spring. Watch the Mikva Challenge program application page or email inquiries@mikvachallenge.org. Phone: (312) 863-6340.
notes: A city-wide teen council. The program page gives ages 16 to 18; the application page says Citywide Youth Councils are for current 9th to 11th graders.

name: Safety and Justice Council (Mikva Challenge)
grades: Citywide Youth Councils are for current 9th to 11th graders

notes: The council includes young people affected by the juvenile justice system. The age range here is 16 to 20, so some members are over 18 and teens work alongside older youth.

name: Mikva Student Election Judge Program
org: Mikva Challenge Illinois with Chicago election officials
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the program page. Ask Mikva Challenge.

The Chicago Board of Election Commissioners website blocked our reader, so pay, age and sign-up rules there were not checked. Confirm with Mikva or the Board.

name: Mikva Summer Fellows
org: Mikva Challenge Illinois with the Illinois Department of Human Services Youth Investment Program
grades: Placed after senior year of high school

duration: 6 weeks between June and August
deadline_text: Recruitment for 2027 programs begins in spring 2027. Exact dates not posted.

how_to_apply: Recruitment for 2027 starts in the spring. Watch the Mikva Challenge program application page or email inquiries@mikvachallenge.org. Phone: (312) 863-6340.
notes: For young people after their senior year. The page does not state an age limit. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

name: Teen Health Council (Mikva Challenge)
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the program page. Ask Mikva Challenge.

deadline_text: Recruitment for 2027 programs begins in spring 2027. Exact dates not posted.
