how_to_apply: Recruitment for 2027 starts in the spring. Watch the Mikva Challenge program application page or email inquiries@mikvachallenge.org. Phone: (312) 863-6340.
notes: Good fit if you want to work in health or public health. The page lists a partnership with the Lurie Children's Center on Childhood Resilience.

name: Recreation Leader in Training (RIT), ages 13 to 15
pay_detail: The program page does not mention pay or a stipend. Confirm with the Park District before you plan around pay.
duration: Spring, fall and winter: 8 weeks, 6 hours a week. Summer: 6 weeks, 30 program days.
deadline_text: 2026 sessions: Winter Jan 12 to Mar 14 (programs viewable online Dec 1, 2025), Spring Apr 6 to Jun 6, Summer Jun 22 to Jul 31, Fall Oct 5 to Dec 11 (viewable online July 27). 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15 who live in Chicago.
how_to_apply: Contact the staff at the park you are interested in to start the application. The process is an application, an interview, a mentoring curriculum and performance check-ins.
notes: Re-read on 2026-10-09: ages 13 to 15, Chicago residence, the apply step (contact the park) and the 2026 session dates all match the page. The page says RIT is a job readiness program and participants are not Park District staff. It does not mention pay, so the pay type was changed from stipend to no pay stated. The next sessions are posted online about a month before each starts.

name: Chicago Park District summer jobs (lifeguard, recreation leader, junior laborer)
pay_detail: 2026 rates: lifeguard $20.50 per hour; recreation leader, special recreation leader and junior laborer $17.77 per hour.
duration: Recreation leaders about 6 weeks, mid-June to early Aug. Junior laborers start April, May or June.
deadline_text: All four 2026 summer positions are marked closed. 2027 dates not posted. The Park District holds free Teen Opportunity Fairs in Feb and March (Feb 21 to Mar 14 in 2026) where teens can apply.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 and older for lifeguards, recreation leaders, special recreation leaders and junior laborers. The page does not state a residency rule, so check with the Park District.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Park District job site. Use the Learn More and Apply Now links on the Summer Jobs page. Or go to a Teen Opportunity Fair. Applications must be in by the closed date on each job posting.
notes: Work permit: Illinois requires employment certificates only for minors under 16 (Illinois Dept. of Labor FAQ). All of these jobs start at 16. Teens 13 to 15 should see the Recreation Leader in Training program. Fair email: teensinthepark@chicagoparkdistrict.com.

name: Rush University Medical Center volunteer program
pay_detail: Unpaid. After 100 hours you can ask a staff member for a reference letter.
duration: At least 6 months, 4 hours a week
deadline_text: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis.
who_can_apply: Anyone at least 17 years old who can give four hours a week, Monday to Friday between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m., for at least six months in a row. Needs TB test and MMR and chickenpox records.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application on the page. Rush replies by email in 5 to 7 business days. The email has steps for orientation and a health screening. Contact: volunteer_services@rush.edu, (312) 942-5574.
notes: No summer-only volunteering. No weekend or evening shifts. Internships and externships are not offered through Volunteer Services. Under 17 does not qualify here. The page lists separate phone numbers for Rush Copley and Rush Oak Park.

name: SAIC Early College Program (ECP) courses
org: School of the Art Institute of Chicago
grades: High school; college credit only for those who finished sophomore year
pay_detail: Noncredit 10-week course $661; 1.0 college credit course $1,982; supplies about $50 to $200 extra. The Smith Scholarship covers 100% of noncredit course tuition for Illinois students. Limited need-based aid.
duration: 10-week courses in fall and spring; the page does not state a summer course length
deadline_text: Register online for each term. No fixed deadline stated on the pages read.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 18. The 1.0 college-credit option is for juniors and seniors ages 15 to 18.
how_to_apply: Sign up for courses on the Early College Program page. For the Smith Scholarship, fill out the scholarship form. Upload your household 1040 and send in three pieces of art to SlideRoom. For need-based aid, say yes at sign-up and upload the 1040 in DocuSign.
notes: Costs money unless you win the Smith Scholarship or aid. Aid is first come, first served.

name: SAIC Early College Program Summer Institute (ECPSI)
org: School of the Art Institute of Chicago
pay_detail: Tuition is $1,908 for 1 week, $3,816 for 2 weeks and $7,632 for 4 weeks. The page also lists housing and meal plan costs, supplies and personal spending. A $100 non-refundable tuition deposit applies to students who apply for aid or scholarships. Merit scholarships and limited need-based aid (US residents) are offered.
duration: 1, 2 or 4 weeks. 2026 sessions ran June 15 to July 31.
deadline_text: Page says registration opens November 1 (year not stated). The 2026 sessions ran June 15 to July 31. A priority deadline is mentioned but not dated on the page read.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18 who have completed their sophomore year by the time of the program. Merit scholarships are open to all students; need-based aid is for US residents.
how_to_apply: Register online when sign-up opens November 1. When you sign up, you can also apply for a merit scholarship or need-based aid.
notes: The page says registration opens November 1 but gives no year. It probably means this coming November for summer 2027, so confirm. The site menu also lists an online version (ECPOSI). Its details were not on the page read.

name: Steppenwolf Young Adult Council
pay_detail: Weekly meetings appear unpaid; the page says community engagement and extra leadership work is paid. Rates not stated.
duration: Weekly Wednesday meetings at Steppenwolf
deadline_text: Page says applications are closed. Next dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students from the Chicago area. The page lists no age or school rule.
how_to_apply: Watch the Young Adult Council page for the next application. Questions: teenprograms@steppenwolf.org.
notes: Members see Steppenwolf plays and many Chicago plays for free. Steppenwolf also runs free Step In theatre workshops and Teen Takeover nights, which have cheap tickets to shows. Join the teen email list on the Teen Programs page for updates.

name: CPS-UChicago Program
org: University of Chicago with Chicago Public Schools
pay_detail: $800 tuition plus $75 lifetime transcript fee (books not included) if household income is over $60,000. $0 tuition, with books and fees covered, if under $60,000.
duration: Autumn, Winter and Spring Quarters; one course per quarter
deadline_text: For 2026-27 the application opened June 8, 2026 and closed July 15, 2026. 2027-28 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: You must have been in CPS this year and last year. You will be a junior or senior. You have a strong record in the hardest courses you can take. You are ready for college work.
how_to_apply: Fill out an online application. It has short essays, a graded work sample, a teacher recommendation and transcripts. It also has an online interview in mid-August. For the $0 tuition option, you need financial aid papers.
notes: UChicago classes do not follow the CPS calendar, so you attend even when your high school is on break. Many students stop after Winter Quarter.

name: Chicago EYES on Cancer
org: University of Chicago Medicine Comprehensive Cancer Center
grades: High school sophomore, junior or senior (or college freshman or sophomore)
pay_detail: Taxable stipend of $5,000 per year
duration: Two summers of 8 weeks (2027: June 14 to Aug 6, 35 to 40 hours a week) plus monthly 2 to 4 hour online sessions from Feb 2027 to Dec 2028
deadline_text: Application and two recommendations due Nov 30, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. CT. In-person interviews Jan 4, 2027.
who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors or seniors who are at least 16 by June 14, 2027 and live in Cook, Lake, Will or DuPage counties in Illinois or Lake County, Indiana. College freshmen and sophomores can also apply. Must commit to both summers.
how_to_apply: Fill out the common Pathway Programs online application (REDCap). Two people must send in recommendations. At least one must be a teacher or professor. Up to 12 applicants are accepted.
notes: You must find your own housing and ride to UChicago. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16. It refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules. One application covers all the UChicago cancer pathway programs that fit you.

name: Healthcare Experience and Research in Oncology (HERO)
org: University of Chicago Medicine Comprehensive Cancer Center
pay_detail: $500 taxable stipend
duration: 2 weeks, July 12 to 23, 2027, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to noon CT, online
deadline_text: Application and two recommendations due Mar 1, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. CT. Interviews in April 2027.
who_can_apply: Full-time high school students who live in Cook, Lake, Will or DuPage counties in Illinois or Lake County, Indiana, and can attend every weekday, 4 hours a day. Up to 20 students per year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the common Pathway Programs online application (REDCap). Two people must send in forms for you. At least one must be a teacher or professor.
notes: Virtual program run with Kentucky, Michigan, Penn and UT Austin. No minimum age is listed. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed for the stipend.

name: UChicago Medicine student volunteer program
grades: High school, college and graduate students
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: One weekly 3 to 4 hour shift for at least 6 months or one school year; 100 hours within a year
deadline_text: Fall window ran Aug 25 to Oct 1, 2026 (may close early). Next cycle starts Jan 10, 2027; closing date not posted.
who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old (some roles need 18+). Must interview, pass health screening, a drug screen and a background check, and not hold certain visas (B-1, B-2, H-1B, H-4).
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Volunteer application. Do it when a recruiting window is open. The form is in Volgistics. Then you talk with Volunteer Services in an interview. For questions, write to vservices@uchicagomedicine.org. You can also call 773-702-4421.
notes: The page says student volunteers must be at least 16, and some opportunities need 18 or older. The summer program opens in early March 2027. One summer block says applicants must be 18 at submission, while the FAQ says the summer rules match the others (16). Confirm the summer age rule.

name: researcHStart
org: University of Chicago Medicine Comprehensive Cancer Center with UIC, UIUC, Northwestern and Rush
grades: High school junior or senior at time of application
pay_detail: Taxable stipend of $4,000
duration: 8 weeks, June 14 to Aug 6, 2027, 35 to 40 hours a week
deadline_text: Application and two recommendations due Jan 11, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. CT. On-campus interviews in February 2027; acceptance notices March 1, 2027.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors who live in Illinois or Lake County, Indiana, are at least 16 by June 14, 2027, and can commit to all 8 weeks. Max 30 students across all sites.
how_to_apply: Fill out the common Pathway Programs online application (REDCap). Pick your site: UChicago, UIC, UIUC, Northwestern downtown or Rush. Two people must send in forms for you. At least one must be a teacher or professor.
notes: No housing or ride is provided, so pick only sites you can reach. The application asks for your GPA and a transcript. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16. It refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

name: University of Chicago Summer Session pre-college programs
grades: High school (programs open depend on your current grade)
pay_detail: Costs in 2026: Enrichment $3,000; Career Insight $5,890 ($4,100 commuting); Immersion $9,300 ($6,100 commuting); Practicum $15,200; online 3 to 5 weeks $4,980. Need-based partial aid is offered (not full), and Enrichment fees can be waived for income under $125,000. $75 application fee.
duration: Varies by program. Online courses run 3 to 5 weeks and the language institute runs 6 to 8 weeks; the page does not state a length for enrichment.
deadline_text: 2026 deadlines: priority Feb 11, regular Mar 12 (Practicum priority only). 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students. The application shows which programs you are eligible for based on your current grade. Chicagoland students can choose to commute for Career Insight and Immersion.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for a profile, transcript, writing sample, supplement and one recommendation letter. It also needs a parent okay and the $75 fee. Test scores are not required. You may rank up to four program choices but can be admitted to one.
notes: Expensive, not a job. Apply by the priority deadline if you need financial aid. Aid is limited and first come, first served.

name: Windy City Harvest Youth Farm
org: Chicago Botanic Garden, Windy City Harvest, with After School Matters
pay_detail: Stipend: 4 hours a week in spring and fall, 20 hours a week in summer. Rate not stated.
duration: Spring, summer and fall growing seasons
deadline_text: No dates posted on the page.
who_can_apply: The page says the program includes 25 neighborhood high school teens, run with After School Matters. The page does not list an age or school rule.
how_to_apply: Use the How to Apply link on the Youth Farm page (an online form). Questions: Aurea France, Manager of Education and Wellness, per the page.
notes: Run in partnership with After School Matters. Confirm ages, dates and pay before relying on this. The Illinois FAQ requires work permits only for workers under 16 and refers 16 and 17 year olds to federal rules.

name: Chicago Youth Works (formerly One Summer Chicago): summer jobs
org: City of Chicago Dept. of Family and Support Services
pay_detail: Paid. The pay rate is set by each partner and is not stated on the program pages. Most summer jobs run 20 to 25 hours a week.
duration: At least 6 weeks; in 2026 most programs ran June 22 to July 31
deadline_text: 2026 application ran March 10 to May 29, 2026. 2027 dates not posted; expect late winter or spring.
who_can_apply: City of Chicago residents. The program covers ages 14 to 24, but most summer jobs are for ages 16 to 24 (14 and 15 year olds: see Chicagobility). Under 18 needs a parent or guardian consent form if offered a job.
how_to_apply: Complete the online Chicago Youth Works application (about 20 minutes, can be saved) plus any partner applications for jobs you choose. Online only. Partners contact applicants for interviews. More applicants than jobs, and you can accept only one position.
notes: The FAQ says youth 16 and older do not need a work permit. Some pages on the site are leftovers from old years, so trust the FAQ and the City press release for 2026. Questions: hotline 312-743-0208. Applicants with DACA need a Social Security number for City-funded jobs. Year-round Chicago Youth Service Corps (ages 16 to 24) is also part of this program.

name: Chicagobility (paid summer career exploration for ages 14 and 15)
org: City of Chicago Dept. of Family and Support Services
pay_detail: Paid stipend for the 120 hours. Amount not stated.
duration: 6 weeks, 120 hours
deadline_text: The 2026 Chicago Youth Works application (which covers 14 to 24 year olds) ran March 10 to May 29, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 and 15 who live in Chicago. At least half of participants come from priority groups (for example youth with disabilities, English learners, youth in foster care or experiencing homelessness).
how_to_apply: Apply through the online Chicago Youth Works application. Youth under 18 need a parent or guardian consent form if offered a position. Partner agencies contact applicants directly.
notes: The Chicago Youth Works FAQ says youth under 16 may be required to have a work permit; Illinois law requires one for most under-16 jobs, issued through the school district or ISBE. Ask the program whether a stipend program needs one. The FAQ says the Chicago Housing Authority, After School Matters and DFSS each also have a limited number of slots for 14 and 15 year olds.

name: VolunTEEN Program (Children's Healthcare of Atlanta)
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost stated on the page.
duration: 8 weeks in June and July (June 8 to July 31 in 2026), one 3-hour day per week, no more than two missed days
deadline_text: The page says the next chance to apply is February 2027; exact open and close dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18. You must be at least 15 by the program start date (June 8 in 2026).
how_to_apply: Read the Volunteer Manual, pass the online volunteer assessment with at least 80 percent to unlock the application, then upload immunization records, photo ID copy, forms and the name of a non-family recommender. Steps may change for 2027.
notes: Mandatory training in early June with no make-up. Needs MMR, chickenpox, Tdap and current flu shot proof and willingness to get a TB blood test. The page also lists an Explorer career program (high school, no patient contact) that is being updated with no details yet, and a Youth Advisory Council for current and former patients ages 13 to 17.

name: CHP Explorer Post (East Sacramento)
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: The CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers; the East Sacramento post page snippet says ages 15 to 21.
how_to_apply: See the CHP Explorer post locator and contact the East Sacramento post.
notes: The CHP site blocked WebFetch (403) and a browser tab loaded blank, so ages come from search results and are unconfirmed. CHP has other posts. Confirm age limits and meeting times with the post. See also California Highway Patrol Explorer Program for the statewide competition. Ages differ by source: the CHP lists 15 to 20 for Explorers, while the post page snippet says 15 to 21. Re-checked on 2026-10-09: the CHP post page returned HTTP 403 again, so it could not be read and the card stays snippet-only.

name: Junior Ambassador Program (high school volunteers)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: Summer: first week of June to first week of August, 40 hours minimum. Fall and spring: 60 hours minimum. One 4 hour shift a week.
deadline_text: Three cycles a year: summer apply by April 30, fall by August 30, spring by December 30. The page lists month and day only, no year.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: Complete the Junior Volunteer Application, submit a school recommendation form from a teacher, counselor or administrator, interview, finish health screenings, pass the orientation quiz and attend the mandatory orientation.
notes: The hospital's general volunteer program is age 16 and up. Perks listed include free parking, a food voucher, a free uniform and a free TB test. The next cycle should be the December 30 spring deadline, but the page gives no year, so confirm.

name: Living Coast Discovery Center Volunteer (ages 16 to 17)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Ongoing, based on availability. In animal care, 3 absences within 60 days may result in losing your spot.
deadline_text: Accepted on a rolling basis. Orientations are on alternating Saturdays and Sundays at 10 a.m. each month.
who_can_apply: There is a separate application for ages 16 to 17. Animal care and docent roles are 18 and up. Animal care also needs 100 hours of earlier volunteering.
how_to_apply: Submit the 16-17 volunteer application. Then go to the next orientation. They tell you about it by email.
notes: The center does not take court-ordered community service right now. If you have questions, write to volunteers@thelivingcoast.org.

name: 10x10 Teen Volunteer Team (Cincinnati Art Museum)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer team
duration: The team meets 4 to 6 p.m. on the first Thursday of each month plus extra dates as needed, and must be free for the opening on Saturday April 10, 2027. The exhibition runs April 6 to 11, 2027.
deadline_text: Volunteer applications for the 2026 to 27 team were due Friday September 4, 2026, with replies by September 11. Next year's dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Volunteer team applicants should be in grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer team form linked on the 10x10 Teen Art Expo page when applications open. Teen artists (age and grade rules for artists are not stated) can submit art when submissions open in mid November 2026. Museum phone: 513-721-2787.
notes: The museum has other volunteer groups. They are docents, visitor service aides, REC volunteers and CAM Cruiser volunteers. The main volunteer page does not state ages for them. Ask the museum before applying to those.

name: Teen Workforce Development (Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Cincinnati)
org: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Cincinnati
pay_detail: Free. The summer and school year programs are listed as completely free. The page does not say that teens are paid.
duration: Summer: June 1 to July 31, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. School year: August 17 to May 14, Monday to Friday, 2:30 to 7:30 p.m. (hours vary by Club).
deadline_text: No deadline is posted. Enroll through the Club member portal.

grades: Apply in 10th grade; program runs 11th and 12th grade
pay_detail: Free: uniforms, materials, snacks and transportation help provided; scholarships possible. A paid summer internship between junior and senior year is possible (pay not stated).
duration: Two years; Tuesday and Wednesday 4:30 to 7:30 p.m., September to May
deadline_text: The application for the class of 2028 is closed. Sophomores apply online each year beginning in February; recruitment events run in February and March. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Sophomores who live in Chicago and attend a Chicago high school (public, private or homeschooled). A 2.3 GPA and 90% attendance are recommended. Needs 2 recommendation letters, a physical and a background check.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application, a signed consent form, a copy of a school or state ID, 2 recommendation letters, a physical exam record and a background check.
notes: Takes up to 125 students each year. Contact: cpfta@cps.edu or 773-553-2486.

name: California State Summer School for the Arts (CSSSA)
org: California State Summer School for the Arts (state program)
city: California (campus not named on the pages read; address on the site is Pomona, CA)
pay_detail: Tuition and fees for California residents were $5,174 for 2026; 2027 rates 'will be posted soon'. Need based aid is available to California residents (nearly half of past students had much of tuition covered). $20 application fee, with fee waivers for students with financial need.
duration: About one month: first day of classes July 5 and graduation July 31, 2027
deadline_text: 2027 application opens in November (timeline lists Nov 1, 2026). Application and scholarship priority deadline is Feb 28, 2027, 6 pm, with no extensions. Session: registration July 3, classes July 5, graduation July 31, 2027.
who_can_apply: California residents in grades 8 to 12. Up to 20 students from out of state and other countries may also be enrolled. Each department has its own assignments.
how_to_apply: Apply online by department. A full application has the form and two teacher references, not peers. It has an unofficial transcript and department assignments. It has the $20 fee. It has the financial aid request if you want aid. Students can apply to more than one department. Each needs a full application.
notes: Students who finish can get 3 units of college extension credit from the California State University system (per the FAQ). Not a job. The pages read did not name the 2027 campus, so check before planning travel.

name: College Now
pay_detail: Free. The CUNY page describes College Now as a FREE program.
duration: Fall, spring and summer semesters
deadline_text: Each campus sets its own deadline. CUNY says spring applications are typically available October to early February, summer March to June, and fall late March to mid-September.
who_can_apply: Students at NYC public high schools. Grade 11 and 12 with an 80+ GPA can take courses on the partner campus, and a 70+ GPA opens some courses. Grade 10 with a 70+ GPA can take non-credit college and career awareness courses only. College Now is geared toward NYC Public Schools 11th and 12th graders.
how_to_apply: Apply to a specific CUNY campus's College Now program. Talk to your school's College Now liaison if your school has a partner campus, or contact a campus program directly. Many programs are first come, first served.
notes: Graduating seniors cannot join summer sessions. Students in Early College high schools can only join in summer. Costs beyond tuition (like textbooks) are not described on the CUNY page, so ask the campus.

name: Cupertino Teen Commission
duration: Two-year staggered terms
deadline_text: The city page says recruitment is currently closed. No reopening date is stated.
who_can_apply: Cupertino residents who are in 7th to 10th grade now. The city page says seniors are not eligible to apply.
how_to_apply: When recruitment is open, use the 'Apply to be a Teen Commissioner' form on the city page. The page also links a supplemental questions list. Questions about applications go to cityclerk@cupertino.gov.
notes: Meets monthly, September through May, at 6 p.m. on the second Wednesday. It meets in the Quinlan Community Center Conference Room (10185 North Stelling Road), with a teleconference option. Commission email teencommission@cupertino.gov. Staff liaison Sonya Lee, Recreation Manager, (408) 777-3121. Pay is not mentioned on the page, so it is listed as unpaid. The page says members may be in 12th grade during their term. The 8th-to-11th rule applies to applicants.

name: Lifeguard Training, Junior Lifeguarding and Junior Swim Instructor
pay_detail: Course fees apply. Amounts are not on the page; check the Rec Guide or online registration.
duration: varies by course
deadline_text: Courses are offered throughout the year. Check WebTrac for sessions.
who_can_apply: Lifeguard Training: you must turn 15 by the last day of the course. Junior Lifeguarding: pass a swim skills check on day one (25 yards of front crawl and breaststroke, tread water 1 minute, and more). Junior Swim Instructor: no age or swim test listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Register for a course through City of Davis online registration (the page links to it). Questions: 530-757-5626 or csweb@cityofdavis.org.
notes: Training can lead to City of Davis aquatics work. Junior Swim Instructor is for teens who may want to work for Davis Aquatics later, with volunteer chances after the training. The page does not promise a job. Lifeguard certification needs full attendance and passing tests. Job minimum ages are set in each posting at cityofdavis.org/jobs.

name: Davis Junior Basketball Coach, Official and Score Keeper
org: City of Davis Parks and Community Services
pay_detail: $17.39 an hour
duration: 6-week season starting the week of January 18, 2027
deadline_text: The posting is open continuously. Mandatory training is the week of January 4, 2027 and a coaching clinic on January 9, 2027.
who_can_apply: Age 15 or older to officiate or keep score, and 16 or older to coach. You need CPR and First Aid certification before the season starts and a working knowledge of basketball rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the City of Davis job page (NEOGOV). Applicants are screened on experience and may be interviewed.
notes: Temporary part-time with no benefits. Games are Saturdays at the Davis High School community gyms. Other City of Davis seasonal postings such as Parks Maintenance Aide (18 and older) and Pool Maintenance Aide (21 and older) are not open to teens.

name: Davis Senior High CTE Pathways
pay_detail: School classes, no pay. Course credit.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Enroll through your counselor during normal course selection.
who_can_apply: DJUSD high school students. The page does not list which schools offer which pathway. Ask your counselor.
how_to_apply: Contact your school counselor to enroll in a CTE course. Internships are on the Student Internships tab. See the Internship and Career Development Course.
notes: Page does not say which schools offer which pathways, or give grade or age rules. DJUSD office: (530) 757-5300. Related: the Internship and Career Development Course and the Summer Apprenticeship.

name: Teen Leadership Council
org: City of Davis Parks and Community Services
duration: Oct 13, 2026 to May 18, 2027, meets 2nd and 4th Tuesdays, 7:00 to 8:30 pm
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application period was extended to Oct 2, 2026 and is now closed. The next call is not posted.
who_can_apply: Davis teens ages 14 to 17. Up to 24 members. Needs a full school-year commitment.
how_to_apply: Fill out the TLC application on the Teens page. Questions: Micayla Valceschini, mvalceschini@cityofdavis.org.
notes: Meetings are at the Veterans Memorial Center, 203 E. 14th St. Up to 24 teens, and it is a full school-year commitment. The application closed Oct 2, so ask the city whether late applicants can still join.

name: De Anza College Dual Enrollment
pay_detail: No enrollment fees for up to 11 units a quarter (De Anza and Foothill combined). You still pay for textbooks in most courses and may pay other fees.
duration: Quarter system (fall, winter, spring, summer); a standard class is 12 weeks
deadline_text: No single deadline. Apply for admission before the quarter you want; see the De Anza academic calendar.
who_can_apply: Students enrolled in any California high school, grades 9 to 12 (rising 9th graders included). Needs permission from a parent or guardian and your school principal. No GPA requirement.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor, apply for admission, set up MyPortal, finish the Dual Enrollment overview, check prerequisites, submit the school permission form, then register. Questions: outreach@deanza.edu.
notes: Math and English classes need an assessment (usually based on your school transcript). Students can buy a VTA SmartPass for unlimited bus and light rail rides. Undocumented students can take part. Parents cannot see your college records without your written consent.

name: DECA (high school division)
pay_detail: Not stated on the pages read. Ask your advisor for chapter dues and conference fees.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Join anytime through your advisor.
who_can_apply: High school students join through a school chapter and its advisor, or a school can start a chapter. Contact the DECA advisor at your school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school for a DECA advisor. DECA lists an Online Membership System for joining.
notes: DECA says it has about 317,600 high school members in 4,510 chapters. Not every school has a chapter. California-specific details were not on the page.

name: DeKalb County Fire Rescue Explorer Post 901
pay_detail: $50 yearly fee, due after you are fully admitted. Not a paid job.
duration: Year-round, with a 2-week summer Cadet Training
deadline_text: No deadline is listed. Meeting times are not listed.
who_can_apply: DeKalb County youth ages 14 to 18 who are in school. You keep at least a C average and have good attendance and behavior.
how_to_apply: Get the DCFR Explorer application packet from the page. Send it in with 3 job references and your latest report card.
notes: Contact frexplorers@dekalbcountyga.gov. Not a paid job, so no work permit.

name: Teen Advisory Board (DeKalb County Public Library)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer hours for attending meetings.
duration: Monthly meetings for the school year; at least one meeting must be in person
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026-2027 school year are closed. The page does not say when the next application opens.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who live in DeKalb County.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application steps; check the library's Teens Get Involved page and volunteer page for the next cycle.
notes: Meeting dates were listed as coming soon. Members can miss a meeting by telling advisors through Slack or the pre-meeting survey. A search result also described a separate Teen Library Board Trustee seat, but that was not on the page read.

name: DeKalb Parks Youth Sports Support Volunteer
org: DeKalb County Recreation, Parks and Cultural Affairs
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Ongoing. Weekday afternoons and Saturdays.
deadline_text: No deadline. Volunteer any time.
who_can_apply: Volunteers ages 16 and older. Adult volunteers also need a background check. The page does not list any other rule for teens.
how_to_apply: There are four steps. Fill out the Volunteer Application. Sign the Volunteer Waiver. Go to a short orientation, online or in person. Then start.
notes: Call 404-294-2838 or write to Monique Larkin at mllarkin@dekalbcountyga.gov. The page gives no direct link to the application. Other park volunteering lists no minimum age. Examples are clean-up days and nature programs.

name: DeKalb County School District Work-Based Learning
org: DeKalb County School District, Career, Technical and Agricultural Education
pay_detail: Paid or unpaid work experience. Pay amounts are not stated.
duration: A school class block (1, 2 or 3 periods in a row)
deadline_text: No dates are posted. Ask your school's Work-Based Learning coordinator.
who_can_apply: DeKalb County School District students, mostly juniors and seniors. You need a parent or guardian OK and at least a 2.0 GPA. You must be on track to graduate. You cannot have had any suspensions this year or last year. You need good attendance: 15 or fewer unexcused absences and tardies in both years.
how_to_apply: Apply to your school's WBL coordinator. The coordinator approves students based on grades, behavior and attendance. You must have room in your schedule. Your family must give you rides to the job. Students who do not meet the rules may qualify for the Great Promise Partnership WBL. Ask your coordinator.
notes: Only for DeKalb schools students. You must leave campus at the start of your first WBL class, even on days you are not scheduled to work. The district CTAE office is at 1701 Mountain Industrial Blvd, Stone Mountain, GA 30083.

name: DeKalb Summer Youth Employment Program (DSYEP)
org: DeKalb County Government and WorkSource DeKalb
pay_detail: $15 per hour in 2025
duration: About 4 weeks (June 2 to July 3 in 2025)
deadline_text: In 2025 registration ran Apr 10 to Apr 20 (11:59 p.m.). No 2026 or 2027 cycle was found on the county site.
who_can_apply: 2025 rules: DeKalb County residents ages 16 to 21 who pass a drug screening and background check. Interns were picked by random lottery.
how_to_apply: In 2025, online registration at dekalbcountyga.gov/dsyep. That address now leads to a registration form marked no longer active. For help the 2025 county release listed the Workforce Development Manager at (470) 572-8229.
notes: Confirm that a new cycle exists before planning around it. All dates, pay and rules here are from the 2025 county release. WorkSource DeKalb also lists youth ages 16 to 24 with barriers as a service group. It sends people to ATLworks.org to check eligibility. Georgia requires a work permit only under 16, and this program starts at 16.

name: Delaware Valley Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

name: Discovery Cube Los Angeles Teen Volunteer
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Minimum 60 hours; two 4-hour shifts every 30 days
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Apply online any time.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 18. If you are 14, you can start the application one month before your 15th birthday.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application for a role. The roles are Exhibit Host, Team Spark and Team Celebration. Email a resume and a letter from an adult who is not family. Send them to VolunteerLA@discoverycube.org. Then do an interview and a mandatory orientation.
notes: The museum is in Sylmar in the San Fernando Valley. The letter of recommendation cannot come from a family member. Questions: 818-686-2835.

name: Discovery Cube Orange County Teen Volunteer
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page lists no fees.
duration: At least one four-hour shift every 30 days. 60 hours of service before the Cube verifies your hours.
deadline_text: Teen application is closed right now. The page says to check back on December 1, 2026 for winter/spring 2027 details.
who_can_apply: The page gives one age rule: if you are 14, you may start the application process one month before your 15th birthday. No grade level is stated.
how_to_apply: Online application form, a resume, a letter of recommendation, then an interview. The full application must be in before an interview is scheduled.
notes: Plan for the 60-hour minimum if you need service hours that are checked. Location: 2500 N Main Street, Santa Ana, CA 92705. Questions: volunteeroc@discoverycube.org.

name: Internship and Career Development Course
fields: any; health; education; engineering; law-government; arts-media
pay_detail: Unpaid internships; course credit with evaluation and reflection required.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. 2026-27 sites are listed now.
who_can_apply: Davis Joint Unified high school students. Some sites have priority rules (Dignity Health for Patient Care pathway students; Ford ACE for Transportation pathway students).
how_to_apply: Talk to your counselor or contact Internship Specialist Alexha Contreras (alcontreras@djusd.net, 530-757-5400 x170).
notes: Many other 2026-27 host sites are listed on the page; some have priority rules (Mercy General: Patient Care pathway students; Ford ACE: Transportation pathway students). Credit needs weekly meetings, an evaluation and a reflection. The page is written for DJUSD students.

name: Lyman Woods Volunteers (camp and program helpers, ages 14 and up)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
duration: Camp volunteers help during the summer. Other roles are ongoing.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Call 630-963-9388 for Lyman Woods volunteer details.
who_can_apply: Camp volunteers and general program volunteers must be at least 14 years old. Other roles do not list an age on the page. Everyone fills out a volunteer waiver. The page says teens to seniors can volunteer.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Lyman Woods application for the role you want. Also fill out the volunteer waiver. Program and camp volunteers send in an application and go to an interview and training. A criminal background check is only for program volunteers 18 or older.
notes: REAP restoration workdays need an RSVP. The park district also runs Counselor in Training (C.I.T.) camps for teens. They have a sign-up fee. The pages read did not list ages or the fee amount.

name: Dublin L.E.A.D. Summer Program
org: City of Dublin, Parks and Community Services
pay_detail: Registration fee for the 2026 program: $119 for Dublin residents, $143 for non-residents. No wage is stated on the page.
duration: The 2026 program ran June 8, 2026 to August 7, 2026. Participants are encouraged to help with recreation or aquatics programs for at least two weeks.
deadline_text: The 2026 application is closed. The 2026 program ran June 8, 2026 to August 7, 2026. The 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens entering 7th grade or higher. Complete the online application; staff review it and then tell you how to register. The page lists separate fees for Dublin residents and non-residents.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application when it is open (closed for 2026). Staff review it and then tell you how to register at dublinrecguide.com. Questions: Dublin.Lead@dublin.ca.gov.
notes: This is a fee-based training and volunteer-style program run by the city, not a paid job. Families pay the registration fee; the city page does not say teens are paid. The page does not name a residency rule for applying. Shifts are not pre-assigned; participants pick their own shifts in the registration system.

name: Dublin Youth Advisory Committee (YAC)
org: City of Dublin, Parks and Community Services
grades: Enrolled in middle school or high school
pay_detail: Volunteer committee seat. No pay is stated on the city page.
duration: One-year term. The 2026-27 members are listed for June 2026 to May 2027.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 seats are filled (term June 2026 to May 2027). The city page we read does not post a recruitment date for the 2027-28 term.
who_can_apply: Must live in the City of Dublin and be enrolled in middle or high school (committee bylaws). The committee has 13 members and 3 alternates; at least 6 members must be high school students.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the city page we read. Call Parks and Community Services at 925-556-4500 or use the contact link on the committee page to ask when the next recruitment opens.
notes: Meets 7:00 pm, second Wednesday of the month, Dublin Senior Center, 7600 Amador Valley Blvd; July and August meet only as needed. Bylaws say members must stay enrolled in middle or high school, and a member is removed if they stop living in Dublin or stop being enrolled. Older (2020 and 2021) notices mention late-winter recruitment; that is last-cycle information and was not confirmed for 2027. Teens who want a seat should check the city page each spring.

name: Duke Cell Biology Academy (CeBA)
org: Duke University Department of Cell Biology
pay_detail: $2,400 awarded on completion of the program
duration: 6 weeks (2026: June 22 to July 31), about 9 am to 5 pm on site
deadline_text: The page says Summer 2026 applications are closed and Summer 2027 applications will be accepted in January 2027. 2026 deadline: the flyer says March 20, 2026 and the FAQ says March 27, 2026 at 5 pm.
who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors in 2026-27 who are at least 15 by June 1, 2027 and from the Research Triangle area. Needs a Social Security Number or ITIN to receive the stipend. Students must provide their own transportation.
how_to_apply: Online application plus a recommendation letter (links on the CeBA page). Applicants hear back in mid-April.
notes: The 2026 deadline is stated two ways. It is March 20 on the flyer and March 27 in the FAQ. The page says there is no housing or transportation help, so only local students are considered. The $2,400 is a completion award. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.

name: Duke Health Youth Symposium on Healthcare Careers
org: Duke Health Volunteer Services (Duke Regional Hospital and Duke Raleigh Hospital)
duration: 2 days (2026: June 23-24 at Duke Regional in Durham; June 24-25 at Duke Raleigh Hospital)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application opened 8 pm Friday April 10 and closed 8 pm Monday April 13, 2026; acceptance emails by May 1, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students who are 16 or 17 (16 by June 24 in 2026). Students must attend both days at one site. Space is limited to 25 slots at each site.
how_to_apply: Student completes the online application and a parent or guardian completes the Participation Agreement (both on Qualtrics links on the page). No late or incomplete submissions.
notes: Both Duke pages are titled Junior Volunteer Program but describe this event for 2026. The application window was only 3 days, so watch the page in early April. Questions: DRHVolunteerServices@dm.duke.edu (Durham) or DRAH_VolunteerServices@dm.duke.edu (Raleigh). Duke University Hospital says it no longer offers a junior volunteer program for high school students.

name: MaryAnn Black Summer Internship at Duke Health
org: Duke Health and Duke Community Affairs, with Durham YouthWorks
pay_detail: Described as a paid internship. The pay amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: 3 weeks (2026: July 6-24, Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: Durham YouthWorks application opened January 23 and closed February 21, 2026; orientation in March. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Durham City or Durham County residents between 14 and 24 as of June 30, 2026, per the Duke page. The Duke article describes participants as Durham-area high school students.
how_to_apply: Submit the Durham YouthWorks application and select the healthcare category (link on the Duke Community Affairs page). Contact: Kimberly Monroe, kimberly.monroe@duke.edu.
notes: Applications go through Durham YouthWorks (City of Durham), whose own page could not be read (blocked). The article says about 50 students were planned for the latest class. North Carolina requires a Youth Employment Certificate for anyone under 18 who works; the employer starts that process.

name: Duke Pre-College Programs (High School)
org: Duke University, Office of the Provost
pay_detail: 2027 residential fee not yet posted (Duke lists it as to be determined). Enrollment deposit: $500 before April 2, 2027, or $1,500 after April 1. Airport shuttle $45 each way; extra nights $120 each.
duration: Three sessions; dates to be announced in October 2026
deadline_text: No application deadline listed. Full payment is due 30 days before each session; immunization proof due June 1, 2027; full refund for cancellations before April 1, 2027.
who_can_apply: High school students in current grades 9 to 12 who are at least 14 to attend. (The page also lists middle school programs for grades 6-8.)
how_to_apply: Join the information request list on the Duke Pre-College page to be told when 2027 dates and courses open.
notes: Courses, session dates and fees for Summer 2027 were not posted on 2026-10-09. Check back after the October 2026 announcement.

name: Junior Counselor Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer position, no cost. You can ask for a letter documenting your hours.
duration: Asked to commit to a 5-day camp week, but you can work any days you are free. Full day 9:00 am to 4:00 pm or half day 9:00 am to 1:30 pm.
deadline_text: The page says applications opened in Spring 2026. No deadline is listed. If applications are closed, your info is kept until the next open period.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 and up at Dunwoody Nature Center (15 and up at Island Ford). Be mature, reliable, flexible and energetic. You must attend a pre-camp orientation, in person the first time.
how_to_apply: Write to the Junior Counselor Coordinator. Ask how to join and what the steps are. The email is juniorcounselors@dunwoodynature.org.
notes: Phone 770-394-3322, info@dunwoodynature.org. The first email link on the page goes to a different address, so use the one in the FAQ (juniorcounselors@dunwoodynature.org). Camp dates are not listed on the page. Unpaid, so no work permit.

name: Teen and Junior Volunteers
grades: Junior program: junior high students. Teen/adult program: 14 or entering high school.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
duration: Teen shifts start at 2 hours. Junior: one weekend day (Friday to Sunday) each week for 3 months.
deadline_text: Junior volunteers are recruited in September and January. Teen and adult openings are posted on the museum site.
who_can_apply: Teen and adult volunteers: age 14 or entering high school. Junior volunteers: junior high school students.
how_to_apply: Junior volunteers fill out the online application, permission form and photo release. Teen and adult volunteers check openings on the museum volunteer page. They can also call Jessica Greenlaw at 630-637-8000 ext. 4640. You get a 2 hour training.
notes: Experience with kids is helpful but not required. Summer teen volunteering is not mentioned on the page, so ask. The minimum age for the junior program is not given, only junior high.

name: Volunteer Programs (teen openings)
org: Forest Preserve District of DuPage County
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
duration: One-time workdays or long-term roles with a yearly minimum of hours
deadline_text: No single deadline. Some roles have deadlines and limited space. New volunteer orientation is held monthly at district headquarters (second Wednesday evening).
who_can_apply: One-time community events: ages 8 and up with an adult. Long-term roles are generally 18 and up, with limited openings for ages 13 to 17. Family roles are ages 10 and up with an adult.
how_to_apply: For long-term roles, apply online through the volunteer portal. Then meet with program staff for an interview. After that, go to orientation and training. For one-time restoration workdays, find a date on the events calendar and register.
notes: Getting started for a long-term role takes about 2 to 3 months. The FAQ page says background checks apply to people 16 and older in one place and 18 and older in another. Ask the Volunteer Services office what applies to you. Call 630-933-7233 or write to volunteer@dupageforest.org. The page does not list which long-term roles take people under 18.

name: Durham County Library Maker + STEAM Volunteers
org: Durham County Library, Maker + STEAM Services
duration: You choose hours per week on the form
deadline_text: No deadline. Capacity is limited, so you may be put on a waitlist.
who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 13, or have a guardian's permission to fill out the form. The form lets you pick the age group you want to work with, including teens 13 to 18.
how_to_apply: Complete the online volunteer form (skills, preferred age group, days and times, hours per week, emergency contact). Questions: Maker_STEAM@dconc.gov.
notes: Days offered are Monday to Saturday. Time options are morning, afternoon or evening. The page does not describe a teen-only volunteer track.

name: Durham County Library Teen Volunteers
duration: Ongoing, set with the branch
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Each branch decides whether it can host volunteers; availability is not guaranteed.
who_can_apply: The For Teens page says the program is for all tweens and teens in grades 6 to 12. The general volunteer page says all volunteers must be 14 or older.
how_to_apply: Contact the teen librarian at your preferred branch. The general volunteer page also says to fill out the volunteer application form (PDF) and bring it to your nearest library.
notes: The two Durham County Library pages disagree on age: the teen page says grades 6 to 12, the general volunteer page says 14 or older. Ask the teen librarian which applies. The library says it cannot currently host court-mandated community service hours.

name: Durham Aquatic School (free lifeguard certification)
pay_detail: Training is free. City of Durham pool lifeguard jobs started at $18.90 an hour on the outdoor pools page.
duration: About 6 hours of online work, then in-person sessions (Spring 2026 courses ran March 30 to April 2)
deadline_text: Spring 2026 course: pre-course swim test Sunday, March 15, registration deadline March 15 at 10 am. New dates are posted each season.
who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 16 years old (bring proof of age to the pre-course swim test). The page also says candidates must be at least 15 on or before the last class session, so ask which rule applies. You must pass the pre-course swim test: a 150 yard swim-tread-swim, then a timed event with a 10 pound object retrieved from 7 to 10 feet deep.
how_to_apply: Sign up online at dprplaymore.org (Register Online). Or sign up in person at any Durham Parks and Recreation site. Then pass the swim test before the course. Apply for lifeguard jobs on the City of Durham career page.
notes: Search ActiveNet for DAS for current dates. Space is limited and filled by order of pre-course test registration. Questions: DPRAquatics@durhamnc.gov, 919-560-4444. Whether teens under 18 need NC working papers was not checked.

name: Teen Volunteers (Durham Parks and Recreation)
pay_detail: Unpaid. DPR can give you a record of service hours for school or scholarships.
duration: Shifts as listed on the volunteer opportunities page.
deadline_text: No deadline. Browse and sign up for open shifts.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. No experience is required.
how_to_apply: Look at the volunteer page and sign up for an open shift. Or email DPRVolunteers@DurhamNC.gov about the role you want. Then fill out the online volunteer application.
