how_to_apply: Email bmarshall@mariettaga.gov to RSVP for a meeting. Attend 4 monthly meetings in a row and fill out the welcome packet. Then you get a background check, interview and a 3-month trial.
notes: The web page says ages 14 to 21; the requirements sheet says applicants must be under 21. The web page says meetings run Thursdays 6 to 8 pm, while the requirements sheet says 6 to 9 pm, so confirm the hours.Meets at 240 Lemon Street, Marietta, GA 30060. Phone 770-794-5355 or 770-794-5300 (ask for the Community Response Unit). The sheet says the fee goes to Learning for Life, Scouts BSA. Not a paid job.

name: Maryland Department of Natural Resources Internships
pay_detail: Some are paid, some are volunteer. Check the Salary section of each posting.
duration: About 10 to 12 weeks (summer June to August, fall October to December)
deadline_text: Summer applications open in February and fall applications in July. No closing dates on the page; check each posting.
who_can_apply: People currently enrolled in high school or college, or graduated within one year of the start date. Needs a 2.5 GPA on an unofficial transcript. Postings have a high school minimum requirements section.
how_to_apply: Apply on the state jobs site (jobapscloud.com/MD). Send a state application, a resume, two letters of support from people who are not relatives and an unofficial transcript. If none are open, fill out the Internship Interest Form to get news. Contact: julie.kline@maryland.gov.
notes: Internships are posted by park, office or program. The places vary around the state.

name: The Maryland Zoo Teen Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. The page mentions no fees.
duration: At least one year: 4 shifts a month, one shift at a zoo event, and a one-week Boot Camp (Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.)
deadline_text: Teen applications are closed. The page says to check back in 2027. For 2026, applications ran Jan 29 to Apr 9, interviews were in May, and Boot Camp ran in late June and early July.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 17. You must be 14 or older by Teen Boot Camp.
how_to_apply: Turn in the full application when it opens. Incomplete ones are not considered. Then go to a group interview. Questions: volunteers@marylandzoo.org or 443-552-5266.
notes: 2026 timeline from the page: selections May 28, parent orientation June 10, Boot Camp sessions June 22 to 26 and June 29 to July 3. The page text is partly inconsistent about dates, so check it when it updates. The Teens menu also lists a Keeper-in-Training Camp that was not read.

name: Massachusetts 4-H
pay_detail: $40 per member each year, with a family cap of $120. Fee waivers can be requested through your 4-H Educator. The page says cash is not accepted.
duration: Annual membership; you re-enroll each year
deadline_text: No deadline posted. All members enroll every year.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 8 to 18 (before January 1) can join and take part in projects and competitions. Ages 5 to 7 join as Cloverbuds and do not compete.
how_to_apply: Contact your local 4-H office to learn about programs and get the New Member Enrollment Packet. Fill it out and return it. The office then tells your parent or guardian where to pay online or by check. Re-enroll through 4honline.
notes: A youth group, not a job. The Get Involved page still shows a 2022-2023 fee note, but the Membership page lists the $40 fee with a $120 family cap, so confirm the current fee with your local office.

name: Massachusetts Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of Massachusetts
city: Massachusetts (2026 session at Stonehill College, Easton)
grades: Finishing or just finished junior year of high school
pay_detail: No pay. Participants are sponsored by an American Legion post, Auxiliary unit, school or community group. The student cost is not stated on the pages read.
duration: One week (2026: June 13 to June 19)
deadline_text: The 2026 session was June 13 to June 19, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Girls who are finishing or just finished their junior year. You must be a U.S. citizen or legal inhabitant. Documents are needed at check-in. You need an interest in government, strong leadership and above average grades. A sponsor is needed.
how_to_apply: Find a sponsor (a Legion post, Auxiliary unit, school or other group). Once your sponsor sends your name and email, the site emails you the online registration form. If you have no sponsor, fill out the sponsor request form on the Registration Forms page.
notes: Girls only. You can also send in an optional bill to be considered by the mock state Congress. The program says it is run by volunteers. Email Director.massgirlsstate@gmail.com with questions.

name: Massachusetts Boys State
org: The American Legion, Massachusetts Boys State Committee
grades: Finished 11th grade, with at least one semester of high school left
pay_detail: No pay. The goal is that tuition is paid by your local American Legion post, the Massachusetts Boys State and Girls State Foundation, a school or town, or a sponsor.
duration: One week: the 83rd Annual Session is June 12 to June 18, 2027
deadline_text: Session dates: June 12 to June 18, 2027. The site says applications open in late 2026. No closing date is posted.
who_can_apply: Boys who finished junior year and have at least one semester left. You cannot have gone to a Boys State before. Leadership, character, grades and service to your school are what count. A parent and a family doctor must sign a medical consent form.
how_to_apply: Fill out the program interest form on the site. You will be told when applications open (late 2026). The application has your information and a short response on what Boys State would mean to you. It also has a reference from a teacher or guidance counselor. You can also ask your local Legion post or guidance counselor.
notes: Boys only (Massachusetts Girls State is a separate program). You are expected to attend the whole week. It falls during many schools' finals, so ask your school about make-up plans early. The interest form link is the one on the home page.

name: Mass Audubon Volunteer Opportunities
pay_detail: Unpaid. Students can earn community service credit. 50 hours a year earns a Volunteer ID card with free sanctuary admission.
duration: One day to weekly shifts; some positions are seasonal
deadline_text: No deadline. Positions are posted on the volunteer portal.
who_can_apply: Volunteers are mostly 16 or older, unless a parent or guardian comes along. The minimum age changes by job. Some jobs need training or a background check (CORI or SORI).
how_to_apply: Browse and respond to openings on the Mass Audubon Volunteer Portal. Large groups can use the group volunteer form.
notes: Busiest months are May to September. Younger teens can ask about parent-accompanied options.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, Massachusetts Wing
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location. Uniform and overnight activity fees are extra. National Headquarters says a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year. Some help is available.
duration: Ongoing. Weekly 2-hour meetings, about one Saturday event a month and a week-long summer encampment (typical, per national page)
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time by visiting a squadron.
who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters can waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Attend at least three squadron meetings.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. You can also ask the squadron about the online application.
notes: No military duty. Cadets can stay in until age 21 and can switch to adult membership at 18. Squadron meetings and costs vary, so ask the squadron near you.

name: YouthWorks
org: Commonwealth Corporation, with local MassHire workforce boards
pay_detail: At least the state minimum wage; hours and pay vary by site
duration: 6 to 8 weeks in summer; a year-round option runs September to May
deadline_text: No youth deadline is posted. Local programs set their own dates. Summer 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 25 with family income at or under 200% of the federal poverty line. You also need at least one listed factor. Examples are one income in the home, being a person of color, a disability, no stable home, or leaving school. Apply through the program in your town.
how_to_apply: Find your town on the 'Find a YouthWorks Program Near You' list, then contact that local workforce board program.
notes: Each local program picks its own jobs and dates. Seats are limited. Whether a Massachusetts work permit is needed was not stated on these pages; ask the local program.

name: Massachusetts FFA
pay_detail: Costs are not stated on the pages read. Ask your ag teacher.
duration: Ongoing while you are in agricultural education
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You join through your school.
who_can_apply: Students at a Massachusetts school with an FFA chapter. The state site lists the chapters (the list includes vocational, technical and agricultural high schools). It does not state an age rule.
how_to_apply: Find your school on the Massachusetts FFA Chapters page. The page does not say how to join, so ask your school how to sign up.
notes: The chapters page lists schools such as Bay Path Regional Vocational Technical H.S. in Charlton, Bristol County Agricultural High School in Dighton and Minuteman High School. Check the full list for your area. The site describes FFA as an intracurricular student group.

name: Summer Science and Engineering Program (SSEP)
pay_detail: 2026 tuition was $4,985 per two-week session, or $9,970 for both. 2027 rates not yet posted. Limited tuition assistance is available.
duration: 2 weeks per session. Session 1: July 3 to 16, 2027. Session 2: July 18 to 31, 2027.
deadline_text: Application opens Dec 10, 2026. Priority deadline Feb 1, 2027. Tuition assistance deadline Mar 1, 2027. International deadline Mar 1, 2027. Closes May 1, 2027 or when full.
who_can_apply: Students going into grades 9 to 12 with strong grades and drive. It is selective. The page says Smith does not treat people unfairly by sex or gender. Students from other countries can apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online with an essay, one letter from a teacher and a transcript. The fee goes up to $100 on Apr 15, 2027.
notes: Costs money. Apply early for the priority date and for aid.

name: Tufts Pre-College Summer Programs
fields: engineering; health; business-finance; arts-media; social-impact; science
grades: Entering grades 10 to 12 (some programs grades 11 to 12)
pay_detail: Tuition varies by program (amount not read on the pages fetched). Limited aid: scholarships usually cover 75 to 100% of the fee, based on need.
duration: 1 to 6 weeks; commuter or residential
deadline_text: Applications for Summer 2027 open Dec 14, 2026. Close date not posted. Aid decisions are made twice a month starting in February.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 10 to 12, or last spring's high school graduates. Residential students must be at least 15 at the start and no older than 19 at the end. Health programs need grades 11 to 12, 1 year of biology and age 16. Homeschoolers can apply. International students can apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online with a transcript. Add a letter where one is needed. Add a form where a parent says yes. See the How to Apply page.
notes: Costs money; check each program page for the price. Many 2027 dates say coming soon.

name: UMass Amherst Pre-College Summer Programs
org: University of Massachusetts Amherst, University Without Walls
city: Amherst, MA (also online and the UMass Charles River Campus in Boston)
grades: Rising sophomores, juniors and seniors (some programs only juniors and seniors)
pay_detail: $45 application fee. Listed fees: 2-week programs $4,119 residential or $2,337 commuter; 3-week $6,125 or $3,397; 6-week Research Intensives $12,813 or $7,247. Some programs add a $95 materials fee. Limited need-based partial scholarships (up to $1,000) for 1 to 3 week programs.
duration: 1 to 6 weeks, depending on the program
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed (2026 deadlines were May 1 extended to May 15, May 15 and May 31 by start date). Research Intensives 2026 deadlines were March 15, extended to April 15. The site says Summer 2027 program details and applications will be available in January.
who_can_apply: Rising sophomores, juniors and seniors in high school, and seniors who just graduated. The Pre-Veterinary Medicine and Veterinary Technology programs are only for rising juniors and seniors.
how_to_apply: Sign up for updates on the Pre-College page now. Applications for 2027 open in January. They are reviewed on a rolling basis. Scholarship applications use the same online system.
notes: Expensive. This is a college course experience, not a job. The page also lists year-round college prep workshops (fall 2026 workshops are open).

name: PROPEL Summer Research Internship
pay_detail: Paid summer internship; rate not stated
duration: Summer 2026 started June 29; length not stated
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications were due Feb 28, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older when the internship starts. You must go to, or just have left, one of these. A trade high school under Chapter 74. A public or charter high school in a listed Gateway City, like Lowell, Lawrence, Worcester, Springfield, Lynn or Brockton. Or a public high school where 25% or more of students have low income.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Write a 250 word essay. Share something that shows your STEM interest, like a poster, slides, posts, a podcast or a video. Make a 1 minute video about yourself. Get a reference from a teacher. Questions: PROPEL@uml.edu.
notes: Eligibility depends on your school type or city. Check the Gateway City list on the apply page. Ask about a Massachusetts work permit.

name: Teen Apprentice (Teen Internship) Program
pay_detail: Paid internship program; pay rate not stated
duration: Flexible hours; the museum usually hires two summer interns
deadline_text: No dates posted on the teen page. Check the museum's Job Opportunities page to see if it is hiring.
who_can_apply: Teens 16 and older who like art, museums or teaching.
how_to_apply: Look at the Job Opportunities page of the Worcester Art Museum. Apply when jobs are posted.
notes: The page says a grant from the National Endowment for the Arts supports the NEA Teen Intern jobs. Ask the museum about a Massachusetts work permit.

name: Frontiers Summer Program
pay_detail: $4,995 per session (includes tuition, housing, meals, field trips, workshops and activities). Financial assistance is explained on the program policies page.
duration: Two weeks, residential. Session I: July 5 to 16, 2027. Session II: July 18 to 30, 2027.
deadline_text: Summer 2027 applications open in early December. The page does not state the year or a close date.
who_can_apply: Rising 10th, 11th and 12th graders. International applicants need an English test (TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo).
how_to_apply: Application is free. It has two short written answers and a list of involvements. Official transcripts are preferred, but self-submitted ones are accepted. Questions: pop@wpi.edu or 508-831-4900.
notes: Costs money. The exact opening day in December is not stated. Ask about financial assistance on the program policies page.

name: Mattel Youth Ambassadors (UCLA Mattel Children's Hospital)
pay_detail: No fee, but each ambassador must raise $1,250 for the hospital to earn an awards package.
duration: Cohort 8 runs 2027 to 2028. Meetings are Wednesdays 3:30 to 4:30 PM, virtual; weekly in summer, monthly in the school year.
deadline_text: The 2026 window ran May 1 to June 6, 2026. Recruitment for Cohort 8 (2027 to 2028) is expected to open in May 2027.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. Must be 16 by Sept 1.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the program page when applications reopen. The page suggests joining an information session. Questions: mya@mednet.ucla.edu.
notes: Fundraising cannot start until you are accepted. It cannot take place on hospital or clinic grounds. Two excused absences are allowed.

name: Teen Art Collective
org: Museum of Contemporary Art San Diego (MCASD)
pay_detail: No stipend or cost mentioned on the page.
duration: Sept 8, 2026 to June 2027; meets the 2nd and 4th Tuesday of each month, 5 to 7 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026-2027 applications were due Friday Aug 28, 2026. Next year's dates are not posted; expect a late-summer deadline.
who_can_apply: 11th and 12th grade students from San Diego. The page says the group draws teens from across San Diego County. Limited to 25 students.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application (one per student). Invited students get an acceptance email and onboarding documents. Questions: education@mcasd.org.
notes: Closed for 2026-2027. The program is supported in part by the California Arts Council.

name: Teen Advisory Board at MCPL
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn Student Service Learning (SSL) hours for attending meetings.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Applicants must be 13 or in 8th grade at the time of application. They can be up to age 17 or 18 and a senior in high school.
how_to_apply: Complete the Teen Advisory Board Interest Form on the MCPL page; someone contacts you after it is received.
notes: Unpaid volunteer role. The page says there will be more chances to volunteer at MCPL in the coming year.

name: Maryland 4-H Youth Development
city: Statewide, Maryland (a local Extension office in each county); state center in College Park
pay_detail: The page says costs are kept to a minimum. No amounts are given.
duration: Year-round, ongoing
deadline_text: No single deadline. Clubs, camps and events set their own dates.
who_can_apply: The Maryland 4-H pages read do not list an age range. Programs vary by county. Contact your local Extension office to learn which clubs and programs fit your age.
how_to_apply: Contact your local University of Maryland Extension office. Ask about clubs, camps and programs in your county. Then use the Enroll in Maryland 4-H link on the Join a Club page.
notes: Maryland 4-H Center: 8020 Greenmead Drive, College Park, MD 20740, 301-314-9070. The leadership page lists a 2026 Volunteer and Teen Forum in Ocean City in November 2026. It has workshops for adults and teens aged 13 and older.

name: Maryland Boys State
org: The American Legion, Department of Maryland
grades: Rising high school seniors (finished grade 11, at least one semester left)
pay_detail: Free. The FAQ says there is no cost to the student or family. Sponsors such as American Legion posts pay.
duration: One week. The 2027 session is June 20 to 26, 2027
deadline_text: 2027 session: June 20 to 26, 2027 at McDaniel College. The 2026 application ran Nov 15, 2025 to May 1, 2026. The 2027 application dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Boys who have finished their junior year of high school by the start of the session, in public, private or home school, with at least one semester left. You cannot have attended any other Boys State.
how_to_apply: Apply online using the Apply now link on the Maryland Boys & Girls State site. Accepted students usually hear back in 2 to 3 weeks.
notes: Students under 17 sleep in college dorms, usually two to a room. Phones, smartphones and smartwatches are not allowed. The site recommends against driving yourself because the week is tiring. Staff are mostly veterans.

name: Maryland FFA
pay_detail: Membership dues are not stated on the pages read. Ask your chapter advisor.
duration: School year, ongoing
deadline_text: The state site lists a deadline to confirm or add chapter affiliation membership on Oct 15, 2026 at 5 p.m. The exact time for students to join is set by each chapter.
who_can_apply: Students in a high school agricultural education program. The site says Maryland FFA has almost 3,000 student members in 50 chapters. Age and grade rules are not listed on the pages read.
how_to_apply: Ask your school whether it has an agricultural education program and FFA chapter. The Maryland FFA home page has a Join FFA button and a chapters page.
notes: The 2026 National FFA Convention and Expo is listed on the site for Oct 20 to 24, 2026 in Indianapolis. If your school has no FFA chapter, contact the Maryland FFA office through the Contact page.

name: Maryland General Assembly Student Page Program
org: Maryland General Assembly, Department of Legislative Services
pay_detail: A meal allowance of about $50 per day worked. The Page Office arranges lodging for pages from outside Anne Arundel County who ask for it. Pages pay their own travel to Annapolis.
duration: Two weeks that are not back to back during the 13-week session (second week of January to early April)
deadline_text: Each county sets its own application deadline and may have extra requirements. The 2027 session will have pages. Contact your county page coordinator now.
who_can_apply: Maryland residents who are seniors at a Maryland public or nonpublic high school and are at least 16 years old. You apply through the school you attend, not where you live.
how_to_apply: Contact your county page coordinator. The page has a list. Get the county's application and find its deadline. The Maryland program page says the coordinator works with your high school.
notes: Each year 105 pages and 36 alternates are chosen from across the state. Program contact on the page: Tawana Offer, Tawana.Offer@mga.maryland.gov, 410-946-5120 (Student Programs). Paid work for people under 18 in Maryland needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=md for the exact permit and steps.

name: Maryland Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of Maryland
grades: Rising high school seniors (finished grade 11, at least one semester left)
pay_detail: Free. The FAQ says there is no cost to the student or family. Sponsors such as American Legion posts pay.
duration: One week. The 2027 session is June 20 to 25, 2027
deadline_text: 2027 session: June 20 to 25, 2027 at Salisbury University. The 2026 application ran Nov 15, 2025 to May 1, 2026. The 2027 application dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Girls who have finished their junior year of high school by the start of the session, in public, private or home school, with at least one semester left. You cannot have attended any other Girls State.
how_to_apply: Apply online using the Apply now link on the Maryland Boys & Girls State site. Accepted students usually hear back in 2 to 3 weeks.
notes: Students under 17 sleep in college dorms, usually two to a room. The Girls State page lists a Samsung American Legion Scholarship event on the last day.

name: Woodstock Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
pay_detail: Free. The national site says Job Corps covers housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The living allowance amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: Open enrollment: you can start at any time. The process usually takes about two months.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must be low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules. You must meet background rules. The pages read do not explain the rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Make a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Fill out the application. Upload the documents that show you are eligible. Then connect with an admissions representative. Call 800-733-5627 with questions.
notes: Center address: 10900 Old Court Rd, Woodstock, MD 21163. No closure notice showed on the pages read on 2026-10-09. The application asks for ID, Social Security number and proof of income. Only enter these on the official jobcorps.gov site, with a parent or guardian. A parent should ask an admissions representative about the rules for 16 and 17 year olds.

name: Youth Volunteer Sessions at MedShare
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: One session at a time: Wed and Fri 9 am to noon; Thu and Sat 9 am to noon and 1 to 4 pm
deadline_text: No deadline. Register for a session before you arrive.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 10 to 17. Ages 10 to 13 must come with a parent or guardian. Ages 14 and up can volunteer on their own. A signed parent permission form is required for all youth.
how_to_apply: Click Register on the volunteer page to pick a session. Everyone must register before arriving. Groups of 5 or fewer register one by one. Larger groups fill out the group request form.
notes: The volunteer page does not name its work site. The only address on the contact page is the Decatur headquarters at 3240 Clifton Springs Road. Confirm the site when you register. MedShare does not host court-ordered or required community service.

name: MemorialCare Long Beach Medical Center High School Volunteen Summer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: 8-week session; 2026 ran June 29 to August 21
deadline_text: The 2026 program was full and its application closed. A waitlist was offered. Next year's dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Students in high school grades 9 to 12. No age range is stated.
how_to_apply: Watch the page for the next application. Accepted students get an email. Then they send shot records (varicella, MMR) and a TB test within 6 months. They also go to a required orientation by invitation only.
notes: The page covers Long Beach Medical Center only. It does not mention an Emergency Room volunteer role or its age rule.

name: Teen Advisory Group (TAG), Menlo Park Library
org: City of Menlo Park, Library and Community Services
pay_detail: Volunteer. Members earn volunteer hours; the page does not say how many.
deadline_text: Rolling membership. The page is accepting applications for new members and states no deadline.
who_can_apply: Applicants should be in grades 7-12. The page does not state a residency requirement.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application linked from the library's Teen services page. Questions to David Jimenez, Librarian I, 650-330-2528 or djimenez@menlopark.gov.
notes: Meets the 1st and 3rd Thursdays, 4:30-5:30 pm, at Menlo Park Library (800 Alma St.), and the 1st and 3rd Wednesdays, 4-5 pm, at Belle Haven Library (100 Terminal Ave.). Members may attend one or both. The page is undated and is the only source; older M-A Chronicle articles describe pandemic-era activities and a different meeting pattern, so confirm the schedule with the librarian before the first meeting.

name: Youth Advisory Committee (YAC), City of Menlo Park
org: City of Menlo Park, Library and Community Services Department
grades: Entering grades 9-12 for the upcoming academic year
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Treated as unpaid committee service; confirm with the city.
duration: One-year term, September through May. About 6 hours per month for meetings and events.
deadline_text: Closed for 2026-27. The 2026-27 window ran May through July 2026 (page lists a July 17, 2026 deadline). The next window is not announced.
who_can_apply: Must be a City of Menlo Park resident and be entering grades 9-12 for the upcoming academic year and committee term.
how_to_apply: Submit the YAC application form and supplemental questionnaire to the Library and Community Services Department. Staff review applications, schedule interviews and make the final selection.
notes: Competitive, and closed now. Members must attend at least 75 percent of meetings. Contact Da'Shawn Williams, Recreation Coordinator, 650-330-2248. The page lists two email addresses (dlwilliams@menlopark.org and dlwilliams@menlopark.gov); confirm which is current. An older city notice said about 8 hours per month; the current page says about 6. The page does not mention pay, so we list it as unpaid; confirm with the city.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadets, Merced County Composite Squadron 147
org: Civil Air Patrol, Merced County Composite Squadron 147
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.
duration: Ongoing. Nationally the ideal time is a weekly meeting of about two hours, one Saturday event a month and a week long summer encampment. The squadron's meeting day and time are not listed.
deadline_text: No deadline. You can ask to join any time.
who_can_apply: The squadron welcomes all community members ages 12 to 18. They join its cadet program.
how_to_apply: Fill in the contact box on the squadron's Join Us page with your contact information and a short description of your interests. Email: christopher.ince@cawgcap.org. The squadron meets at 3515 Hardstand Ave, Atwater, CA 95301.
notes: Confirm first: the squadron pages do not list meeting times, dues or the first visit steps. The national Civil Air Patrol cadet page says cadets can join at ages 12 through 18.

name: College and Career Access Pathways (CCAP) at Merced College
pay_detail: No tuition and no books.
deadline_text: You apply for each semester you plan to attend. No dates were listed on the page.
who_can_apply: Students at high schools that offer Merced College CCAP courses. Grade levels and partner schools are not listed. Ask your counselor.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the CCAP link. A parent fills out the Dual Enrollment Parent Consent Form. Pick classes with your counselor. Then give the K-12 Permit PDF to your high school CCAP counselor.
notes: The Dual Enrollment Coordinator is Jourdan L. French. Her number is 209-384-6189. For classes taken on campus, see the separate Merced College K-12 concurrent enrollment card.

name: K-12 Concurrent Enrollment (Merced College)
grades: K-12 students (high school students check with a counselor)
pay_detail: K-12 students can enroll in Merced College classes tuition free (limitations may apply). Some physical activity courses need an extra K-12 Permit, and some fees may still apply.
duration: By semester, including summer
deadline_text: No dates are listed on the page. Registration timing is on the College's When is Registration page.
who_can_apply: K-12 students. Ask your high school counselor if you are eligible. English C1000 is only open to eligible 11th and 12th graders. K-8 students need a written recommendation from their principal or designee. They also need current transcripts.
how_to_apply: 1) Apply for admission for the semester you want. 2) Turn in the Dual Enrollment Parent Consent Form once during high school, after you get your 7 digit Merced College ID. 3) Complete the K-12 Permit form for your school level. 4) Wait for the email that lets you register in the MC Portal. 5) Pay fees online or at the Student Fees Office. Phone for the Merced campus: 209-384-6000.
notes: This is the college's own concurrent enrollment page. Merced Union High School District also has its own dual enrollment partnership with Merced College (see that separate card). Kinesiology courses with a physical activity part are capped at 10 percent of K-12 seats.

name: EMPOWER Program (Merced County Office of Education)
pay_detail: Paid and/or unpaid work experience; wages are not stated.
duration: Not stated; follow-up services for at least 12 months after the program
deadline_text: No dates posted on the page; it has an online interest and application form.
who_can_apply: Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 21 (for example, youth without a high school diploma). Teens 16 to 18 qualify only if they are out of school.
how_to_apply: Use the Click here to apply form on the EMPOWER page, or call 209-381-5926. The office is at 658 W. Main Street, Merced.
notes: Prospero (the Merced County workforce board, formerly WorkNet) lists EMPOWER as its main youth program for out-of-school youth. Prospero Youth Team: 209-724-2036. Confirm first: the page gives no start dates or wage.

name: High School Regional Occupational Program (ROP)
pay_detail: Cost, pay and credit are not stated on the page.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the page.
who_can_apply: High school students across Merced County. The page lists the ROP at Delhi, Dos Palos, Gustine, Hilmar, Le Grand, Los Banos and Pacheco high schools. It also lists Merced Scholars Charter School. It also lists Valley Community School in Atwater and in Los Banos. Grade rules are not stated.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to enroll. Ask your school counselor, or contact Dora Robles, Staff Secretary, at (209) 381-6684 or drobles@mcoe.org.
notes: Confirm first. The page does not list the courses, grades, cost or how to enroll. The MCOE college and career page also lists the EMPOWER program (see the separate EMPOWER card). It also lists Cal-SOAP for college and financial aid information.

name: Volunteer at Mercy Medical Center Merced
org: Dignity Health (CommonSpirit), Mercy Medical Center Merced
deadline_text: The page does not say whether applications are open now. Ask Volunteer Services.
who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. Mercy Medical Center in Merced is a listed place to volunteer.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer interest form. The volunteer team then contacts you about an interview and orientation. You also need a background check and shots.
notes: This is the Central California system volunteer page. It lists no phone number, so use the contact page at commonspirit.org/dignity-health-central-cal-contact-us. The page does not say whether applications are open, so ask before you plan on it.

name: Dual Enrollment and Merced College Classes (Merced Union High School District)
org: Merced Union High School District and Merced College
pay_detail: Free: students can take college courses at no cost, up to 11 units a semester. Textbook fees are waived for CCAP classes; textbook fees apply for concurrent enrollment.
duration: By semester
deadline_text: No dates posted on the district page; check with your school's Pathway Counselor.
who_can_apply: Students in good academic standing at a Merced Union High School District school (Atwater, Buhach Colony, El Capitan, Golden Valley, Livingston, Merced, Sequoia, Yosemite). Complete the Merced College application, a parent consent form and a High School Permit.
how_to_apply: Apply to Merced College, submit the parent consent form and High School Permit, and talk to your school's Pathway Counselor.
notes: College privacy law applies once you enroll: parents do not get progress updates from Merced College. A college GPA below 2.0 can affect future college eligibility and financial aid.

name: Teen Library Volunteer
org: Montgomery-Floyd Regional Library (Blacksburg and Christiansburg branches)
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: 1 to 2 hour shifts
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Teens must be 11 or older. Volunteering is during the school year, with extra hours in summer for the Summer Reading Program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application and return it to the front desk. An application does not guarantee acceptance. Missing 3 shifts without notice removes you from the schedule.
notes: The page was last updated Nov 12, 2024, so call your branch to confirm. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

name: American Legion Auxiliary Michigan Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of Michigan
pay_detail: Cost to the student is not stated on the pages read. The page asks people to donate to send a young woman to Girls State.
duration: One week, June 13 to 19, 2027
deadline_text: The 86th session is June 13 to 19, 2027 at Michigan State University. The 2027 application is posted online. No closing date is stated on the flyer or page.
who_can_apply: Female high school students who will finish their junior year in spring 2027. You must have at least one more semester before graduation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online delegate application. The link is on the Michigan Girls State page and the 2027 flyer. Questions go to the Girls State chairman, Beryl Robbins, at berylrobbins1980@gmail.com or (313) 318-6845.
notes: Not a job. A closing date was not on the page or flyer, so apply early. The page also lists a Samsung scholarship and a government manual to read before attending.

name: American Legion Michigan Boys State
city: Hillsdale, MI (2026 session at Hillsdale College); office in Lansing
pay_detail: $25 application fee paid by the student. The $400 program fee is paid by a sponsor such as a local American Legion Post or other community group (2026 brochure).
duration: One week (2026: June 21 to 27)
deadline_text: 2026 session: June 21 to 27, 2026 at Hillsdale College; application deadline was June 1, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted on the pages read.
who_can_apply: Males who have completed their junior year and have at least one year of high school left, with an interest in government and strong leadership, character and school or community service. Applicants must be a U.S. citizen. Anyone who already attended Boys State cannot attend twice.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on michiganboysstate.org (the 2026 brochure says to visit the website to apply). Pay the $25 application fee and find a sponsor for the $400 program fee. Office: (517) 371-4720 ext. 123 (site) or 517-220-2754 (brochure), legion@michiganlegion.org.
notes: Not a job. Dates, fees and the deadline above are from the 2026 brochure and flyer, so confirm the 2027 details with the office. The resources page still showed a May 1, 2024 deadline, so it is out of date. Office address: 212 N. Verlinden Ave., Lansing, MI 48915.

name: Pre-Employment Transition Services for blind and low vision students (BSBP)
org: Bureau of Services for Blind Persons, Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity
pay_detail: Not stated
duration: Programs run throughout the year
deadline_text: No deadline. Check the program calendar on the page for current programs.
who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 26 with a visual impairment. The school can refer you at your IEP meeting.
how_to_apply: Contact your local BSBP office or your school special education office. You can also fill out the form at the IEP meeting.
notes: Programs may target a certain age group, interest or skill.

name: Michigan DECA chapters and state conference
org: Michigan DECA (chartered association of DECA Inc.)
pay_detail: $17 per student member: $9 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapter fees are not stated.
duration: School year
deadline_text: The Michigan DECA conference is March 11 to 13, 2027 at Huntington Place in Detroit. No membership deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: Members must be enrolled in a marketing, management, finance, hospitality or entrepreneurship course. Grades and ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's business or marketing teacher about a DECA chapter. Send state questions to the Michigan DECA advisor, Dave Wait. His email is dwait@emich.edu.
notes: Not a paid job. The state website listed on the page is mideca.org. This card is based on the DECA Inc. page for Michigan.

name: Michigan FFA membership through a school ag class
pay_detail: Dues are not stated on the pages read.
duration: School year
deadline_text: No membership deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: Students ages 12 to 21 who are enrolled in a state-approved agricultural education course. The page does not list grades.
how_to_apply: Use the chapters and regions page to find a chapter near you, then ask that school about its agriculture class. Questions can go to the state office.
notes: Not a job. The homepage says there are over 10,000 members in 137 chapters. State office: association@michiganffa.org or (517) 353-9221.

name: FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC) in Michigan
pay_detail: Registration cost not stated. Scholarships are listed through FIRST.
duration: Build and competition season
deadline_text: No 2027 dates are posted on the FRC page. It only shows 2026 events.
who_can_apply: Teams of high school students. The page does not give an age or grade rule. It links to Start a Team and Run a Team.
how_to_apply: Join an existing school or community team or use the Start a Team link on the FIRST in Michigan site. Contact on the page: Gail Alpert, 248.425.4148.
notes: Ask your school if it has a team. FIRST in Michigan also runs FTC and FIRST LEGO League for younger students.

name: Pre-Employment Transition Services for students with disabilities (Michigan Rehabilitation Services)
org: Michigan Rehabilitation Services, Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity
pay_detail: MRS pays for services in your employment plan. Not a wage.
duration: Ongoing
deadline_text: No deadline. Apply any time.
who_can_apply: Students with disabilities ages 14 to 26 who are in school or have been accepted at school after high school. If you are under 18, a parent or guardian must sign a consent form. Your school fills out a form that shows the disability.
how_to_apply: Use the MRS Online Application. Forms MRS-4.0a (parent consent) and MRS-4.0b (school verification) are on the page. Phone 517-241-5324 or toll-free 800-605-6722.
notes: Work-based learning is one of five services. Ask your school transition coordinator or counselor too.

name: Michigan Tech Summer Youth Programs
org: Michigan Technological University, Summer Youth Programs
grades: Middle and high school (exact grades not stated)
pay_detail: Exploration programs start at $1,175 live-in (tuition, fees, meals, room and board) or $700 commuter. A $150 non-refundable deposit is due at registration. Pathway program fees vary. Scholarships exist.
duration: Week-long programs
deadline_text: 2027 registration and program dates are not posted yet on the pages read. Balances are due in full by May 1 and most scholarships are reviewed on a rolling basis.
who_can_apply: Middle and high school students from around the world. The cost page lists no grade rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Sign Up Now link on the Summer Youth Programs page and pay the $150 deposit at registration. Pathway programs have nothing due at application. Contact syp@mtu.edu or 906-487-2219.
notes: Extra costs can include lab fees, a $20 weekly parking pass and charter bus service. Check the Course Catalog and Scholarships pages on the SYP site for current offerings.

name: Civil Air Patrol cadets, Michigan Wing
pay_detail: Annual dues are $40 for cadets. The page estimates a fully active cadet could spend $300 to $600 in the first year, minus help for uniforms and overnight fees.
duration: Weekly 2-hour meeting, about one Saturday event a month, and one week-long summer encampment
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time through a local squadron.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 through 18.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Contact it to confirm a meeting. Go to about three meetings before you finish the membership application.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Wing HQ mailing address: 43401 N. Jefferson, Bldg. 825, Rm 317, PO Box 450048, Selfridge ANGB, MI 48045-0048. School comes first; the page says school-based squadrons may differ.

name: WIOA Youth Program through your local Michigan Works! agency
org: Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity, delivered by local Michigan Works! agencies (Michigan Works! Southeast for Washtenaw County, Capital Area Michigan Works! for the Lansing area)
pay_detail: Not stated. The state page lists both paid and unpaid work experiences, including summer employment, as possible services.
duration: Varies by local agency
deadline_text: Operated year round by local Michigan Works! agencies. No state deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: In-school youth ages 14 to 21 who are low income and have at least one listed barrier (for example basic skills deficient, English language learner, homeless or foster youth, pregnant or parenting, disability). Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 with a listed barrier.
how_to_apply: Call Michigan Works! at 1-800-285-WORKS (9675). Or find your local agency by ZIP code at michiganworks.org. Then ask about WIOA Youth eligibility.
notes: Not open to every teen: eligibility depends on income and barriers, so a short call to the local agency is the real first step. The state page does not list a local application form or local youth contacts. Capital Area Michigan Works!' own site (camw.org) mentions WIOA and says 259 youth were served but does not describe its youth program in detail. Work experience for anyone under 18 in Michigan needs a work permit under the state's youth employment law.

name: YMCA Michigan Youth in Government
pay_detail: The base fee is not stated on the page read. A $25 late fee applies to late Lansing registration. A financial aid application is linked on the page.
duration: Fall district conference, then a Lansing conference of about four days
deadline_text: 2026-27: February Lansing conference Feb 18 to 21, 2027, regular registration Nov 10 to Dec 27, late Dec 28 to Jan 13. April Lansing conference Apr 22 to 25, 2027, regular registration Nov 10 to Feb 28, late Mar 1 to 17. Fall district conferences are scheduled Oct 2 to Nov 9, 2026 (registration closes two weeks before each), so some may already be closed.
who_can_apply: High school students (a separate middle school program exists). The pages read do not list grades. You join through a school or YMCA delegation.
how_to_apply: Check the map on the YMCA page to see if your school or YMCA has a delegation. If not, use the Contact us page to start one. Then register for the conferences your delegation attends.
notes: Not a job. The deadline_iso is the end of regular registration for the February Lansing conference. Fall conference sites include Marquette, Grayling, Allendale, Saginaw, Kalamazoo and Detroit.

name: Michigan Youth Challenge Academy (MYCA)
org: Michigan National Guard, Michigan Department of Military and Veterans Affairs
pay_detail: Free to parents. No obligation to join the military.
duration: 5.5 months residential plus 12 months after. Cycles start mid-January and mid-July.
deadline_text: Two cycles a year. The January start application opens Aug 1. The July start application opens Feb 1. The application takes place over the 4 to 5 months before each cycle. No closing date is posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 1/2 to 18 on day one (15 1/2 means you turn 16 during the cycle). Must be a Michigan resident and a U.S. citizen or legally present, not yet have a high school diploma, not be on reporting probation, and have no felonies. Ages 15 1/2 can only do credit recovery and return to their high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Inquiry Form on the MYCA site. Then follow the steps on the Admissions Process list.
notes: It has a military style setup, but the page says you do not have to join the military. The page calls it a program for at risk youth who want to finish high school.

name: Opportunity Youth Program, Middlesex College
pay_detail: Paid training and work experience are listed; the wage is not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No dates listed.
who_can_apply: Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 who live in Middlesex County and meet additional eligibility criteria. Not for teens currently enrolled in high school.
how_to_apply: Email opportunityyouthprogram@middlesexcollege.edu to start. Office: 550 Jersey Avenue, New Brunswick, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
notes: The page does not name the funding source. Teens under 18 who are not in school should check eligibility with the office. Paid work for people under 18 in New Jersey needs working papers (online). See permit.html?state=nj for the exact permit and steps.

name: Milpitas Youth Advisory Commission
duration: Three-year terms (seven commissioners and two alternates)
deadline_text: The city says commission applications are accepted year-round, and appointments are made as needed. No closing date is stated.
who_can_apply: Commissioners must be in grades 7 through 12 and live in Milpitas. Applicants also complete the Youth Advisory Commission supplemental questionnaire.
how_to_apply: Submit a commission application online, by email, by mail, or in person, with the Youth Advisory Commission supplemental questionnaire. Questions go to the City Clerk's Office at cityclerk@milpitas.gov or 408-586-3001.
notes: Regular meetings at 6 p.m. on the second Thursday of every month, Milpitas Teen Center, Rooms 140/141, 40 N Milpitas Boulevard. Founded April 1996. The page lists current members with terms ending September 2028. Pay is not mentioned on the page, so it is listed as unpaid. The supplemental questionnaire PDF could not be read, so its questions are not summarized here.

name: Teens at Mingei
pay_detail: $750 for full participation
duration: 15 sessions, twice a month on Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:30 p.m., October to May
deadline_text: 2026-2027 applications ran March 2 to April 1, 2026, with interviews April 20 to 24 and notices in August. Next cycle not posted; expect a similar spring window.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 17, entering 10th or 11th grade in fall 2026, and attending a San Diego County high school.
how_to_apply: Online application, then a mandatory in-person interview and group interview if advanced. Contact the museum's Education Specialist or see the program PDF on the page.
notes: Closed for the 2026-2027 cohort. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

name: Step Up (Foundations level)
org: City of Minneapolis, Community Planning and Economic Development
pay_detail: Paid by the City of Minneapolis (Foundations level); hourly rate and weekly hours not stated on the page. Teens not matched can do a 5-week online Career Exploration Program and earn up to $599 plus elective credit.
duration: About 2 months (June 22 to August 21 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 window was Jan 5 to Mar 1, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted; the city says applications open each January and offers a sign-up for 2027 updates.
who_can_apply: Minneapolis residents ages 14 to 21 who are not enrolled in college. The Foundations level is for ages 14 to 21; the Pro level is for ages 16 to 21 with previous work or volunteer experience.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the January window. Accepted students (notified by about Mar 10) complete a required in-person orientation in March and April, then are matched with an internship.
notes: Step Up Director phone 612-673-5041; program phone 612-673-5118. The page does not mention work permits. Not every applicant is matched with a paid internship.

name: Minnesota 4-H
org: University of Minnesota Extension, Minnesota 4-H Youth Development
grades: Kindergarten through one year past high school (grade 13)
pay_detail: Minnesota 4-H does not charge a state membership fee. Some local clubs or programs charge dues, and help may be available.
duration: One 4-H year runs Oct. 1 through Sept. 30. You re-enroll each year.
deadline_text: No fixed deadline on the Join page. Membership lasts Oct. 1 to Sept. 30 and you re-enroll each year.
who_can_apply: Anyone from kindergarten through one year past high school. Independent membership means you are not in a club. It needs 6th grade or older and at least two years of 4-H club experience. It also needs an adult 4-H volunteer as your mentor.
how_to_apply: Get in touch with local 4-H staff near you, or fill out the interest form. Then complete your enrollment online or with a paper form.
notes: Clubs and costs can differ by county, so contact your county 4-H staff first. This is a youth club and learning program, not a paid job.

name: Minnesota American Legion Boys State
pay_detail: Fees are paid by the sponsoring American Legion Post or other community group. No dollar amount is listed. Spending money for the camp store is optional.
duration: One week. 2027 session: check in Sunday June 13, check out Saturday June 19, 2027.
deadline_text: No application deadline is posted. Each sponsor sets its own. Ask your school counselor or a local American Legion Post.
who_can_apply: Young men who have just finished their junior year of high school. The Legion says picks are based on merit and ability. A sponsor, usually a local American Legion Post, chooses from students your school recommends.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or contact a local American Legion Post. Forms and delegate information are on mnboysstate.org. For questions, call 651-291-1800 or email jkelley@mnlegion.org.
notes: Boys State is for boys. The 2026 session was June 14 to 20 at Saint John's University. Girls State is a separate program run by the American Legion Auxiliary. The Boys State pages give no age number, only the junior-year rule.

name: Minnesota DECA (high school)
org: Minnesota DECA, chartered association of DECA Inc.
pay_detail: Student dues are $13 total: $5 to the state association and $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapters may add costs.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Membership deadlines are set by the state advisor. The 2027 state conference is Feb 28 to Mar 2, 2027 at the Hyatt Regency Minneapolis.
who_can_apply: Students at a Minnesota high school with a DECA chapter. Chapters must have business and marketing courses and an advisor employed by the school. The official pages list no grade or age rule, so ask your advisor.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's DECA advisor, usually a business or marketing teacher. The advisor registers members online. If your school has no chapter, DECA lists six steps to start one. State advisor: Jacklyn (Jackie) Schiller.
notes: DECA's page lists 86 chapters in Minnesota (high school and college counts are not split). The state site mndeca.org lists phone 218-847-5355 and posts role play and judging information. It does not explain joining, so start with your advisor.

name: Minnesota FFA
pay_detail: National FFA dues are $7 a year. Minnesota State FFA dues are $11 starting in 2026. That is $18 for both. Local chapters and regions may charge more.
duration: School year, tied to your ag class
deadline_text: No application deadline. You join through your school's agriculture program.
who_can_apply: You must be enrolled in an agriculture, food and natural resources (AFNR) course at a school with an agricultural education program. The page lists no age or grade rule. If your school has no program, the site links to how to start one.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or agriculture teacher and sign up for an agriculture course. Joining FFA goes through that class.
notes: The home page reports 218 agricultural education programs in Minnesota. Ask your counselor whether your school has one.

name: Minnesota House High School Page Program
org: Minnesota House of Representatives, Sergeant at Arms Office
pay_detail: Small meal stipend. The program pays for the hotel. You pay your other personal costs.
duration: One week (Monday to Friday) in Saint Paul. 2027 weeks run from Jan 25 to May 14, 2027.
deadline_text: Complete applications are due by end of business on Nov 10, 2026 for the 2027 session. Selected students are told by email by mid-December.
who_can_apply: Any Minnesota high school junior. You can go to a public or private school or be home schooled. Selection is competitive. The program tries to include students from all parts of the state.
how_to_apply: Download the 2027 Page Application PDF from the House Sergeant at Arms site. Email it to EducationalPrograms@house.mn.gov. You also need a 500-word essay. You need one letter of recommendation. It can come from a teacher, counselor or academic advisor.
notes: Participants stay together as a group each evening at the program-designated hotel. Questions: Sergeant at Arms office, 651-296-4860.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, Minnesota Wing
city: Statewide, MN (squadrons in Duluth, St. Paul, Alexandria and more)
pay_detail: National Civil Air Patrol page: annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location, and about $300 to $600 in costs in the first year, less any financial assistance. Ask your squadron for exact costs.
duration: Ideally a 2 hour squadron meeting each week, one Saturday event a month, and one week-long encampment in summer. School-based squadrons may differ.
deadline_text: Join any time. Visit a squadron meeting first.
who_can_apply: At least 12 and not yet 19. You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (headquarters may waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). You must attend at least three squadron meetings first. Cadets can stay until their 21st birthday.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the Civil Air Patrol unit locator or the Minnesota Wing Locations page. Visit a meeting with a parent. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. Ask whether you can apply online.
notes: Example squadrons: Duluth (MN-016), St. Paul (MN-042), Alexandria (MN-135). Wing office: 6275 Crossman Lane, Inver Grove Heights, MN 55076. This is a youth program, not a paid job.

name: Minnesota Youth Council
pay_detail: The Council pages do not mention pay or a stipend.
duration: Two-year term. You travel to the Twin Cities area at least five times a year for retreats, Youth Day at the Capitol and hearings.
deadline_text: The 2026 round (for the 2026 to 2028 term) took applications from January to March 2026: Feb 28 for priority consideration, Mar 31 for all applications. No 2027 dates are posted. Seats also open when members graduate or step down.
who_can_apply: Minnesota residents ages 13 to 19 who attend a middle or high school in Minnesota. Four representatives come from each of the eight congressional districts, plus at-large seats. Applicants should be active in their community and know the three branches of Minnesota government.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, then interview in spring. Selected applicants meet the Council director with a trusted adult in May and are sworn in. You may get a follow-up call or text.
notes: The apply page has a caption with an older appointment date from the last round, so trust the Feb 28 and Mar 31 dates above. Full Council meetings are usually one Sunday afternoon a month. Check the apply page again in January 2027.

name: Minnesota Youth Institute (MNYI)
org: University of Minnesota College of Food, Agricultural and Natural Resource Sciences
pay_detail: Free. Participants are eligible for a $1,000 CFANS scholarship.
duration: Paper due early April; event on one day in May
deadline_text: 2026: register by March 27, paper due April 3, event May 14, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12 who live in Minnesota.
how_to_apply: Sign up on the online form. Pick a topic and write the paper. Send it in with the permission form.
notes: Participants get Borlaug Scholar recognition.

name: ZooTeen volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid. Benefits include free admission for you and your immediate family and shop discounts.
duration: Summer camp season (details not stated)
deadline_text: Applications for the Summer 2026 ZooTeen camp season are closed. The page says to check the website in 2027 for next summer.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. (Zoo Ambassador volunteers must be 18 or older.)
how_to_apply: Watch the Minnesota Zoo volunteer page in 2027 for the application. Questions go to the volunteer services email on the page.
notes: ZooTeens do not handle or care for animals; they work with campers.

name: Mission College High School Dual Enrollment
pay_detail: Enrollment fees waived; you pay only for textbooks and materials (many courses have no textbook cost)
duration: By term (fall, winter, spring, summer)
deadline_text: No deadlines listed on the page. Follow the term dates.
who_can_apply: High school students prepared for college-level work. Students in 9th grade or below need special approval from the Director of Outreach and Student Development. English and math placement rules apply. No GPA rule stated.
how_to_apply: Apply through OpenCCC, do the placement assessment, submit the Dual Enrollment Form (parent and school counselor signatures, 2 to 3 business days), meet prerequisites, then register in the My Mission portal. Phone (408) 855-5007.
notes: Unit limits: up to 8 in fall or spring (non-MECHS students), 6 in winter, 9 in summer; more needs a petition. Undocumented students are welcome. Getting to campus is on you.

name: MOCA Teen Program (paid)
org: The Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles (MOCA)
pay_detail: Teens are paid. The page does not give an amount.
duration: 2026-27 group starts mid-September 2026
deadline_text: Applications for 2026-27 are closed (over 130 applied). The next window is not posted.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors. MOCA aims for a group with different school, area and arts-access backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Not open now. See mocateens.org and the MOCA Teens page for the next call.
notes: Competitive. Check the page in summer for the next cycle.

name: Montgomery County Recreation seasonal part-time jobs
pay_detail: Part-time/seasonal pay starts at $18 per hour and increases with experience (no benefits).
duration: Seasonal
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Summer camp positions fill in spring.
who_can_apply: The department says teens interested in seasonal part-time positions can apply. The page I read does not state a minimum age for these jobs. It lists 15 for TeenWorks and 14 for volunteers.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Search and Apply' link on the Recreation employment page to apply for seasonal part-time positions.
notes: Call or check the posting for the minimum age of each job (lifeguard and camp roles usually have their own age and certification rules). Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.

name: Summer RISE
org: Montgomery County Public Schools, Department of Partnerships
pay_detail: Stipend, if funded (amount not stated).
duration: 5 weeks, 50 hours (Jun 21 to Jul 23, 2027)
deadline_text: Student registration opens in January and runs January to February (year not stated on the page). Placements are announced in April or May.
who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors in Montgomery County Public Schools with parent or guardian permission. Must be free weekdays Jun 21 to Jul 23, 2027, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.
how_to_apply: Register online (parent or guardian reads the Parent/Guardian Agreement first), choose your top three career areas and in-person or virtual preference. If accepted, attend a mandatory workshop on professional skills and financial literacy.
notes: Hours are set by each host. Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer. See permit.html?state=md for the exact permit and steps.

name: TeenWorks Employment Program
pay_detail: Minimum wage (county FAQ). Maximum hours depend on grade when first hired: 9th grade 350, 10th grade 300, 11th and 12th grade 200.
duration: Full-year commitment; assignments run 200 to 350 hours
deadline_text: Application windows on the page: Jan 2 to Mar 30 (spring/summer) and Aug 1 to Nov 30 (fall/winter). The page does not state the year, so the fall/winter window may be open now.
who_can_apply: Montgomery County residents who are high school students and at least 15, can work for a full year, attend a mandatory information session, and have a parent or guardian's consent.
how_to_apply: Attend the mandatory TeenWorks information session, interview with the TeenWorks team, then complete the county employment application when the posting is available. Phone 240-777-8080.
notes: The 15 year minimum comes from the Recreation employment page, not the program page. The window dates have no year on the page, so confirm that the fall/winter window is still open. TeenWorks staff are seasonal county employees. Maryland rule (Maryland Department of Labor): work permits are required for all minors under 18 to work in Maryland, issued only after a job offer.

name: Montgomery Parks volunteering and Student Service Learning hours
city: Montgomery County, MD (park sites countywide; office in Wheaton)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. Only opportunities approved by MCPS and the Montgomery County Volunteer Center give SSL hours.
duration: Varies by project
deadline_text: No deadline is listed. Browse the opportunities list and sign up for events.
who_can_apply: Volunteers without a parent or guardian must be 14 years old. Some jobs have higher age limits. Younger children can volunteer with a parent. This is the Family Volunteer program. The adult must register separately.

name: MSM S.T.E.A.M. Academy (Grades 9 to 12)
grades: Rising 9th to 12th (3-week option). Rising 10th to 12th (6-week research option)
pay_detail: 3-week option $1,000. 6-week research option $1,500. No stipend listed.

deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Jan 26 and closed Mar 25, 2026 (reviewed on a rolling basis). 2027 dates not posted.

notes: Costs money. A session can be cancelled if too few students sign up. Contact on the pipeline page: Dr. Ryan Clark, 404-752-1843. Dates shown are from summer 2026.

name: Summer Pre-College Program
pay_detail: $3,500 flat fee for up to three courses, plus up to $100 per course for books and a $30 non-refundable application fee

notes: Costs money. The page also calls the group rising juniors and seniors in places. Confirm your grade with the Summer Academy (academicsuccess@morehouse.edu). Dates shown are from the 2026 summer.

name: Youth Volunteer Program

notes: Weekday daytime shifts at most branches. Shift hours, fees and training are not listed on the page. The Arboretum's paid science fellowships are for college students, so they are not in the guide. Eagle Scout and Gold Award projects are taken by emailing volunteer@mortonarb.org.

name: City of Mountain View Teen Volunteer Summer Program
org: City of Mountain View, The View Teen Center
pay_detail: Free to participants; unpaid

notes: Age limits are not listed on the page, so email The View Teen Center to check yours. Shifts are weekdays (Junior Lifeguards also Saturdays). Transport to Deer Hollow Farm is provided from the Community Center.

name: Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee (YAC)
pay_detail: Unpaid; no cost stated

name: GROW CELLS Cancer Research Summer Program

notes: The same page lists three other programs (FIRE UP, CADET, SCREP) that are for college or graduate students, not high schoolers. The symposium is in person for all summer students. The application form link is the 2026 one.

name: High School Ambassadors Track (Health Careers Exposure Program)

duration: 4 weeks (2026 program dates not stated on the page)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: apply Feb 1 to Mar 27, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

how_to_apply: Fill out the online Apply Now form. Teacher recommendations, grades and an interview help pick who is chosen.
notes: Costs money. The same page lists a separate college track, which is not for high schoolers. Contact on the pipeline page: Dr. J. Wesley Lockhart, 404-752-1197.

name: Norman Mineta Bay Area Summer Academy (MTC)

deadline_text: The 2026 program is over. The 2026 call was announced March 24, 2026; exact open and close dates are not on the page. 2027 not posted.

name: Summer Camp Youth Volunteer
duration: Camp weeks; schedule not stated on the pages read

who_can_apply: Youth volunteers ages 14 to 17.

notes: The camp-specific application page returned an error, so the camp schedule, requirements and deadline were not confirmed. The general volunteer perk is a free membership after 100 hours in a year (not confirmed for youth).

name: NAACP/JMRL Paid Library Internship and Scholarship
org: Jefferson-Madison Regional Library and Albemarle-Charlottesville NAACP

pay_detail: $3,000 stipend for 200 hours, plus eligibility for a $2,000 yearly scholarship toward an associate's, bachelor's or master's degree (up to $5,000 a year total)
duration: 200 hours of library work
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications due 5 pm, March 27, 2026; award announced by April 30, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

Whether a Virginia Employment Certificate is needed for 14 and 15 year olds was not stated (applicants are 17 or entering 12th grade).

name: Naperville Community Job Fair
pay_detail: The fair itself is free. Employers there hire for paid jobs.
duration: One day, 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.
deadline_text: Saturday, January 2, 2027, 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., Fort Hill Activity Center, 20 Fort Hill Drive, Naperville.
who_can_apply: Job seekers from high school students (ages 15 and up) to older adults. Free.
how_to_apply: Walk in. KidsMatter says no registration is necessary. You can try a mock interview, work on a resume and talk about financial literacy there. Questions: sherilyn@kidsmatter2us.org or 630-864-3960.
notes: The Park District says students can use the January fair to plan summer jobs. KidsMatter's 2027 page lists mock interviews, resume help and money skills. Last year's fair also had panels on the 7 Illinois career paths. Confirm what is offered in 2027. A news post from March 2025 also described a spring job fair for summer jobs. Illinois: the Evanston Township High School work permit page says workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before starting.

name: Teen Pitch Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. The library pays for the program supplies.
duration: Application in fall. Event runs 30 to 90 minutes in June, July or August 2027
deadline_text: The 2026 application ran August 1 to September 30, 2026 and is closed. The page does not give 2027 dates. Teams picked for the in-person pitch are contacted by mid October 2026.
who_can_apply: Groups of 2 to 5 teens in grades 7 through 12 when the application is sent in.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application during the August 1 to September 30 window. The top three to five teams give a short in-person pitch, and one team is chosen to run its program.
notes: Programs cannot sell products. They cannot be about politics, medicine or religion. The idea has to be new to the library calendar.

name: Teen Volunteers and Teen Advisory Group (TAG)
grades: Volunteers: 9th grade and up. TAG: grades 6 to 12
pay_detail: Unpaid. TAG members earn community service hours for each meeting.
duration: TAG meets once a month for two hours at rotating library locations
deadline_text: No deadline stated on the page.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be in 9th grade or above. You do not need a Naperville library card. TAG is open to teens in grades 6 through 12.
how_to_apply: Volunteers fill out the online volunteer application. For TAG, write to the teen librarians and ask how to attend. The email is teenlibrarians@naperville-lib.org.
notes: The volunteer coordinator's phone on the page is 630-637-2226.

name: Mayor's Chief of Staff Internship (KidsMatter)
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page. Ask the city.
duration: Until July 31, 2027 for the 2026-27 term
deadline_text: 2026-27 applications were due 5 p.m. Friday, Sept. 4, 2026. Selected students start at the KidsMatter Leadership Academy on Saturday, Nov. 7 (this fall). The city post is dated August 10, 2026. Next year's call is not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Up to 8 sophomores and juniors who live in Naperville. You must live inside the city limits. Freshmen and seniors cannot apply. Students who served on a board or commission cannot apply.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply button on any board or commission page of the city site. Answer yes to the Mayor's Chief of Staff question. Upload a resume or a note about your interest. Say that you are free all year.
notes: The news post does not say whether it is paid. Ask Rachel Pruneda (prunedar@naperville.il.us, 630-420-6018). A full job description is on the city boards page.

name: Seasonal and Part-Time Jobs (Centennial Beach, camps, parks)

duration: Seasonal. Summer jobs include Centennial Beach and the Paddleboat Quarry.
deadline_text: The page's table says Centennial Beach jobs (lifeguard, concession, swim instructor), paddleboat jobs, camp counselors and Knoch Knolls nature camp jobs are usually posted in mid December. Other jobs post in May, June or August. The Community Job Fair is January 2, 2027.
who_can_apply: Minimum age differs for each job. Check the age listed on the posting.
how_to_apply: Find a posting on the district job board and fill out the online application for that job. Mail, email or fax is not accepted. Apply for each job separately.
notes: Only applicants chosen for an interview are contacted. The page has a table of when each job is usually posted. Ages and pay are on each posting, so check them before you apply. In Illinois, workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before they start. This comes from the Evanston Township High School work permit page.

name: Volunteer Programs and Events (ages 14 and up)
pay_detail: Unpaid. The district can sign off on volunteer hours for school.
duration: Dates listed this fall (no year printed; the weekdays match 2026): Kids' Night Out on Fridays, Nov 20 to Dec 18, 5:30 to 9:00 p.m. Santa's Workshop on Dec 1, 3, 6, 8, 10, 13, 15, 17 and 20.
deadline_text: Apply at least two weeks before the date you want to volunteer. Santa's Workshop runs December 1 to 20 and Kids' Night Out runs November 20 to December 18 (no year printed on the page; weekdays match 2026).
who_can_apply: Ages 15 and up can volunteer on their own. Kids' Night Out and Santa's Workshop are open at age 14 (high school freshman). Anyone 14 or younger who is not in those roles needs a parent or guardian with them. BINGO volunteers must be 18.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Application (17 and under) and approve a DCFS background check, at least two weeks ahead. Then email Becca (address on the Programs volunteer page) to sign up for a program. You cannot just show up, except at Nature Champion days.
notes: Volunteer hours can be confirmed by email, a signed letter or a school form.

name: Police Cadet Program
pay_detail: No pay is mentioned on the page. Cadets help with security and traffic control at events.
duration: Ongoing, two meetings a month
deadline_text: No deadline is stated on the page.
who_can_apply: At least 14 years old, finished 8th grade, and not older than 21. Needs a C average or better, and no serious arrests or convictions.
how_to_apply: Download the cadet application and turn it in at the front desk, 1350 Aurora Ave. A committee checks references and does a background check and an interview. Questions: NPDCadets@naperville.il.us.
notes: The police internship on the same site is for college students, so it is not listed. The department points younger people to the cadet program.

name: Youth Academy
grades: In high school or entering high school
pay_detail: Free
duration: 6 weeks, Thursday nights 6 to 8 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026 class: June 11 to July 23, 2026, applications due June 4, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Students in high school or going into high school in fall 2026. You live in Naperville or go to high school there. You need parent permission and your own ride. You need good standing at school and no criminal contacts.
how_to_apply: Print and fill out the application and waiver at naperville.il.us/youthacademy. Send the signed forms to Sergeant Greg Rink at rinkg@naperville.il.us. Or drop them off at 1350 Aurora Ave.
notes: First come, first served and space is limited.

name: Student Representatives on City Boards and Commissions
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page calls it a volunteer role.

deadline_text: 2026-27 applications were due 5 p.m. Friday, Sept. 4, 2026. Selected students start at the KidsMatter Leadership Academy on Saturday, Nov. 7 (this fall). The city post is dated August 10, 2026. Next year's call is not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Students who live inside Naperville city limits. You are a sophomore, junior or senior. Freshmen cannot apply. If you already served on a board or commission, you cannot apply.
how_to_apply: Click Apply on any board's page on the city Boards and Commissions site. Fill in the profile and the student rep questions. Upload a resume or a short statement. You can apply to up to three boards.
notes: 24 positions, two per board. Contact: Rachel Pruneda, prunedar@naperville.il.us, 630-420-6018. The dates come from an August 2026 city news post.

name: NASA Citizen Science Projects
pay_detail: Free
duration: Whenever you want
deadline_text: Always open.
who_can_apply: Open to everyone, and no citizenship is needed. Age rules vary by project: some (GLOBE Observer, NeMO-Net) are marked kid friendly; Growing Beyond Earth is for middle and high school teachers.
how_to_apply: Browse the project list, pick one, and follow that project's own sign-up steps.
notes: Some projects need a telescope or other gear. Projects are free to join.

name: NASA GeneLab for High Schools (GL4HS)
city: Virtual (hosted by NASA Ames, Mountain View, CA)
grades: Rising juniors and seniors (and college freshmen)
pay_detail: Free. No stipends since 2026.
duration: 12 weeks, June 1 to Aug 28 in 2026
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran Feb 15 to Mar 15, 2026, or until 1,000 applicants. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: U.S. citizens or permanent residents attending a U.S.-based high school; rising juniors, seniors, or college freshmen; unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher; at least one high school biology course; a computer with stable internet.
how_to_apply: Apply online with a PDF high school transcript when the window opens.
notes: The real NASA Ames option for high schoolers. NASA's main OSTEM internships are college-only. Acceptance was rolling through April 30, 2026, and the cap was 1,000 applications, so apply early. Needs a PDF high school transcript. No 2027 dates posted.

name: Nasher Teen Council

how_to_apply: Watch the Nasher Teen Council page for the next application. The page does not say when it opens. Meetings are every Thursday evening during the school year.
notes: Durham County students only. Watch the page for the next application.

name: High School Career Academy

Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) requires an age and schooling certificate (work permit) for working minors of school age; 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer months can instead give the employer proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement.

name: Youth and Young Adult Employment Program (paid summer work experience)
pay_detail: Paid; hourly rate not stated
