how_to_apply: Register online during the registration window. Questions: HNHFWorkforceDev@NationwideChildrens.org.
notes: Popular: the page says there is overwhelming interest, and about 108 young adults took part in 2025. Schedules are Monday to Friday starting at 9 or 10 a.m. All participants are 16 or older, and Ohio law (ORC 4109.02) lets 16 and 17 year olds working in the summer give proof of age and a signed parent or guardian consent statement instead of a work permit; the hospital may still ask for paperwork, so confirm.

name: North Carolina 4-H teen programs
org: North Carolina 4-H, NC Cooperative Extension (NC State and NC A&T)
city: Statewide, North Carolina (local 4-H office in every county)
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the pages read. Ask your county 4-H office.
duration: Year-round, ongoing
deadline_text: No single deadline. Programs and events vary by county and have their own dates on the NC 4-H calendar.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18 can join the teen programs. Age is counted as of January 1 of the program year. You join through your local county 4-H program.
how_to_apply: Find your county 4-H program. Then enroll through 4-H Online. That is the system for joining, renewing and signing up for events.
notes: The teen page was updated April 30, 2026. Clover Crew is listed as new in 2026. Programs differ from county to county. The pages read do not give a fee or the dates for the teen events.

name: North Carolina FFA
org: North Carolina FFA Association (NC State University Agricultural Education)
grades: Middle and high school (the page says national FFA has members in grades 5 to 12)
pay_detail: 2026-27 dues: $12 for high school students ($7 national plus $5 state) and $8 for middle school students ($7 national plus $1 state). Many chapters collect these through the school.
duration: Membership year runs Aug 1 to July 31
deadline_text: The membership year runs Aug 1, 2026 to July 31, 2027. The state membership deadline is March 1, 2027.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 5 to 12 who belong to a school FFA chapter, which runs through a school agricultural education program. Homeschool students can join if they take an agriculture course and have an SAE project (for example through the NCSU Agriscience Academy chapter).
how_to_apply: Ask your school counselor or agriculture teacher if your school has an FFA chapter. Take an agriculture class. The chapter advisor sends in the roster and dues. Homeschool families use the Homeschool FFA Membership Application on the page.
notes: The state office is at 4111 Beryl Road, Raleigh, NC 27606, 919-515-4206. The site says North Carolina has over 47,000 FFA members. If your school has no ag program, the page explains how a school can start one.

name: North Carolina Governor's Page Program
org: North Carolina Office of the Governor, hosted by VolunteerNC
grades: High school students or recent high school graduates
pay_detail: $200 stipend per week to help with travel and lodging costs. A limited number of host families provide meals and rides for a $100 fee paid by the page.
duration: One page week of four days (Monday afternoon, then Tuesday to Thursday)
deadline_text: The application for 2026 is closed. The page says applications are taken on a rolling basis until spots are filled, so apply as soon as the next application opens. No 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: High school students or recent high school graduates in good academic standing. Seniors may apply to take part the summer before college. College students are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Governor's Page application and send the online recommendation form to two people: a non-relative school staff or faculty member (unless homeschooled) and a non-relative adult who can speak to your fit. Applications without both recommendations are not processed.
notes: Founded in 1973. The work location is the Albemarle building, 325 N Salisbury St, Raleigh. Business clothes are required. Pages and their guardians arrange where to stay and eat in Raleigh. Office of the Governor phone: (919) 814-2000. The page does not list dates for page weeks. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.

name: North Carolina Governor's School
city: Raleigh and Greensboro, NC (Meredith College and Greensboro College)
grades: Grade 11 when nominated (grades 10 and 11 for dance, choral music and instrumental music)
pay_detail: $600 tuition per student, collected through the school or district. Need-based scholarships are offered by the NC Governor's School Foundation. Families pay for travel.
duration: Four weeks (June 20 to July 17, 2027)
deadline_text: Application forms were released in Sept 2026. Local school deadlines vary and come in fall 2026. Selection news goes out in early to mid March 2027.
who_can_apply: North Carolina residents in public or non-public schools. You must meet one of the GPA or course rules in the family overview, for example a 3.25 unweighted GPA. You cannot apply on your own. Your school or district must nominate you first.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor or local Governor's School coordinator. Turn in the student application at your school, not to the state office. It has one essay or audition and a personal readiness form. Turn in two recommendation forms too.
notes: Competitive. The family overview says about 1,800 students are nominated and about 800 are picked in a typical year. Students must stay the whole session and may attend only once. The overview says you may not use AI on the application.

name: North Carolina House Page Program
org: North Carolina General Assembly, House of Representatives
grades: Current sophomores, juniors and seniors (grades 10 to 12)
pay_detail: $150 stipend for the week, or 30 hours of community service credit instead. No housing is provided.
duration: One week, Monday to Thursday, while the legislature is in session
deadline_text: Information on the 2027 House Page Program will be posted late this fall (2026). Applications are taken on a first-come basis until all spots for the session are full.
who_can_apply: Current high school sophomores, juniors and seniors in good school standing. A North Carolina House member must sponsor you. You must not have been a House Page before. School principal approval is needed if you serve during the school year.
how_to_apply: Ask your own House member to sponsor you (find yours with the Find Your Legislators tool). Then fill out the online application, which goes to that member. You can ask the House Page office, Room 1329, 16 W. Jones Street, Raleigh, for a paper copy.
notes: Very competitive and you can apply with only one member. The Speaker of the House makes the final appointments. Housing in Raleigh is up to your parent or guardian. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.

name: Job Corps in North Carolina (Schenck, Kittrell, Oconaluftee)
org: U.S. Department of Labor, Job Corps
city: Pisgah Forest, Kittrell and Cherokee, NC
pay_detail: Free. The national site says Job Corps covers housing, meals, basic medical care and a living allowance. The living allowance amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: Open enrollment: you can start at any time. The process usually takes about two months.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules. You must meet background rules. The pages read do not explain the rules for applicants under 18.
how_to_apply: Make a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Fill out the application. Upload the documents that show you are eligible. Then connect with an admissions representative. Call 800-733-5627 with questions.
notes: Centers: Schenck, 98 Schenck Dr, Pisgah Forest, NC 28768. Kittrell, 1096 U.S. Highway 1 South, Kittrell, NC 27544. Oconaluftee, 502 Oconaluftee Job Corps Rd, Cherokee, NC 28719. No closure notice showed on the pages read on 2026-10-09. The application asks for ID, Social Security number and proof of income. Only enter these on the official jobcorps.gov site, with a parent or guardian. A parent should ask an admissions representative about the rules for 16 and 17 year olds.

name: Lady Cardinal Mentorship Program
org: NC Department of Administration, Division for Women and Youth
grades: Grades 9 to 12 (girls; rising 9th graders cannot apply)
pay_detail: $1,700 stipend, paid on the second to last day of the program. No housing is provided.
duration: 4 weeks, 40-hour weeks Monday to Friday (July 2027, exact dates not posted yet)
deadline_text: 2027 plan: applications open early Jan 2027 and close in Feb 2027 (the FAQ says the firm deadline is the end of February). Phone interviews in March, notices in April, program in July 2027.
who_can_apply: High school girls in grades 9 to 12 who are enrolled in a North Carolina public, private, charter or home school. Rising 9th graders are not eligible. Open to girls from across the state, but all placements are in the Raleigh area.
how_to_apply: Apply when the application portal opens in early January 2027. The FAQ says to check the program website for current deadlines. Email your resume, cover letter and transcript to doa.youth.involvement@doa.nc.gov. Students who skip these documents are dropped from the process.
notes: Only 15 to 20 spots. You must get yourself to your job site every day; the program only gives rides to Wednesday and Thursday events. Contact named on the page: Jean McBride. Paid work for people under 18 in North Carolina needs a Youth Employment Certificate. See permit.html?state=nc for the exact permit and steps.

name: Cafe Coordinators

name: East Brunswick Youth Council
pay_detail: Membership dues are $40 per school year.
duration: School year
deadline_text: No closing date posted. Registration is on the Volunteer Matrix site.
who_can_apply: East Brunswick residents in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Sign up on the Volunteer Matrix site. The page links to it. Email ebyouthcouncil@eastbrunswick.org.
notes: Run with the Township Division of Recreation and Community Services. The page also links to a membership guide for 2025-2026.

name: Soup Kitchen Volunteering, Elijah's Promise
pay_detail: Unpaid. Court-ordered service hours are not accepted.
duration: One shift at a time, Monday to Saturday between 8:00 am and 12:30 pm
deadline_text: Sign up for open shifts online; if none show, they are filled.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. Anyone under 18 must come with a guardian, and you must secure an individual volunteer slot for both the adult and child.
how_to_apply: Register for a shift on the volunteer site linked from the page; a minor and the supervising adult each need their own slot. Questions: volunteer@elijahspromise.org or 732-545-9002 ext. 122.
notes: Wear closed-toed shoes and long pants; expect to stand for the whole shift. Only five people fit in the kitchen at once. Large groups are booked through January 2027.

name: Teen Volunteering (Teen Action Group and Kindness Club)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Kindness Club gives 1 volunteer hour per meeting.
duration: School year 2026-27 for the Teen Action Group; Kindness Club meetings; summer Reading Buddies
deadline_text: The Teen Action Group form is for the September 2026 to August 2027 school year. Kindness Club needs no application, but teens must register for each meeting. Summer 2026 Reading Buddies applications are closed.
who_can_apply: Students ages 12 to 17 who live in Franklin Township (Somerset County). You need a Franklin Township library card that is active. Reading Buddies are teens going into grades 8 to 12.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Action Group form on the teen volunteering page. Register online for each Kindness Club meeting. Questions: use the Reference Desk form or call 732-873-8700, option 3.
notes: Only for Franklin Township residents with an active Franklin Township library card. The page does not give the Kindness Club meeting date or place. Search the teen event calendar.

name: Teen Volunteer at New Brunswick Free Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Regular, ongoing help; hours not stated
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Apply any time.
who_can_apply: The library says a volunteer is someone 16 or older who helps on a regular basis. If you are under 18, use the teen form. Call the library to ask if younger teens can apply.
how_to_apply: Download and print the teen volunteer application from the volunteering page, fill it out, and bring it to the library at 60 Livingston Ave. There is no online submission. Phone: (732) 745-5108.
notes: The teen form file name says 2018, so ask the library if it is still current. The page does not mention work permits; ask the library.

name: Teen Advisory Board and Teen Volunteering, Metuchen Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid. The Teen Advisory Board has a 15 hour service minimum for the year.
duration: Summer volunteering runs July to August. The board meets once a month.
deadline_text: The summer application goes up every year on the second Wednesday of June at 12 pm. School-year volunteer spots are limited to 5.
who_can_apply: The Teen Advisory Board is open to Metuchen residents in grades 6 to 12. Summer volunteering is open to all teens in grades 9 to 12. In the school year, volunteering is only for grades 9 to 12. You must have volunteered in a summer or be active on the board.
how_to_apply: Use the volunteer application on the teens page. Then contact the Teen Services Librarian. Her name is on the application.
notes: Board meetings in fall 2026 are listed for Oct 20 and Nov 17 on the page.

name: Middlesex County Magnet Schools Career and Technical Programs
org: Middlesex County Magnet Schools (East Brunswick, Perth Amboy, Piscataway, Edison and Woodbridge)
pay_detail: No tuition for Middlesex County residents. Non-residents pay tuition set by the board.
duration: High school years
deadline_text: No closing date is posted on the admissions page. See the page for open house dates.
who_can_apply: High school age youth in Middlesex County who finished 8th grade for 9th grade entry. Students are picked by grades, a career-tech test, an interview and a counselor's note. Space is limited. County applicants are admitted first.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the district enrollment link. A parent or guardian must say yes. You can also get applications at the schools in all county towns.
notes: This is a school program, not a job. Students from outside the county are admitted only if there is space.

name: Early Career Exploration Institute, Middlesex County Magnet Schools
city: East Brunswick, Perth Amboy and Piscataway, NJ
pay_detail: Free. Students provide their own transportation.
duration: 12 days: July 6 to 23 in 2026, Monday to Thursday
deadline_text: The 2026 session ran July 6 to 23, 2026 and was at capacity (waiting list only). 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Any Middlesex County student who finished 7th grade and is going into 8th grade. You should like the idea of career and tech classes.
how_to_apply: In 2026 the page offered a waiting list form. Watch the Magnet Schools site for the 2027 sign up.
notes: For younger teens only: students must have just finished 7th grade.

name: Teen Volunteering and Teen Advisory Board, Old Bridge Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer credit hours.
duration: Varies by role (Math Tutors are Saturdays 11 am to 1 pm during the school year; Tech Helpers work Mondays and Saturdays, year-round)
deadline_text: Organization Club requires an orientation; the page says to check back for more orientation dates. Tech Helpers and Teen Advisory Board need an application.
who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12 (the library cannot accept volunteers after they turn 18). Math Tutors are grades 9 to 12; Chess Tutors are grades 8 to 12. Teen Advisory Board needs an application.
how_to_apply: Stop by the Youth Services desk to get an application. If you want to try for an Organization Club spot, write to teenvolunteers@oldbridgelibrary.org. There are not many spots.
notes: You can request a letter that confirms your volunteer hours by email.

name: Teen Volunteering and Teen Advisory Board, Plainsboro Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteer hours can be confirmed.
duration: Shelvers get one 1 hour shift a week. The Teen Advisory Board meets about twice a month.
deadline_text: Weekly volunteering registration for 2026-2027 is closed. The page says Teen Advisory Board applications open in September, at the start of each school year. Join the volunteer mailing list for new openings.
who_can_apply: Shelvers must be going into 9th grade or older. Teen Advisory Board needs an application.
how_to_apply: Apply with the Teen Advisory Board form on the page. For volunteering, email the Teen Volunteer Coordinator and join the volunteer mailing list. Shelvers interview and train first.
notes: Selection is not first come first served.

name: Teen Volunteers, Plainsboro Township Recreation and Community Services
org: Plainsboro Township Recreation and Community Services
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: As needed; events are in early May, October and December
deadline_text: Volunteers are used as needed. No dates are posted for applying.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be ages 14 and older. Teens who are younger than that cannot join.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Registration Form linked on the page.
notes: The township public safety page lists separate police volunteer options. The ages for those were not read.

name: Rutgers 4-H STEM Ambassadors Program
grades: Entering 9th or 10th grade (apply in 8th or 9th grade)
pay_detail: Free: direct summer program expenses are paid by a scholarship valued at $1,000. No wage or stipend is listed.
duration: Year-round, multi-year; 2026 summer program at Rutgers-New Brunswick was July 6 to 10
deadline_text: 2026 cohort application closed. The page says check back in early 2027 for the next cohort.
who_can_apply: College-bound youth from urban communities in Atlantic, Camden, Essex, Hudson, Mercer, Middlesex, Passaic and Union counties, with a B or better GPA, top 25% of the class, and interest in volunteering to help 4-H with STEM programs.
how_to_apply: Online application on the program site (opens early in the year). About 60 students are accepted each year. Contact on the Rutgers 4-H STEM site: Chad Ripberger, ripberger@njaes.rutgers.edu.
notes: Only students in the listed counties qualify. Selected students start with an orientation in May and two short online modules.

name: BOLD Summer Camp (BioCONECT Oncology Leadership Development), Rutgers Cancer Institute
org: Rutgers Cancer Institute and Rutgers School of Public Health
pay_detail: No application fee. Accepted students paid a non-refundable $500 enrollment fee in 2026 (due June 1, 2026).
duration: 1 week, 9:30 am to 4:00 pm (July 20 to 24 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed (acceptances by May 15, 2026). 2027 dates not posted. Join the mailing list at BOLD@cinj.rutgers.edu.
who_can_apply: High school students entering 10th, 11th or 12th grade in the fall. Only 45 students were accepted in 2026. Applicants write a five paragraph personal response.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application and write the five paragraph answer. Questions: BOLD@cinj.rutgers.edu.
notes: Two groups run it. They are the LIFE Center at Rutgers Cancer Institute and the Center for School and Community-Based Research and Education. A reunion camp is open to past campers.

name: TARGET Summer Engineering Program, Rutgers School of Engineering
grades: 6 to 11 (sessions by grade; grades 9 to 11 in July)
pay_detail: $500 for the one-week program. Need-based sponsorship is available after acceptance. Families provide transportation.
duration: 1 week, 9 am to 5 pm
deadline_text: Summer 2026 dates are posted (July 13 to 31, 2026). 2027 dates and the application deadline are not posted.
who_can_apply: Middle and high school students. Sessions are by grade level in spring 2026: 9th graders July 20 to 24, 10th graders July 27 to 31, 11th graders July 13 to 17 (2026 dates). Open to all students of any gender.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the application steps in the text read. Check the TARGET page and the School of Engineering contact page.
notes: Program director is named on the page. Programs for grades 6 to 8 run in June and July too.

name: Rutgers Pre-College Summer Academies
org: Rutgers University-New Brunswick, Office of Summer and Winter Sessions
pay_detail: 2026 cost was $2,899 for most academies ($3,887.50 to $5,068 for the two credit academies), with a $500 non-refundable deposit. Includes dorm for the week.
duration: One week, residential
deadline_text: The Summer 2026 application is closed. Summer 2027 dates are not posted; the page offers an email list for updates.
who_can_apply: High school students finishing sophomore or junior year, ages 16 to 18. The page states this age rule for Summer 2026, so check the 2027 rules. U.S. and international students.
how_to_apply: Online application on the Pre-College Summer site. Join the email list for 2027 updates.
notes: Costs money. Check the Costs page for the current year before planning. The page did not list financial aid; ask the program.

name: SLAAM Engineering Summer Academy, Rutgers Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
org: Rutgers School of Engineering, Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
pay_detail: $875 for the two-week session.
duration: 2 weeks, 9 am to 4:30 pm (July 6 to 17 in 2026). Non-residential.
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed May 1, 2026 (6 pm Eastern). Notices went out by May 18 and payment was due June 7. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Strong high school students, from 8th graders going into 9th through 12th graders about to graduate. You need a transcript. You also need letters from your math, science or engineering teachers.
how_to_apply: Apply online with your transcript and letters from your teachers. Applications that are not complete are not reviewed.
notes: Selective program. Email the coordinator listed on the page if you need help getting a laptop.

name: Rutgers Summer Scholars Program
org: Rutgers University-New Brunswick Pre-College Summer Programs
grades: Current high school students (graduating seniors not eligible)
pay_detail: 2026 rates per credit: in-state $482 (Arts and Sciences) to $551 (SEBS), out-of-state $1,148 to $1,338, plus a one-time $162 student fee. Courses are typically 3 credits; up to two courses.
duration: Summer Session I (started May 26, 2026) or Session II (started July 6, 2026)
deadline_text: 2026: applications opened February 2; last day to apply May 17 (Session I) and June 28 (Session II). 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Current high school students ages 16 to 18 (must be 16 by the course start date) with at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA, who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents. Graduating seniors are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Online application plus unweighted transcript, a Parent/Guardian Permission Form and a letter of recommendation (teacher or anyone who knows your work). Reviewed first come, first served; decisions in 5 to 7 business days.
notes: Some courses need extra technology or prerequisite courses. Withdrawing after the add/drop period puts a W on a Rutgers transcript. Questions: summerscholars@rutgers.edu.

name: Toxicology, Health and Environmental Disease (THED) High School Summer Program
org: Rutgers Environmental and Occupational Health Sciences Institute (EOHSI)
grades: Entering 10th, 11th or 12th grade in fall 2026, with at least one high school biology course
pay_detail: $975 non-refundable camp fee covers tuition, manuals, materials, safety equipment, lab supplies and lunch. Need-based financial aid may be available. No housing or transportation provided; no stipend.
duration: One week, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. (2026 sessions: July 20 to 24 and July 27 to 31)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: enrollment opened January 5, 2026; deadline was Monday, March 2, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Motivated high school students entering grades 10 to 12 who have completed at least one high school biology course.
how_to_apply: Online application only: about 250-word essay on your interest, high school transcripts or report cards, and your preferred session. Acceptance emails go out in the first week of April; pay within 2 weeks to hold the spot.
notes: Held at EOHSI, 170 Frelinghuysen Road, Piscataway. Questions: THED@eohsi.rutgers.edu. Expect the 2027 cycle to follow the same winter pattern, but confirm on the page.

name: Rutgers Upward Bound Math-Science (RUBMS)
pay_detail: Free program. A stipend is not stated on the page read.
duration: Year-round, with a six-week Summer Institute
deadline_text: The page says online applications open in mid-September and close in mid-December each year. A 2027 application link is posted.
who_can_apply: Students who finished 8th grade and are in 9th, 10th or 11th grade. You must live in and go to school in New Brunswick, Perth Amboy or Plainfield. You must be first in your family to go to college, or low income. You must be a US citizen or permanent resident. You need at least a C average and a plan to go to college. You must send an application and a personal statement, and do an interview.
how_to_apply: Use the Upward Bound Math-Science 2027 Application link on the page. Questions: upwardbound@echo.rutgers.edu or (848) 445-3090. Virtual open houses are held in fall in English and Spanish.
notes: Students must be willing to get to campus every day of the summer (parent ride or bus program). A separate Pre-College Outreach program is described on the same page.

name: Rutgers Young Scholars Program in Discrete Mathematics
pay_detail: Expected $4,800 for 2026 (tuition, materials, housing and Monday to Friday meals). Partial and need-based scholarships available.
duration: Four weeks (2026: July 6 to 31), residential, home on weekends
deadline_text: 2026: reviewed first come, first served from February 2026; completed application, including solutions to the problems, by March 31 if seeking a scholarship; financial aid applications by April 15, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Mathematically talented high school students. No specific grade or age is listed. You must submit solutions to the Problems to Explore.
how_to_apply: Four parts: Student Information and Consent Google Form (with a parent), your solutions to the Problems to Explore, a teacher recommendation emailed directly, and a transcript emailed by your counselor.
notes: Residential; students go home on weekends. Page read was the Summer 2026 listing.

name: Teen / High School Volunteers, Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital
org: RWJBarnabas Health, Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital
pay_detail: Unpaid. The required urine drug screen is free to the volunteer; no other costs are listed.
duration: Minimum 100 hours of service per year; the hospital hopes for 2 to 3 hours a week. Shifts mornings, afternoons and evenings, 7 days a week.
deadline_text: No application deadline or dates are listed on the page.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18 who have completed ninth grade. Weekday shifts are 4 to 6 p.m. for ages 15 and up, or 6 to 8 p.m. for ages 16 and up.
how_to_apply: Email the Volunteer Director (Jacob.Persily@rwjbh.org) with the teen's name, high school and current grade. Applications are not sent at a parent's request. Then comes orientation. Next is medical clearance. That is a health form from a doctor covering TB screening, immunizations and flu vaccine. Then a drug screen. Phone: 732-937-8507.
notes: Volunteers must be fully vaccinated and wear the provided uniform. The page says internships and shadowing are not offered. A newer and an older version of this page disagreed on hours (75 vs 100 a year); the page read on 2026-10-09 says 100.

name: Waksman Institute Summer Experience (WISE)
org: Waksman Institute of Microbiology, Rutgers University
grades: High school students who completed a high school biology course
pay_detail: $2,200 for the in-person WISE (non-refundable, due 2 weeks after approval). A virtual vWISE costs $600.
duration: Two weeks, Monday to Friday (2026 sessions: June 22 to July 2, July 27 to August 7; vWISE August 10 to 21)
deadline_text: 2026 application opened February 2, 2026 and was first come, first served (sessions expected to fill). Application forms for the Summer 2027 WISE Programs will be posted in late January 2027.
who_can_apply: High school students who have completed a high school level biology course. No age or grade range is stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Online application posted on the WISE page; first come, first served. Pay the fee within 2 weeks of approval.
notes: In-person sessions are non-residential at the Waksman Institute on the Busch campus in Piscataway. The year-long Waksman Student Scholars Program (WSSP) is a separate, school-based program that starts with teachers.

name: Student Volunteering, Woodbridge Public Library
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer hours and signatures.
duration: Most roles are all year, about 1 hour a week. Summer Reading Club volunteering is June to August, up to 5 hours a week.
deadline_text: For summer reading help, sign up in April or May. Other roles run all year.
who_can_apply: Library patrons in grades 7 to 12. Book reviews are for grades 8 to 12 who live in Woodbridge. Details differ by branch.
how_to_apply: Contact the branch library. You can also write to the Teen Services team at teenservices@woodbridgelibrary.org. You can just drop in to a Community Service Club meeting.
notes: The Fords Branch Library will help you get volunteer hours for National Honor Society applications. It does this when other ways do not work.

name: Youth Recreation Advisory Board, Woodbridge Township
pay_detail: Not stated; this is a civic board.
duration: One year term, August 1 to July 31
deadline_text: Terms start each August. The page gives no application dates.
who_can_apply: 15 high school students. High school principals suggest them, one member and one backup per school. The Mayor then names them for one year starting in August. Members can apply again until they graduate.
how_to_apply: Ask your high school principal to recommend you. The Mayor then appoints members for a one-year term starting in August.
notes: Very small: about 15 seats. The page lives on a township website that uses the woodbridgelibrary.org address.

name: New Jersey 4-H Youth Development
pay_detail: Costs are not stated on the pages read. Ask your county 4-H office.
duration: Ongoing clubs and programs; camp is a week in summer
deadline_text: No single deadline. Clubs and programs run through the year.
who_can_apply: Youth in grades K to 13. The Rutgers 4-H homepage says it serves everyone in grades K through 13.
how_to_apply: Use the Join 4-H form on the New Jersey 4-H site, or find your county 4-H office on the Rutgers 4-H page.
notes: Not a job. It is a youth group. The Rutgers homepage has a Join 4-H form and a link to the New Jersey 4-H Camp. The pages read did not give fees, so ask your county 4-H office.

name: American Legion Auxiliary Jersey Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of New Jersey
city: New Jersey (2026 session at Centenary University)
grades: Junior in high school when applying
pay_detail: No pay. Sponsors (units, posts or other groups) enroll and sponsor delegates; the site does not list a fee to the student.
duration: About 5 days (2026: Sunday June 21 to Thursday June 25)
deadline_text: 2026 sponsorships were filled and no applicants were being accepted. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Juniors who live or go to school in New Jersey and are legal U.S. residents. You must be fluent in English and able to attend the whole session. You must be willing to take part in nondenominational prayer, patriotic ceremonies, the Pledge and the National Anthem. An Auxiliary unit must sponsor you.
how_to_apply: Contact a local American Legion Auxiliary unit or a county chairperson to ask for sponsorship. The site lists contacts. You cannot apply without a sponsor.
notes: Girls only. Start asking local Auxiliary units in the winter. The 2026 site says sponsorships were already filled. A matching program for boys (Jersey Boys State) is run by the American Legion.

name: American Legion Jersey Boys State
org: American Legion Department of New Jersey
grades: 11th grade (junior) with at least one semester of high school left
pay_detail: Post-sponsored: parents pay a $50 non-refundable fee and the post pays the rest. Self-sponsored: $50 non-refundable application fee plus $325 tuition if accepted (food, housing and supplies included). Scholarships may be available.
duration: One week; delegates arrive on Father's Day (the 80th session began June 21, 2026)
deadline_text: For the 2026 session (began June 21, 2026) the home page said applications were open through June 7. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school juniors with at least one semester left. Posts pick students with school help, or you can apply on your own as self-sponsored.
how_to_apply: If a post sponsors you, your school staff recommend you. The local American Legion post interviews you. If you sponsor yourself, make an account on the ALJBS CampSite portal. Fill out the questionnaire. Add a 300 to 500 word essay, or a video or a counselor reference. Pay the $50 fee.
notes: Boys only (Jersey Girls State is a separate program). Post-sponsored and self-sponsored costs are in pay_detail.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, New Jersey Wing
org: Civil Air Patrol, New Jersey Wing
city: New Jersey (local squadrons across the state)
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location. Uniform and overnight activity fees are extra. National Headquarters says a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year. Some help is available.
duration: Ongoing. Weekly 2-hour meetings, about one Saturday event a month and a week-long summer encampment (typical, per national page)
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time by visiting a squadron.
who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters can waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Attend at least three squadron meetings.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. You can also ask the squadron about the online application.
notes: No military duty. Cadets can stay in until age 21 and can switch to adult membership at 18. Squadron meetings and costs vary, so ask the squadron near you.

name: Governor's School of New Jersey in Engineering and Technology
org: Rutgers School of Engineering / State of New Jersey
pay_detail: Free to students and families (tuition, room and board paid by donations). FAQ says students bring a $65 key deposit returned at the end. The FAQ page is undated.
duration: About 4 weeks, starting close to the beginning of July, with about 40 hours of prep work beforehand
deadline_text: 2027 application not posted on the pages read. The state page (updated 11/13/25) said 2026 applications were open; decisions are emailed in early April. Ask your school counselor about the school nomination deadline.
who_can_apply: New Jersey residents who have finished their junior year at a public, private or home school. Applicants must be nominated by their high school (one nominee per 325 juniors). It is competitive. Fewer than 25% of nominees get offers.
how_to_apply: Get nominated by your high school, then submit the online application with essays (admission is based heavily on essays). Contact: njgset@soe.rutgers.edu or 848-445-4753.
notes: Residential at Rutgers School of Engineering, 98 Brett Road, Piscataway. The Application Instructions page on the program site still mentions the Summer 2023 application, so rely on the state page and director for 2027 dates.

name: New Jersey Youth Corps
org: New Jersey Department of Labor and Workforce Development
city: New Jersey (local sites across the state)
pay_detail: Corpsmembers get a stipend while enrolled. The amount is not stated on the state page.
duration: Full time, year-round program; length of each cohort is not stated on the state page
deadline_text: No deadline posted. The program is described as year-round.
who_can_apply: Young adults ages 16 to 25 who do not have a high school diploma.
how_to_apply: Send the online services request form on the NJ Department of Labor page for general questions. The state page does not list sign-up steps, so ask for the site that serves your county.
notes: For teens 16 and up who left school without a diploma. Not for students still working toward a diploma in a regular school. It includes help getting a high school equivalency diploma or an adult high school diploma. It includes counseling and help moving on to college or jobs. Paid work for people under 18 in New Jersey needs working papers (online). See permit.html?state=nj for the exact permit and steps.

name: New Jersey Youth Institute (World Food Prize)
org: Rutgers School of Environmental and Biological Sciences, with the World Food Prize Foundation
pay_detail: Free to take part (no registration cost). For students invited to the Global Youth Institute in Des Moines, most expenses are covered by the World Food Prize, but travel is not included.
duration: One day (2026 date: March 6, 2026)
deadline_text: 2026: registration and paper due by February 6, 2026; the Institute was March 6, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 through 12. The page does not list an age rule or a residency rule; it describes students from New Jersey.
how_to_apply: Research a global issue and write a paper with a teacher or mentor, following the guidelines PDF on the page. Register and submit the paper through the World Food Prize website.
notes: The Rutgers page was read through a summarizing fetch tool because the site blocks plain page requests, so check the page itself for the 2027 date. It is listed on the New Jersey 4-H page as a program for high school students.

name: Dual Enrollment (New River Community College)
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.
duration: Semester by semester
deadline_text: The page links to a dual enrollment calendars page. No dates are listed on this page.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors who go to a high school in the NRCC service region. You must meet college placement rules. You need a note of support from a high school official and a signed form from a parent. Strong freshmen and sophomores may be able to join. They need the OK of the high school principal and the college president.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school counselor and use the dual enrollment forms on the NRCC page. The parent signature form is required.
notes: The NRCC page still showed an old campus closure banner, so confirm the details with the college. Cost to students is not stated on the page.

name: New York State 4-H
org: Cornell Cooperative Extension, New York State 4-H
city: New York State (run through county Cornell Cooperative Extension offices)
pay_detail: Fees are not stated on the pages read. Ask your county office.
duration: 4-H year runs October 1 to September 30; you can re-enroll each year
deadline_text: No single deadline. The 4-H year runs October 1 to September 30.
who_can_apply: Youth from kindergarten up to age 19. A kindergartner must turn 5 by January 1 of the 4-H year. A teen cannot enroll or re-enroll if they will turn 19 before January 1 of the new club year (club year runs Oct 1 to Sept 30). Counties can set their own details.
how_to_apply: Contact your county Cornell Cooperative Extension office. Join a club. If you cannot join a club, you can enroll as an independent member. You work on projects at your own pace with an adult helping.
notes: Not a job. The rules are for New York State 4-H as described by two county Cornell Cooperative Extension pages (Jefferson and Erie). The listed URL is the Erie County page. Your own county office has the sign-up steps and costs.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, New York Wing
org: Civil Air Patrol, New York Wing
city: New York (local squadrons across the state)
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location. Uniform and overnight activity fees are extra. National Headquarters says a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year. Some help is available.
duration: Ongoing. Weekly 2-hour meetings, about one Saturday event a month and a week-long summer encampment (typical, per national page)
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time by visiting a squadron.
who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters can waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Attend at least three squadron meetings.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. You can also ask the squadron about the online application.
notes: No military duty. Cadets can stay in until age 21 and can switch to adult membership at 18. Squadron meetings and costs vary, so ask the squadron near you.

name: NYS DEC Summer Camps (Colby, DeBruce, Pack Forest, Rushford)
org: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC)
city: New York State (camps in Franklin County, the Catskills, Allegany County and the southern Adirondacks)
pay_detail: $350 per camper per week, with meals and trips included. Transportation to and from camp is not included. Many campers are sponsored by local conservation groups, clubs and community groups.
duration: One week, Sunday afternoon to Friday afternoon (2026 teen weeks ran July 12 to Aug 7, depending on the camp)
deadline_text: Registration for 2026 opened Sunday March 22, 2026 at 1 PM and weeks fill quickly (waitlist available). 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Youth 14 to 17 can go to the weeks set aside for that age. Campers must be the minimum age by December 1 of the calendar year. The pages do not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Set up a family account in the DEC online registration system. Fill out the camper forms and waivers in the Document Center before registration opens. Then register for a week and pay online. If a week is full, join the waitlist.
notes: This is a camp for campers, not a job. The main camp page still mentions a March 2025 opening, so use the How to Register page for dates. Ask DEC about sponsorships early.

name: American Legion Auxiliary Empire Girls State
org: American Legion Auxiliary, Department of New York
city: New York State (check-in at SUNY Brockport)
pay_detail: A non-refundable application fee is required. The amount is not stated on the pages read. Optional extras (shirts, survival kit) have order forms.
duration: One week: Sunday June 27 to Friday July 2, 2027
deadline_text: 2027 session: Sunday June 27 to Friday July 2, 2027 (from the site's save-the-date notice). No 2027 application deadline or registration opening is posted.
who_can_apply: Girls. Your local American Legion Auxiliary unit picks citizens and alternates, sometimes with interviews, essays or a nomination. The pages read did not list a grade or residency rule, so ask your unit.
how_to_apply: Contact your local American Legion Auxiliary unit. Ask your guidance counselor or email egsregistrar@gmail.com with your hometown, county and school. Join the local selection. Then use the login the unit gives you. Register online and pay the fee.
notes: Girls only. The site says there is a virtual orientation on Zoom in May or June. The program says it is not a sports camp or a recreational camp.

name: New York State Parks Lifeguard
org: New York State Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation (OPRHP)
city: New York State (state parks, pools and beaches; Long Island has its own process)
pay_detail: Paid job. Candidates are in pay status during the mandatory 40 hours of training. The hourly rate is not stated on the page read.
duration: Seasonal; the page says the peak operating season is May through September
deadline_text: No application deadline is posted on the page read. Register for a lifeguard qualifier; the page links the qualifier dates.
who_can_apply: Strong swimmers who meet the age and certification rules. Outside Long Island, the minimum age is 15 for pool posts and 16 for other posts. On Long Island the minimum is 17 (16 for pool posts only). You also need a background check, a medical form and an interview.
how_to_apply: Fill out the lifeguard job application and email it to the address on the page. Then sign up for a qualifier. Long Island has its own preregistration. After you pass, regional staff tell you the next steps.
notes: The minimum age depends on region (see who_can_apply). Confirm your age with the regional office. The New York Department of Labor page returned an access error. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.

name: Newport Beach Public Library Teen Volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 20 hours of service per year. Children's Department shifts are 1 to 2 hours a week. YAAC also meets monthly.
deadline_text: No deadline. Applications are first-come, first-served and accepted as needed.
who_can_apply: Youth volunteers must be in 7th through 12th grade and age 12 to 18. The Young Adult Advisory Council (YAAC) is only for teens who live in Newport Beach.
how_to_apply: Teens fill out the online application themselves on the library's volunteer portal (application form number 2) and lead communication with staff. You must attend volunteer training before starting.
notes: Volunteers age 15 and up must complete fingerprinting and a background check. Applying does not guarantee a spot. Questions go to the library's Teen Services team through the email link on the page.

name: Newport Beach Teen Leader Program
org: City of Newport Beach Recreation and Senior Services
pay_detail: Unpaid. Selected teens pay a $206 program fee for 2026.
duration: The 2026 session; exact length not stated
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed Thursday, May 1, 2026. Next year's dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Submit a Teen Leader Application. Qualified applicants may be interviewed and the top candidates are chosen. Selected teens pass a background check, register online and pay the fee. Contact Recreation and Senior Services at (949) 644-3151.
notes: This is a volunteer role with a fee, not a paid job. The same page lists the Mayor's Youth Council (an unpaid internship that runs October 2026 to August 2027, applications May 15 to Sept 4, 2026), but it does not state an age or grade, so it is not listed as its own card.

name: Marine Teens Internship
org: Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County (NHMLAC)
pay_detail: Interns are paid museum employees. The hourly rate is not stated.
duration: Spring: select Saturdays in April and May (about 10 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.). Summer: six weeks in June and July, 24 hours a week.
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back in February 2027 for the application link and deadline.
who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors who live in or attend high school in Boyle Heights. A work permit and proof of authorization to work in the U.S. are required.
how_to_apply: Online application. The link and deadline are posted on the program page each February.
notes: Narrow: ten spots a year (eight new interns and two returning peer mentors) for Boyle Heights students. Transportation is provided.

name: NISRA Volunteers and Summer Camp Jobs (Elgin and 12 other member communities)
city: Elgin and 12 other member communities, northern Illinois
pay_detail: Volunteering is unpaid. Part-time jobs (1 to 20 hours a week) are paid, but pay is not on the page read.
duration: Program seasons are 6 to 8 weeks. Volunteers are asked to commit for the full season.
deadline_text: No deadline. NISRA says it hires summer camp staff each winter and spring. Postings are on the ADP Workforce Now site.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 15 years old. The page does not list a minimum age for the part-time and camp jobs, so check the posting.
how_to_apply: For jobs, apply on NISRA's ADP Workforce Now site from the Employment page. For volunteering, use the Volunteer Opportunities link on the same page. Call NISRA at 815-459-0737.
notes: The City of Elgin is a member of NISRA. The city says NISRA offers programs at Elgin sites. The 15 week internship is for therapeutic recreation college students. Jobs need a reliable ride. Illinois: the Evanston Township High School work permit page says workers under 16 need a work permit.

name: NIST Summer High School Intern Program (SHIP), Gaithersburg
org: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
grades: High school juniors and seniors when you apply
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page calls it a competitive volunteer program.
duration: Seven weeks, mid-June to early August (2027 dates to be decided)
deadline_text: For 2027, the job announcement is expected to open on USAJOBS in mid-October 2026, and applications are due at the end of January 2027. Another line on the page says applications generally open Nov 1 and close in the last week of January.
who_can_apply: U.S. citizens who are a high school junior or senior at the time of application, with at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA on a 4.0 scale. You must be able to do the full seven weeks and live within 50 miles of the host campus. Families must provide their own housing and transportation.
how_to_apply: Watch for the SHIP job announcement on USAJOBS and follow the application page linked from the SHIP page. The page says to read the application process page for the full steps.
notes: The page lists two NIST campuses (Boulder, CO and Gaithersburg, MD); this card is for Gaithersburg. The 2026 poster session was held in Gaithersburg on Aug 6, 2026. The exact application dates for 2027 were not final on the page read, so check it again in late October.

name: Teen Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: Fall 2026 registration is closed. Registration for January 2027 opportunities opens Dec 17 at 5 p.m.
who_can_apply: Teens in grades 8 to 12. Volunteers who work with the public must pass a criminal background check.
how_to_apply: Fill in the teen volunteer form on the library page when it opens.
notes: Questions: 604-998-3450. The Dec 17 date comes from the Teens' community hub page. Exact roles are not listed on the page read.

name: Become a Lifeguard and Swim Instructor at NVRC
org: North Vancouver Recreation and Culture Commission
pay_detail: Course fees not stated on the pages read. Job pay not stated.
duration: Several courses
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Age minimums by course. Bronze Medallion is 13. First Aid is 15. National Lifeguard is 15. Swim Instructor is 15. Lifesaving Instructor is 16. To apply for a job, you must be a citizen, a permanent resident or have a valid work permit.
how_to_apply: Sign up for courses online. After you are certified, apply on the NVRC job site. Email swim@nvrc.ca with questions.
notes: Courses need 100% attendance. Withdraw 8 or more days before the start for a full refund. The minimum age to be hired is not stated on the pages read.

name: Volunteer with North Vancouver Recreation and Culture (NVRC)
org: North Vancouver Recreation and Culture Commission
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Varies. Early years roles ask for 4 to 6 months.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. Some roles need an older age or certificates (for example Aquatics needs age 15, Bronze Cross and Swim Instructor). Under 18 needs a parent signature.
how_to_apply: There are eight steps. Fill out the online form. Give two references. Sign the volunteer agreement. Get a police check at the RCMP where you live. Sign the photo release. Upload your forms. Go to orientation. Then email volunteer@nvrc.ca.
notes: Contact volunteer@nvrc.ca or 604-983-6345. The police check must be done where you live.

name: Youth Train in Trades (North Vancouver School District)
org: North Vancouver School District 44 with BCIT, VCC and SkilledTradesBC
pay_detail: Tuition covered by the school board
duration: One school year of training
deadline_text: Deadline is the end of February for programs the next school year. Year not stated.
who_can_apply: Domestic students in North Vancouver School District, mainly grade 12. Seats are limited.
how_to_apply: Talk to your school Career Program teacher. If you missed the deadline, email jkinakin@sd44.ca.
notes: The page lists 16 programs.

name: Civic Leadership Institute (CTD Summer Camp)
org: Northwestern University Center for Talent Development
pay_detail: Summer 2026 tuition: $5,530 residential camp or $3,125 day camp. Financial aid for qualified students is given on a rolling basis while funds last.
duration: 3 weeks (June 28 to July 17 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 camp ran June 28 to July 17, 2026. 2027 dates and prices are not posted yet. The program has said to apply early for aid.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. CTD uses levels based on test scores. Or it uses a school record and teacher recommendation. Check the course page and the CTD eligibility page.
how_to_apply: Apply online through MyCTD. For admission, you use test scores or a portfolio. The portfolio is your report card and a teacher recommendation. If you have questions, email ctd-admissions@northwestern.edu.
notes: Costs a lot and is for advanced learners. CTD also has many other summer and weekend courses for grades 6 to 12 that are not listed here.

name: Summer Volunteer Service for Students
org: Northwestern Medicine (Delnor in Geneva, Central DuPage in Winfield, Lake Forest and other suburban hospitals)
city: Geneva, Winfield, Lake Forest and other suburbs, IL
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
duration: One day a week for 8 weeks between May and August
deadline_text: 2027 summer applications are open December 1, 2026 to January 15, 2027. The 2026 summer period is closed.
who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16 years old. For Northwestern Memorial Hospital the age is 18, and it has no summer program. You must pass a health screening and an interview. You must also go to a virtual orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application during the window. Then do an interview. Onboarding includes a health screening and an orientation. Ages 18 and up also get a background check.
notes: Volunteer offices: Delnor, 630-938-2180. Central DuPage, 630-933-6207. Lake Forest, 847-535-6851. Call the one near you.

name: Medill Cherubs Journalism Institute
org: Northwestern University, Medill School of Journalism
grades: Current high school juniors (rising seniors), no exceptions
pay_detail: Tuition $5,000 including room and board. Up to $100,000 in financial aid and scholarships is available. $55 application fee.
duration: 4 weeks (June 27 to July 23, 2027)
deadline_text: No applications before December 1, 2026. All materials are due by noon Central on March 1, 2027. Decisions by March 24, 2027.
who_can_apply: Current high school juniors who will be seniors in fall 2027. The page says no exceptions.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form, write a 200 to 225 word essay, list your journalism activities and send up to three work samples. Pay the $55 fee. Your counselor emails your transcript, GPA and school profile to Prof. Roger Boye. Add the financial aid form and a parent tax return if you want aid.
notes: Questions: r-boye@northwestern.edu (email is best) or (847) 491-2069.

name: National High School Institute (Cherubs): Policy Debate Institute
pay_detail: 2026 tuition: $3,500 for the 4 week institute, $5,000 for the 6 week institute. $60 application fee.
duration: 4 or 6 weeks
deadline_text: Summer 2027 application opens this winter. Rolling admission through April or until the labs are full. 2026 dates were June 28 to July 25 (4 weeks) and June 28 to August 8 (6 weeks).
who_can_apply: Students rising into grades 9 to 12 the summer they attend. The page asks for a class rank near the top 30 percent and experience or interest in policy debate.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with the $60 fee. Then send extra materials such as a debate record, a letter of recommendation and your transcript. You need a laptop with a webcam, a mic and Microsoft Word.
notes: The 2026 program was online only. Check whether 2027 is online or on campus. Financial aid and scholarship page exists on the NHSI site but was not read.

name: National High School Institute (Cherubs): Film and Video Division
pay_detail: 2026 tuition was $8,000 (includes room and board for 5 weeks). Need-based financial aid is available. $60 application fee, which can be waived for families with financial need.
duration: 5 weeks
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: early deadline January 9, 2026 and regular deadline March 13, 2026, with rolling late applications for some concentrations. 2027 dates are not posted yet. The home page says applications open in November.
who_can_apply: Students in their sophomore or junior year who will be rising juniors or seniors. The page asks for a class rank in or near the top 30 percent. It also asks for proof of special skill or strong interest in media arts.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with the $60 fee. Then send extra materials. These may include two essays, a resume, a letter of recommendation, test scores and your transcript.
notes: Competitive and costly. Travel is not included. Aid is need-based only. Not a paid program.

name: National High School Institute (Cherubs): Theatre Arts Division
pay_detail: 2026 tuition was $8,000 (includes room and board for 5 weeks). Need-based financial aid is available. $60 application fee, which can be waived for families with financial need.
duration: 5 weeks
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: early deadline January 2, 2026 and regular deadline February 27, 2026 (online form). 2027 dates are not posted yet. The home page says applications open in November.
who_can_apply: Students in 10th or 11th grade who will be rising juniors or seniors. Juniors get priority. The page asks for a class rank near the top 30 percent and some theatre experience or strong interest.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with the $60 fee. Then send a resume, two essays, a letter of recommendation and your transcript. Test scores are optional. The Musical Theatre track needs a third essay.
notes: Competitive and costs a lot, but the program says need-based aid is given and does not offer merit aid. Travel is not included. Not a paid program.

name: Waterpark seasonal jobs with free training
org: NOVA Parks (Northern Virginia Regional Park Authority)
city: Northern Virginia (Fairfax, Alexandria and Arlington waterparks)
pay_detail: Pay rates not stated on the page. Free uniforms and free training.
duration: Seasonal (summer)
deadline_text: Page says NOVA Parks is hiring; no deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Attendants must be at least 14, lifeguards at least 15, cooks at least 16.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Apply Now' link under the position on the Waterpark Employment page (current listings: lifeguard at Atlantis and Pirate's Cove, water safety instructor at Great Waves and Ocean Dunes).
notes: Atlantis is at Bull Run and Pirate's Cove at Pohick Bay (Fairfax County); Great Waves is in Alexandria and Ocean Dunes is at Upton Hill in Arlington. Virginia rule (Virginia Department of Labor and Industry): 14 and 15 year olds need an Employment Certificate before working; the page read does not list a certificate for 16 and 17 year olds.

name: NOVAworks Young Adult Services
city: Sunnyvale, CA (serves San Mateo County and northern Santa Clara County)
pay_detail: Coaching is free. Paid internships start at $19.50 per hour (Sunnyvale minimum wage), at least $7,800 for 400 hours. Internships are for ages 18 and up.
duration: 4 to 5 weeks of career readiness first, then an internship (most interns work 10 to 20 hours a week)
deadline_text: Open enrollment. No deadline posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24 who live in San Mateo County or Cupertino, Los Altos, Milpitas, Mountain View, Palo Alto, Santa Clara or Sunnyvale. High school students who live outside the area qualify if their school is inside it. In-school youth 17 to 21 need low household income plus justice involvement, unstable housing or foster care.
how_to_apply: Fill out the short interest form on the NOVAworks Young Adults page, then meet a Career Advisor. You can also email youngadults@novaworks.org, call 408-730-7640 or text 408-568-7776.
notes: Narrow eligibility. The FAQ says internships are 18 and up, so a 17 year old gets coaching and training first. Teens under 17 do not qualify. Most applicants need a documented barrier and income under the program limits.

name: National Park Service Youth Conservation Corps (YCC)
city: Participating national parks (see the NPS park list)
pay_detail: At least the higher of the state or federal minimum wage, usually for a 40 hour week
duration: 8 to 10 weeks (can go up to 18), usually 40 hours per week
deadline_text: Applications for the 2027 season open in late January or early February 2027. Closing dates are set by each park and are not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18, permanent US residents, and able to commute daily. Nearly all sites are day programs with no housing.
how_to_apply: Check the NPS YCC page in late January or early February 2027 for the park list and contacts, then apply to the park you want.
notes: Applications are closed right now. Each park runs its own program, so check whether a park near you takes part. Contact the national office through the link on the NPS page with general questions.

name: ACE Mentor Program of Greater New York
org: ACE Mentor Program of Greater NY
city: Teams in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, Long Island, White Plains and Riverdale (and remote)
pay_detail: Free. No pay is mentioned. Scholarship and internship chances are listed as benefits.
duration: Late October through May (about 2 hours after school per meeting). Some teams start in January.
deadline_text: Team selection emails start in September. The page gives no registration dates and no closing date, and does not say whether registration is open now.
who_can_apply: Any high school student in grades 9 to 12. No experience is needed. No grades, essays or recommendation letters are needed. A parent consent form is needed.
how_to_apply: Register on the ACE GNY website. Use the yellow button on the students page. Get a parent to sign a consent form. Pick a team from the map you get by email. Then wait for a confirmation email.
notes: Teams meet at host firms or universities. The page also links to a Summer Internship Program for alumni, which this card does not cover.

name: Arts & Entertainment Production Internship (Apollo Theater Academy)
pay_detail: $17.00 per hour
duration: The 2026 internship ran Apr 21 to May 21, 2026, on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays 3 to 6 PM. The page calls it six weeks in one place and eight or ten weeks in others.
deadline_text: The spring 2026 application closed Friday, Mar 27, 2026. The next cycle is not posted. Check the Apollo page for the next cycle.
who_can_apply: High school seniors (12th grade) who live in one of the five boroughs. You must send a current transcript or report card that shows 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application form linked on the Apollo page. It includes an essay, a transcript or report card, and recommendations. All are due by the deadline. Late or incomplete applications are not read.
notes: The FAQ says accepted interns under 18 must give the Apollo a copy of their New York State working papers before orientation. Ask your school guidance counselor how to get working papers. The Apollo also runs a paid technical theater internship in the summer. The page text about length is not the same in two places. Confirm with the Apollo.

name: Technical Stage Production Internship (Apollo Theater Academy)
pay_detail: $17 per hour
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Friday, on site. The 2026 program ran July 13 to Aug 21, 2026.
deadline_text: The 2026 application closed June 26, 2026. Interviews were June 30 and July 1. The 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising seniors going into 12th grade in September who live in the five boroughs of New York City. You like technical theater. You must come to the full program and a parent or guardian orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on Formstack before the deadline. The page says group interviews happen by appointment. Accepted teens and a parent or guardian go to an orientation on the first day.
notes: The Apollo Arts Administration internship page says interns under 18 must show New York State working papers. This technical internship page does not say so. Expect to need them for a paid job.

name: Garden Apprentice Program (GAP)
pay_detail: Tier 1 $600, Tier 2 $700, Tier 3 $800 as a one-time nontaxable reimbursement in November, plus a $75 perfect attendance bonus. Tier 4 (by invitation after Tier 3) is a part-time staff job at $17 per hour. No fee to join.
duration: 9 months, March to November 2027 (about 4 to 6 hours a week in spring and fall, 20 to 25 hours a week in summer; about 190 to 220 hours total).
deadline_text: Submit your materials before Dec 4, 2026 to be invited to an interview. No final deadline is posted. Info session Sat Oct 17, 2026, 11 a.m. to 1 p.m.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 11 who start in Tier 1 (9th grade), Tier 2 (10th grade or Tier 1 done) or Tier 3 (11th grade or Tier 2 done). No age or borough rule is stated. You do not have to share immigration status for Tiers 1 to 3.
how_to_apply: Apply online (account lets you save progress): short answers plus references, then a group interview. Apprentices must reapply every year. Two references use a separate online reference form.
notes: Tiers 1 to 3 are not employees. Tier 4 apprentices must be legally authorized to work and eligible under NYC Department of Labor rules, per the program page. Partial participation is not allowed. Questions: gap@bbg.org (shown on the page) or 718-623-7252.

name: Upward Bound Math & Science
org: Bronx Community College (CUNY), Federal TRIO program
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the pages read. The pages do not list a cost.
duration: Academic year: 21 Saturdays from September to April, 10 AM to 2 PM plus STEM labs 2:30 to 4:30 PM. Summer: six weeks, with three weeks as a commuter at BCC and three weeks at a residential site.
deadline_text: No application dates are posted on the pages read.
who_can_apply: High school students who are U.S. citizens, permanent residents or in the U.S. for other than a temporary purpose, from a low-income household and/or first in the family to go to college. About 60 students are served each year.
how_to_apply: The Program Overview page says to click its apply link (a short link). Phone: 718-289-5855. Ask the program about this year's dates.
notes: The page says low-income means family taxable income at or below 150 percent of the poverty level. Two thirds of participants must be both low-income and first generation. One third must be one or the other. After-school tutoring runs 4:30 to 7 PM on weekdays when the host school does not offer it.

name: Teen Council and Teen Summer
org: The Bronx Museum of the Arts
pay_detail: Teens are paid a stipend. The amount is not stated on the pages.
duration: Teen Council: two four-month sessions a year (fall and spring), twice a week after school. Fall 2026 runs late October 2026 to mid-February 2027, Mondays and Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:30 PM. Teen Summer: four weeks, three afternoons a week.
deadline_text: The Fall 2026 application closed Oct 4, 2026. The spring and summer 2027 dates are not posted yet. The page says teens can apply for fall, spring and/or summer sessions each year.
who_can_apply: New York City high school students ages 14 to 19. Twelve students are chosen for each session. The page encourages you to apply again if you were not accepted before.
how_to_apply: Fill out the free online application on the Bronx Museum event page for the session. Educators read the applications and pick 12 students. If you have questions, write to education@bronxmuseum.org.
notes: The fall 2026 application form is closed, so no apply link is listed here. Check the Teen Programs page for the next one. The museum is under renovation but stays open Wednesday to Sunday, 11 AM to 6 PM, at 1040 Grand Concourse. The pages do not say whether a work permit is needed.

name: Brooklyn Interns for Arts and Culture (BIAC)
pay_detail: The page says the internship is paid. The amount is not stated.
duration: One year in 3 sessions: one week in August (Mon to Fri, 11 a.m. to 3 p.m.), October to December, and February to June (1 to 2 days a week, 4 to 6 p.m.). The 2026-27 cohort runs Aug 2026 to Jun 2027.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application closed Friday, June 12, 2026. The next deadline is not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising seniors at a high school in any of the five boroughs. You need an interest in the arts, a GPA of 2.0 or higher, and an unofficial transcript.
how_to_apply: Use the Enroll button on the BAM BIAC page, which links to an online form. The page lists the Education Program Manager for questions. Include an unofficial high school transcript.
notes: Only 13 spots. After the program, BAM Education alumni ages 18 to 24 can join a separate paid Creative Career Collective (virtual, Oct to Dec). Pay amount and work-permit rules are not on the page.

name: Youth Advisory Council
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.
duration: Throughout the school year, 2 meetings a month.
deadline_text: The page says applications typically open at the end of the school year. Exact dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Students going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade in New York City public schools.
how_to_apply: The page does not give steps. It says applications usually open at the end of the school year. Check the Youth Advisory Council page or ask the Borough President's office.
notes: The council is run with the Brooklyn North and Brooklyn South high school superintendents and Sadie Nash Leadership Project. The page does not say whether members are paid or where teens must live, so ask the office.

name: BRIC Teen Filmmaking Bootcamp
pay_detail: Free class with a $200 stipend if you attend every session.
duration: 8 sessions, 16 hours. Fall 2026: Tuesdays Oct 13 to Dec 8, 4 to 6 p.m.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 (Cycle 9) applications closed Sept 27, 2026. New cycles open through the year.
who_can_apply: High schoolers ages 14 to 18 who live in Brooklyn. BRIC picks students from groups with less access to media training.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the class page. Attending every class is required to get the stipend.
notes: The class page says students under 18 need working papers from their school. Finishing the program makes you eligible for other paid BRIC work, per the page. The page says eight sessions but lists nine Tuesdays, and gives Dec 9 in one place and Dec 8 in another, so confirm the last date.

name: BRIC Teen Media and Teen Curatorial Fellowships
pay_detail: $17 per hour for 2 hours a week, paid every two weeks, based on attendance.
duration: 2026-27 school year. Curatorial meets Wednesdays 4 to 6 p.m. Media meets Thursdays 4 to 6 p.m. In person at BRIC.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 application deadline was Sept 24, 2026 (extended). Offers were due by Sept 30, 2026. The next call is not posted.
who_can_apply: NYC high school age teens. You can apply to only one of the two fellowships. The current page does not list exact ages; the 2023-24 page said NYC sophomores, juniors or seniors, or ages 15 to 19.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. You cannot edit it after you submit. Then you have a virtual interview. After that you get an offer and steps to start.
notes: Pay is called a stipend on the page. Working papers are not mentioned for the fellowships, but BRIC requires them for its bootcamps for under 18, so ask. BRIC also accepts youth under 21 for its film festival.

name: Capture Your World: BRIC Teen Photography Bootcamp
pay_detail: Free class with a $200 stipend if you attend every session.
duration: 8 sessions, 16 hours. Fall 2026: Mondays Oct 5 to Nov 30, 4 to 6 p.m. (no class Oct 12). Exhibition Thu, Dec 10, 5 to 7 p.m.
deadline_text: Cycle 4 applications closed Sept 27, 2026. New cycles open through the year.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. Beginners are welcome. You must attend every session; if you miss the first day your spot goes to the waitlist.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the class page.
notes: The class page says students under 18 need working papers from their school. Class is at Clarendon Library in Brooklyn, not at BRIC House. The page text says Mondays but its class-times list shows Thursdays (Oct 8 to Nov 26), so confirm the weekday.

name: Green Team and Coastal Cleanup Volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering.
duration: Green Team: twice a month on Saturdays, 10 a.m. to noon, April to October. Coastal Cleanups: about 2 hours each, now and then from April to October. Sign up for as many as you like.
deadline_text: No deadline. Sign up for each event. Most activities run April to October. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: All ages can join. Teens under 16 must be with a parent or guardian the whole time, so teens 16 and up can volunteer on their own. Event volunteer roles are usually 18 and up.
how_to_apply: Make a Volunteer Profile with the Volgistics link on the park's volunteer page. Then pick events.
notes: Coastal Cleanup is best suited for ages 10 and up. Tasks happen outdoors on uneven ground. Ask staff about accommodations.

name: Summer Scholars Internship
org: Center for Brooklyn History (Brooklyn Public Library)
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page. Ask CBH Education whether there is a stipend.
duration: Summer. The 2026 program had a final reception; exact weeks and hours are not stated.
deadline_text: The page says applications for the 2026 program are closed. The 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising 10th, 11th and 12th graders who live in Brooklyn or go to school in Brooklyn. A strong interest in Brooklyn's past.
how_to_apply: The page does not give steps. It says the 2026 application is closed. Questions: CBHEducation@bklynlibrary.org.
notes: Confirm first: pay, exact dates and application steps are not on the page we read (it showed the 2026 application as closed). Ask CBH Education whether it is paid.

name: Groundswell Studio Programs (free after-school art and social justice)
pay_detail: Free. No pay is mentioned for the studio classes.
duration: The 2025-26 session ran Oct 27 to Mar 12, with one class a week (afternoons, about 2 to 2.5 hours).
deadline_text: Last year (2025-26) open enrollment ended Nov 3, 2025, taken on a rolling basis. The 2026-27 dates were not posted on the page we read.
who_can_apply: Youth from across New York City. Most classes are ages 14 to 19; the Advanced Portfolio class is ages 16 to 24. You do not need to be an artist.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the Studio Programs page. Questions: Phoebe@groundswell.nyc or Brandon@groundswell.nyc (shown on the page), or call 718-254-9782.
notes: The page we read described the 2025-26 school year, so check the page for the 2026-27 session. Classes are at the Gowanus studio, in person.

name: Summer Leadership Institute (paid mural apprentices)
city: Brooklyn, NY (murals across New York City)
pay_detail: The page says youth get stipends and calls it a summer jobs program. The amount is not stated.
duration: July to August
deadline_text: No application dates are posted on the program page.
who_can_apply: Youth. Ages, grades and how to join are not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the program page. Contact Groundswell: Office@groundswell.nyc or 718-254-9782 (shown on the site), or check the Youth section for application news.
notes: Confirm first. The page does not list ages, pay amount or how to apply. It says murals are made throughout New York City, and one project title mentions Queensbridge House.

name: Health Scholars Program (Emergency Department internship)
pay_detail: Unpaid. You get a certificate of completion from the hospital.
duration: Three rotation blocks a year: Dec 11 to Mar 10, Mar 11 to May 31, and Jun 1 to Sep 2.
deadline_text: Deadline to send all materials for each block (year not printed on the page): Block 1 (Dec 11 to Mar 10) by Oct 31; Block 2 (Mar 11 to May 31) by Feb 1; Block 3 (Jun 1 to Sep 2) by Apr 30.
who_can_apply: High school students in 11th or 12th grade, and college students, who like health careers. You must also be processed as a hospital volunteer. That means a form, a medical packet, an in-person interview and a 3-hour orientation.
how_to_apply: Send the intern application and the under-18 release form. Add a short essay (500 words max) on why you want it. Add proof of vaccination (COVID and flu) and two short recommendation letters. Then you have a 15 to 20 minute virtual interview. Questions: Volunteer@maimo.org or 718-283-3980.
notes: Unpaid, so no work permit. Students under 18 may only volunteer 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday to Friday, per the page. Check the page for the year of each deadline.

name: High School Volunteer Programs
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get a cafeteria meal voucher and discounted parking. A recommendation letter is offered after at least 150 hours.
duration: At least two 4-hour shifts a week. In the school year, volunteers under 18 must give at least 6 hours per workweek.
deadline_text: The page does not state a deadline or whether applications are open now.
who_can_apply: High school students. The page says volunteers range in age from 14 to 90 but does not state a minimum teen age. All volunteers need medical clearance, references, an interview, a background check and orientation.
how_to_apply: Download the High School Student Application Packet from the volunteer page. Email it to Volunteer@maimo.org. Or mail it to Department of Volunteer and Student Services, 5014 Fort Hamilton Parkway, Brooklyn, NY 11219. Phone 718-283-3980. They send medical clearance forms after they get your application.
notes: Students under 18 may not volunteer outside 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday. The page says volunteering does not lead to a paid job at Maimonides. Some programs (Feeders, Summer Youth) go through partner schools.

name: Science Scholars Program (summer surgery internship)
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.
duration: 4 weeks. The 2026 session ran Mon, July 6 to Fri, July 31, 2026.
deadline_text: 2026 application deadline was March 26, 2026. Interviews were the third week of April and decisions by end of April. The 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students entering their senior year. Strong essay needed. You must be free Monday to Friday for all four weeks with no vacation or summer classes.
