notes: The page describes youth activism and does not mention a work permit. The page lists meetings on the last Friday of each month from 4:30 to 6 PM, and says meetings are hybrid. Confirm before you go.

name: NYC Votes Youth Ambassador Program
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the pages read. Ask the program.
duration: Weekly meetings, with weekly summer trips. The full length of the program is not stated.
deadline_text: The Youth page says applications for 2026 are now closed. No 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: New Yorkers ages 14 to 18. The program page does not list other rules.
how_to_apply: Check the NYC Votes Youth Ambassadors page for the next call for applications.
notes: Run by the City of New York Campaign Finance Board. Past ambassadors registered voters at public events and with other city agencies. The pages do not say whether the work is paid or needs a work permit.

name: Art, Community, Education and Science (ACES) Internship
pay_detail: $17 per hour
duration: 13 months, about 4 to 8 hours each weekend (14 at most), plus two Saturday workshops a month and July weekday training
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back next winter for 2027 internships. No 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Enrolled in high school, 15 years old by July 1 of the program year, eligible to work in the United States. You must be free on weekends and for the full 13 months (June to June). The 2026 page said June 2026 to June 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply to Wave Hill when applications reopen. Watch the ACES page for news. If you have questions, write to education@wavehill.org or youthprograms@wavehill.org.
notes: Wave Hill House, where this program meets, is wheelchair accessible. Interns travel off site for some field trips.

name: Forest Project
pay_detail: About $2,275 for the summer, paid through the NYC Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP). You also get credit for one college course.
duration: One summer (exact weeks not stated on the page)
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back next winter for 2027 internships. No 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Enrolled in high school, 16 years old by May 1 of the program year, a New York City resident eligible to work in the United States. The 2026 page asked for May 1, 2026.
how_to_apply: Apply to Wave Hill when applications reopen (watch the Forest Project page). Pay runs through SYEP, so you also need a separate SYEP application; for 2026 that was due before March 1. Wave Hill tells interviewed teens which SYEP provider to pick. Questions: youthprograms@wavehill.org.
notes: Fieldwork is hard physical work outdoors with heavy tools on unpaved ground. The Ecology Building has 28 stairs and is not wheelchair accessible. You must be ready to join all of the program.

name: Woodland Ecology Research Mentorship (WERM)
pay_detail: About $3,500 paid across the whole program, plus credit for three college courses.
duration: 14 months: first summer (July to August), school year (September to June), second summer (July to August)
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back next winter for 2027 internships. No 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Enrolled in high school, 15 years old by July 1 of the program year, a New York City resident eligible to work in the United States. The 2026 page asked for July 1, 2026. You must be free for all 14 months.
how_to_apply: Apply to Wave Hill when applications reopen (watch the WERM page). Questions: youthprograms@wavehill.org.
notes: Courses are taught at Wave Hill and the University of Mount Saint Vincent. Fieldwork is outdoors on rough ground with heavy tools. The Ecology Building is not open to wheelchairs. The page names partners such as the American Museum of Natural History.

name: Discovery Guide Youth Volunteer Program
org: Wildlife Conservation Society (Bronx Zoo, Central Park, Prospect Park and Queens Zoos, New York Aquarium)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. WCS says youth volunteers earn over 100 hours of community service.
duration: Usually a spring session and a summer session; hours not stated.
deadline_text: Not accepting applications now. Applications for the next cycle open in late December 2026 for Spring 2027. No closing date posted.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 22 at any of the five WCS parks. No borough rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form to be told when recruitment opens. Questions go to the park's volunteer email (discoveryguide@wcs.org for the Bronx Zoo).
notes: The apply link is the interest form, not the application. WCS also lists 30+ internships and paid jobs for ages 14 to 24 (WCS Career Lattice) and the Youth JIVE job and volunteer expo in early February. Those pages did not state ages or dates for individual internships, so only this program is listed.

name: Youth Insights (YI Artists, Arts Careers, Introductions, Leaders)
grades: Grades 9 to 12 (varies by program; YI Leaders is grades 11 and 12)
pay_detail: YI Leaders is a paid internship; the page does not state the amount.
duration: YI Artists: one semester after school. Summer programs: length not stated. YI Leaders: yearlong, 3 to 10 hours a week.
deadline_text: YI Artists (this semester) deadline was Sep 9, 2026 (extended). YI Arts Careers and YI Introductions list no 2026 deadline and reopen in Summer 2027. No YI Leaders deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: NYC high school students. YI Artists: grades 9 to 12. YI Arts Careers: entering grades 10 to 12. YI Introductions: entering grades 10 to 12 who are English Language Learners. YI Leaders: grades 11 to 12 who finished at least one semester of YI Artists or YI Arts Careers.
how_to_apply: Online form for each program (links on the Youth Insights page). YI Leaders is for teens who have already done another Youth Insights program.
notes: The page's closing note also lists YI Introductions graduates as eligible for Leaders. That conflicts with its Open to line. The page lists no program contact. Use whitney.org/contact. The Whitney also runs a separate Open Studio for Teens (free).

name: Career and Technical Education (CTE) high schools
pay_detail: Part of the school day at no cost. Some work-based learning (such as apprenticeships) can be paid, but pay is not stated on this page.
duration: Grades 9 to 12
deadline_text: Enroll through the regular NYC high school admissions process. Dates are not stated on the CTE page.
who_can_apply: NYC public high school students at one of the 130+ schools with CTE programs. Students who finish a state-approved program can earn a CTE endorsement on their diploma.
how_to_apply: Browse programs on NYC MySchools. Talk to your guidance counselor or a Family Welcome Center about admissions and enrollment.
notes: This is a school choice, not a job. Ask your guidance counselor or a Family Welcome Center how enrollment works for your grade. The CTE endorsement needs 44 credits, 5 Regents exams, a technical assessment and work-based learning.

name: Career Readiness and Modern Youth Apprenticeship (CRMYA)
org: NYC Public Schools with CareerWise New York
pay_detail: Paid work experience. Pay rate is not stated on the page.
duration: 2 to 3 year apprenticeship starting junior year
deadline_text: Dates are not stated. Juniors apply during the school year; ask your school.
who_can_apply: Students at participating NYC public high schools. Juniors apply for the apprenticeship.
how_to_apply: Ask your school if it participates. Juniors apply for apprenticeships through the program. The page does not list an application link.
notes: Only at participating schools; the page does not list which ones. Apprentices attend school mornings Monday to Thursday and all day Friday, and work Monday to Thursday afternoons. Apprenticeships are registered with the NYS Department of Labor. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.

name: Leading Edge Teen Advisory Board (LETAB)
pay_detail: No pay is mentioned on the page. It does not say if service hours are given.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No dates are posted. The page has an Apply now button.
who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12, per the page. The page does not list residency rules.
how_to_apply: Complete the application on the LETAB page. Questions: mhs@oppl.org.
notes: The page has an Apply now button and says questions go to mhs@oppl.org. It does not give dates.

name: Acorns to Oaks Volunteer Team (teens 14 and up)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get rewards for their hours.
duration: Event and program based
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: The page says boys and girls at least 14 years old are invited to learn new skills and gain work experience.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer form and waiver on the volunteer page. Volunteers also go through a criminal background check.
notes: The page says the volunteer background check applies to volunteers. Ask whether it applies to under 18.

name: Summer and Seasonal Park District Jobs
pay_detail: Pay is listed on the job postings, not on the main jobs page.
duration: Seasonal, with set start and end dates
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the jobs page. Applications are kept for one year, then you must reapply.
who_can_apply: Open to job seekers. The page does not list minimum ages. Check the age on each job posting.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online job form. You can upload a resume and cover letter. Hiring supervisors review it. The district cannot talk about forms with anyone but the person who applied.
notes: The page does not say when seasonal hiring opens. Check it in winter. Inclusion partner jobs are handled by WSSRA, a partner group. Illinois: the Evanston Township High School work permit page says workers under 16 need a work permit (employment certificate) before starting.

name: Mayor's Summer Youth Employment Program (MSYEP)
org: City of Oakland, Oakland Workforce Development Board, and partner nonprofits
pay_detail: At least Oakland's minimum wage; exact rate set by each partner
duration: Up to 100 paid hours (varies by partner)
deadline_text: Deadlines vary by partner. For Summer 2026 one partner (ACOE) closed recruitment June 18, 2026. 2027 dates not posted; check partner sites in early 2027.
who_can_apply: Must live in Oakland. No work experience needed. Free. Partner groups set their own ages (for example YEP 14 to 18, Youth UpRising 14 to 21, Lao Family 16 to 21).
how_to_apply: Pick a partner from the City list (YEP, Youth UpRising, Lao Family, Trybe, Rising Sun, Destiny Arts, Soccer Without Borders, YouthBeat, Alameda County Office of Education GCGI-GET) and apply on that group's site or by phone.
notes: City Council approved more than $3.1 million for 2026 and 2027 summer youth jobs, so a 2027 round is expected. Another City page lists ages 16 to 21, so check each partner's own age rule. Under-18 workers need a work permit (OUSD Linked Learning can help OUSD students).

name: Oakland Workforce Development Board Youth Summer Jobs (Lao Family, YEP, Trybe)
org: Oakland Workforce Development Board (City of Oakland)
pay_detail: Not stated on this page; the City's MSYEP page says at least Oakland's minimum wage
deadline_text: No dates posted. Contact the partners for the current cycle.
who_can_apply: Oakland youth ages 16 to 21, per this City page.
how_to_apply: Contact Lao Family Community Development (510) 533-8850, Youth Employment Partnership (510) 533-3447, or Trybe (510) 985-9915. OWDB email: OWDB@oaklandca.gov.
notes: This City page is older than the MSYEP page (which lists partners with other ages, such as YEP 14 to 18 and Lao Family 16 to 21). Treat 16 to 21 as the safe range and confirm with the partner.

name: Oakland Parks, Recreation and Youth Development (OPRYD) Part-Time Jobs
pay_detail: Not posted on the page; see each job posting
duration: Varies by posting; mostly seasonal
deadline_text: Deadline Oct 25, 2026 for Spring/Summer 2027 starts; Feb 7, 2027 for Summer 2027 starts; Aug 8, 2027 for Fall/Winter 2027 starts.
who_can_apply: Open recruitment for the City's recreation jobs; the page does not state a minimum age (lifeguards and many City jobs need 16 or older). Spanish, Cantonese and Mandarin skills are encouraged.
how_to_apply: Apply at governmentjobs.com/careers/oaklandca. Questions: parksandrec@oaklandca.gov, (510) 238-7275.
notes: The hiring process takes several months, so apply early. Check each posting for minimum age and pay. The governmentjobs.com/careers/oaklandca portal showed 0 openings on Oct 7, 2026. If you cannot find the posting, call (510) 238-7275.

name: Oakland Public Library Teen Advisory Board (TAB)
duration: One meeting a month
deadline_text: Rolling
who_can_apply: Teens who join through the library teen volunteer application: ages 13 to 17, or 18 and still in high school. The TAB page itself states no age rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application and choose 'leadership', or ask your branch teen librarian.
notes: Meets monthly at Main (TeenZone), 81st Ave, Asian, Cesar Chavez, Dimond and Rockridge. The same page also covers the Oakland Youth Poet Laureate program.

name: Oakland Public Library Teen Volunteer Program
duration: Shifts when the library is open; the form asks for morning and afternoon or evening availability, any day of the week
deadline_text: Rolling. Not every branch has space at all times.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 17, or 18 and still in high school. Also takes teens with court-ordered service hours.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen Volunteer Application, or stop by a branch.
notes: The library cannot promise a spot at a specific branch. About two thirds of library volunteers are teens, per the page.

name: Teen Summer Internship (California Trail Interpretation)
pay_detail: $50 non-refundable fee when selected (aid available). No stipend is listed.
duration: About 200 hours over 7 weeks (June 10 to July 28 or Aug 1 in 2026); shifts 9 am to 4:30 pm, Sunday to Wednesday or Wednesday to Saturday
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Students entering 11th or 12th grade interested in animal care or environmental education.
how_to_apply: Online form with a cover letter (500 words max) and resume or transcript, then an interview.
notes: Up to 6 interns, so it is likely competitive. No stipend is listed; ask. Financial aid is available for the $50 fee.

name: Teen Wild Guides
pay_detail: $50 first year, then $25 a year; financial aid on request
duration: School year: every other weekend. Summer: about once a week. Shifts 9:30 am to 4 pm.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 info meetings Aug 15 and 16, applications due Sept 1, 2026, trainings Sept 26 and Oct 4. The page says applications are accepted year-round and later ones are reviewed in the next enrollment period.
who_can_apply: Must be 13 or turning 13 in the application season. Zoo page lists grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application, interview, then attend both mandatory training days.
notes: Unpaid, and teens pay a small fee (aid available). Must be 13 or turn 13 in the application season.

name: ZooCamp Teen Assistant and Teen Interns
pay_detail: Teen Assistant unpaid (community service hours). Interns: $400 per week stipend, assuming full attendance.
duration: 1-week sessions, Mon to Fri, June 1 to Aug 7 (2026); at least 3 sessions (Administrative Intern: 3 sessions in a row)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened Feb 1 and closed April 1, 2026 at 5pm. Summer 2027 dates not posted yet; the page says to check back.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 for Teen Assistant (no experience needed). Paid Teacher and Administrative Intern roles are for grades 11 to 12 with previous camp experience and one letter of recommendation. All roles need at least 3 one-week sessions.
how_to_apply: Each role has its own online application (Volgistics link on the Oakland Zoo page). Interns also need one recommendation letter. A required training day is held in May.
notes: Great first step: be a Teen Assistant, then apply to be a paid intern. The 2026 info meetings were in March and the 2026 training was Sunday May 17; expect similar timing for 2027.

name: OC Fair & Event Center Jobs (annual OC Fair)
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the page
duration: The OC Fair runs for a few weeks in summer. Fairgrounds also hosts 150+ events a year.
deadline_text: No hiring dates posted on the jobs page for 2027.
who_can_apply: You must be at least 16 to work at the annual OC Fair. Some jobs require 18 or older. Applicants 17 and under must provide a valid work permit, available through their school, unless they have already graduated from high school. You must show documents proving identity and work eligibility in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Read the Fair's jobs page, then contact Human Resources at (714) 708-1563 or humanresources@ocfair.com. The page lists no application link.
notes: The page does not describe an application link or a pay rate, so call or email HR to ask when summer 2027 hiring opens. Applicants 18 and older must pass a background screening.

name: OC Public Libraries Teen Volunteer
city: Orange County, CA (any OC Public Libraries branch)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Flexible shifts, set by the branch
deadline_text: No deadline. Openings are limited and depend on each branch.
who_can_apply: Teens are typically 12 to 17, but each branch sets its own age range, so check with your local branch. Court-ordered community service is not offered.
how_to_apply: Contact your local branch to confirm there is an opening. Once a spot is confirmed, fill out the OCCR Volunteer Registration Form, print it, and drop it off at the branch.
notes: The registration form is shared by several county agencies, so some questions may not apply to you. Ask your branch what it needs. Arrive on time and tell the branch as early as you can if you miss a shift. OC Public Libraries points teens who need court-ordered hours to the OneOC Court Referral Program.

name: OC Workforce Development Board READY S.E.T. OC (WIOA Young Adult Program)
pay_detail: Work experience can be paid or unpaid. Wage not stated on the page.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Start by filling out the interest form.
who_can_apply: In-school young adults ages 14 to 21 who are low income (free or reduced-price lunch counts) and have at least one barrier: basic skills deficient or English learner, offender, homeless/runaway/foster, pregnant or parenting, or disabled. Out-of-school youth ages 16 to 24 who are not in school (adult education is allowed) and have a barrier such as dropout, offender, homeless/runaway/foster, pregnant or parenting, or disabled.
how_to_apply: Fill out the READY S.E.T. OC interest form (Interest and Eligibility Assessment) linked on the page. Services are delivered by a network of regional providers, which the page does not name.
notes: Federal WIOA program, so eligibility rules apply (income and barriers). Cost to the student is not stated on the page. Questions: County Directory Assistance 855-886-5400. Many teens will not qualify, so read the eligibility list first.

name: Ohio 4-H clubs and projects
org: Ohio 4-H Youth Development, Ohio State University Extension
pay_detail: Membership fees are not stated on the page. Ask your county Extension office.
duration: Project year
deadline_text: Each county sets an enrollment deadline. The state page does not list a date.
who_can_apply: Eligibility is based on age and grade as of January 1 of the project year. Any youth age 9 or older can do a project, whatever the grade. Eligibility ends December 31 of the year you turn 19. You must join an authorized Ohio 4-H club or group.
how_to_apply: Contact your County Extension Office to be connected with a club. Go to a first meeting. Pick a project. Then enroll in 4-HOnline with your club volunteer or the county office. Do it before the county deadline.
notes: Club membership, not a paid job. The site menu has a Just for Teens section that was not read. The ohio4h.org home page was down (503) when tried, so only the join page was read.

name: Buckeye Boys State
grades: Interview in junior year, attend before senior year
pay_detail: No cost to the student or family when a local American Legion post sponsors you (stated on the Parent Information page).
duration: Eight days
deadline_text: Session dates and deadlines are not posted on the pages read. Legion post interviews are usually held in winter or spring at high schools.
who_can_apply: Students who interview in their junior year for the next summer's program. That means incoming seniors from across Ohio. Local American Legion posts sponsor delegates. The pages read do not list other rules.
how_to_apply: Ask a counselor, administrator or history teacher if a Legion post is interviewing at your school. If not, use the Apply or Become A Delegate form on the site. The program will match you with a post. Chosen delegates go to an orientation.
notes: Not a job. Office phone is 513-529-3860. The site describes the program as drawing over 1,200 young men a year.

name: Ohio DECA chapters and state conference
org: Ohio DECA (chartered association of DECA Inc.)
pay_detail: $16 per student member: $8 to the state association plus $8 to DECA Inc. Local chapter fees are not stated.
duration: School year
deadline_text: The Ohio DECA conference is February 22 to 24, 2027 at the Greater Columbus Convention Center. No membership deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: Members must be enrolled in a career-technical education program approved by the Ohio Department of Education and Workforce. Grades and ages are not listed.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's career-technical or business teacher about a DECA chapter. State questions go to the Ohio DECA advisor, Drew Goldfinger, at Drew.Goldfinger@education.ohio.gov.
notes: Not a paid job. Your school must have an approved career-technical program with a DECA chapter. The state website listed on the page is ohiodeca.org.

name: ExploreAg (Ohio Farm Bureau career camps)
city: Ohio (one-day camps in Columbus, Wilmington, Findlay and more)
grades: Entering freshman year of high school through freshman year of college
pay_detail: Free to students. A deposit confirms your spot and is returned on the day of the program (amount not stated).
duration: One-day camps in fall (the weeklong camp is over for 2026)
deadline_text: Fall 2026 one-day camps: Wilmington Oct. 13, Columbus Oct. 21, Findlay Nov. 3, COLT Lineman Training (Mount Gilead) Oct. 23, Meat Processing (Yorkshire) Oct. 27. Registration closes 10 days before each event, so the Columbus day closes about Oct. 11, 2026.
who_can_apply: Any Ohio student who is entering 9th grade through 12th grade, or freshman year of college, this fall.
how_to_apply: Pick the camp on the ExploreAg page and fill out its registration form. For questions, use the Contact Us page at ofbf.org/contact/.
notes: The Oct. 11 close date is figured from the "10 days prior" rule on the flyer, so check the Columbus registration page. Sign up on the page for email notices about future ExploreAg camps.

name: Ohio FFA membership through your school chapter
org: Ohio FFA Association (Ohio Department of Education and Workforce)
pay_detail: $17 per member covers State and National FFA dues. The school is invoiced by Ohio FFA. Local chapter dues are not stated.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Membership opens each August through FFA.org. Ohio FFA lists September 30, 2026 for students in Fall CDEs and November 30, 2026 for all chapters.
who_can_apply: Students at schools with an Ohio FFA chapter. The membership page does not list grades or ages. Ask your chapter advisor.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's FFA chapter advisor to add you. Chapters submit membership through FFA.org. Schools with no program can contact Ohio FFA about starting a chapter.
notes: Not a job. The homepage reports 30,880 members in 345 chapters. State office phone is (614) 387-7575. The September 30 and November 30 dates are chapter deadlines, so a student should ask the advisor early.

name: STEM Summer Camps (Ohio State Marion)
org: The Ohio State University at Marion
grades: Rising 9th to 12th graders (for the two high school camps)
pay_detail: $185 per camp, which includes lunch and lab costs (2026 price).
duration: 1 week, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
deadline_text: 2026 camps ran June 22 to 26, 2026 and registration closed May 31, 2026 or earlier if full. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th graders in any United States school can sign up for Science Adventurers or Horizons of Science. A third camp is for rising 5th to 8th graders.
how_to_apply: Online application and payment for each camp (separate forms on the page). Questions go to Tiffiny Rye-McCurdy at rye-mccurdy.1@osu.edu.
notes: This is at the Ohio State Marion campus, not in Columbus. The page mentions no housing or rides, so plan your own.

name: Ohio State Fair Junior Fair Board
org: Ohio Expo Center, Ohio State Fair
pay_detail: Flat-rate stipend, higher in the second year. The amount is not stated. Housing and meals are provided in dorms at the fair.
duration: About 2 weeks (arrive the Monday before the Wednesday opening)
deadline_text: The page says the online application portal opens January 1 and the application is due March 1. Notices come early to mid March, interviews mid to late March, selection early April. No year is shown, so confirm the 2027 dates in January.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 20 who are now in a youth or career tech group. Examples are 4-H, FFA, DECA, Girl Scouts, Scouting America and Key Club. You need strong leadership and a record of being involved. Members serve one two-year term.
how_to_apply: Send the official Junior Fair Board application in the online portal on the Ohio State Fair page. Do it between January 1 and March 1. Interviews come next. Send questions to the co-coordinators listed on the page.
notes: The page does not say whether a work permit is needed for minors. Ask the coordinators.

name: Teen Volunteer Program at The Wilds
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer
duration: At least 40 hours through the summer
deadline_text: No deadline or dates are posted on the volunteer page. The visitor season runs May through October for adult volunteers.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 through 17 who like animals and nature and enjoy talking with visitors. The page asks for at least 40 hours of volunteer service over the summer.
how_to_apply: Click the Apply Now button under Teen Volunteers on the volunteer page. It is an online form.
notes: The page says nothing about housing or rides.

name: Civil Air Patrol cadets, Ohio Wing
pay_detail: Dues and fees are not stated on the page. Payment options are on the last page of the application.
duration: Weekly meetings all year, plus a summer encampment
deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time through a local squadron.
who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. You must be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (national headquarters may waive this for some non-citizens). You must attend at least three squadron meetings first.
how_to_apply: Find a cadet or composite squadron with the unit locator. Visit with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then complete the application. Some squadrons take it online.
notes: Volunteer youth program, not a job. Ohio Wing office: 6031 E Main Street, PO Box 301, Columbus, OH 43213, phone 614-338-8198.

name: Ohio Youth & Government (YMCA model government)
org: Ohio Alliance of YMCAs, Ohio Youth & Government
city: Columbus, OH (State Assembly), delegations across Ohio
pay_detail: Registration fee amount is not stated on the pages read. A $25 late fee applied last year. Financial aid pages exist for middle and high school.
duration: Fall prep, then a 3-day State Assembly in spring
deadline_text: Last cycle: State Assembly February 12 to 14, 2026 at the Hyatt Regency Columbus. Registration closed November 28, 2025, with late registration December 1 to 10, 2025. 2027 dates are not posted on the page read.
who_can_apply: Middle school (6th to 8th) and high school (9th to 12th) students. You join through a local delegation run by a school or YMCA.
how_to_apply: Join or start a delegation at your school or YMCA in the fall. New delegations can email yg@ohioymcas.org or call (614) 407-4819. Students and advisors register on the State Assembly registration page.
notes: Not a job. The registration page still showed the 2026 assembly dates, so check it for the 2027 dates.

name: Teen Tutor and Session Lead Volunteers
city: Libraries in Texas and Pennsylvania (ask which one has a chapter)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers earn volunteer hours.
duration: 2 to 3 hours a week. Commit to at least one session, preferably a year.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Register to volunteer on the site.
who_can_apply: Tutors are ages 13 to 18, love working with young kids, have a B or higher in high school math, and bring a laptop.
how_to_apply: Sign up to volunteer on the OneInMath site. Use the register-volunteer page.
notes: The pages read do not list chapter locations. The tutor page's library news mentions North Texas libraries, so ask the group which library near you has a chapter.

name: Oneonta Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

name: Mi4 Summer Internship at CHOC
org: Rady Children's Health (CHOC) Medical Intelligence and Innovation Institute
pay_detail: No cost to join. Pay is not mentioned on the page. Meals, housing and travel are on you; help for low-income students may be available.
duration: About 8 weeks, June 15 to Aug 7 (2026 dates). Monday to Thursday plus Friday field trips.
deadline_text: The 2026 round is over. The page says next year's application opens in February 2027. For 2026 it opened Feb 1 and closed Feb 28, with rolling interviews.
who_can_apply: Students in high school, college, grad school or medical school who are interested in health care and innovation. You must be at least a high school freshman. You need to be on site 40 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Apply on the CHOC website when the form opens. Interviews are rolling, so apply early. You are admitted by form and interview.
notes: The page links to a CHOC volunteer page but does not state its age rule here. Hospital and outpatient shadowing rotations are 18 and up. Business casual dress is expected.

pay_detail: Free to join. The page does not say the externship is paid.

name: Golden West College Dual and Concurrent Enrollment

The page says tuition is free, but students may still owe college fees and course costs. It offers a Foundation financial aid form and a possible fee waiver.

name: Orange County Young Curators (OCYC)
org: UC Irvine Langson Orange County Museum of Art
pay_detail: Not stated on the pages read

deadline_text: Application dates for the next group are not on the museum pages read.

how_to_apply: Application steps are not listed on the pages read. Email langsonteens@uci.edu to ask.
notes: The museum is named UC Irvine Langson Orange County Museum of Art on the page. Confirm dates and any stipend with the museum first.

name: Library volunteers, ages 14 and up (Orange County Public Library)

notes: The county document is titled 2024, so confirm shifts and openings with the library before you go. Main branch only: 137 W. Margaret Lane, Hillsborough.

name: OC Parks Volunteer

notes: Volunteers 16 and 17 need parent permission. The page lists historic docent, backcountry patrol and OC Zoo roles. It lists others too.

name: OC Pathways Student Ambassador Program

notes: Ask your school CTE teacher or counselor too. Confirm the spring dates with OC Pathways.

name: OCFA Fire Cadet Program

pay_detail: Not stated; described as a community-based youth program

how_to_apply: Fill out the Cadet Interest Form on the OCFA site to join the interest list. Later, people on the list are asked to finish a longer form.
notes: OCFA serves many Orange County cities. Ask which cadet post is nearest to you.

name: Santa Ana College Dual Enrollment

notes: If you go over the unit limit you pay the enrollment fee for all units, not only the extra ones. The office is closed on Fridays in summer.

name: Santiago Canyon College Early College (Dual Enrollment)
pay_detail: The page says free transferable college units. Fees for books or other costs are not listed on the page.
duration: By semester

name: Otis College Summer of Art
org: Otis College of Art and Design

name: OUSD Linked Learning Internships
org: Oakland Unified School District, High School Linked Learning Office
fields: any; health; tech-cs; arts-media; engineering; business-finance

name: Pacoima Beautiful Agua University

name: Teen Service Projects, Volunteers and Teen Advisory Board

name: Palo Alto Art Center Summer Camp Counselor in Training

notes: Check the current deadline with Mitchell Park Teen Services (3700 Middlefield Rd, or @mpteenservices on Instagram and Facebook). Pay is not mentioned on the page; treat as unpaid until confirmed.

notes: Pay is not mentioned on the page; treat as unpaid until confirmed. Term length is not stated. Contact Mitchell Park Teen Services (3700 Middlefield Rd).

name: Pasadena City College Dual and Concurrent Enrollment for Middle and High School Students

Send your latest unofficial transcript as well. Then turn on your LancerPoint account and register. Questions: outreach@pasadena.edu.

name: Pasadena Humane Teen Volunteers (15 and up, Ambassador at 14 with a parent)

notes: The page does not say which roles are only for adults. Kids ages 6 to 14 have separate roles (Shelter Greeter, Boredom Busters). Those need a parent who volunteers too.

name: The Rose, Pasadena's Youth Literary Magazine

notes: The library page does not say the age rule for the Teen Volunteer Application, so ask the teen librarian. Teen librarian contact is on the page. The page does not say whether contributors are paid.

notes: The home page names Pathful and Pathful Junior and does not use the name Pathful Explore. It is a school-run tool; individual students likely cannot join without a school plan.

name: Pennsylvania 4-H
pay_detail: Members pay a fee for educational materials. Extra fees vary by county and project area. Financial help is available. Amounts are not stated.

notes: A youth group, not a job. Ask your county educator what clubs and teen leader roles are near you.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, Pennsylvania Wing
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location. Uniform and overnight activity fees are extra. National Headquarters says a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year. Some help is available.

deadline_text: No deadline. Join any time by visiting a squadron.
who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters can waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Attend at least three squadron meetings.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. You can also ask the squadron about the online application.
notes: No military duty. Cadets can stay in until age 21 and can switch to adult membership at 18. Squadron meetings and costs vary, so ask the squadron near you.

name: Pennsylvania FBLA (Future Business Leaders of America)
city: Pennsylvania (statewide, state office in Jersey Shore)

deadline_text: Join through your chapter adviser any time. Next State Leadership Conference: April 12 to 14, 2027.

It is also open if your school has no FBLA chapter. The Virtual Chapter page says members must take a business class. Students at schools with an active FBLA chapter cannot join it.
how_to_apply: Ask your chapter adviser at school. If you do not know who that is, contact Bruce Boncal, PA FBLA Executive Director, bboncal@pafbla.us. Virtual Chapter members fill out an online application signed by a parent.
notes: Virtual Chapter members pay their own travel costs. State office: (570) 398-4652, stateoffice@pafbla.us.

name: Pennsylvania FFA Association

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 in Pennsylvania: public, private, parochial or home schooled. You need an adult sponsor (a teacher, parent or scientist). You must do your own research and your own presentation.

notes: A science fair, not a job. Your project may need extra approval forms depending on your research field, so ask your sponsor or Regional Director early. Regional pages list the exact deadlines.

name: Keystone Boys State

notes: The page says volunteers must be vaccinated and that the library is accepting volunteers; check with your branch for the current rule. Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit.

name: Volunteer Program, Academy of Natural Sciences
org: Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University
pay_detail: Unpaid

deadline_text: No deadline listed.

how_to_apply: Complete the online application linked on the page, then email the Volunteer Coordinator at volunteers@ansp.org about specific openings.
notes: The page does not say which areas teens can join. Bird Safe Philly runs April to May and September to November.

name: Teen Sketch and Teen Podcast, Philadelphia Museum of Art
pay_detail: Pay or stipend not stated on the page.
duration: Fall 2026 programs. Teen Sketch length is not stated.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 programs are listed with Apply links. No closing date is posted on the page.

how_to_apply: Each program has its own Apply now link (a Google form) on the teens page. Questions: teens@philamuseum.org.
notes: The page does not say whether the programs are paid or free, or when the forms close. Email the teen team before you plan around it. The museum also ran A Future of Artists, a June to August 2026 exhibition of work by Philadelphia-area high school students.

name: Outdoor and Wilderness Leadership Skills (OWLS), Awbury Arboretum
pay_detail: Summer 2026 price was $675 ($641 for members) for the 2 week session. The camp page says scholarships (75% off) and sliding scale fees (30% to 60% off) are available to families in local zip codes.
duration: 2 weeks (June 15 to 26 in 2026)
deadline_text: Summer 2026 session ran June 15 to 26, 2026 and was sold out. The camp FAQ says Summer 2027 registration opens Monday, Feb. 1, 2027 at 9 am; OWLS 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17 only.
how_to_apply: Sign up through the Awbury Adventures Summer Camp page. Ask for financial aid BEFORE you sign up, because aid spots are few.
notes: This is training, not a paid job. The page does not say whether graduates get counselor jobs. A 2021 posting on the same site said 2 to 6 trainees were chosen as stipend-paid counselors in training; that is old, so ask.

name: Paid Youth Internships, Bartram's Garden
pay_detail: $11 to $12.50 per hour in 2025-26; 8.5 hours a week in the school year. Some interns can continue in summer at 20 hours a week.
duration: October to spring in the 2025-26 cycle; some interns continue in summer.
deadline_text: The 2025-26 cycle closed Sept 23, 2025 (program started Oct 6, 2025). The page says applications reopen in August for the 2026-27 school year, but still shows the 2025 dates.
who_can_apply: Current high school sophomores, juniors and seniors ages 14 to 18. You must live, go to school or have other ties in Southwest Philadelphia. Priority goes to 49th to 65th Streets between Chester Avenue and the river. You must have a work permit or be able to get one.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application with short written answers. Then you have an in-person interview. If you are hired, you sign up for the city C2L-PHL program. It needs a Social Security card, an ID, proof of citizenship and Philadelphia home address, and a W-9.
notes: Competitive: about 50 students a year across all programs. The page still showed 2025-26 dates when read, so check it for the 2026-27 deadline. The Garden will never ask for birth dates or Social Security numbers by text message.

name: Bloomberg Arts Internship (BAI)
pay_detail: $20+ per hour for Summer 2026, plus transportation and meal support
duration: Eight weeks, up to 35 hours a week (2026: June 19 to August 14); select interns may continue in a school-year program up to 10 hours a week
deadline_text: The page posts no intern application dates. Its only application notice is for worksite hosts: Summer 2026 applications are officially closed.
who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors in Philadelphia. The page does not state an age range or residency proof.
how_to_apply: The program page gives no intern application steps. Contact info@philaculture.org or 215-557-7811.
notes: Pennsylvania's Department of Labor and Industry page says children need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer. The permit is not mentioned on the program page.

name: Career Connected Learning PHL (C2L-PHL) Summer Program
org: City of Philadelphia Office of Children and Families, with JEVS Human Services
pay_detail: Stipend on a prepaid debit card, paid every other week; total $1,300 to $1,500 depending on the program (hourly rate not listed).
duration: Summer program (plus school-year programming)
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed. FAQ: summer applications open between March and April each year.
who_can_apply: Philadelphia residents ages 12 to 24. In-school youth get priority. You can apply to one program per cycle.
how_to_apply: Apply through the C2L-PHL Youth Portal (phila.gov/c2l-phl). Documents: photo ID, school records, Social Security card, birth certificate or passport, and a work permit. Not first come, first served. Help: C2LPHL@jevs.org or 833-750-5627.
notes: Application is English only; call for help in other languages. Roughly 8,000 city-funded slots a summer (per PYN's site). Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadets, Northeast Philadelphia Composite Squadron
org: Civil Air Patrol, Northeast Philadelphia Composite Squadron (PA-214)
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.
duration: The squadron meets Fridays from 7:00 to 9:15 p.m. at the Naval Support Activity Center, 700 Robbins St, Philadelphia, PA 19111.
deadline_text: No deadline. Contact the squadron any time.
who_can_apply: Cadets ages 12 to 18. The Pennsylvania Wing page lists Become a Cadet as ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: The squadron page does not describe a visit process. Contact the squadron: cc214@pawg.cap.gov (squadron commander) or 215-531-2278. The wing's Join CAP page has the cadet steps.
notes: The Pennsylvania Wing lists five other squadrons in the Philadelphia area. They are Willow Grove, Liberty, Griffin, Gen Carl A Spaatz and Chester County. Ask the wing which is closest to you. The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.

name: Neuroscience Camp for High School Students, Drexel
org: Drexel University Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences and Professional Studies
grades: Rising high school juniors and seniors with a background in biology, chemistry or research
duration: 10 days, in-person commuter (2026: July 20 to 31)
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was April 3, 2026. The page says 2027 Summer Institutes information will be posted this winter.
who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors with a biology, chemistry or research background. Admission is competitive.
how_to_apply: Submit transcripts and two letters of recommendation. Contact camp assistant Ipatia Daigle (ied26@drexel.edu) or director Dr. Jed Shumsky (js52@drexel.edu).
notes: Drexel runs other Summer Institutes (arts and sciences, business, engineering, design, nursing, public health); their pages did not list grades, costs or dates when read.

name: Teen Lounge, Fleisher Art Memorial
pay_detail: Free. No attendance requirement. Snacks and bus passes provided.
duration: Tuesdays and Wednesdays, 4 to 6 pm, while Philadelphia schools are in session. Fall 2026 workshops start Sept 8.
deadline_text: Teen Lounge 2026-2027 runs during the school year. Fall workshops started Tuesday, Sept 8, 2026. It is drop in.
who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not list ages or grades.
how_to_apply: Drop in at 719 Catharine St, or email cy@fleisher.org.
notes: Not a job. Lead support from the William Penn Foundation and others is listed on the page.

name: Immersion Science Program (Fox Chase Cancer Center)
pay_detail: Nearly all programming is cost free to participants. No pay for the winter course. Fox Chase cannot provide transportation.
duration: 11 weeks of Saturday sessions from early January to mid March: Section 1 meets 8:30 to 11:30 a.m. and Section 2 meets 12:30 to 3:30 p.m. There are 16 seats, 8 per section.
deadline_text: The application launches in mid to late October each year and stays open about 3.5 weeks. The exact 2026 dates are not posted on the page read. Interviews are in early to mid December and letters go out by email before December 31.
who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old who finished both high school biology and chemistry. Neither can be taken at the same time. Open to students in the Philadelphia Tri-State area. You can apply to a Philadelphia-only section.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google form application. It cannot be saved, so a PDF version is available to draft offline. Two letters of recommendation are required. One must come from a science or STEM teacher who has known you at least a year. Applications are blind reviewed. Then three committee members interview 20 to 25 applicants.
notes: The FAQ says the application launches in mid to late October, so it may open any day now. Check the page for the real dates. General Fox Chase number: 888-369-2427. A summer fellows track is funded by National Cancer Institute grants. Its pay and rules are not stated on the pages read.

name: PACTS (Partnership for Achieving Careers in Technology and Science), The Franklin Institute
pay_detail: Free program.
duration: School year, workshops meet twice a month on Saturday mornings
deadline_text: The page has an Apply link but no dates for the current year.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 8 who live in the Philadelphia area.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply to the PACTS Program online form on the page.
notes: For younger teens (grades 6 to 8). Older teens can join the Franklin Ambassador program through STEM Scholars, which has its own card.

name: STEM Scholars, The Franklin Institute
grades: Apply as a high school freshman (grade 9)
pay_detail: Free to students; rising seniors are paid for lab research (rate not stated). Fees covered by donors.

deadline_text: Applications for the next freshman cohort are currently closed; check back for the 2027 class. FAQ says applications usually open late September or early October and are due mid-December.
who_can_apply: Students living in Philadelphia and surrounding areas who are entering 9th grade, interested in STEM, able to commit to four years, with a 3.0 GPA (per FAQ). Non-freshmen are rarely accepted.
how_to_apply: Online application, essay, transcript, two recommendation letters, then an interview with Youth Programs staff.
notes: The FAQ timing and the 'currently closed' message are not fully consistent, so confirm on the page. The sister middle-school program PACTS is for grades 6 to 8.

name: Teen Ambassadors, Independence Seaport Museum
pay_detail: Described as a ten-week paid work and learning experience. The hourly rate is not stated.
duration: June through August, plus select Saturdays in September
deadline_text: The page says apply by April 20 (priority interviews); its flyer link is dated March 2026. Next dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Philadelphia teens about to enter grades 10 to 12 who go to a high school in the city. You must be allowed to work in Philadelphia. If you are under 18, you must be able to get a work permit. You must be free for the whole program. It runs June through August, plus some Saturdays in September.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google form linked from the program page. Early applications get interviews first.
notes: Funded by The W.W. Smith Charitable Trust and The Hamilton Family Charitable Trust, both named on the page.

name: Summer Student Volunteer Program, Jefferson Health Northeast
org: Jefferson Health Northeast (Torresdale, Frankford and Bucks County hospitals)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get their own transportation.
duration: 8 weeks, 4 hours a day, one day a week
deadline_text: The program page gives no application dates and no year. The 2024 packet said applications are accepted from February until April.
who_can_apply: Students 16 or older who can keep a regular weekly shift. Needs two school references from teachers and proof of vaccines (measles, mumps, rubella and a TB test).
how_to_apply: Send the application, two letters of support from teachers and shot forms to the Volunteer Services Department. You can send by mail, scan, fax or email. Phone: 215-612-4170.
notes: Facts come from the 2024 application packet on the Jefferson site. The program web page shows only its title (checked 2026-10-09 with a normal fetch and with curl), so the age, time, pay and how-to-apply details are not confirmed on the page. Confirm the current dates, ages and form first. Spots are limited.

name: Philadelphia Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
city: Philadelphia, PA (campus; page lists transportation and no dorms)
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists transportation to and from campus, breakfast and lunch, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: the Philadelphia campus page lists transportation and no dorms. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

name: Dr. Charis Eng Monell Science Apprenticeship Program (MSAP)
grades: Currently enrolled in high school or an undergraduate school
pay_detail: Described as paid. The amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: The program page says eight weeks of paid full-time structured research. The 2026 program ran June 15 to July 31, 2026, which is shorter than eight weeks, so confirm the length. The page does not give the 2027 dates.
deadline_text: The page says applications for the Summer 2027 program will open in October 2026. The deadline is not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Students now in high school or college from the greater Philadelphia area, including Camden, NJ. You must be able to prove you can work in the United States. No age or grade is stated. The committee gives strong preference to students from groups underrepresented in science.
how_to_apply: Use the MSAP Applications page on monell.org when it opens. Sign up for Monell's newsletter for updates. Questions: AcademicAffairs@monell.org or 267-519-4700. About 200 applications come in each year. 18 to 24 students are usually enrolled.
notes: Minors do not need working papers to apply. They must get them after they are admitted. They come from the School District of Philadelphia, per the Monell FAQ. The Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says minors under 18 need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer. Monell does not provide housing or meals. Students must commit to the full program with no vacations.

name: Art Education high school programs (Mural Arts Philadelphia)
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the pages read. The page says students can later apply for scholarships, internships and jobs in the creative field.
duration: Twice a week. The 2026 to 27 school year programs begin in late September 2026 (the page says they end in early June and prints the year 2026, which looks like a typo for 2027).
deadline_text: Rolling admission is open. The page says the fall session begins in late September 2026.
who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 22 at the high school sites. Ages 10 to 13 are served at middle school sites. A parent or guardian must sign and provide extra information before a youth under 18 can be enrolled.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Inquiry Form on the Mural Arts enroll page. It is not an application and does not confirm enrollment. An Art Education staff member follows up about classes near you. Contact: natalie.gearin@muralarts.org or (215) 685-0750.
notes: The pages say 3 high school sites and 6 middle school sites on the enroll page but 16 sites in total on the program page, so ask which site is near you. Mural Arts also has paid summer work experience through Career Connected Learning (see the C2L PHL card). Ask whether classes are free. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Living History Youth Summer Institute, Museum of the American Revolution
pay_detail: The page says it is a paid six-week program. The pay amount is not stated. Public transportation help is offered.

deadline_text: The page names a 2026 session but gives no application dates. The 2026 program is finished and no 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: High school and college students. You must be able to go on weekdays for the whole program. You must live close enough to the museum to travel there each day.
how_to_apply: The program page does not explain how to apply. Contact the museum education team through the museum website.
notes: This is a small program. The 2023 press release said eight took part. It is part of the museum's African American Interpretive Program. Check the museum site for the next call for applications.

name: Youth Council, Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts
org: Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts (PAFA)

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Use the Register link on the Youth Council page.
notes: PAFA is on North Broad Street. The status is shown as open because the page lists a Register link for both sessions; the page gives no closing date.

name: Become a Lifeguard, Philadelphia Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Starts at $16.85 per hour, about 35 hours a week from June through August. Red Cross certification is free for ages 16 to 24 who work at a Parks and Rec pool.
duration: June through August, about 35 hours a week; free training runs year-round
deadline_text: Free training is offered year-round; reserve a slot on Eventbrite.
who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older to work as a city lifeguard; you can attend the screening at 15.
how_to_apply: Choose a pool and contact its supervisor, train with Aquatics staff to pass the screening, then finish the Red Cross certification and pre-employment steps. Contact: lifeguard@phila.gov.
notes: Free training is at Lincoln High School and Friends Select School. Pennsylvania's Department of Labor and Industry page says children need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer; workers under 16 also need a parent statement (Form LLC-75).

name: Parks and Rec Summer Youth Employment Program
pay_detail: Not stated on the page
duration: Summer
deadline_text: The page still says registration closed for the C2L-PHL Summer 2025 program. No 2026 or 2027 dates posted.
who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 14 to 24. Residency is not stated on this page (the parent C2L-PHL program requires Philadelphia residency).
how_to_apply: Not described on this page; positions come through C2L-PHL. Questions: PPRC2L@phila.gov or 215-683-3683.
notes: Check the C2L-PHL listing for the actual application. The page I read had not been updated after Summer 2025. Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says work permits are required for minors under 18 hired to fill a position; the Parks and Rec page itself does not mention permits.

name: Provost's Summer Mentorship Program (Penn)
grades: Currently 9th or 10th grade (entering 10th or 11th grade in fall 2027)
pay_detail: Cost and stipend are not stated on the pages read, so ask the program before you plan around either.

who_can_apply: Students who live in Philadelphia. You must go to a Philadelphia public, Catholic, private or charter high school. You need a minimum GPA of 3.0.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page on the program site when it opens in January 2027. You will need a high school transcript with fall 2026 grades. You need a 250 word essay about yourself and your interest in the program. You need an up to date vaccine record.
notes: The two pages word the grade rule differently (currently 9th or 10th on the apply page, entering 10th or 11th in fall 2027 on the main page); they describe the same group. Office: St. Leonard's Court, Suite 110, 3819 Chestnut Street, Philadelphia, PA 19104; contact form at https://vpse.upenn.edu/smp/contact-us/.

name: Penn Arts and Sciences High School Summer Programs
org: University of Pennsylvania, Penn LPS High School Programs
grades: Academies and Online Seminars: current 9th to 11th grade. Pre-College: current 10th to 11th grade.
pay_detail: 2026 tuition: 2-week Academy $6,700; 3-week Academy $10,050; Pre-College Residential $15,192 to $23,604; Pre-College Online $8,692 or $14,300; Online Seminars $2,950. $1,500 deposit and $100 application fee (waived for School District of Philadelphia applicants).
duration: 2 to 6 weeks depending on program (2026 Academies: July 11 to August 1)
deadline_text: 2026: May 1 for Academies and Pre-College Residential/Online Session I; June 1 for Online Seminars and Pre-College Online Session II. Rolling admissions. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Current 9th to 11th graders (Pre-College: 10th to 11th).
how_to_apply: Online application from the student: essays (400 words each), transcript, recommendations. For the scholarship, say you attend a School District of Philadelphia school and fill in the scholarship section.
notes: There are no scholarships for the Pre-College programs. Contact hsprogs@sas.upenn.edu or 215-746-2309.

name: Police Explorer Cadet Program (Post 991)
org: Philadelphia Police Department, with Learning for Life
pay_detail: Pay, stipend or fees are not stated on the pages read.
duration: Every Saturday 10 am to 5 pm at the Philadelphia Police Academy, plus optional summer camps and a Washington DC trip.
deadline_text: The program site says applications are open for 2026-2027. No closing date is posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 20 who want a law enforcement career. 14 year olds must be in high school. Under 18 needs a parent or guardian consent. Needs a passing behavior grade, good health for running and agility drills, and no arrests or convictions that would block a future police job.
how_to_apply: Use the online intake form on the program site. It is on the Apply and Forms page. If you are under 18, get a parent or guardian to say yes.
notes: Most cadets are not paid, but the pages do not say. Cadets who want to be officers are urged to join the police recruit testing later. Other Explorer camps listed include a Pennsylvania State Police week and a camp at Fort Indiantown Gap.

name: AIM Afterschool, Philadelphia Youth Network
pay_detail: Not stated; no cost is listed on the page read.

deadline_text: The page says enrollment is open all year round.
who_can_apply: Middle school students in the School District of Philadelphia. They must go to one of the PYN school sites.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online forms in the PYN application portal. There are no paper applications. Send questions to afterschool@pyninc.org.
notes: For middle schoolers, so it suits younger teens. Pick a school site from the list on the page.

name: NextGen Career Clubs, Philadelphia Youth Network
pay_detail: Free career exposure program. The club itself is not described as paid.
duration: 3 days a week, 2 hours a session
deadline_text: The page says it is recruiting at high schools across Philadelphia. No closing date posted.
who_can_apply: Rising 11th or 12th graders at one of the PYN host high schools in Philadelphia. You must be able to come three days a week after school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Participant Interest Form on the PYN page. Questions: 267-502-3800.
notes: The page also lists a NextGen Career Club (Health Care).

name: PYNtern Program
grades: Rising 9th to 12th grade (Junior PYNtern rising 9th to 10th; Senior PYNtern rising 11th to 12th)
pay_detail: Up to $1,500 for a 6 to 8 week experience, depending on hours and milestones
duration: 6 to 8 weeks per cohort (page also says experiences last 6 to 12 weeks)
deadline_text: Summer cohort applications open early March; Fall/Winter cohort open early August; Winter/Spring cohort open in November. Page says Now Recruiting for Summer + Fall 2026.
who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 18, primarily rising 9th to 12th graders. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Use Apply Now or the interest form on the page (name, contact, current grade, cohort, three career fields). Phone 267-502-3800 or info@pyninc.org.
notes: About 400 internship slots a year across cohorts. The city's large summer jobs program is C2L-PHL, a separate application. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: City-Wide Philly Youth Opportunity Fair
pay_detail: Free event.
duration: Friday Oct 23, 3 to 7 pm
deadline_text: Friday, October 23, 2026, 3:00 to 7:00 pm. Pre-registration deadline is Oct 15. The page says registration is not required to attend.
who_can_apply: The page says young people ages 16 to 24. Families and supporters can come too.
how_to_apply: Fill out the free pre-registration form on the event page (deadline Oct 15). Bring several copies of your resume.
notes: The page gives the day and month only; the year is taken from Oct 23 falling on a Friday in 2026. Under 16 is not listed as eligible.

name: Career and Technical Education (CTE), School District of Philadelphia
pay_detail: School program; the page does not say whether internships are paid.
duration: Typically 3 years, 1,080 hours of instruction; some programs 1 or 2 years
deadline_text: Follow the School Selection timeline for middle schoolers; high schoolers ask their counselor.
who_can_apply: District high school students starting in 10th grade. Middle schoolers choose a CTE program on their School Selection application; high schoolers can join if their school has the program and space allows.
how_to_apply: Middle school: pick schools that offer your CTE program on the School Selection application. High school: talk to your school counselor.
notes: The page notes that students ages 14 to 17 need working papers to work. Which schools offer which programs is in the CTE Programs List.

name: Counselor-in-Training Program, Camp Schuylkill
pay_detail: Volunteer program with no fee listed; hours can count as school or organization service hours.
duration: Two full weeks required; may be asked to work up to three weeks; one Saturday training in May
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was March 31, 2026. Camp Schuylkill runs on a weekly schedule from June 21 to August 13, 2027.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. Positions are limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form on the camp page, including a one-page essay (why you want to volunteer as a CIT, experience with children, what you enjoy about nature).
notes: Camp is at 8480 Hagy's Mill Road, Philadelphia, PA 19128. The page's date line looks like a typo (June 15, 2025 to August 14, 2026), so confirm dates when the 2027 application posts.

name: Wildlife Clinic Support Volunteer, Schuylkill Center
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Minimum one 4-hour shift a week (about 20 hours a month)
deadline_text: 2026 in-person info sessions were February 7 and February 28; virtual sessions as needed. Fill out the application to hear about future sessions.
who_can_apply: Clinic Support volunteers must be 16 or older (Animal Care requires 18+). Must attend a training session, sign the volunteer agreement and finish online ethics and safety courses.
how_to_apply: Complete the Wildlife Clinic volunteer Google Form. It is linked on the page.
notes: The general volunteer page says regular volunteers who work with children need Pennsylvania child abuse and criminal history clearances (free for volunteers).

name: Temple Summer Academy (pre-college)
pay_detail: There is a program fee and optional housing. The cost page was blocked when read, so the amount is not confirmed here. Optional financial aid essay is on the application.
duration: 4 weeks on campus
deadline_text: The page says registration for Summer 2027 begins in December. No closing date was readable.
who_can_apply: Students about to enter grade 11 or 12. You need a transcript, a list of activities and a personal statement of 250 to 500 words. You also need a recommendation from a teacher or counselor.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Add your transcript, a list of what you do outside class and a personal statement. Temple will email a form to your teacher or counselor. They use it to write about you.
notes: Finishing with a B or better can earn a Temple tuition grant of $1,000 a year for four years if you later enroll at Temple full time and keep a 3.0 GPA. Phone: (215) 204-7200.

name: Temple Upward Bound and Upward Bound Math & Science
org: Temple University College of Education and Human Development
pay_detail: Free to students. A pay or stipend is not stated on the pages read.
duration: Runs year-round, with a six-week summer program on campus.
deadline_text: Rolling applications. The page says the Summer Academy deadline is May 31.
who_can_apply: Students in 9th or 10th grade at Philadelphia public district or charter high schools. They come from low-income families, or their parents do not have a bachelor degree, or both. They also plan to go to college. Five named schools get priority. They are Benjamin Franklin HS, Dobbins CTE, Gratz Mastery, Strawberry Mansion and The U School.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Send papers that show you are eligible, like a report card, test scores and proof of income. Then you have a virtual interview. Questions: 215-204-3636.
notes: Federally funded and free. You must have a goal of going to college. Income is not the only factor in who is accepted.

name: Pre-College Summer Academy, Villanova University
org: Villanova University College of Professional Studies
pay_detail: Residential $8,000 (room and meals). Non-residential $6,000. $2,000 deposit due at acceptance. $50 application fee.
duration: 4 weeks in July
deadline_text: Applications for 2027 are open now. No closing date is posted. The page says 2027 dates are being finalized, with classes expected in July, and it encourages early applications.
who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors, and incoming college freshmen. Needs a personal statement of 250 to 500 words.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Pre-College Summer Academy application online. Pick the Pre-College Summer Academy choice from the list. Add your personal statement to the form too.
notes: The page says that being accepted does not promise acceptance later at Villanova. It also does not give you an edge. A virtual info session is offered.

name: High School Program in Biomedical Research (Wistar Institute)
pay_detail: $1,500 stipend for finishing the program, plus SEPTA passes for travel
duration: Four weeks (the 2026 session ran July 6 to July 30). An optional three week extension in August depends on funding.
deadline_text: The 2026 program has ended. The page says to check back in January for the 2027 summer program. Last year's cycle had interviews in April and decisions in the first week of May.
who_can_apply: Students who are at least 16 by the program start date and have finished at least one high school science course. The program gives priority to students in the School District of Philadelphia. It strongly encourages Philadelphia high school students to apply. No grade level or residency rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Send an online application. It has a personal statement of one page, single spaced. It has two letters of recommendation. One from a science teacher is preferred. It has an unofficial transcript or list of classes with grades. Finalists have a 15 minute virtual interview in April. Participants and a parent or guardian go to a mandatory orientation in June.
notes: Contacts: Jason Diaz, 215-898-3803, jdiaz@wistar.org, or Cailey Bice, 215-898-3749, cbice@wistar.org. Absences of more than two days in a row cannot be accommodated. The stipend is not called a wage on the page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: WorkReady BOOST (year-round paid career program)
pay_detail: $11 an hour starting wage, 120 paid hours split between classroom and job site.
duration: 6 to 12 weeks per placement
deadline_text: No closing date posted. The page still lists 2025 summer jobs, so check PYN for new openings.
who_can_apply: Any young person who is in a Philadelphia high school now will be considered. The program is for Philadelphia youth ages 12 to 24.
how_to_apply: Fill out the PYN youth interest form (Google form) and look at the opportunity list. Questions: 267-502-3800.
notes: PYN also runs a PYNtern program.

name: WorkReady VIP (violence prevention paid work program)
pay_detail: $11 an hour starting wage, 120 paid hours.
duration: 6 to 12 weeks per placement
deadline_text: No closing date posted.

how_to_apply: If a program provider already knows you, they send a link and referral code. If not, pick a provider from the map on the PYN page and email their recruiter.
notes: Spots are limited. A job is never promised. PYN suggests you email your chosen provider yourself with a short hello.

name: Youth Navigators, Philadelphia Works and PA CareerLink Philadelphia

notes: This is a guide to programs, not one job. Also links the PHL Career Portal, apprenticeship search and the School District Opportunity Network.

notes: City-wide teen council. The committee form on the current page is an interest form, not confirmed to be the membership application. Ask the office how members are chosen now.

name: Volun-TEENS, Philadelphia Zoo

duration: Not stated

notes: Separate options: Special Events volunteers (13+ for family events) apply through an online form; school groups of grades 9 to 12 can join Boo at the Zoo takeover shifts (those 2026 dates have passed). Docents must be 21+.

name: Teen Volunteer Program at Piedmont Atlanta Hospital
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is a $25 program fee. Uniform shirts are provided.
duration: June 8 to July 30, 2027: at least one shift a week for at least six of the eight weeks
deadline_text: Application period Feb 26 to Mar 12, 2027. Mandatory orientation Monday June 7, 2027. Up to 30 teens accepted.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17 (must be 16 by June 1). A recent graduate can still apply if they are still 17 on June 1. Recent graduates who are 18 go to the college or adult programs. You need a 3.0 GPA or higher and interest in a health career.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Two or more recommendation forms (teacher, counselor, coach or boss, not family). Show you are immune to measles, mumps, rubella and chickenpox, and have a TB test. Send a headshot and parent signatures.
notes: You must go to the required orientation, or you can apply next summer.

name: Teen Volunteer Program, Piscataway Public Library
grades: Grades 6 to 12 (high school volunteers: grades 9 to 12 and at least 14)
pay_detail: Unpaid; earns community service hours
duration: Regularly scheduled volunteer hours after training
deadline_text: Adopt-a-Shelf: the Session 1 application period has ended; Session 2 applications open November 2 (year not stated on the page). High school volunteers attend an orientation session; check the library calendar for dates.
who_can_apply: Piscataway residents only. Grades 6 to 12 and at least 12 years old; high school volunteers must be in grades 9 to 12 and at least 14. Must sign a Teen Volunteer Code of Conduct at training.
how_to_apply: High school: attend a library orientation session with a mandatory training video, then enroll if you meet requirements. Adopt-a-Shelf (grades 6 to 8): apply on the volunteering page when the session opens. Questions: teens@piscatawaylibrary.org (subject line Volunteer).
notes: Latecomers are not admitted to training sessions. Open only to Piscataway residents.

name: Allegheny County Parks Lifeguard
city: Pittsburgh area, PA (Boyce, Settlers Cabin, South and North Park pools)
pay_detail: $16.00 to $18.00 an hour (listed for the summer of 2026)
duration: The full pool season. Exact start and end dates are not stated.
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Your application packet must be on file before you can take a certification class or aquatics test.
who_can_apply: Age 15 or older. You need a current lifeguard certification, or you can take the county course. A background check is required before a final offer.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Lifeguard Employment Application Packet and email it to lifeguards@alleghenycounty.us. Then sign up for a county course to get certified. If you already have a card, sign up for an aquatics test. Call 412-350-2455 with questions.
notes: The county lifeguard course is 2 days with the American Red Cross. It is for ages 15 and up. It costs $250 for residents and $312 for non-residents. You need a physical first. If you get certified through the county and work at least 225 hours at a county pool that season, the $250 fee can be paid back in full. The Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says minors under 18 need a work permit from their school district.

name: Teen Workforce Pathways (Boys & Girls Clubs of Western Pennsylvania)

how_to_apply: Use the Returning Teen or New Teen registration link on the Workforce Pathways page. Or use Register Now at bgcwpa.org/registration. Financial assistance is available. See the Financial Assistance page. Phone: (412) 782-5710. Email: contact@bgcwpa.org.
notes: Confirm first: ages, cost, schedule and whether any work is paid are not on the pages read. The Clubs also run two Club Teen Centers (Downtown and McKeesport).

name: Summer Camp Teen Volunteers (Carnegie Museums)

The Natural History page also lists a Teen Advisory Board with an interest form (https://form.jotform.com/243505851081150); its ages are not stated. The Kamin Science Center teen volunteers are a separate card.

name: City of Pittsburgh Citiparks Lifeguard
org: City of Pittsburgh Department of Parks and Recreation (Citiparks)
pay_detail: $18.00 to $20.76 an hour (2026 posting)
duration: Part-time seasonal. Training starts in April; the end date is not stated.

who_can_apply: At least 15 by June 6, 2026 (the 2026 posting). You must live in the City of Pittsburgh and hold current lifeguard, first aid, AED and CPR certificates. You must pass the Citiparks lifeguard performance exam and a background check.
how_to_apply: Fill out the City of Pittsburgh job application online. It is on governmentjobs.com. Then call the Citiparks Aquatics Office at (412) 323-7928. Ask them about test dates, classes and cards.
notes: The posting says applicants 18 and under with no high school diploma or GED must show a valid work permit before they are hired. It also needs Pennsylvania Act 153 clearance, fingerprints and a medical exam. The job number in 2026 was 26-LG1A-01.

org: Civil Air Patrol, Allegheny County Composite Squadron

notes: The Pennsylvania Wing lists other squadrons in the Pittsburgh area. They are Golden Triangle, Jimmy Stewart, Washington, Beaver Falls and Butler. Ask the wing which is closest to you. The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.

name: CS Scholars

notes: Status is unconfirmed only because the application opening date is not posted; the 2027 deadlines are confirmed on the program pages (the apply portal could not be read). Limited spots. The admission page lists two different dates for this application (February 1 and March 1, 2027); the program page and the deadlines table both say February 1, 2027, so apply by then. Completers may be invited back to AI Scholars.

notes: Status is unconfirmed only because the application opening date is not posted; the 2027 deadlines are confirmed on the program pages (the apply portal could not be read). Expensive; shown so families know the cost and the scholarship route. The three fully funded programs (AI Scholars, CS Scholars, SAMS) cost nothing. Check the cost page again in November 2026 for 2027 prices.

Competitive and limited spots. The page gives no application opening date. Scholars cannot take other summer programs that overlap. Questions: cmu-sams@andrew.cmu.edu.

name: Urban Farmers in Training (UFIT)
pay_detail: $12 an hour, 20 hours a week

deadline_text: 2026 applications ran March 2 to June 5, 2026 and are closed. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 to 18 from surrounding neighborhoods. You must apply through Learn & Earn (Partner4Work).
