notes: Work sites: Shiloh Farm (7209 Thomas Blvd., 15206) and the Grow Pittsburgh office (6587 Hamilton Ave. #2W). The year includes a Garden Youth Summit (2026: July 30). The Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says minors under 18 need a work permit from their school district issuing officer.

name: Pittsburgh Job Corps Center
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.
duration: Not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: No deadline posted. You start by making a MyJobCorps account on the Job Corps website.
who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.

name: Teen Volunteer Program

name: Summer Learn & Earn

A separate Year-Round Learn & Earn (fall, winter, spring work sessions) serves ages 16 to 23 in the City of Pittsburgh but only for people who already finished a summer. notes: Questions go to the volunteer contact on the National Aviary volunteer page.

name: EcoLeader Academy
pay_detail: Free to join. Participants receive a stipend (amount not stated on the page).

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 19 who have finished at least one year of high school. You pick one of two weekly groups (Wednesday or Thursday) and must attend all of the dates.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form on the Phipps page when the next group opens. Use the sign-up form on that page to be notified. Questions go to the high school programs coordinator at amule@phipps.conservatory.org or 412-622-6915 ext. 3804.
notes: The page lists two different dates for the final Youth Garden Summit, so confirm with Phipps. The stipend is not described as a job on the page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Summer Camp Teen Volunteers (Phipps)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. Clearance fees are reimbursed.

The page does not give a form just for teens. Email the volunteer coordinator listed on the Phipps volunteer page to ask. That is Deb Knorr, dknorr@phipps.conservatory.org.
notes: Confirm first. The volunteer page gives no teen deadline or teen form. Ask Phipps for the current age rule and dates before you plan around this.

notes: No research experience is needed. Free PRT bus passes are available. The honorarium is not called a wage on the page. The page's dates (June 28 to July 16) are shorter than 'four weeks', so confirm the length. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Public Health Science Academy
org: University of Pittsburgh School of Public Health
pay_detail: Students who finish receive a $1,000 award at the end. Public transportation support to and from campus is provided, and transportation for field trips.
duration: Four weeks. The 2026 session ran June 22 to July 17, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.
deadline_text: The 2026 application ran Feb 4 to March 14, 2026, and is closed. The 2027 dates are not posted yet. Expect a similar winter to March window.
who_can_apply: Current 10th or 11th graders at a high school in the Greater Pittsburgh area or Western PA. You need a strong interest in science and a GPA of 3.0 or above. You must finish a biology class by the end of the school year. You must commit to the full four weeks.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It has two essays of up to 200 words each. A high school teacher must complete the recommendation form. It is uploaded at the end of the application or emailed to phsa@pitt.edu by the deadline. Incomplete applications are not considered. Applicants are told by email in mid to late March. They confirm by April 1.

Applicants without a computer or reliable internet are encouraged to apply. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. name: Tween and Teen Volunteers and Book Buddies (summer)

name: Teen Advisory Boards (branch libraries)

duration: Not stated

name: Leadership Development Program (LDP)
org: City of Roseville Parks, Recreation and Libraries

notes: The page does not say what day applications opened, only the May 5, 2027 deadline. You pay the course fee only after you are chosen. A separate LDP information sheet is linked on the page.

name: Volunteer at the Roseville Public Library
deadline_text: Rolling.
who_can_apply: Must be 13 or older.
how_to_apply: Complete the online Volunteer Form and a staff member will contact you. (916) 774-5221
notes: The page lists no parent permission rule, tasks, or hours. Call (916) 774-5221 or ask the staff member who contacts you.

name: Round Rock Public Library Teen Advisory Board
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn community service hours and recognition.

deadline_text: The page says no positions are open now. An application form is posted when positions open. No dates are given.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Watch the library volunteer page for the application form. Questions go to Teen Librarian Jane Dance at jdance@roundrocktexas.gov or 512-218-7012.
notes: New members attend an orientation. Members also tidy and shelve on the 2nd floor.

name: Teen Summer Reading Challenge Volunteer, Round Rock Library
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: June 1 to July 31 in 2026

notes: General library teen volunteers must be at least 13. They must give at least 30 hours a year. They must bring a letter from a teacher, coach or a similar adult. If you worked a Summer Reading shift in the past two years, you are asked not to apply.

name: Round Rock Lifeguard Training and Seasonal Aquatics Jobs
org: City of Round Rock Parks and Recreation
pay_detail: Lifeguard pay shown as $15 to $19.50 per hour (from a graphic on the page; a separate rate sheet is the official source). Training costs $215 to $305, or $75 if you sign a full season work commitment. Scholarships are available.
duration: Seasonal summer job. Training classes run November to May.
deadline_text: No application deadline is listed. The 2026 classes ran Mar 16 to May 30, 2026. 2027 class dates are not posted on the page I read.
who_can_apply: Must be 15 or older before the last class. Must pass a swim test: swim 150 yards, tread water 2 minutes, then swim 50 yards, and retrieve a 10 pound object from 7 to 10 feet.
how_to_apply: Sign up for training at roundrockrecreation.com. Then apply for jobs on the city job portal. To get the $75 rate, email the signed Commitment Letter to pardcustomerservice@roundrocktexas.gov. Call 512-218-5540 with questions.
notes: It is smart to apply early. If you pass the class, you get Lifeguard, CPR/AED and First Aid cards. They are good for 2 years. You must come to every class.

name: Research Science Institute (RSI)
org: Center for Excellence in Education with MIT
pay_detail: Free to students
duration: About 7 weeks
deadline_text: RSI 2027 applications are open through 11:59 p.m. on December 11, 2026. No late applications.

how_to_apply: Apply on the CEE site: essays, two or three teacher recommendations, official transcript, and PSAT, SAT, ACT or AP scores.
notes: Extremely selective (the FAQ says under 2.5% are accepted). Held in Cambridge, Massachusetts, so plan for travel. The older FAQ page mentions a $75 application fee with waivers and a minimum age of 16 by July 1, but it also lists a six-week program, so it may be out of date. Confirm with CEE.

name: Teen Volunteer Program at Rush Copley Medical Center
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering

how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application and print and complete the Minor Volunteer Consent Form. If your interests match, they will schedule an interview and registration. Call (630) 978-4826.
notes: No shadowing or observation. The page still has older COVID-19 wording (vaccine proof, medical conditions list), so ask the office what applies today. The page says the process depends on the background check, TB testing, health screening and orientation dates. A background check is for ages 18 and up.

name: Student Summer Volunteer Program at Rush Oak Park Hospital

notes: No shadowing or observation. Applying does not guarantee a spot and does not lead to a job automatically.

name: RYSE Center (youth membership and paid internships)

Pay and ages for each cohort are not stated.

name: Youth volunteers at Sacramento animal shelter
duration: Needing school hours: at least 30 hours of shifts over about 3 months. No school requirement: at least 12 hours on site.

notes: Log hours online and also sign in and out in the paper student binder. Cat shifts need extra training. Court-ordered hours use a separate page.

name: WIOA In-School Youth Program

how_to_apply: Download the application from the page and email or hand it in, or pick up a paper copy at Belle Cooledge Community Center (9:30 am to 4:30 pm). WIOA@cityofsacramento.org
notes: Only for low-income students with at least one listed barrier. You can qualify as low-income through free or reduced lunch, SNAP or TANF, or a qualifying ZIP code. Work experience must start at age 18 or younger.

name: Jr. Rec Aide (JRA)

notes: Only one absence allowed because of the stipend. Waitlist spots are filled until the second week. Classes are in person at a community center. Youth who are 18 must show proof of school attendance. The page says sessions are held throughout the year.

name: Landscape and Learning (L&L) Youth Aide

notes: Fills fast because the window closes at 350 applications. Applications are online only during a recruitment window. Hiring includes getting a work permit. The page also lists a Crew Leader job ($21.83 per hour) that includes driving city vehicles. It states no age rule, so do not assume it is for teens.

You must meet the age rule by the session start date. Only one absence is allowed or you may lose the stipend. Only one session is open for registration at a time.

name: Prime Time Teen (PTT)

notes: Fall sessions are at Evelyn Moore (Mon and Wed) and Clunie (Tue and Thu) Community Centers, 4:30 to 7:00 pm. You must be 13 on the first day. Only one absence is allowed. Graduated high school seniors who are in college do not qualify.

name: Teen volunteers at Sacramento Public Library

name: Sacramento Youth Commission

notes: Appointed by the Mayor and City Council, so not every applicant is picked. The FAQ says the $50 stipend applies to the 1st and 3rd monthly meetings. No experience needed. Seats open at different times; check the Become a Commissioner page. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

name: Sacramento County fire explorer, academy and high school fire pathways list

name: Right Track youth jobs (YJ1 and YJ2 summer internships)

duration: At least 6 months, one 4-hour shift each week
deadline_text: Applications are taken on a rolling basis. Volunteers are trained four times a year. The next onboarding starts with a virtual info session in early 2027.
who_can_apply: People age 16 and up. You need two reference letters to apply and must commit to at least six months.
how_to_apply: Get two reference letters ready. Then fill out the online volunteer application. Training happens four times a year.
notes: No short-term or summer internship spots. Not good for a one-time service-hours project because of the six-month rule.

name: Cabrillo National Monument Volunteers-In-Parks
org: National Park Service, Cabrillo National Monument
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: One-time service days or recurring roles
deadline_text: Group projects are open year-round. No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Group volunteering (3 to 25 people) takes volunteers age 8 and up. The page does not give an age rule for individual volunteers.
how_to_apply: For one-time or individual service, email cabr_volunteers@nps.gov. Groups use the Group volunteering page on the park website.
notes: Ask the park about age rules for each repeat role, since the page does not say.

name: Employ & Empower City Internships
pay_detail: $19.47 to $22.75 per hour, set by education level
duration: Varies by posting. Hiring takes about 6 to 8 weeks.
deadline_text: Internships are posted one at a time. On Oct 9, 2026, six internship postings were listed with closing dates from Oct 14 to Oct 30, 2026.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 30 who are enrolled in a school or training program (show proof). Priority goes to people from communities of concern. You must have the legal right to work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: Pick a posting on the City internship job site. Attach proof that you are enrolled in a school or training program. Then apply. The city strongly urges you to add a resume and cover letter. The job site says to consider unpaid internships too.
notes: Interns are City employees. Interns need a work permit, Social Security Number, background check and ID. The job site says to consider unpaid internships too. Funded by the state Youth Service Corps.

name: Future Civic Leaders
org: City of San Diego (Internship and Work Readiness Program)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Gift card rewards at 40 service hours and a certificate signed by the Mayor at 80 hours.
duration: Weekly online meeting (Mondays 5:30 to 6:30 p.m.) plus one in-person meeting a month
deadline_text: No deadline is listed on the application page.
who_can_apply: Middle and high school students ages 13 to 15 who can come to the meetings. You show interest in service and leadership.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online form linked from the City youth volunteer page. Questions? Write to workreadiness@sandiego.gov.
notes: Only for ages 13 to 15, so a 16 year old is too old. For older teens, see the City paid internships. Confirm the current cycle with workreadiness@sandiego.gov, the contact listed on the City page.

name: Recreation Aide and Pool Guard (City of San Diego Aquatics)
org: City of San Diego Parks and Recreation, Aquatics
pay_detail: Hourly pay is not stated on the page; see the posting on governmentjobs.com.
duration: Flexible hours that work around school and sports
deadline_text: Year-round hiring. Pool Guard hiring events are monthly; Recreation Aide interviews are quarterly.
who_can_apply: Recreation Aide: at least 15 and a half years old. Pool Guard: at least 16 at the time of application, no certification needed.
how_to_apply: Apply for 'Recreation Aide' or 'Pool Guard 1' on the City's governmentjobs.com portal. The City then sends interview and skills-test details.
notes: Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

name: San Diego Youth Commission
org: City of San Diego (Office of Child and Youth Success)
pay_detail: Not stated; this is an advisory board
duration: 2 year term, monthly meetings (currently Saturday mornings at a public library)
deadline_text: The page says some of the 20 seats are unfilled and invites youth to apply. No deadline is listed.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 25 who live in or go to school in the City of San Diego. You must be able to serve a 2 year term and go to monthly in-person meetings.
how_to_apply: Apply on the City boards website. Choose Youth Commission and your seat from the Boards and Seats menu.
notes: Seats are nominated by the Mayor and each Councilmember (2 each). Contact is the Office of Child and Youth Success. The chair's bio on the About page says she first learned of the commission through the Employ & Empower internship.

name: Teen Service Learner
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn community service hours.
duration: Flexible hours, weekdays and Saturdays
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Ask your branch.
who_can_apply: Teens, generally ages 12 to 17. The exact age range varies by branch, so ask your branch.
how_to_apply: Ask a staff member at your San Diego County Library branch how to sign up.
notes: Run by the County library system. It is separate from the City of San Diego Public Library. The page lists no teen requirements. The background check and medical exam it mentions are for adult volunteers. Confirm your branch's age range before going.

name: Cuyamaca College Dual and Concurrent Enrollment
pay_detail: Tuition is waived for concurrent enrollment. You pay minimal fees and buy textbooks.
duration: By semester or session
deadline_text: Start at least one month before the semester or session. No set deadline on the page.
who_can_apply: Students now in high school, in at least 9th grade. You need high school approval and written parent approval before you apply. You can appeal if you do not meet every rule.
how_to_apply: Apply online to become a Cuyamaca student. Then get approval from your high school administrator. A parent or guardian must approve too. Do this every term, before you register.
notes: All classes make a permanent college record, so choose with care. Your high school district decides if the class counts toward graduation.

name: Feeding San Diego Volunteer
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Single shifts; you sign up for dates that work for you
deadline_text: No deadline.
who_can_apply: At food handouts, volunteers must be 14 or older. Anyone 15 or younger needs a chaperone over 18. The Distribution Center takes volunteers who are 6 and up.
how_to_apply: Sign up for shifts through the volunteer page on the Feeding San Diego website. Shifts are posted one month in advance.
notes: Closed-toe shoes are required. Shifts are posted one month ahead.

name: San Diego Fire-Rescue Cadet Program
org: San Diego Fire-Rescue Department (City of San Diego)
pay_detail: Not stated; described as a youth program
duration: Ongoing. A one week Cadet Academy is held each summer.
deadline_text: New cadets are accepted quarterly. No dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21 with at least a 2.0 GPA. The page does not name a city residency rule.
how_to_apply: To get on the waitlist, email sdfdcadets@sandiego.gov. Give your name and date of birth, and say that you want to join.
notes: Phone on the page: 619-643-2505. Pay is not mentioned, so treat it as unpaid until the department says otherwise.

name: San Diego Food Bank Volunteer Shifts
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: One shift at a time. You can come once or on a regular basis.
deadline_text: No deadline. All volunteer visits must be scheduled in advance.
who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 15 can volunteer with a registered adult (18+). Ages 16 and up can sign up on their own. School groups from middle and high school are welcome.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the Food Bank volunteer site, then sign up for open shifts. Under 18 volunteers use the minor waiver, which guardians sign.
notes: Good for a first volunteer experience or school service hours. Shifts are at the Miramar warehouse and the North County site in Vista. Wear closed-toe shoes.

name: La Jolla Playhouse Summer Conservatory
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $500 for Junior Conservatory, $850 for Conservatory. A scholarship application is offered.
duration: 9 days (Junior) or 15 weekdays (Conservatory)
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed Apr 6, 2026. Summer 2027 applications are expected to open on or around Feb 1, 2027. 2027 dates are not set.
who_can_apply: Junior Conservatory is for students going into grades 8 and 9. Conservatory is for students going into grades 10 to 12. To get in, you send a form and two letters of support. You also do an audition.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Have two references send letters. Then go to an in-person audition at the Playhouse. A separate scholarship form is linked from the page.
notes: The page prints 2025 in a few date lines for the 2026 program, so check dates on the page. The Playhouse has a form to get a note when 2027 applications post.

name: Playhouse Teen Council
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the page
duration: One school year (2026/27 first Teen Council meeting is listed for Oct 12, 2026)
deadline_text: 2026/27 applications ran Aug 3 to Sept 4, 2026. Next year is not posted yet; expect a similar late summer window.
who_can_apply: Any San Diego high school student who is a rising 10th to 12th grader.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Teen Council application form during the open window. Applicants were told the result by Sept 18 in 2026.
notes: The page still says applications are now open, but its own deadline of Sept 4, 2026 has passed. Questions: Gia Battista Figueroa (email on the page).

name: Camp Aides (Youth Volunteers)
org: San Diego Natural History Museum (The Nat)
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page says you gain work experience and/or college credit.
duration: Summer camp season; exact dates not stated
deadline_text: Page says recruitment for camp aides begins in May. No 2027 dates posted.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 18.
how_to_apply: See the museum's main volunteer page and Volunteer Application link, or contact the museum at 619-232-3821.
notes: The page gives no application steps beyond pointing to the volunteer application. Ask the museum about the time commitment.

name: Palomar College Concurrent Enrollment for High Schoolers
city: San Marcos, Escondido, Fallbrook and Rancho Bernardo, CA
pay_detail: The $46 per unit tuition is waived for concurrent enrollment. You pay for books and some fees. Dual enrollment at partner high schools is free.
duration: Up to 7 units in fall or spring and 5 units in summer without a petition
deadline_text: No single deadline. Check the Palomar calendar for each term.
who_can_apply: High school students with approval from their high school district and a parent or guardian. Students under 16 also need each instructor to sign an Under 16 form. Home-schooled students need extra forms.
how_to_apply: Get approval from your high school district and a parent. Apply online to Palomar. Fill out the K12 Special Admission Approval Form once. Turn it in at Enrollment Services or email it to admissions@palomar.edu.
notes: Part-time (11 units or fewer) enrollment fee is waived. Everyone pays the mandatory Health Fee and Student Center Fee. The same page lists GEAR UP, Upward Bound and Educational Talent Search for some North County schools.

name: Palomar UC San Diego Health Junior Volunteer
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is a one-time processing fee; the amount is not on the pages read.
duration: 100 hours minimum. Juniors can do a 4-hour shift every week or every other week.
deadline_text: Applications are taken all year.
who_can_apply: Junior volunteers are 16 and 17 years old. A parent or guardian must come to the interview, orientation and TB test. You give a school counselor contact.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Junior Volunteer application online. A parent or guardian must attend the interview, orientation and TB test. Give a school counselor or advisor contact. Screening can take up to six weeks.
notes: The processing fee pays part of the TB screen and background check. It also pays for uniforms and badge parts. You can volunteer at one site at a time, so pick Poway or Escondido, not both. Volunteers in good standing can ask for a letter of recommendation.

name: San Diego Parks and Recreation Volunteer Program
org: City of San Diego Parks and Recreation Department
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: One-time events or regular roles
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Minimum age is 13. Under 13 must come with an adult. Volunteers (including 13 to 17 year olds) who work with minors, seniors or people with disabilities must be fingerprinted and cleared by state law.
how_to_apply: Register on the volunteer sign-up page, then pick events or roles. Fingerprinting is by appointment (619-236-6686) for roles that need it. Wear closed-toe shoes and bring water, a hat and sunscreen.
notes: Not every role needs fingerprints. The page lists Tecolote Nature Center and Tri-Canyon among its chances.

name: San Diego Police Cadet Program
org: San Diego Police Department (City of San Diego)
pay_detail: Described as a voluntary position
duration: Ongoing. You finish a Cadet Academy first, then go to two meetings a month (first and third Tuesday, 6 to 9 p.m.). Time ranges from 4 hours a month to over 40.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Recruiting meetings are held on the second Tuesday of each month at 5 p.m.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21. You need to be a high school graduate or have at least a 2.0 GPA if still in school. You pass a written exam, a character interview and a background check.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Then go to a recruiting meeting at Police Plaza (4020 Murphy Canyon Rd). Bring a government photo ID. The meeting can last up to three hours. It includes a 20 question test.
notes: The activities page describes some activities. One is minor decoy work with detectives. A parent should read the page. You must finish the Cadet Academy first. Then you can become a cadet.

name: Teen Team Program Assistant
org: San Diego Public Library (City of San Diego)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Apply any time through the City volunteer system.
who_can_apply: Teenagers only. The library's general volunteer rule is that volunteers must be at least 13. Annual volunteer training is required.
how_to_apply: Open the library volunteer opportunities link, pick the Teen Team Program Assistant listing, click the information icon, then 'Fill in an Application'. Sign in or create a MyImpact account and submit. If your branch has no listing, email LibraryVolunteer@sandiego.gov.
notes: Applies to City of San Diego library branches only. San Diego County Library is a different system (see the Teen Service Learner card). The page does not say how many hours a week. Background check and mandated reporter training are listed only for volunteers 18 and older.

name: Reality Changers College Town
grades: Grades 8 to 11 (College Apps Academy is for grade 12)
pay_detail: Free for students and families. Not a paid program.
duration: 3 or more hours a week after school, plus summer
deadline_text: Applications are taken all year. All applicants are added to a waitlist, and staff follow up with next steps.
who_can_apply: Students who go to school in San Diego County and will be the first in their family to graduate from a four-year college. You must meet the program entry rules and reapply each year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. You get a confirmation email and staff follow up with next steps.
notes: This is a college-prep program, not a job. It is a good fit for a teen who wants help planning for college and careers. First-generation means neither parent or guardian has a four-year U.S. degree.

name: Research Experience for High School Students (REHS)
org: San Diego Supercomputer Center, UC San Diego
pay_detail: Free to apply. Registration fee is $2,000 if accepted. Full and partial scholarships are available based on need.
duration: 8 weeks, 10 to 20 hours a week (2026 ran June 8 to July 31)
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran Feb 15 to Mar 15, 2026. The 2027 dates are not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Southern California residents in grade 10, 11 or 12 who have finished a semester of high school. You are 16 by June 15 and have a 3.0 GPA or higher. You are college bound. You must come to the final poster session.
how_to_apply: Apply online (free). Mentors read applications and interview students. If you accept, you get a registration link and pay by the end of May unless you get a scholarship.
notes: The page calls it a volunteer internship. Pick project prerequisites carefully. Students may do only one REHS internship per summer. 2027 dates are not posted, so check the page in early 2027.

name: Sharp Grossmont Hospital Junior Volunteer
pay_detail: Unpaid. You buy a uniform shirt for a small cost.
duration: At least 1 year, one shift a week or two a month
deadline_text: As of Oct 9, 2026 the page says it is no longer accepting applicants from the high school class of 2028. That means current 9th and 10th graders (classes of 2029 and 2030) may still apply. No deadline is posted.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 11 who are at least 14, with a 3.0 GPA or higher and a written recommendation from a school counselor. The page says it is not accepting the class of 2028 now.
how_to_apply: Download and print the junior volunteer form. Fill it out and mail it to Volunteer Services. Then go to a 30 minute interview and a 2 hour orientation with a parent or guardian. You also do a TB test and health screening.
notes: The page accepts applications only from grades 9 to 11 and says it is no longer accepting the class of 2028. Call 619-740-4175 to confirm your class year can apply. Mail address is on the page (Volunteer Services, Sharp Grossmont Hospital, PO Box 158, La Mesa, CA 91944).

name: Sharp Memorial and Mary Birch High School Volunteers
org: Sharp Memorial Hospital and Sharp Mary Birch Hospital (Sharp HealthCare)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Benefits listed include a cafeteria discount, meal credit and free parking.
duration: At least 1 year and 100 service hours, with 75 percent attendance
deadline_text: The high school application is closed, and the page does not say when it will reopen. The adult application reopens Oct 19.
who_can_apply: The page has a separate high school student application. The minimum age and any GPA rule are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: When the form opens, submit it. Then go to an in-person info session at Sharp Memorial. After that there is an interview. Onboarding includes a background check and health clearances.
notes: Health clearances include MMR, chickenpox, Tdap, TB blood test, and flu and COVID vaccine or a declination. Check the page for when high school applications reopen.

name: UC San Diego Bioengineering Research Scholars
org: UC San Diego Department of Bioengineering and Division of Extended Studies
city: La Jolla, San Diego, CA (live online)
pay_detail: Tuition $2,700 for the BE-BOAT intro course. Other course prices are on the course pages.
duration: About 7 weeks (Winter 2027 intro course: Jan 9 to Feb 27, 2027)
deadline_text: Winter 2027 application deadline Dec 18, 2026, with a last call through Jan 3, 2027. Space is limited and may fill sooner.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. Entry is by application. The intro course (BE-BOAT) comes first.
how_to_apply: Apply online. You hear back 7 to 10 business days later. Payment is due within 2 weeks of acceptance.
notes: Costs a lot. Scholarships exist for some Research Scholars programs but the scholarship page did not list Bioengineering. Email precollege@ucsd.edu with questions.

name: UC San Diego Health Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: One 4-hour shift a week for at least 100 hours over 6 to 8 months. Summer-only option: about 12 weeks and at least 100 hours.
deadline_text: Year-round application. Summer-only applicants must apply between Mar 1 and Apr 15, and say so on the application.
who_can_apply: Anyone 16 and older. You need two reference responses from people who are not friends or family. You cannot serve where you or a family member has worked.
how_to_apply: Apply online and line up two references. They can be work or school contacts, not friends or family. Then do a virtual interview. Send vaccine records for measles, mumps, rubella and chickenpox. Get a TB test and pass a background check. Finish online training. Then go to an in-person orientation and tour.
notes: You may start 2 to 3 months after applying. Questions: volsvcs@health.ucsd.edu or 619-543-6370. Applications outside the summer window will not be considered for summer-only.

name: UC San Diego Marine Science Research Scholars
org: UC San Diego Division of Extended Studies (with Scripps Institution of Oceanography mentors)
city: La Jolla, San Diego, CA (live online)
pay_detail: Fall 2026 Tier 1 course cost $2,000 in tuition. Scholarships were listed but closed.
duration: About 7 weeks per course (Fall 2026 Tier 1 ran Sept 22 to Nov 12)
deadline_text: Winter 2027 applications are listed as coming soon. The Fall 2026 deadline (Sept 17, 2026) has passed.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 who are at least 14 when the program starts. You finish one Tier 1 course before applying for Tier 2.
how_to_apply: Apply online when a term opens. Students are accepted on a rolling basis and pay within 2 weeks of acceptance.
notes: Price for Tier 2 and Tier 3 was not checked. Email precollege@ucsd.edu with questions.

name: San Diego Workforce Partnership youth career services
pay_detail: Services are free. Some opportunities include paid training or paid on-the-job work experience; rates are not stated.
duration: Varies by program
deadline_text: No deadline. The online application takes about 10 to 15 minutes, then staff contact you about next steps.
who_can_apply: Free career centers. The page says it has helped thousands of 16 to 24 year olds and states no eligibility age, so ask.
how_to_apply: Complete the online program application (10 to 15 minutes). The team follows up about next steps.
notes: The programs page also lists GenAI, workforce support for in-school youth across San Diego County school systems, and EXCEL for in-school and out-of-school young adults in the South Bay; their ages and dates were not checked. Pay and permit rules for under-18 placements are not stated.

name: San Jose Middle College (San Jose City College)
org: San Jose Unified School District with San Jose City College
pay_detail: Free college classes (6 to 9 college credits). The page does not state other costs.
duration: Junior and senior years (the page does not state a fixed length)
deadline_text: Not stated on the San Jose City College page. Ask the Middle College office for the application timeline.
who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors. The application needs an administrator recommendation, a teacher recommendation (core subjects), a parent questionnaire, a student questionnaire and an unofficial transcript, plus a 504 plan if applicable. The page does not say whether students outside San Jose Unified may apply.
how_to_apply: Deliver the application packet (administrator and teacher recommendations, parent and student questionnaires, unofficial transcript) to the Middle College office, Business Building B-107, San Jose City College. Questions: Lisa Canton, lcanton@sjusd.org, 408-298-2191 ext. 3996.
notes: Re-read the SJCC Middle College page on 2026-10-07. The SJUSD Middle College page it links to (https://www.sjusd.org/our-schools/middle-college/nav/) returns 404, so the district's application steps, deadline and selection rules could not be confirmed. Students are responsible for their own transportation. Students from SJUSD can still play sports and join clubs at their home high schools. Confirm the deadline and whether non-SJUSD students can apply with Lisa Canton before applying.

name: San Jose Public Library Teen Volunteers (Teens Reach, Teen Book Reviewer)
deadline_text: Rolling. Each branch has its own Teens Reach sign-up. No single deadline.
who_can_apply: Teens Reach is for ages 13 to 18. You need a strong interest in the library and must go to meetings and join in activities. The library does not list an age for Teen Book Reviewer on its volunteer page, so ask Volunteer Services if you are 12 or younger.
how_to_apply: Teens Reach: find your branch's Teens Reach sign-up on Better Impact (each branch has its own) or ask the branch. Teen Book Reviewer: search for it on Better Impact from the library volunteer page, and attend an orientation (on-site or virtual). Questions: volunteer.sjpl@sjlibrary.org or volunteer@sjlibrary.org, or call Volunteer Services at 408-808-2181.
notes: The volunteer page lists both Teens Reach and Teen Book Reviewer as teen roles, and links Teens Reach to its own page at sjpl.org/teensreach, so this one card covers both. Teens Reach meeting times differ by branch; check your branch's page. TeenHQ is at the King Library, 150 E San Fernando.

name: San Jose Works
org: City of San Jose (work2future and Mayor's Gang Prevention Task Force)
pay_detail: Rate not posted (checked 2026-10-07)
deadline_text: No deadline posted on the city pages. Apply any time with the online youth application.
who_can_apply: San Jose residents. The paid work experience is for ages 14 to 18 who face barriers to employment. Job help (resumes, job fairs) is open to ages 16 to 29. Free to join.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Youth Application on the San Jose Works page. A staff member contacts you afterward.
notes: Pay rate and placement dates are not posted on the pages I read. The paid work experience is for youth 14 to 18 with barriers to employment; placement is not guaranteed. The FAQ says job help is free for San Jose residents 16 to 29. Under 18 needs a work permit.

name: San Jose Youth Commission and Youth Advisory Council
duration: Two-year term
deadline_text: Youth Advisory Council (open now): no deadline posted. Youth Commission (closed): recruitment is closed, no reopening date posted.
who_can_apply: Youth Advisory Council: ages 13 to 19 who live in a San Jose City Council district. Youth Commission: ages 14 to 20. You must live in the district you represent. The term is two years (up to two terms). It meets 4th Monday at 6:30 p.m.
how_to_apply: Fill out the District Youth Advisory Application for the YAC. A Youth Commissioner contacts you within about two weeks.
notes: Page is hosted by the library. Some council districts are unavailable or paused. YAC members earn community service hours. Pay not mentioned.

name: San Leandro Library Teen Volunteers
duration: At least 4 months
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications are closed. The page says to check back in November 2026. Summer applications open in mid March, per the summer page.
who_can_apply: Teens in grades 9 to 12 who can commit to a regular weekly shift for at least 4 months. You must attend one orientation each school year.
how_to_apply: Apply online, attend an in-person orientation at the Main Library, sign the waiver, and commit to a regular shift. Returning volunteers must use their old MyImpact login.
notes: The page mentions both 2026 and January 2026 timing, so confirm the next cycle with the Teen Librarian. It also says a teen should handle their own emails, because the program is meant to prepare you for a first job.

name: San Leandro Youth Advisory Commission
org: City of San Leandro Recreation and Parks
deadline_text: The page does not say when applications open.
who_can_apply: The page does not state ages or grades. Ask the Recreation office.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Call Recreation at 510-577-3462 or email SLRec@SanLeandro.Org.
notes: Meets at 6 p.m. on the first Tuesday of the month at the Marina Community Center, 15301 Wicks Blvd. Events listed for the 2025-2026 term include the MLK Celebration and the Cherry Festival and Parade.

name: Jobs for Youth (County of San Mateo)
org: County of San Mateo Human Resources
pay_detail: Workshops and job board are free. Twenty $2,000 scholarships each year. Pay for the county summer internship is not stated on the pages I read.
duration: County summer internship: June to August, about 8 to 10 weeks, 20 to 40 hours a week
deadline_text: Membership: register any time. Summer internship: 2026 applications are closed; the page says next summer opens early 2027 (no date posted). Scholarship deadline not stated.
who_can_apply: San Mateo County youth ages 14 to 21 can join. The county summer internship is only for members ages 18 to 21. You must attend a 1 hour job prep workshop before using the job board.
how_to_apply: Register as a student member on jobsforyouth.org, attend the 1 hour job prep workshop, then use the job board. For the internship you also attend a mandatory orientation.
notes: Teens under 18 can use the workshops and job board but not the county internship. Phone 650-599-7215, email jobsforyouth@smcgov.org. Must be a San Mateo County resident for the internship.

name: San Mateo County Libraries Teen Volunteers
duration: 6 months or 1 semester
deadline_text: Ongoing. Openings vary by branch and there may be a waiting period.
who_can_apply: Age 14 or older. Minimum commitment 6 months or one semester. A free background check is required at 16 and older (takes 3 to 6 weeks).
how_to_apply: Pick a branch and apply for a role on Better Impact through the library volunteer page, or email volunteer@smcl.org.
notes: The page did not list a Teen Advisory Board. Roles are set by branch, and there may be a wait for an opening. Apply for your own branch (13 locations).

name: SPARK High School Internship
org: Sanford Burnham Prebys Medical Discovery Institute
pay_detail: Described as fully paid; the page does not state an amount.
duration: 6 weeks, starting mid-June
deadline_text: Next application dates not posted on the page. Use the Request Info form or email the program director.
who_can_apply: California high school students who are at least 16 at the mid-June start. Preference goes to students living in San Diego or Imperial County. A few spots are reserved for San Diego MESA Alliance students.
how_to_apply: Use the 'Request Info' form on the SPARK page, or contact Program Director Sanjeev Ranade, PhD at cirmsparkinternship@sbpdiscovery.org.
notes: Confirm the current deadline before planning; the official page lists none. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

name: City of Santa Ana Student Intern
org: City of Santa Ana Human Resources
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page
duration: Not stated. Interns keep their spot by sending proof of school enrollment and their GPA after each semester.
deadline_text: The city recruits interns about once a year or as needed. No dates are listed on the page.
who_can_apply: People currently enrolled in high school who can get a work permit. The page does not give a minimum age or a city residency rule.
how_to_apply: Check the city job site for internship openings and apply there. If none are open, check back later.
notes: Pay and hours are not stated. The job list loads by script, so open internships could not be checked on Oct 9, 2026. Other levels on the page are for college students.

name: City of Santa Ana Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: Varies by role
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Anyone age 12 and older. Under-18 volunteers use the minor waiver form. TB test results must be submitted as part of the application process.
how_to_apply: Fill out the forms in the Volunteer Handbook. Then send a volunteer form on the city volunteer page with the forms attached. Roles with children need extra forms.
notes: Ages 18 and up also do an online background check. Open roles were not listed on the program page.

name: Santa Ana Youth (SAY) Employment Program
org: Santa Ana WORK Center (City of Santa Ana)
pay_detail: Paid. The pay rate is not stated on the pages read.

The interest form is for a reopening notice. The main page says applications are open. The interest page says the program is closed to new applications.

name: Santa Ana Zoo Volunteers (including Zoo Buddies)
org: Santa Ana Zoo (City of Santa Ana)

how_to_apply: Long-term volunteers and Zoo Buddies apply with the online volunteer application on the zoo page. Short-term volunteers contact the zoo through its Contact Us page. The zoo does not accept walk-up volunteers.
notes: Short-term needs the City of Santa Ana one-time volunteer waiver. Long-term needs the city volunteer application, a TB test and a background check. The City of Santa Ana volunteer page says volunteers under 18 must complete a minor waiver form. The Santa Ana library teen volunteer program was not listed because the only page found was from 2021.

notes: Confirm first: the dog and cat roles were full when checked, and the page gives two different time commitments. Younger volunteers need a parent or guardian to volunteer with them.

org: Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History

deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications opened April 1 and were due April 30, 2026. Training was May 16-17, 2026. Next cycle dates are not posted.

how_to_apply: Fill in the online VolunTEEN application. Contact Haylee Rosso at hrosso@sbnature2.org or 805-682-4711 ext. 170.
notes: Dates shown are the 2026 cycle. Expect applications to reopen around April 1, 2027 (the page did not say).

name: Parks and Recreation Seasonal Jobs (lifeguard, camp staff)
org: City of Santa Barbara Parks and Recreation

Under-18 workers need a work permit from their school district. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

name: Teen Volunteering and Teen Advisory Board (Santa Barbara Public Library)

how_to_apply: Online application form (linked from the library news post).
notes: Meets at Central Library, 40 E. Anapamu St. Posted October 4, 2026, so the deadline is close. Supported by a federal library grant.

name: Dual Enrollment (Santa Barbara City College)
pay_detail: Applying to SBCC is free. High-school-based courses cost nothing. For online and campus courses, enrollment fees are waived but students pay student fees and textbooks.

notes: Your school counselor or College and Career Center can help choose courses.

name: Sea Center Volunteers (Ty Warner Sea Center)

who_can_apply: Anyone age 11 and up. Volunteers 11 to 13 must volunteer with a parent or guardian. Aquarist volunteers must be 14 or older and have done 48 hours of service first. Commit to one shift a week for at least four months.

notes: Counts for the community service hours needed to graduate from high school in Santa Barbara Unified (per the Museum). Shifts are 9:45-12:45, 12:30-3:30 or 3:00-5:00.

name: Research Mentorship Program (UCSB Summer Sessions)
grades: 10th or 11th grade (outstanding 9th graders considered case by case)
pay_detail: 2026 cost page (the 2027 price is not posted): commuter $5,675 total ($75 application fee + $1,000 deposit + $5,600 tuition and program fees); residential $13,274 total (adds $7,599 housing and meals). A limited number of need-based scholarships exist, with priority for California residents.

notes: Competitive. Costs shown are the 2026 figures because the 2027 cost page was not updated. Residential students live on campus and housing is billed by Summer Discovery. Contact: precollege@summer.ucsb.edu.

name: Summer Research Academies (UCSB Summer Sessions)
pay_detail: 2026 cost page (the 2027 price is not posted): commuter $3,475 total ($75 application fee + $900 deposit + $3,400 tuition and program fees); residential $9,874 total (adds $6,399 housing and meals). A limited number of need-based scholarships exist, with priority for California residents.

notes: Costs shown are the 2026 figures because the 2027 cost page was not updated. The younger, shorter and cheaper of the two UCSB pre-college programs. Contact: precollege@summer.ucsb.edu.

notes: The City's recruitment page lists Youth Council interview dates but this check did not confirm which seats are open this round, so call Nicole Morgan. The City also has a one-year Youth Intern seat on some boards and commissions (nominated by a high school principal).

name: Santa Barbara Zoo Jobs for Teens (Guest Experience Specialist and seasonal)

Students with no prior work experience: 'We will consider your application for our entry level positions.'

notes: The Employment Listings page was not read, so check whether any openings are posted now. Under-18 workers need a work permit from their school district. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

city: San Diego County, CA (La Jolla, Encinitas, San Diego, Chula Vista)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

duration: At least 6 months and 100 hours
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Applications are accepted online year-round, and the office is looking for weekday morning or afternoon shifts.

name: ANEW Construction Trades Training (teens with disabilities)
city: Washington (site not stated on the page)
pay_detail: Paid training. $500 completion stipend.

deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed. The 2026 application deadline was April 30, with notice in early June. No 2027 dates are posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18 with an IEP, a 504 plan or other proof of a disability. Tacoma Public Schools students and other students can join.
how_to_apply: Fill out the ANEW form linked on the Tacoma Public Schools summer credential page. Contact Stacy Kidd, who is listed on the page.
notes: The Tacoma Public Schools page says this is not an official Jobs 253 program. ANEW location is Lincoln High School per the page. The page lists Cohort 2 as July 13 to 16 but also says M to F, so confirm dates with ANEW. Work permit rule not stated.

name: Youth Ocean Advocates
grades: 9 to 12 (high school, Running Start, GED or homeschool)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program. The page does not mention a cost.
duration: One school year or one summer; at least 8 activities of about 3 to 5 hours each; can stay until the summer after senior year
deadline_text: School Year 2026-27 Currents interest form is closed. The page says to check back in February 2027 for the Summer 2027 interest form (its general timeline says January; confirm with the Aquarium). Info sessions run over Zoom in March (summer) and September (school year).
who_can_apply: Students enrolled in grades 9 to 12 in a high school, Running Start, GED or homeschool program when they apply. Tides is the easiest level (any high school-aged person); Currents is the hands-on volunteer level.
how_to_apply: Attend a required online info session, then complete the application, then interview. Accepted teens do training before starting shifts. Questions: YOA@seattleaquarium.org.
notes: The page says its timeline is rough and may change. Washington L&I says its child labor rules 'only apply to minor employees, not volunteers.'

name: YouthForce Teen Jobs
org: Boys & Girls Clubs of King County
pay_detail: Paid internships. Pay amount not stated.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No dates posted. The page has an Apply button for TeamWork internships and a resume help form.
who_can_apply: Ages are not stated on the YouthForce page. Contact the program to ask.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply button for the TeamWork Internship or the Contact Us buttons on the YouthForce page. Call (206) 436-1843 if urgent.
notes: The page does not give ages, pay amounts, or an application window. Ask about age and school rules before applying. Work permit rule not stated.

name: Voices in Science: Burke-ology (high school)
pay_detail: Free
duration: Sessions run by topic (a spring 2026 session studied paleobotany); dates are posted on the Burke e-newsletter
deadline_text: Applications for the spring 2026 session are closed. Future dates are not posted; the Burke asks teens to join its Youth and Family Programs e-newsletter.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. Priority goes to teens with limited access to STEM role models or science resources.
how_to_apply: Apply online when a new session opens (see the Burke-ology page). Join the e-newsletter for dates.
notes: Not paid. The page lists no meeting dates for the session; the e-newsletter is the way to get them.

name: Seattle Children's Hospital Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get a badge and free on-site parking.
duration: Most shifts are 3 hours on the same day and time every week; at least 6 months in a row (check each role)
deadline_text: Applications open each March, July and November and stay open until positions are filled. The site lists the next open date (not read).
who_can_apply: People 16 and over for some positions and 18 and over for others. You must meet the minimum age when you apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online during an open period (you have one hour to finish), complete online training and forms within 2 weeks, do a 1-hour virtual group interview, then accept a placement. Onboarding includes a Washington State background check, an in-person health screening and a 90-minute orientation. Email VolunteerServices@seattlechildrens.org or call 206-987-4655.
notes: The youth service projects page (for ages under 16, such as donation drives or junior guilds) still carries a COVID-era notice, so it may be out of date. Nearly all shifts are weekdays starting between 9am and 2pm. Washington L&I says its child labor rules 'only apply to minor employees, not volunteers.'

name: Research Training Program for High School Students
pay_detail: Free. A stipend is paid to cover transportation and meals (amount not read).
duration: 4 weeks, weekdays 8:30 am to 3 pm (2026: July 13 to Aug 7)
deadline_text: The 2026 application closed March 8, 2026 (letters due March 29). The page says to check back in late 2026 for summer 2027.
who_can_apply: Students in grade 10 or 11 who live close enough to travel to downtown Seattle. You need no research experience. You must have a Social Security Number or ITIN to take part.
how_to_apply: Apply online and send a letter of support. You must go to an orientation in person. In 2026 it was May 21, 4 to 5:30 p.m.
notes: Competitive: the 2026 lab has capacity for 24 students. The 2026 stipend is $2,000 to cover transportation and meals, and the IRS treats it as reportable income. Not a medical program and no patient contact. Work permit rule not stated.

name: Youth Voice Research Liaison Program
pay_detail: $200 training stipend
duration: Four 1.5-hour training sessions (the 2025 training day was a Saturday, Nov. 1, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.), then monthly 1-hour hybrid sessions and consultations through the year
deadline_text: No application cycle for 2026-27. The next cycle is 2027-28 and dates are not posted. (The 2025-26 deadline was Sept 1, 2025.)
who_can_apply: Students now in grades 10 to 12. Grades 10 and 11 go first. You must have taken at least one science course. You must live close enough to travel to downtown Seattle. You need a device with internet.
how_to_apply: Online application when the next cycle opens. Check the program page.
notes: Hybrid (virtual and in person). Each research consultation also has a stipend, amount not stated. Breakfast and lunch are provided at the in-person training; students arrange their own transportation. Work permit rule not stated.

name: Fred Hutch Summer High School Internship Program (SHIP)
grades: Entering senior year (the page also says 'between 11th and 12th grade')
pay_detail: Paid internship; the amount is not stated on the page.
duration: 8 weeks full time (2026: June 22 to Aug 14)
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. The page says information on the 2027 program will be posted in November 2026.
who_can_apply: High school students entering senior year who are 16 or older by the program start. You need strong science interest. You must live in Greater Seattle or nearby. Out-of-state and international students are not accepted. You must be free for all eight weeks and able to do a Zoom interview.
how_to_apply: Online application with short essays, email addresses for two references (they get a recommendation link after you submit), a PDF transcript and a PDF resume. Applicants must be able to attend a Zoom interview with the selection committee.
notes: Highly competitive and designed for students without much research experience. Fred Hutch does not provide or arrange housing, and interns arrange their own transportation. In Washington there is no permit the teen carries: the employer must hold a minor work permit endorsement, and a parent/guardian (and the school during the school year) signs a parent authorization form (Parent Authorization for Summer Work if hired during summer break only) before the minor starts.

name: Henry Teen Art Collective
pay_detail: Free
duration: Weekly meetings through the school year
deadline_text: Dates for this year are not posted on the pages read. The only call for applications found was for 2023-24 (deadline Oct 10, 2023), so check the Henry teen page.
who_can_apply: High school students in the Seattle area who care about modern art.
how_to_apply: Submit the Call for Applications form on the Henry teen page when it is open.
notes: The teen page lists ages 14 to 18 but the application page found is old (2023). The page does not state cost; confirm cost and the current cycle before relying on it.

name: History Lab
pay_detail: $150 stipend for the work
duration: 2 weeks, Monday to Friday 10 am to 4 pm (2026: July 27 to Aug 7)
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was May 22, 2026 and has passed. The page says to check back in spring 2027.
who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 10 to 12 in the school year after the summer. Only six spots. You do not need to be a history fan.
how_to_apply: The page says the 2026 deadline has passed. Check back in spring 2027 for information about next year's session (details on the History Lab page).
notes: Very small group (6 teens). Based at MOHAI with some field trips. Work permit rule not stated.

name: Youth Volunteer (ages 16 to 17)
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: The museum asks for 8 hours a month; hours vary by role
deadline_text: Roles are recruited by season. No single deadline. Browse current roles and apply online.
who_can_apply: The page says anyone age 16 and above can volunteer. Youth use the Youth Volunteer Application. One reference is required (the Youth Reference Form). Not all roles are open to youth.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth (16-17) Volunteer form. Attach the Youth Reference Form. The Volunteer Office reviews it and may set up an interview. New volunteers go to an orientation.
notes: Exact museum address is not on the page read. The page does not state an upper age limit of 17; max_age is kept at 17 only because the card needs an integer, so confirm with the Volunteer Office (volunteers@museumofflight.org). Not a paid job.

name: Career Explorations (Mentorship and Internship)
pay_detail: Mentorship: $300 stipend if you attend all 4 Saturdays. Internship: Seattle minimum wage, listed as $21.30 per hour in 2026.
duration: Mentorship: 4 Saturdays (28 hours), offered 5 times a year. Internship: 8 summer weeks, 20 hours a week.
deadline_text: Page says mentorship applications opened in August 2026. Mentorship starts the first Saturday of October, November, February, March and April. No close date stated.
who_can_apply: Mentorship is for ages 13 to 21. The paid internship is for ages 15.5 to 21 and requires finishing the mentorship first. An E-13 form is required under 18.
how_to_apply: Apply online for the mentor program. Links are on the page. Go to all four Saturdays. Then apply and interview for the summer internship. You must apply again each year.
notes: Free to join. Food and supplies are provided. Mentorship location rotates around Seattle (North, Central, Southeast, Southwest). Interns can return for up to 3 years. Work permit rule not stated on the page.

name: Seattle Parks and Recreation Lifeguard
pay_detail: Listed on the Parks summer jobs page as 'starts at $26.92' (the unit is not stated on the page).
duration: Summer-only at beaches and outdoor pools, or year-round at indoor pools
deadline_text: The last posting closed June 16, 2026. The Aquatics page says Temporary/Intermittent Lifeguards are hired year-round, even when no posting is active.
who_can_apply: Seattle Parks summer jobs are open to ages 16 and up (18 and up for some positions). Lifeguards need a current American Red Cross Lifeguarding, First Aid and CPR/AED certification. The Red Cross course requires you to be at least 15 on or before the last class. You must also pass a swim test.
how_to_apply: Get Red Cross certified. Then apply on GovernmentJobs.com when a listing is active, or email an Aquatic Application (or resume and cover letter) to parksaquatics@seattle.gov, or give it to the Aquatic Center Coordinator at any Seattle indoor pool. Hired lifeguards pass a background check, a physical and the NW Lifeguard Test. Call 206-684-4078.
notes: Red Cross certifications last 2 years. The cost of the Red Cross course is not stated on the Parks pages. Seattle Parks is a municipal employer; Washington L&I says state and municipal governments are not subject to Washington's child labor rules (federal rules still apply).

name: Teen Late Night Internship
pay_detail: City of Seattle minimum wage, listed as $21.30 per hour in 2026.
duration: Two 6-month cohorts a year: January to June and June to December
deadline_text: Applications for the January to June cohort open in December. Applications for the June to December cohort open in May. Exact close dates are not stated.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 18 and in grades 6 to 12. You must first finish at least one cohort of the Youth Leadership Program (40 hours in a quarter).
how_to_apply: Finish the Youth Leadership Program first. Then apply when the window opens. You need a Participant E-13 form for internships. Contact the Late Night and Youth Leadership Coordinator listed on the page.
notes: Paid City of Seattle intermittent employee job. Sites include Bitter Lake, Garfield, Meadowbrook, Rainier Beach, Southwest and Van Asselt. Spaces are limited. The page does not mention a work permit.

name: Teen Summer Musical
pay_detail: Cost $350 for ages 13 to 15 ($400 for ages 9 to 12) but participants get a stipend: $599 for ages 13 to 15. Ages 16 to 18 are paid minimum wage ($21.30 per hour in 2026) every 2 weeks.
duration: 2026: rehearsals June 29 to Aug 27, shows Aug 28 to 30
deadline_text: 2026 auditions were April 17 and 18. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 9 to 18, aimed at youth of color. Auditions are held each spring.
how_to_apply: Audition in the spring. Contact the director listed on the page for sign-up details.
notes: Breakfast and lunch are provided. The page says costs are paid by ages 9 to 15 and stipends are paid at the end. Work permit rule not stated.

name: Seattle Parks Youth Employment and Service Learning: Pre-Employment Training
pay_detail: After finishing the training you may earn a $300 stipend or Service Learning credit toward high school graduation. Internship pay is not stated on the page.
duration: 7 weeks, 14 hours total, offered each Fall, Winter and Spring quarter
deadline_text: Offered each Fall, Winter and Spring quarter. The page does not list current dates, so email to ask.
who_can_apply: Pre-Employment Training is for ages 13 to 18, and you can take it once every 2 years. It is the prerequisite for Parks paid internships (Teen Late Night, Summer, Community Learning Centers), which are for ages 15 to 21.
how_to_apply: Email PKS_Teen_Employment@seattle.gov (phone 206-684-4575) for details and to apply. The page also lists career readiness workshops (resumes, mock interviews, food handler permit help) at Teen Life Centers and community centers.
notes: Youth may do one paid internship at a time. Seattle Parks is a municipal employer; Washington L&I says state and municipal governments are not subject to Washington's child labor rules (federal rules still apply). The page also mentions free college tours for Seattle Public Schools students in grades 9 to 12.

name: Summer Youth Employment Program
city: Seattle, WA (serves SW and SE Seattle and South King County)
grades: Entering 9th grade (fall 2026) through high school seniors (Class of 2030)
pay_detail: Stipend paid after successful completion. 2026 page does not state the amount (older SafeFutures pages said $1,000).
duration: 6 weeks, July 2 to Aug 14 in 2026, Monday to Thursday, 12 pm to 6 pm
deadline_text: 2026 applications opened in April 2026. Close date not stated. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. Grades: entering 9th grade (fall 2026) through high school seniors. Selected teens must give a copy of a Social Security card and complete a W-9.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form linked on the SafeFutures internship page. If you are picked, you have 2 business days to say yes.
notes: Very competitive: the page accepts 20 applicants. The page URL says 2023 but the content is the 2026 program. The 2026 page states no stipend amount. Work permit rule not stated.

name: The New Guard (teen arts leaders)

notes: The page says there is no cost to participate and all New Guardians receive monthly stipends (amount not stated). Its only year reference is 2025-26, so confirm the program is running and the cycle dates before applying. Work permit rule not stated.

name: TeenTix Newsroom
pay_detail: The page says writers are paid for their writing. The amount is not stated. You also get free press tickets to the events you review.
duration: September to June
deadline_text: The page does not give application dates or say whether applications are open. It refers to the 2026-2027 season. Check the TeenTix Program Applications page.

how_to_apply: Check the TeenTix Program Applications page to see the current round. The page is teentix.org/programs/apply.
notes: The Newsroom runs from September to June on the school year schedule. It is good for building a writing portfolio. Ask TeenTix how much writers are paid.

name: Changemakers in Computing
org: University of Washington Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering
grades: Washington high school students in 10th or 11th grade when applying (rising juniors and seniors)
pay_detail: Free. Every mentee gets a $1,200 stipend; lunch and materials are provided. No housing, and bus passes are not provided.
duration: 4 weeks, Monday to Thursday, about 9am to 3pm (2026: July 6 to 30)
deadline_text: 2026 cohort: applications opened March 4 and closed April 1, 2026 (11:59pm PT); decisions April 27; orientation May 16. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Washington state residents enrolled in a Washington high school in 10th or 11th grade. No coding experience needed. The program aims to include economically disadvantaged and future first-generation college students; the home page says it is open to all rising juniors and seniors at Washington state high schools.
how_to_apply: Apply online by the deadline (every application submitted on time is reviewed equally). Questions: cic@cs.washington.edu.
notes: Students must be able to get to the UW campus on their own. Absences are limited: after four absences students are dismissed. The stipend is described as a stipend, not a wage. Paid work for people under 18 in Washington needs a parent and school authorization form (the employer holds the Minor Work Permit). See permit.html?state=wa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Engineering Academy
org: University of Washington College of Engineering
grades: 10 or 11 (during the school year before the summer)
pay_detail: Free
duration: 1 week, Monday to Friday, 10 am to 4 pm (2026: July 20 to 24)
deadline_text: The 2026 application is closed. The page says the 2027 application will open in March.
who_can_apply: Any Washington state high school sophomore or junior in the 2025-2026 school year can apply. You need no engineering experience. You get yourself to and from the UW Seattle campus.
how_to_apply: Apply online when it opens in March 2027.
notes: Free of cost to participants. The page is an introductory program for students curious about engineering. Work permit rule not stated.

name: Business and Leadership Program (UW Foster School of Business)
org: University of Washington Foster School of Business with Summer Springboard
pay_detail: Commuter tuition $4,498 (lunch, a course, excursions, 9am to 5pm Monday to Friday). Residential adds $3,000. Commuters can join weekend excursions for $125 per day. Financial aid is not mentioned on the page.

deadline_text: No deadline stated; 'spaces are limited.' The only session listed was July 5 to 17, 2026. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students (page lists rising 10th, 11th and 12th graders and graduating seniors; no age range stated). No business experience required.
how_to_apply: Apply through partner Summer Springboard's online portal (Apply now link on the program page). Program questions go to the program contact listed on the page.
notes: Expensive paid pre-college program from a real university. The page says students can attend both experiences during a single extended stay, but it does not name a one-week Business Startup Bootcamp.

name: UW Summer Sessions for High School Students
pay_detail: $80 nonrefundable application fee plus UW Summer Sessions tuition (amount not read; see the UW tuition page).
duration: Summer quarter (2026 started June 22)
deadline_text: The page gives 2026 steps (eighth grade completed by June 30, 2026; summer began June 22, 2026). Its calendar lists February 2027 as when the Time Schedule and application open for 2027, with no exact date.
who_can_apply: U.S. high school students who have finished eighth grade or equivalent by June 30 of the summer. If under 18 on the first day, you and a parent must sign an Under 18 form.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the Summer Sessions form. Pay the $80 fee. Send the Under 18 form signed by you and a parent. Then sign up for courses once sign up opens.
notes: Costs real money and registration is first come, first served. Not a job or internship.

name: YouthCAN
pay_detail: Free. Students get a museum membership.
duration: After school, Wednesdays 4 to 6 p.m. The page gives no date for the group show.
deadline_text: No dates posted. The page says registration typically opens in the spring and is first come, first served. Email the museum to ask about info sessions.
who_can_apply: Anyone ages 13 to 19. All art levels welcome. Capacity is 15 students, first come, first served.
how_to_apply: Registration is first come, first served. Email youthcan@wingluke.org to ask about info sessions.
notes: Only 15 spots.

name: Woodland Park Zoo Teen Ambassador Volunteer Program
grades: Entering 10th to 12th grade in the fall of the program year (2026 page)
pay_detail: Active teen volunteers receive a $300 summer stipend to help with transportation, lunches and shoes. No participation fee is listed.
duration: June to September: orientation day, at least 7 of 10 Wednesday meetings (3:30 to 6:30 pm), 20 volunteer hours between June 29 and Sept 6 (2026 dates)
deadline_text: 2026 cohort: application deadline Friday, March 27, 2026, 5:00 pm; Q&A sessions in March; interviews mid-April; decisions early May. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 10 to 12. No prior experience required. The teen page does not state a minimum age; 15 teen volunteers were taken in 2026.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application by the deadline. Email teenambassadors@zoo.org for help. Sign up for recruitment updates at zoo.org/volunteer.
notes: The zoo's general volunteer program has its own rules (at least 16, one-year commitment, applications opening January 2027); those do not appear on the teen page. Applicants who identify with autism or ADHD can get application and interview support from Canopy Neurodiversity Foundation. Paid work for people under 18 in Washington needs a parent and school authorization form (the employer holds the Minor Work Permit). See permit.html?state=wa for the exact permit and steps.

name: Seattle Youth Commission
pay_detail: Unpaid. No fees. Can count toward Seattle Public Schools service hours.
duration: Two-year term; monthly hybrid meetings on the 4th Saturday of each month, 9 to 11 am, at City Hall
deadline_text: Applications are paused. Email the commission to be told when it reopens. No dates posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 19 who live in Seattle or go to school in Seattle. Two-year term. Parent or guardian consent is needed if under 18.
how_to_apply: Email SeattleYouthCommission@seattle.gov to hear when applications reopen. Then apply. If you are under 18, add the parent consent form.
notes: Not a paid job. Good for civic and government interest. The page does not list a deadline.

name: Seattle Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
org: City of Seattle Human Services Department
pay_detail: Internship: at least Seattle's minimum wage, listed as $21.30 per hour. Learn & Earn Foundations: $325 stipend at the end of each module. Pathways: monthly stipend, amount not stated.
duration: Internship about 6 weeks (July 6 to Aug 18, 2026). Foundations: October 2026 to March 2027 (tentative), 2-hour weekly sessions.
deadline_text: 2026 internship applications ran March 18 to May 5, 2026 (closed). Learn & Earn Foundations 2026-27 applications ran Aug 11 to Sept 25, 2026 (closed). 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Age 16 to 24 at the start of the program (you can apply at 15 if you will be 16 by the start date). You must live in Seattle or attend Seattle Public Schools or Seattle Colleges, and household income must be at or below 80% of Area Median Income (for example $81,700 for 1 person, $116,650 for 4).
how_to_apply: Create an account and complete the online application at youthconnect.powerappsportals.us (the page links a help guide). The 250 internship spots are chosen by lottery. Pathways requires finishing SYEP Foundations or passing the Assessment of Skill.
notes: Proof of authorization to work in the U.S. is required for the internship, and an SSN or ITIN is needed to receive stipends and take part. The SYEP page does not mention work permits. Placements include City departments, which Washington L&I says are exempt from state child labor rules ('Public entities, including state and municipal governments, are not subject to Washington's child labor rules'; federal rules still apply), and private businesses and nonprofits, which are not exempt, so ask your placement about the parent/school authorization form. Questions: SYEP@seattle.gov or 206-386-1375.

name: 826 Valencia Youth Programs
grades: Programs for ages 6 to 18; stipended roles for grades 8 to 12
pay_detail: Free programs; some leadership roles are stipended (amounts not posted)
duration: Varies
deadline_text: No dates posted. Check the 826 Valencia program calendar.

how_to_apply: Check the calendar on the 826 Valencia site or contact a Writing Center.
notes: All 826 Valencia programs are free, and most students join through partner schools. The stipended Youth Leadership Advisory Board (grades 8 to 12) and Black Literary Achievement Club are listed on the SFPL page; the stipend amount is not posted.

name: Breakthrough Leadership Program (BLP)

deadline_text: The summer 2026 application is closed. The page says the summer 2027 application launches in early 2027; exact dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Any current high school student in grades 9 to 12. Preference goes to students in Breakthrough now. It also goes to people who are or were Breakthrough volunteers.
how_to_apply: Fill in the notify form on the BLP page to hear when the summer 2027 application opens.
notes: Breakthrough's separate Teaching Fellow job is a paid summer teaching residency with housing for people from outside SF and does not say it is for high schoolers, so it is not listed here. Located at 350 Masonic Ave.

name: Careers in Science (CiS) Intern Program
pay_detail: Paid above minimum wage (rate not posted)
duration: 2 to 3 years through graduation
deadline_text: Applications are closed. The page says to check back in February 2027; closing date not posted.
who_can_apply: Current 9th or 10th graders at an SFUSD school, with a 2.5 GPA and a C or higher in science and math, authorized to work in the US, able to commit 2 to 3 years through high school, and able to get to the Academy after school and on Saturdays.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the window opens in February 2027. Contact CiS@calacademy.org.
notes: SFUSD students only. Sign up for the Academy's Youth Programs mailing list to hear when applications open. Questions: CiS@calacademy.org.

name: CCSF Dual Enrollment (free college classes)
org: City College of San Francisco and SFUSD
pay_detail: Free
duration: By semester
deadline_text: Not stated on the page. Ask your counselor before each term.
who_can_apply: SFUSD high school students, through a partnership with City College. Talk to your high school counselor about which classes are offered. Non-SFUSD students, or SFUSD students who want a class their school does not offer, use the Concurrent Enrollment page.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school counselor. Questions: dualenrollment@ccsf.edu. Non-SFUSD students use the CCSF Concurrent Enrollment page.
notes: Classes can be at your high school or at a CCSF location. A permission consent form for high school students is linked on the page. Grade and credit rules are not stated on the page, so ask your counselor.

name: Community Youth Center Youth Job Fair
org: Community Youth Center of San Francisco
pay_detail: Free event
duration: Wed Oct 14, 2026, 12 to 4 p.m.
deadline_text: Wednesday, October 14, 2026, 12:00 to 4:00 p.m. at Stonestown Galleria.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24. Register with the Google Form on the DCYF listing.
how_to_apply: Register using the form linked from the sf.gov youth opportunities page. Bring a resume if you have one.
notes: The page does not list which employers will attend. It is a free event, not a job offer.

name: High School Elections Ambassador Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. Ambassadors get a participation certificate signed by the Mayor and community service hours.
duration: About 2 weeks: Sept 14 to 27 in fall 2026, plus a 90 minute in-person training
deadline_text: Fall 2026 applications are closed (the round ran Sept 14 to 27, 2026). The program runs twice a year, in April and September. Spring 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: San Francisco high school students. No prior experience needed.
how_to_apply: Watch the Department of Elections high school programs page for the next application. Questions: hsp@sfgov.org or 415-558-6100.

name: High School Explainer Program
pay_detail: Paid job; the wage is not on the program page
duration: A summer session or a school-year session, with over 60 hours of training (20 before working with visitors)
deadline_text: School-year applications are typically posted in July and summer applications in March. Closing dates are not stated.
who_can_apply: High school age students, 15 to 18 for first-time Explainers (up to 20 for returning ones). Must be able to get a work permit, attend all training dates and work the whole school year or summer session. No science background needed.

name: San Francisco Fire Youth Academy
pay_detail: Free to join. Cadets get breakfast, lunch and a bi-weekly stipend (amount not stated).
