who_can_apply: Cadets must attend high school in San Francisco (or equivalent) or live in the City and County of San Francisco. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page on the academy's website.
notes: The site does not list an age range or application dates, so ask the academy. It is a project of the SF Black Firefighters Association. Paid work for people under 18 in California needs a Permit to Employ and Work. See permit.html?state=ca for the exact permit and steps.

name: Girls on the Run Bay Area Junior Coach
org: Girls on the Run Bay Area
pay_detail: Unpaid
duration: 8 to 10 weeks, 1.5 to 3 hours per week; season starts early September, 5K on Nov 14, 2026

how_to_apply: Complete the Junior Coach application on the Girls on the Run Bay Area site. Email admin@gotrbayarea.org or call (415) 863-8942 to ask about late spots or the next season.
notes: The Oct 12, 2026 date on the sf.gov listing is for adult coaches (18 and up), not Junior Coaches. Teams meet at least once a week.

name: Mission Bit Free Coding Classes
pay_detail: Free
duration: Semester long. Fall 2026 classes ran Sep 8 to Dec 4, 2026.

how_to_apply: Pick a class. Then register on the Mission Bit Classes page when registration opens.
notes: Mission Bit's Tech Start career prep is ages 18 to 26, not for most high schoolers. College Connections (Nov 7, 2026, 10:30 a.m. to noon at Chase Center, grades 9 to 12) closes registration Oct 27, 2026 per sf.gov.

name: Mayor's Youth Employment and Education Program (MYEEP)
org: Japanese Community Youth Council (JCYC), funded by SF DCYF; Buchanan YMCA is a partner site
pay_detail: Paid work experience (hourly rate not posted on the pages read)
duration: School year: Oct to April, with an 8 hour per week internship Jan to April. Summer: June to August, 20 hours per week.
deadline_text: School-year round closed Sept 14, 2026. The YMCA page says summer applications are due the first week of April; school-year applications the first week of September.
who_can_apply: San Francisco youth ages 14 to 17 (the DCYF newsletter lists grades 9 and 10 for this round). Apply through the JCYC Workhub.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the JCYC Workhub (jcycworkhub.org). Ask the YMCA contact on the program page about your neighborhood site.
notes: Pay rate is not stated on the pages read, so ask your site. Contact the Buchanan YMCA ((415) 931-9622) about eligibility.

name: New Door Ventures Employment Program
pay_detail: Paid (rate not posted)
duration: 6 months
deadline_text: Applications accepted all year (per the sf.gov youth listing).
who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24. Aimed at 'opportunity youth' who are out of school or not working.
how_to_apply: Apply on the New Door intake portal linked from their site. The application link is on the official page.
notes: Mainly for 17 year olds and older who are not in a regular school path; not the usual fit for a student who is in school. Pay is not stated on the pages read.

name: Opportunities for All (OFA) and Black 2 San Francisco
org: San Francisco Human Rights Commission, with JCYC
pay_detail: Paid; the hourly rate and hours are not posted on the pages read
duration: B2SF is 6 weeks; OFA length not stated on the pages read
deadline_text: The 2026 OFA deadline was April 10, 2026. The summer application is closed; 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 24 who live in or go to school in San Francisco (that is the only rule on the OFA page).
how_to_apply: Create an account on the JCYC Workhub, complete the application and submit before the spring deadline.
notes: JCYC runs the applications. B2SF and the OFA fellowships share an application with other youth programs. Your interests decide where you are placed.

name: California Pre-Register to Vote (ages 16 and 17)
pay_detail: Free
duration: A few minutes
deadline_text: Always open.
who_can_apply: California residents ages 16 and 17 who are US citizens and not in prison for a felony or ruled mentally unable to vote by a court.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online form at registertovote.ca.gov (linked from the Secretary of State page).
notes: Not a job or internship, but a real civic step. Your registration becomes active when you turn 18. Citizenship is required.

name: Project Pull
org: SF Public Utilities Commission and partner City departments
pay_detail: Paid (rate not posted on the page read)
duration: About 8 weeks (per the SFPUC page)
deadline_text: The 2027 timeline on the application page says 'details coming soon'. Dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: San Francisco high school students (there are separate college tracks). The application page says details are coming soon.
how_to_apply: Use the High School Internship application page. Questions: sfprojectpull1996@gmail.com.
notes: The pages do not list age, pay or a deadline yet. Check the application page in early 2027.

name: YEP! Youth Employment Program
org: San Francisco Recreation and Park Department
pay_detail: Pay not posted on the page read

deadline_text: No dates posted. Email the program to ask when the next round opens.
who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 in San Francisco.
how_to_apply: Email yep@sfgov.org or call Yuri Ugarte at 415-452-3863.
notes: This page replaced the older Workreation name on the department site. An older listing says applicants need work-permit papers and no citizenship is required.

name: SFPL School-Year Teen Volunteers
pay_detail: Unpaid

deadline_text: Rolling. Some positions start late October or early November 2026.

how_to_apply: Fill in the online volunteer form at https://on.sfpl.org/yva
notes: FOG Readers tutoring takes select volunteers age 15 and up (6 month commitment, needs fingerprinting). The same page lists paid teen jobs: YELL (summer, applications open each March) and the Youth Advisory Board (applications for this year closed Sept 14).

name: SSIP CityWorks (Sewer System Internship Program)

notes: Narrow neighborhood focus (southeast San Francisco). The same SFPUC page also lists YouthWorks and Project Pull.

name: Teen Volunteer Programs (Nature Trail, Junior Zoologists, Leadership Fellows)

deadline_text: Nature Trail applications open each March (the page says 2027 applications open in March). Junior Zoologists and Leadership Fellows were closed on the pages read; 2026 Leadership Fellows group interviews were Apr 25, 2026. No 2027 closing dates posted.

notes: Located in San Francisco (a long trip from Sacramento). Applications were closed when checked. The Leadership Fellows page gave 2026 dates, so check for 2027 dates.

name: UCSF ImmunoExplore Summer Camp

It posts no grade range, camp dates or deadlines, so none are listed here. Confirm dates and grades with ImmunoX before applying.

name: UCSF SEP High School Intern Program
org: UCSF Science and Health Education Partnership
pay_detail: $4,500 paid after completing the program (35 hours a week for 8 weeks)

name: Youth Art Exchange After-School Programs
pay_detail: Free
duration: After school
deadline_text: Contact YAX for current sessions.
who_can_apply: Mainly public high school students in San Francisco. Programs are free.
how_to_apply: Call (415) 574-8137. Or send an email to info@youthartexchange.org.
notes: Also runs summer camps for grades 3 to 5 and classes for adults. The page does not mention paid internships or exact ages.

name: SF YouthWorks
org: City and County of San Francisco, run with JCYC and DCYF
pay_detail: $19.61 per hour for school-year interns; $20.36 per hour for Youth Leadership Team members
duration: School-year and summer internships
deadline_text: The 2026-27 school-year application is closed (the DCYF newsletter listed Sept 14, 2026). The Youth Leadership Team application is marked coming soon. Summer dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: 11th or 12th graders (rising juniors, rising seniors and graduating seniors) who live in or go to school in San Francisco and can get a work permit. Youth Leadership Team members must have finished a full YouthWorks session.
how_to_apply: Create an account and apply through the JCYC Workhub portal. Expect a short application and an interview step.
notes: Interns work in City departments such as the SFPUC, the Library and SFO. Former interns can return as paid Youth Leadership Team members. Ask JCYC about work permit help.

name: Junior Volunteer Program
org: Sharp Chula Vista Medical Center Auxiliary (Sharp HealthCare)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Minimum 1 year, 2 to 4 hour shift once a week
deadline_text: Application window Oct 1 to Nov 13, 2026 (per the program page). Application packet due 6 p.m. Nov 12, 2026. Teacher evaluation due Dec 11, 2026. Results by email Jan 31, 2027.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 through 11, at least 14 years old, who have finished 8th grade and have a GPA of 3.0 or higher. Seniors are pointed to the college or adult program after graduation.
how_to_apply: Use the 'High school volunteers (junior volunteers)' online application during the window. A follow-up email asks for your transcript and parental consent, then teacher referrals, an interview and orientation.
notes: The hospital calls this program highly sought after and competitive, and says onboarding can take up to three months. Health requirements after acceptance include MMR, varicella, Tdap, COVID, flu and TB testing. Contact scv.volunteers@sharp.com or 619-502-3606. The two official pages differ by one day on the close date; use Nov 12 to be safe.

name: SJSU Summer Session (Open University) for High School Students
city: San Jose, CA (online, hybrid and in person)
pay_detail: Price not on the page; ask Summer Session (see SJSU Fees, Payment and Refund)
duration: 5 or 10 week sessions (2026: June 1 to Aug 7)
deadline_text: Summer 2026: Open University registration began April 15 and closed July 13. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students can register for summer classes through Open University without being admitted to SJSU.
how_to_apply: Register as an Open University student using the first-time or returning student steps on the SJSU Summer registration page. Questions: professionaled@sjsu.edu or 408-924-2670.
notes: You pay college tuition. The page does not state age, grade or approval rules for high schoolers or the cost, so ask Summer Session. For fall and spring the page points to the Dual Enrollment Program (dualenrollment@sjsu.edu).

name: SkillsUSA
pay_detail: Membership dues are not stated on the pages read; ask your CTE teacher.
duration: School year
deadline_text: Join through your CTE teacher. No cycle stated.

how_to_apply: Ask your CTE teacher, or use the 12 Steps to Start a Chapter or Virtual Chapter on skillsusa.org. Phone 844-875-4557, email customercare@skillsusa.org.
notes: Most useful if your school has a trades or tech CTE pathway.

name: Skirball Teen Advisory Committee
pay_detail: Paid stipend plus community service credit. The amount is not listed.
duration: October 2026 to May 2027, meeting online and in person
deadline_text: Applications for 2026-27 are closed. The next window is not posted.
who_can_apply: Current high school students in grades 10 to 12. The page describes it as an opportunity for Los Angeles teens.
how_to_apply: Closed now. Email youthprograms@skirball.org or use the inquiry form on the Skirball youth programs page.
notes: The same page offers TeenTix LA. It is a free pass for teens to visit museums and culture events across Los Angeles (la.teentix.org).

name: Teen Volunteer Service and Teen Library Council
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering
duration: Teen Library Council meets Thursday afternoons
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Middle and high school students who are 18 or younger and either live in Skokie or attend a Skokie school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Service contact form to join the email list. Or email teenteam@skokielibrary.info. You can also come to an upcoming teen volunteer event.
notes: Some opportunities are only on school breaks or days off. If you need hours for a ticket or a court order, the page says to email the teen team with your name and school.

name: SLAC Regional High School Science Bowl
org: SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory (U.S. Department of Energy National Science Bowl)
duration: One day, Feb 27, 2027
deadline_text: Registration opened Oct 5, 2026. High school event is Feb 27, 2027 (middle school is Feb 6, 2027). Registration deadline not posted.

how_to_apply: A teacher or coach pre-registers the team on the National Science Bowl coach site (apps.orau.gov/nsb-coach). You do not need all team details for step one.
notes: Needs a school team and coach. Volunteer sign-up info is due to be shared by December 2026 (no experience needed). Event is at SLAC, 2575 Sand Hill Road, Menlo Park.

city: Menlo Park and Palo Alto, CA

deadline_text: 2026 applications ran Feb 24 to Mar 17, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

notes: The page says the camp is free. Whether it is overnight, and the 2027 dates, were not on the page I read. Check the SAGE site in February.

name: SMASH Residential (UC Berkeley site)
pay_detail: Free; tuition-free
duration: One year with a residential summer
deadline_text: Application dates for 2026 to 27 are not posted. Join the interest list for updates.
who_can_apply: Students in grade 10 or 11 with a 3.0 GPA and strong math scores. You must be at a public or scholarship-funded private high school. You need a strong interest in computer science. Bay Area schools within the radius are preferred.
how_to_apply: Join the interest list on smash.org/programs and watch for the application. Contact devo@smash.org.
notes: Based in Oakland (2148 Broadway). SMASH Virtual is a separate online option for a national audience; its cost is not stated. SMASH Morehouse is for males and SMASH Spelman for females.

name: Skyline College Dual Enrollment (San Mateo County CCD)
org: Skyline College, San Mateo County Community College District
pay_detail: Free
duration: Per term
deadline_text: No deadline on the page. Ask your counselor about each term.
who_can_apply: Students at partner high schools: Jefferson Union HSD, San Mateo Union HSD, South San Francisco USD, Sequoia Union HSD and Gateway charter school. Need a C or better to get college credit.
how_to_apply: Sign up through your high school (talk to your counselor), submit the Skyline application on CCCApply, then attend an enrollment workshop to register and get parent approval.
notes: Grades become part of a permanent college record and can affect financial aid and college admission. Contacts on the page: hendrieg@smccd.edu or fuentesa@smccd.edu. Canada College and College of San Mateo run their own dual enrollment pages, not checked here.

name: SMUD High School Internship Program
org: SMUD with Sacramento Employment and Training Agency (Sacramento Works)
pay_detail: $16.90 per hour (2026), about 36 hours per week.

who_can_apply: 16 or older (by June 2 in the 2026 cycle), current junior or senior, 2.5 GPA or higher, attends an eligible school in the service area, no relatives who work for the internship host, own transportation.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Sacramento Works site before the deadline. Steps: application review, document check, computer random drawing (55 candidates), work readiness workshops and video interview, manager review, in-person interview. Up to 25 interns are chosen.
notes: Questions: SacramentoWorksFor.Youth@seta.net. Random drawing means even qualified students may not be picked. Check the school list on the Sacramento Works SMUD page. Age rule and school-area details come from the 2026 posting; confirm for 2027.

notes: Teen Centers for ages 13 to 17 (Inglewood Mon to Thu 3 to 6 PM, Hawthorne Mon to Fri 3 to 6 PM) are listed too but are not job programs. Bridge to Work is for foster youth only. The page does not mention work permits. California requires a permit for paid work under 18.

how_to_apply: Fill out the Summer Programs Interest Form for news. Then apply in the online portal when it opens Jan 29, 2027.
notes: Costs money. The Mar 29 closing date is on the main summer programs page; the ECP page itself does not give a due date.

name: High School Volunteer Program

org: Stanford Medicine Children's Health (Lucile Packard Children's Hospital)

name: Stanford Health Care High School Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer

notes: About 35 to 40 students are admitted. The page says in person, with some remote work possible. The 2027 timing is a guess from last year.

pay_detail: 2026 tuition $3,200. Application fee $65 (the aid page says $60); waivers on request. Limited need-based aid. Some courses need materials costing up to $100.

name: Texas 4-H

how_to_apply: Contact your County Extension Office. Find a club. It needs at least five youth from three families. Choose at least one project. Then enroll online in 4HOnline.
notes: The October 31 date is the price cutoff, not a closing date. Counties customize their programs, so call your county Extension office first. This is a club and leadership program, not a paid job.

name: Texas Boys State

pay_detail: American Legion Posts or other community groups often pay the fee, so the cost to the boy is often little to nothing. The fee amount is not stated on the pages read.

how_to_apply: A school official nominates you. That can be a principal, teacher, coach or counselor. A local American Legion Post certifies and sponsors you. Ask your counselor or contact your local Post. The program's site is texasboysstate.com.

notes: Girls State is for girls. Texas Boys State is a separate program run by the American Legion. Students chosen must attend the whole session to earn the certificate and pin.

who_can_apply: High school students who finished at least one high school chemistry course before the summer. The pages give no grade, age or residency rule. You need a recommendation from a high school chemistry teacher. Selection is merit based and space is limited to 20 students.

notes: The program ran for the first time in 2025 (July 14 to 25). The fee and rules above come from the 2026 pages, so check them again when the 2027 application opens. The program site is a Google Sites page run by the department.

name: Summer Earn and Learn (SEAL) for students with disabilities
org: Texas Workforce Commission, Vocational Rehabilitation, with local workforce boards
pay_detail: Wages for hours worked. Each local board sets one hourly wage for its program. The amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: At least five weeks of paid work, with at least four hours in a week to count as a week. No more than 40 hours a week.
deadline_text: No dates for summer 2027 are posted on the pages read. It is a summer program. Ask your local office in the fall or winter.
who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 22 (and under 22 as of September 1 of the previous year) who get special education services under IDEA or have a disability under Section 504, and who are in an educational program. That includes secondary school, home school and other recognized programs.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Texas Workforce Solutions Vocational Rehabilitation Services office. Counselors refer current VR participants. Students who have not applied for VR but meet the disability rule may also be candidates. Statewide contact: 512-936-6400 or vr.office.locator@twc.texas.gov.
notes: Only for students with disabilities. Texas child labor hour limits for 14 and 15 year olds still apply. The pages read do not give a posted 2027 timeline.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, Texas Wing
pay_detail: National Civil Air Patrol page: annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location, and about $300 to $600 in costs in the first year, less any financial assistance. Ask your squadron for exact costs.
duration: Year-round program with squadron meetings, plus encampments and other events
deadline_text: Join any time. Attend three squadron meetings first.
who_can_apply: Ages 12 through 18. You must be in school or a graduate with a satisfactory record. You must be unmarried (except marriage under 18) and not on active duty. You must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (headquarters may waive). You must be of good moral character. Cadets who join before age 19 can stay until 21.
how_to_apply: Pick a local squadron from the Texas Wing unit listing. Go to three squadron meetings as a trial. The squadron and higher headquarters must accept you. Call Wing headquarters at 936-205-9013 with questions.
notes: Meeting times differ by squadron. This is a youth program, not a paid job.

name: The Trade Collective (skilled trades student sign-up)
grades: High school students and recent graduates
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.
duration: Not stated
deadline_text: No deadline stated.
who_can_apply: Students or recent high school graduates who want to learn about skilled trades.
how_to_apply: Fill out the student intake form on the Student page. Parents can email info@thetradecollective.org.
notes: The page does not list specific internships or pay. It says the group is forming partnerships with high schools, colleges and universities. Address on the site: 1910 Greenwood Street, Evanston.

name: Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
org: Travis County Health and Human Services with Austin Public Health
pay_detail: Paid work experience; hourly rate not stated on the program page
duration: not stated
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed and the page is labeled Expired. 2027 dates are not posted; the county has a 2027 interest form to get notified when applications open.
who_can_apply: Must be 14 to 18 (14 by April 1) and in middle or high school, and must live and/or attend school in Travis County. Teens with disabilities can apply up to age 22. Other factors such as household income may also be considered.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application (Jotform) and upload a Social Security card and a school ID or recent report card. Eligible applicants are invited to a mandatory job readiness training, then matched to a host site if space allows. Applying does not guarantee a placement.
notes: Phone 512-854-4590. Pay rate, hours and program length are not stated on the page. The page does not mention a work permit. Texas rules for 14 and 15 year olds limit hours (see Texas Workforce Commission child labor page).

name: TreePeople Volunteer Events (all ages with parent consent)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role
duration: Single events; calendar posted at least a month ahead
deadline_text: Sign up for each event on the Events Calendar. No program deadline.
who_can_apply: No age limit. Minors need a signed parental consent form. Volunteers 15 and under (the FAQ says under 15) need an adult chaperone age 21 or older, one adult per 10 young volunteers.
how_to_apply: Sign up for an event on the TreePeople events calendar. The confirmation email has the waiver and parent consent forms. Groups must email volunteer@treepeople.org first.
notes: TreePeople's jobs page lists only an 18+ fellowship, so this is the way in for teens. The page gives two versions of the chaperone age rule (15 and under vs under 15), so confirm by email.

name: Youth Tree Team
grades: Currently in high school or about to start high school
pay_detail: Starting at $12 per hour
duration: 7 weeks, Monday to Friday, 7:30 am to 12:30 pm
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: opened Nov 15, 2025, closed Feb 2, 2026, job ran June 1 to July 17, 2026. The page says 2027 details are coming later.
who_can_apply: Teens who are in high school or about to start, and at least 14 as of May 1.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the link is posted. You must finish every step. These are a required Challenge Day, a required volunteer tree planting and an interview.
notes: Competitive. Not everyone who applies gets a job. Returning members can apply for outside study spots with partner groups. 2026 dates are shown. Watch the page for the 2027 schedule. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit (employment certificate) is required for minors under 16, so 14 and 15 year olds need one. A school issuing officer or the county school superintendent gives it.

name: Tri-Valley ROP (Regional Occupational Program)
fields: trades; health; tech-cs; engineering; education; law-government
pay_detail: Free classes; you earn high school elective credit (many satisfy a-g requirements)
deadline_text: Registration for the 2026-2027 school year is closed. Talk to your school's College and Career Specialist or counselor.
who_can_apply: High school students in Dublin Unified, Livermore Valley Joint Unified or Pleasanton Unified school districts.
how_to_apply: Sign up through your high school's regular class registration; your school's College and Career Specialist finishes the ROP signup. Phone (925) 455-4800.
notes: You must arrange your own transportation to off-site classes. Classes run at six high schools and Las Positas College, during the school day and after school.

name: Trybe Summer Jobs and Paid Internships (East Oakland)
pay_detail: City of Oakland's 2026 list says paid, 100 hours, at least Oakland minimum wage. Trybe's own 2022 posting said $15.06 per hour (old).

notes: Trybe's free summer camp is for kids 0 to 14; the paid youth internship is separate and the summer page shows only a flyer with no details. Call to ask about 2027. Do not confuse oaklandtrybe.org with trybe.org.

name: Tucker Youth Council

notes: The page lists no direct phone or email; it links to the city's Contacting the City page. The page does not post the next application date. Unpaid, so no work permit.

name: Summer Speech and Debate Camps (high school)

how_to_apply: Register online through the link on the camp page. Aid questions: mnudlcamps@augsburg.edu.
notes: Students on free or reduced lunch with qualifying GPA may get full tuition for the July 6 to 10 week.

name: Minnesota Business Venture (MBV)

notes: The page also lists youth tryouts for student actors ages 8 to 18. Those roles are unpaid.

Do not mix this up with the Summer Youth Corps, the live-in camping crew. That program is not active in 2026 and the Corps is rethinking its youth programs.

name: Cookie Cart Youth Employment Program

notes: Camp is listed as an example of past offerings; 2027 camps are not posted yet.

name: Pathways to Careers (youth chapter)
pay_detail: Hourly stipend for the 3 week summer experience (amount not stated). Scholarship of up to $10,000 a year for two years for those who enroll at Dunwoody.

notes: Must attend a fall orientation and at least 85 percent of monthly workshops. Selection is not guaranteed.

name: Genesys Works Twin Cities (training and paid internship)

The site did not agree with itself, so ask which grade to apply in. The families page gives $10,000-$12,000 for the internship year. Its summary gives $10,000-$13,000. Ask which is right.

name: Student Summer Volunteer Program

deadline_text: The page says applications for summer 2026 are closed. Dates for summer 2027 are not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 and 17. You need a reliable ride to the hospital. You must be able to keep patient info private.
how_to_apply: Email three things to volunteer@gillettechildrens.com. They are the application, a Student Reference Form from a teacher or advisor, and a Parent Release Form. If a piece is missing, they will not review it. Some applicants are interviewed in person with a parent.
notes: Before starting you must pass a background check and fingerprinting and show proof of vaccination and a QuantiFERON-TB Gold blood test. These may cost money.

name: Girls Inc. Eureka! STEM program (YWCA Minneapolis)
org: Girls Inc. at YWCA Minneapolis, with University of Minnesota College of Science and Engineering
grades: Grades 8 to 12 (the University of Minnesota page says students entering grades 8 and 9 can apply)
pay_detail: Eureka! interns get a stipend from Girls Inc. after completing a 4 week internship (20 hours a week). The amount is not stated. The cost of the summer program is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Youth in grades 8 to 12 who like STEM, from across the Twin Cities. The University of Minnesota summer camps page says students entering grades 8 and 9 are eligible to apply. The page describes a pro-girl program. It does not say whether boys can join.
how_to_apply: Use the Eureka! online application or the PDF application on the program page. Do this when registration opens. The PDF comes in English, Spanish or Somali. Contact: girlsinc@ywcampls.org or 612-215-4369.
notes: Described as a pro-girl program (Girls Inc.), so ask whether it is for girls only. Interns are treated as volunteers by the worksite because the stipend comes from Girls Inc., not the worksite. Minnesota work permit rules were not checked.

name: Microscope Adventure Summer Camp
pay_detail: $598 before April 30; $698 after. Need-based scholarships can cover full tuition.

notes: The page gives no year for the Oct 26 open date; Oct 26, 2026 is a Monday, which matches.

name: HealthPartners volunteer program for high school students
pay_detail: Volunteer

deadline_text: No deadline is listed. The process takes about 3 to 4 weeks.
who_can_apply: You must be 15 or older. High school students bring a reference form, a parent consent form and a health screening form to the interview. Some roles have higher age limits.
how_to_apply: Send the volunteer application and do an interview. Finish an online orientation. Pass a Minnesota background check. Then train on site. For questions, call 651-254-5709. You can also write to volunteerservices@healthpartners.com.
notes: The page does not name which hospitals take teens, so ask when you call.

name: Youth and Young Adult Services

deadline_text: No deadlines. Staff follow up quickly after you send the referral form.
who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 28 who live in Hennepin, Ramsey or Dakota County. You must meet low income (WIOA) rules. You must also have at least one more barrier. Examples are being a parent, not having stable housing, being 1 to 2 grade levels behind, or being at risk of dropping out. You can still ask if you are not sure.
how_to_apply: Submit the youth and young adult referral form or the Inquire Now form on the Hired page. You must enroll to get services. Offices: Minneapolis 612-808-9500, Saint Paul 651-328-2777, Bloomington 952-303-8303.
notes: Funding sets what is offered. Help with school costs and living costs depends on what money is on hand.

notes: Held at 1108 West Broadway, Minneapolis.

Southdale is in Edina. The U of M Medical Center has an East and a West Bank site. Woodwinds is in Woodbury. Lake Medical Center is in Wyoming. Northland is in Princeton.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Then you have an interview and online learning. You also need a background check, fingerprints, a TB test and proof of shots. Last is an online orientation. Call 1-855-324-7843.
notes: A flu shot each year is required. The 100 hour minimum is listed for volunteers in general.

The Park Board teen page also lists Youthline, a mentorship program for ages 12 to 17. Minnesota work permit rules were not checked.

name: Naturalist Youth Leader Program
org: Three Rivers Park District (Eastman Nature Center)
pay_detail: Listed as a volunteer opportunity; pay is not mentioned.
duration: Camps run June to August
deadline_text: Applications usually open in January, with interviews in February. Exact 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: Contact Vicky Wachtler, the staff contact named on the page.
notes: Site: Eastman Nature Center. The date pattern comes from the general text on the page.

name: Pathways Internships
pay_detail: At least $15 an hour
duration: June through August, about 20 hours a week (some roles 40)
deadline_text: The page says applications for the 2026 program are closed. Next dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Meant for young people, most of all those who face barriers to work. The minimum age depends on the role. It is 15 for Explorers Camp and Community Engagement. It is 16 for Outdoor Education, Farm Garden, Outdoor Recreation School and IT/GIS. It is 18 for several others.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps. Contact Char Myers (Char.Myers@threeriversparks.org) or Terrell Lhotka (Terrell.Lhotka@threeriversparks.org).
notes: The Three Rivers Park District Foundation gives rides money if getting to work is a barrier. The work permit rule was not checked.

name: Silverwood Teen Arts Council
pay_detail: Listed as a volunteer opportunity; pay is not mentioned.
duration: June to March, 30 hours of service
deadline_text: Applications are usually accepted April to June, and may be accepted later in the year.
who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 19.
how_to_apply: Contact Seth Eberle, the staff contact named on the page. No online form is described.
notes: Site: Silverwood Park. The date pattern comes from the general description. It is not a date posted for 2027.

name: ThreeSixty Journalism summer programs
org: ThreeSixty Journalism, University of St. Thomas
pay_detail: Free in 2026 (the Multimedia Storytelling Institute is normally $3,000 and the College Essay Workshop $1,000). Students get a stipend for finishing, plus free lunch and transit passes.
duration: MPR Radio Camp 1 week; Multimedia Storytelling Institute 3 weeks; College Essay Workshop 4 days
deadline_text: 2026 priority deadline was April 17 (radio camp April 30), with rolling admission to May 31. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Twin Cities high school students, new or skilled. Spots are limited. It is hard to get in.
how_to_apply: Use the application links on the Summer Programs page. Questions: denise.huang@stthomas.edu.
notes: Stipend amount is not stated. Radio Camp cost is not listed.

name: Biomedical Engineering High School Internship Program
org: University of Minnesota Department of Biomedical Engineering
pay_detail: A stipend and bus transportation are provided; the amount is not stated.
duration: 6 weeks
deadline_text: The page says it is not accepting applications for Summer 2026. Check back for Summer 2027.
who_can_apply: Students entering their senior year. No other rules are listed.
how_to_apply: Not described. Phone the department at 612-624-4507.
notes: At the end, interns get a letter of support. It comes from the engineering faculty.

name: Discover STEM (University of Minnesota College of Science and Engineering)
org: University of Minnesota College of Science and Engineering Student Services
pay_detail: The page says there is no cost to apply and attend, thanks to 3M. It also mentions an enrollment fee or scholarship request after admission, so confirm that nothing is charged.
duration: 1 week, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. daily (day program)
deadline_text: Summer 2026: sessions were Aug 3 to 7 and Aug 10 to 14, 2026. Applications were open April 20 to May 18, 2026 and decisions went out by May 29. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students entering grade 11 or 12. Priority goes to students who have not been in Discover STEM before. Admission is competitive, and the program especially encourages applicants from underrepresented communities.
how_to_apply: Apply online, or by mail on request. Send an unofficial high school transcript and personal statement answers. Do not send the application in pieces. Those are not reviewed.
notes: The camps page for the college also lists other high school options, such as the Run the World AI Explorers Camp (grades 11 and 12) and a Summer Computer Academy for girls in grades 6 to 12. Not a job.

name: Go4Brains High-School Summer Neuroscience Program
org: University of Minnesota, Department of Neuroscience
pay_detail: Free for selected students; meals and travel are covered and students get a $400 stipend.
duration: One week (July 20 to 24 in 2026)
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was March 1, 2026,. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 11 who have met barriers to science and medicine chances. The program focuses on high schoolers in the Twin Cities area.
how_to_apply: Fill in the enrollment survey on the program site. Send back the signed form by the deadline. You need a letter of support from a science teacher or a group leader.
notes: The site says both ten and twelve students are chosen, so it is a small cohort.

name: LHI-AHA Summer Research Scholars Program (high school)
org: University of Minnesota Medical School, Lillehei Heart Institute
pay_detail: Scholars earn an hourly wage; the amount is not stated.
duration: 8 weeks, May 31 to July 23, 2027 (tentative), 40 hours a week
deadline_text: Applications open Dec 1, 2026 and close Feb 15, 2027.
who_can_apply: Must be 16 or older, a current junior or senior at the time of application, and a U.S. citizen.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Add a resume that lists your test scores, a transcript and two letters from faculty. Also add a statement of interest and a statement of goals.
notes: No housing or meals are provided. Applicants under 18 need an adult chaperone for University housing, or can stay off campus with family or friends. Number of spots is not stated.

name: IMA-MathCEP Math Modeling Camp
org: University of Minnesota MathCEP and the Institute for Mathematics and its Applications
pay_detail: Cost and stipend are not listed. No housing or meals are provided.
duration: 1 week (June 22 to 26 in 2026), about 9 am to 3:30 pm
deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was May 31, 2026, with a waitlist after. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Enrolled high school students who completed a full year of single variable calculus by the end of 2025-26. Graduating seniors still count.
how_to_apply: The student fills out the online form. A math teacher emails a short note of support. UMTYMP students do not need the note.
notes: This is a commuter camp only. You do not stay overnight.

name: Rooted in STEM
org: University of Minnesota College of Science and Engineering
pay_detail: Free; lunch and a gift included. No stipend. Students who attend through fall of 12th grade and are admitted to the College of Science and Engineering can get a $40,000 scholarship ($10,000 a year for 4 years, from 3M).
duration: January of 10th grade to December of 12th grade
deadline_text: Applications open in early November and close in early December. The page lists a Dec 1 deadline and Dec 19 decisions but the years on the page look mixed up, so check the page for the current cycle.
who_can_apply: Current 10th graders from groups that are not well represented in STEM. You should plan to go to a four year college. You must commit to one Saturday a month through December of 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It needs a note from a STEM teacher or counselor, personal essays, your GPA and a list of your courses.
notes: You must get yourself to the program. Money for rides is available if you ask. Only 10th graders are accepted from 2025 on.

name: VetCamp
org: University of Minnesota College of Veterinary Medicine
grades: 6 to 12 (high school sessions are grades 9 to 12)
pay_detail: $15 registration fee for self-hosted camps; families with financial need can ask for a waiver.
duration: One afternoon. Self-hosted camps are about 3 hours; the Aug 12, 2026 high school camp ran 12 to 5 pm. 2026 high school dates: June 10, July 15, Aug 12.
deadline_text: No deadline listed. The 2026 sessions were June 10, July 15 and Aug 12. The organizers say new dates are added from time to time.
who_can_apply: Middle and high school students in grades 6 to 12. High school sessions are for grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Register through the online form linked on the VetCamp page, or join the mailing list for new dates.
notes: It is held at the Ben Pomeroy Student-Alumni Learning Center. That is on the St. Paul campus. The Minnesota Veterinary Medical Foundation is the sponsor.

name: Walker Art Center Teen Arts Council (WACTAC)
pay_detail: Pay or stipend is not stated on the page.
duration: Weekly meetings during the school year
deadline_text: Applications for the 2026-27 school year have closed. Applications for 2027-28 will open in spring 2027.
who_can_apply: Teens from across the Twin Cities. The page does not state an age or grade range.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application steps. Applications for 2027-28 open in spring 2027. Follow @walkerteens on Instagram for programming info and updates.
notes: The Walker also offers free Teen Maker Break art sessions, monthly on the third Saturday from 2 to 5 p.m. (materials and snacks provided). Ask the Walker whether WACTAC members are paid and what ages can join.

name: Summer VolunTEEN Program
duration: 8-week program, 6-week minimum (2026: June 15 to Aug 7)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application completion deadline May 4, 2026 (first come, first served). 2027 dates not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Must be 16 by the program start (June 15 in 2026). Two references (at least one from a school mentor), signed parent consent form, English fluency, proof of MMR, varicella and Tdap shots, and TB testing. The page names no upper age limit.
how_to_apply: Register in the UC Davis Health VolunTEEN portal, finish all health clearance items, and submit references. Questions: 916-734-2401 or volunteer.services@health.ucdavis.edu.
notes: Located at the Sacramento medical campus (Davis II Building, 2420 Stockton Blvd). Health clearances (MMR, varicella, Tdap, TB test) take time, so start early. Spots are limited and filled first come, first served.

name: UC Davis Medical Microbiology and Immunology high school research internship
org: UC Davis School of Medicine with DJUSD and Esparto CTE
pay_detail: The DJUSD CTE page says its internships are unpaid. The UC Davis article does not mention pay.
duration: 10 weeks (2025 cohort: Mar 18 to May 22)
deadline_text: 2026-27 cohort not confirmed. Last known cohort ran Mar 18 to May 22, 2025.
who_can_apply: Students in career programs at Davis Senior High, MLK Jr. High, Da Vinci Charter Academy and Esparto High (2025 cohort). Through DJUSD, students are matched to internships by the Internship Specialist.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's CTE teacher or the DJUSD Internship Specialist (Alexha Contreras, 530-757-5400 ext 170). The DJUSD list shows an internship in the spring. It is at the UC Davis Center for Valley Fever.
notes: Based on a July 2025 UC Davis Health news story and the DJUSD CTE internship list. There is no UC Davis application page. Confirm that it runs in spring 2027.

name: Summer at UC Davis Pre-College Program
org: UC Davis Continuing and Professional Education
pay_detail: 2025 tuition was $6,985 plus a $100 application fee (includes dorm and meals). 2027 price not posted yet.
duration: about 2 weeks per session (2025: July 7 to 18 and July 21 to Aug 1)
deadline_text: 2025 cycle deadline was May 16, 2025 (the fee page still shows 2025). 2027 dates not posted yet.
who_can_apply: High-achieving high school students. No minimum GPA. Admission is first come, first served once your application is complete. No academic credit.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, two short-answer questions, and pay the application fee. Transcript and personal statement are optional but helpful.
notes: Expensive. The program moved to a new website (discoveryprograms.ucdavis.edu), and the fee page still shows 2025 numbers, so confirm the 2027 price and deadline. Age rule differs between UC Davis pages: other UC Davis pages say ages 16 to 18. A $1,500 deposit is due at enrollment. The apply page says a decision takes about 10 business days after your application is complete.

name: UC Davis Upward Bound
pay_detail: No fee listed on the page. Confirm with the program.
duration: school year plus summer
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Check with an Upward Bound advisor at your school.
who_can_apply: High school students at partner schools in Sacramento, Solano, Shasta and Siskiyou counties who are low income or whose parents did not attend college.
how_to_apply: Get an application from the Upward Bound advisor at your school (Shasta County students ask the GO Center). Send student info and a short essay, a parent-signed eligibility form and two recommendation letters back to the advisor. Questions: eduadvising@ucdavis.edu or 530-752-5887.
notes: Only available at partner schools. Federally funded TRIO program for low-income or first-generation students. No fee or stipend is listed on the pages read, so ask.

name: Young Scholars Program (YSP)
pay_detail: 2026 program cost $7,750 (housing, meals and 5 units of credit included). Application fee $45 in 2026. Fee reduction and application fee waiver available.
duration: 6 weeks (2026 dates: June 21 to Aug 1)
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: applications Jan 1 to Mar 1, 2026, teacher references by Mar 3. 2027 dates not posted yet.
who_can_apply: Rising junior or senior. Must be 16 by the first day and not turn 18 before the last day. Must be a permanent US resident living and attending school in the US. Two teacher references needed (one must be a science teacher).
how_to_apply: Apply in the YSP portal between Jan 1 and Mar 1. Submit grades, activities, essays and two teacher references. Ask for fee reduction by the deadline if you need it.
notes: Very competitive (about 40 students). Residential, so you live on campus. Late and incomplete applications are not accepted. Application fee waivers are given on request. Contact ysp@ucdavis.edu.

name: UC Scout Online High School Courses
pay_detail: Fees vary by course and prices are not on the home page. The site lists free options for California public schools and scholarships. The page does not say anyone is paid.
duration: Self-paced
deadline_text: Fall 2026 enrollment is open (as of Oct 7, 2026).
who_can_apply: High school students looking to get ahead or recover credit. The site mentions free options for California public schools and scholarship applications for eligible students.
how_to_apply: Enroll from the courses page, ask your school counselor about school-paid seats, or call (408) 450-4962.
notes: This is coursework, not a job. Included because many teens use it to free up schedule time for jobs and internships.

name: COSMOS at UC Irvine (California State Summer School for Mathematics and Science)
pay_detail: Fee-based residential program. The 2027 cost is not stated on UCI's page, so check the COSMOS site for the current fee.
duration: 4 weeks, residential (2027 session dates TBA)
deadline_text: Statewide COSMOS dates: application opens Jan 6, 2027 at 8:00 AM and closes Feb 5, 2027. Financial aid forms postmarked by Feb 6, 2027. Decisions Mar 25, 2027. UCI's own pages still show 2026 dates, so confirm there.
who_can_apply: California high school students in grades 8 to 12, per the COSMOS application site. A GPA of 3.5 or above is typical.
how_to_apply: Online application with a personal statement, teacher recommendation(s), transcripts and a parent or guardian e-signature, plus the application fee. You choose one campus and cluster. Pay one-third of tuition by Apr 7, 2027 and the rest by Apr 16, 2027 if accepted.
notes: Competitive. About 160 to 200 students join per campus. UCI says the 2027 application will be available in January 2027. Watch for info sessions in December. Students must live on campus for the full program. COSMOS runs on several UC campuses. This card is the UC Irvine campus.

name: UCI Health High School Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid.
duration: One 3-hour shift a week, Monday to Friday 4 to 7 p.m., minimum 75 hours
deadline_text: Volunteer applications are currently closed. The page says it is under construction and will be back soon, with no date.
who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 and over. Selection looks at your application, your ability to keep the weekly schedule, past community service, and your education and career interests.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the application steps. Email ucimcvolunteer@uci.edu or call 714-456-5541 to ask when applications reopen.
notes: Requires a physician-signed medical clearance with immunity proof (measles, mumps, rubella, varicella), Tdap, hepatitis B series, COVID-19 vaccine with booster, flu shot in season, and a negative TB blood test within 90 days of your start date. Also a three-hour orientation.

name: UCLA Health Westwood High School Summer Volunteer Program
pay_detail: Unpaid. Parking is not free for student volunteers.
duration: At least 50 hours, finished by August 31
deadline_text: The page says the High School Summer Program is now closed. Information for Summer 2027 will be posted starting January 1, 2027. Hours must be done by August 31.
who_can_apply: Must be 16 by June 1. Grade and residency are not stated. A government photo ID and immunization proof are required.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a required Zoom info session. You get the form by email. Send it back with proof of shots (varicella, MMR, TB test). Then go to one required in-person orientation. Email studentvol@mednet.ucla.edu.
notes: Info sessions fill fast. Every slot showed FULL or CLOSED when read. The page also points to the Mattel Youth Ambassador program as another option. Santa Monica and West Valley campuses have their own student pages.

name: UCLA Summer Sessions for high school students
pay_detail: Fee-based. Ask UCLA Summer Sessions for current fees. Scholarship programs described on the page include BASE and Summer Scholars Support.
duration: Focus Series: 3 weeks; other formats vary (2026 sessions ran June 22 to July 31)
deadline_text: Summer 2026 enrollment is closed. Summer 2027 programs and dates are not posted yet; the site offers a sign-up for 2027 updates.
who_can_apply: High school students. The Summer Precollege Focus Series requires being at least 15 by the first day of Summer Sessions, and some programs set older ages. Regular summer courses must come from a pre-approved high school list.
how_to_apply: Apply or enroll through each program page on summer.ucla.edu. California students in grades 9 to 11 can apply for Summer Scholars Support (need and merit scholarships), and 10th and 11th graders from under-resourced California communities can apply for BASE, a free 6-week online course with a UCLA mentor.
notes: Out-of-state and international students cannot receive UCLA Summer Sessions financial aid. Exact program prices were not found; use UCLA's fee calculator before applying.

name: UCR TRIO Pre-College: Upward Bound and Educational Talent Search
pay_detail: Free to join. Only Upward Bound summer participants receive a stipend (amount not stated).
duration: Year-round support; UB summer program is 6 weeks (5 weeks bused to campus, final week in residence halls)
deadline_text: No deadline posted. Apply with the interest form or ETS application.
who_can_apply: Students at participating schools. Upward Bound: freshmen or sophomores at Moreno Valley, Perris, Rubidoux, Banning, Norte Vista, Ramona, Bloomington, Colton or Eisenhower High School. Talent Search: Arroyo Valley, Indian Springs, Pacific, San Bernardino or San Gorgonio High. Both need a 2.5 GPA, U.S. citizenship or permanent residency, low income and/or first generation, and interest in college.
how_to_apply: Upward Bound: fill out the interest form on the page to receive an application. Talent Search: fill out the ETS application and give it to your school's ETS contact or email ets@ucr.edu; phone (951) 827-7863.
notes: Only students at the listed schools qualify. The page does not list grade levels for Talent Search.

name: COSMOS at UC San Diego
org: UC San Diego (Jacobs School of Engineering) / California State Summer School for Mathematics and Science
pay_detail: 2026 program cost $5,518 (housing, meals, field trips) plus a $46 application fee. Financial assistance form available for California residents. Amounts for 2027 not posted.
duration: 4 weeks (2026: July 5 to July 31)
deadline_text: 2027 applications open Jan 6, 2027 at 8 a.m. and close Feb 5, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. The program says no exceptions to the deadline.
who_can_apply: Motivated students completing grades 8 through 12 with strong interest and achievement in math and science. In 2026 the in-person program was limited to California residents. Students can attend COSMOS only once.
how_to_apply: Online application through the COSMOS portal: choose UCSD, rank two clusters and write an essay for each, one or two online recommendations from a math or science teacher, current and prior-year transcripts, and the application fee.
notes: 2027 dates come from the statewide COSMOS site; the UCSD page still shows 2026 dates. Fees shown are for 2026. 2026 rules asked for proof of COVID vaccination and a negative test; check whether that still applies. If admitted, a non-refundable deposit of one third of tuition holds your spot.

name: Sports Medicine Summer Academy (Research Scholars)
org: UC San Diego Division of Extended Studies
pay_detail: $3,500 for the July 2026 session (commuter only; no housing or transportation). A hybrid fall session cost $2,000.
duration: 3 weeks, weekdays 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. (2026: July 6 to July 24)
deadline_text: 2026 summer enrollment closed June 26, 2026; fall 2026 enrollment closed Sept 21, 2026. Summer 2027 dates not posted; you can sign up for notifications on the program page.
who_can_apply: Incoming 11th and 12th graders with a cumulative GPA of 3.3 or better who are interested in sports medicine. No application is needed; you enroll directly.
how_to_apply: Enroll directly on the Extended Studies registration page. Add the course to your cart. No application or essay is needed. Questions: precollege@ucsd.edu.
notes: Earns 3 to 6 UC pre-college units. UCSD's Research Scholars also offers life sciences and marine science courses; its older Academic Connections summer program was canceled for 2026. Marine science fall 2026 application closed Sept 17, 2026.

name: UCSF Health Volunteer Program (includes BCH Oakland campus)
org: UCSF Health / UCSF Benioff Children's Hospitals
city: Oakland, CA (BCH Oakland) and San Francisco
duration: One weekly 3 to 4 hour shift for 6 months
deadline_text: Page update dated Sept 22 (year not stated): registration opens Tuesday Oct 13 at 9:30am only for two high-need SF programs. Other opportunities, including others at BCH Oakland, are listed as full.
who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. You must be 18 to volunteer in pediatric inpatient units or the Emergency Department. Minimum 6 months, one 3 to 4 hour weekday shift each week.
how_to_apply: Attend a virtual info session, in-person group interview, online training and health clearance (background check if 18+). Volunteer Services (415) 502-9888.
notes: The Oct 13 opening is for Parnassus and Mt. Zion or Mission Bay programs in San Francisco, not Oakland. UCSF says it cannot take new volunteers for other roles right now. Under 18 needs a parent at the health clearance visit. No high school summer program was found on the official pages.

name: Young Scholars Program (UGA College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences)
org: University of Georgia, College of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences
city: Athens, Griffin or Tifton, GA (UGA campuses)
grades: Finished sophomore year of high school (first time in the program)
pay_detail: Described as a paid internship, 30 hours a week. The pay amount is not stated on the pages read.
duration: Five weeks (June 1 to July 7 on the page, plus a three day conference July 8 to 10). The page does not show the year.
deadline_text: Last cycle: application opened Nov 3, 2025 and closed Jan 23, 2026. The program page now says the application is closed for this cycle. Next cycle dates not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students who finished sophomore year and are 16 by the program start date. You must have taken one high school lab science course and one semester of algebra. You should be interested in ag, food and environmental science. First time participants only.
how_to_apply: Send an online application with short essays. Pick a campus (Athens, Griffin or Tifton). Add two recommendation letters from science or math teachers. Upload an official transcript.
notes: Not residential. You must arrange your own housing and transport, and travel to the campus daily. Contacts on the page: Athens 706-542-2713, Griffin 770-228-7264, Tifton 229-326-4663. Georgia Department of Labor says a work permit is required only for minors who have not reached their 16th birthday. This program requires age 16.

name: Georgia Ready Summer Institute (UGA)
org: University of Georgia, Office of Academic and Community Engagement
grades: Rising high school seniors (going into senior year), Georgia students
pay_detail: Free to attend. The pages say there is no cost and that housing and meals are included.
duration: One week, residential
deadline_text: The 2026 application is closed (the application page says the deadline passed). Dates for the next cycle are not posted. Contact oace@uga.edu for future application cycles.
who_can_apply: High-achieving high school students from across Georgia who are going into their senior year. No other rules are listed on the pages read. In 2026 exactly 50 students were chosen from 664 applications.
how_to_apply: Apply through the UGA Admissions application portal when it opens. Ask the Office of Academic and Community Engagement (oace@uga.edu) about future cycles. Admissions phone on the application page: 762-400-8800.
notes: Very competitive: a UGA news story dated Sep 3, 2026 says the program got a record 664 applications for 50 spots. Exact 2026 dates and application requirements were not on the pages the reader could open.

name: ESTEEM/SER-Quest Summer Program
org: A. James Clark School of Engineering, University of Maryland (Center for Minorities in Science and Engineering)
pay_detail: No cost to students selected (stated on the page). No stipend is stated.
duration: 4 weeks (Jul 7 to Jul 31 in 2026), commuters only
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application deadline Mar 29, 2026; teacher recommendations due Apr 9, 2026; program Jul 7 to Jul 31, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
who_can_apply: Rising 12th graders with at least a 3.2 GPA and no C's in math or science, who finished Trigonometry, Chemistry and Pre-Calculus with a B or better, want to study engineering at UMD, and can attend full time for all 4 weeks.
how_to_apply: Online application with an essay and resume, two teacher recommendations (one math, one science), and a virtual interview with the student and a parent or guardian.
notes: The page says taking part does not guarantee admission to UMD. No housing is offered. A free program, not a job, so no work permit.

name: Terp Young Scholars
org: University of Maryland, College Park (Extended Studies)
pay_detail: 2026 package fee: $1,791 campus option or $1,420 online option (3 credits, tuition and fees). Also a $75 application fee and a $275 program deposit that is credited to the bill. Partial scholarships, none above 30% of the package fee.
duration: 3 weeks (Jul 13 to Jul 31 in 2026)
deadline_text: Application window dates are not stated on this page. The page says the application for this year is currently closed.
who_can_apply: Page lists rising 10th through graduating 12th grade; minimum age 13 and the 3.0 GPA rule are not stated on this page.
how_to_apply: Pick a course and the campus or online option, then apply online with a transcript, health insurance card and card payment for the application fee and deposit. No essays or recommendations.
notes: Costs shown are the 2026 prices; 2027 prices are not posted. Commuter program: no campus housing except the business course BMGT262. The grade posts to a UMD college transcript. Not a job, so no work permit.

name: Teen Counselor-in-Training (CIT) program
pay_detail: One-time $100 registration fee (orientation, training, t-shirt, certificate, supplies); financial aid available for students who qualify for free or reduced school lunch. CIT service is volunteer time.
duration: Flexible half or full days over the summer
deadline_text: Applications for 2026 are closed. The page says to check back in January 2027 for the next session; an info session is held each February and the 2026 orientation was June 12.
who_can_apply: The page title says ages 12 to 15 (the University youth programs list says 12 to 16). Applicants attend a February info session, interview, and a mandatory one-day orientation in June.
how_to_apply: Attend the free virtual info meeting in February, get the application, sign up for an interview, pay the fee if accepted, then attend orientation. Call 612-301-1210 for questions.
notes: Good first leadership experience for younger teens. Volunteer hours can be logged.

name: Connected and Automated Vehicles (CAV) Camp
org: University of Minnesota, Minnesota CAV program
pay_detail: Free to attend; lunch is provided
duration: One week, day camp
deadline_text: Information about the 2027 camp will be available in early 2027.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 10 to 12 with an interest in automotive tech, manufacturing, engineering, planning or robotics. Space is limited to 20 students.
how_to_apply: Application steps for 2027 are posted early in 2027 on the camp page.
notes: Competitive: 20 spots. Day camp; the page does not mention transportation.

name: National Summer Transportation Institute (NSTI)
org: University of Minnesota Center for Transportation Studies
pay_detail: Free two-week day camp
duration: Two weeks, day camp
deadline_text: Dates and application instructions for the 2027 camp will be announced in early 2027.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 7 to 9 with a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0, who have completed or can enroll in pre-algebra and are interested in engineering, science, transportation or technology.
how_to_apply: Application information for 2027 is posted early in 2027. Selection process details are on the camp's admission decisions page.
notes: For younger teens. The University's youth programs list shows ages 13 to 16 for this camp.

name: Explore@UNC
pay_detail: $625 per student per week (includes a $50 non-refundable registration and placement fee); some tracks may add a $25 activity fee; lunch and snacks included. Need-based aid for permanent NC residents who are rising seniors.
duration: 1 week. 2027 weeks: June 14-18, June 21-25, June 28-July 2, July 12-16. Commuter only, no residential option.
deadline_text: Pre-registration runs mid-December 2026 through mid-January 2027; placement notices early February 2027; financial aid paperwork due January 28, 2027.
who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 in fall 2027, at a high school or homeschooled. Not open to 8th grade or below or to graduates.
how_to_apply: Pre-register online (interest form on the Explore@UNC pages). Pre-registering improves placement chances. Payment details come after placement.
notes: Families must have a local trusted contact. A temporary drop-off pass is $25 for the week and all-day parking is the family's cost. UNC also lists dual enrollment as a visiting student for rising seniors (see summer.unc.edu/dual-enrollment/); its cost was not read. Questions: explore@unc.edu.

name: UNC Summer School Visitor (rising high school seniors)
pay_detail: Summer School tuition applies. Amount is not on this page.
duration: Summer Session 2
deadline_text: The 2027 application is not open yet. Decision letters go out starting March 2027.
who_can_apply: Honor roll students who have finished their junior year. International high school students cannot be considered. If you are under 17, you must say you will live with a parent or legal guardian during Summer School.
how_to_apply: Make an account in the Summer Visitor application. Send a transcript. Send a personal statement that names the course. Also send a letter of support from a teacher, principal or counselor.
notes: You can only take courses in Summer Session 2. High school seniors cannot audit courses. The 2027 application is not open yet, so no dates exist to confirm.

name: Union City Youth Commission
duration: August to May
deadline_text: The page lists applications from February 1 to April 1, interviews in April and appointments in May. It gives no year, so treat this as last year's pattern.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 who live in or go to school in Union City.
how_to_apply: Submit an application between February 1 and April 1, then interview in April.
notes: Follow @UCTeens on Instagram for events, per the city page. The program runs out of the Kennedy Youth Center.

name: U.S. Senate Page Program
pay_detail: $35,360 per year, prorated
duration: Spring 2027 session: Jan 24 to June 4, 2027. Summer 2027 dates to be announced.
deadline_text: Padilla's office: opens Oct 13, 2026, closes Oct 26, 2026 for the Spring 2027 session.
who_can_apply: US citizen (the Senate application guide also mentions permanent residents; ask the office) with a Social Security number. Must be 16 or 17 at appointment, a junior (semester) or rising junior or senior (summer), with a 3.0 GPA and health forms. Needs a Senator's sponsorship. Senator Padilla sponsors California residents only.
how_to_apply: Send a cover letter, resume, recent transcript and two recommendation letters to Senator Padilla's office at Page_Program@padilla.senate.gov. Other Senate offices have their own rules; the central Page Program does not take applications.
notes: Only about 30 positions in the whole Senate. Pages pay their own travel to and from Washington, DC. The job is in DC, so a California work permit likely does not apply; ask the office. Moving to DC for a semester is a big step for a family.

name: United States Senate Youth Program
org: Hearst Foundations, with the California Department of Education
grades: Juniors and seniors (rising juniors and seniors may apply)
pay_detail: $12,500 college scholarship; travel, hotel and meals paid by the Hearst Foundations
duration: Washington Week March 6 to 13, 2027
deadline_text: California's deadline for the 2027 program is October 7, 2026. That date has passed. The next cycle is expected in fall 2027.
who_can_apply: High school juniors or seniors holding an elected or appointed leadership office this school year, such as student body or class officer. Must be a US citizen or green card holder and live in California. Get the application from your principal, counselor or social studies teacher, or the state contact.
how_to_apply: Ask your principal or counselor for the application, or email the California coordinator at ussyp@cde.ca.gov (California Department of Education, Sacramento).
notes: Very competitive. Clubs, debate, Model UN, jobs and self-made groups do not count as qualifying offices. The CDE page was blocked by a bot check, so the coordinator name and contact are from the USSYP site only. If you are a junior now, plan for next fall.

name: USC Summer Programs (pre-college)
org: University of Southern California, Summer Programs
pay_detail: 2026 total for domestic students: $8,130 commuter or $11,570 residential. That adds tuition $7,401, course materials $300, program fee $325 and health center $104; residential adds $3,440 room and board. Also a $85 nonrefundable application fee and a $1,000 deposit that counts toward the total.
duration: Four weeks, 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. each class day (2026 classes began June 22)
deadline_text: 2026 deadlines were May 8 for domestic and March 13 for international applicants. 2027 dates and prices are not posted.
who_can_apply: High school students who have completed ninth grade by the start of the program and are pursuing a rigorous curriculum. Domestic and international students may apply.
how_to_apply: Online application with the $85 fee. Email summer@usc.edu with questions.
notes: Expensive. The admissions page read does not describe financial aid, so ask summer@usc.edu. The prices and dates above are the 2026 numbers and may change for 2027.

name: USC Viterbi Energy of STEM Summer Camp (free)
pay_detail: Free to attend. No pay.
deadline_text: The 2026 application closed May 4, 2026 and applicants were told by the end of May. The 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Students in grades 8 to 11 in 2026, rising grades 9 to 12. Active MESA, Mission Science and Engineering Transformer students come first. So do students at STEM Center schools. All students are considered.
how_to_apply: When it is open, send a student form and a teacher recommendation. You can use the online form or the PDF. Forms that are not complete are not considered. Contact k12summer@usc.edu.
notes: The program page says in person at USC main campus. The USC Viterbi summer programs list calls it virtual. Confirm the format before you count on it.

name: USS Hornet Museum Volunteer (ages 16 and up)
org: USS Hornet Sea, Air and Space Museum
duration: Set weekly shifts, for example Wed and Sat 8:30 to noon (aircraft), Tue and Sat (ship), first Saturday monthly (radio)
deadline_text: Rolling
who_can_apply: Ages 16 and up for aircraft restoration, ship restoration, radio, community outreach and visitor services (16 and 17 year olds work with an adult). Collections: 18 and up. Docents, events, security: 21 and up.
how_to_apply: Apply at volgistics.com/appform/1737643431 or call (510) 521-8448 ext. 243.
notes: Ship work involves climbing ladders and tight spaces. Another museum page lists overnight programs for groups, but no teen intern program.

name: SEES (STEM Enhancement in Earth Science) Summer High School Intern Program
org: UT Austin Center for Space Research with NASA and the Texas Space Grant Consortium
pay_detail: No stipend. Free for scholarship recipients and for virtual participation; paid participants pay $2,000 tuition (meals, housing, tours and local travel included, travel to Austin not included). Travel scholarships are available.
duration: Online work in June and July plus a 2-week on-site session in Austin (July 5-18 in 2026)
deadline_text: 2026 deadline: February 22, 2026 at 8:00 p.m. PT, no late applications. 2027 dates are not posted; the page says future funding is not guaranteed.
who_can_apply: Current high school sophomores or juniors who are 16 by July 5 of the program year, interested in STEM, and U.S. citizens. Past SEES interns cannot repeat.
how_to_apply: Apply online at spacegrant.net/apps/sees: essays (maximum 250 words per response), a short intro video (submit the link), an unofficial transcript or report card, and a recommendation form. Travel scholarships are available and do not affect your selection.
notes: Very competitive: about 2,000 applications and 215 accepted in 2024 (FAQ). It is an educational internship, not a paid job.

name: High School Summer Research Academy (HSRA)
org: College of Natural Sciences, The University of Texas at Austin
grades: Rising sophomore, junior or senior (preference for rising juniors and seniors)
pay_detail: Summer 2027 tuition is $4,500. Payment is due only after you accept a lab placement. Financial aid is not mentioned on the page.
duration: 5 weeks, June 7 to July 14, 2027 (off June 18 and July 5)
deadline_text: The 2027 application opens mid January 2027. Deadline is listed as March 2027 (no day). Late applications may be accepted on a limited basis.
who_can_apply: Texas residents are prioritized. You must be 15 or older by June 1, 2027 and available all five weeks. In person only. You arrange your own housing and transportation.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the application opens in mid January 2027. First round notices go out at the end of April and second round in early May, with a deposit due one week after you accept. Email hsra@utexas.edu.
notes: This costs a lot and is hard to get into. The page says a few need-based scholarships may be available. They give a stipend plus free tuition. There are no merit scholarships now. Your lab spot is based on your interests, your free time and space. Full tuition is due in mid May.

name: Summer Discovery at UT Austin
org: The University of Texas at Austin Office of Admissions with Summer Discovery
pay_detail: Costs $3,799 to $7,999 depending on the options chosen (the Summer Discovery page gives one range). Some courses add fees. Financial aid is not mentioned.
duration: 2 week or 3 week sessions (2026: June 14 to 26 and June 28 to July 17)
deadline_text: 2026 sessions were June 14 to 26 and June 28 to July 17. 2027 dates and deadlines are not posted on the pages I read.
who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. Participation does not guarantee admission to UT Austin.
how_to_apply: Click the Apply Now button on the UT page. Summer Discovery, not UT, handles applications and sign-up. You can email summerdiscovery@utexas.edu. Or call 516-447-4907.
notes: Expensive. Students get a certificate of completion and a campus grade letter. The Summer Discovery page shows an early enrollment discount ending Oct 31 but does not say the year.

name: Longhorn Engineering Summer Camp (LESC)
org: Cockrell School of Engineering, The University of Texas at Austin
pay_detail: $75 commitment fee for Austin participants, collected only after acceptance (day camp, no lodging)
duration: 4 days (Austin sessions June 8-11 and July 6-9 in 2026; both were full)
deadline_text: Registration for 2026 closed March 12, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Students entering 8th or 9th grade. A panel reviews applications (not first come, first served), and students who attend schools without engineering or STEM offerings are encouraged to apply. Houston and San Antonio sessions are by invitation only.
how_to_apply: Register through the camp page; you are notified by email by mid-May. Questions: cseoutreach@utexas.edu.
notes: For younger teens (about 13 to 15). Both 2026 Austin sessions are listed as full.

name: My Introduction to Engineering (MITE)
org: Cockrell School of Engineering, The University of Texas at Austin
pay_detail: $200, paid only after acceptance (students stay in a campus residence hall)
duration: 5 days (June 21-25 and July 12-16 in 2026)
deadline_text: Applications for MITE 2026 closed March 1, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. 2027 dates are not posted.
who_can_apply: Current high school juniors with a strong interest in engineering, science or math who live in the United States. About 50 students per session are chosen by holistic review. Students from low-income backgrounds or with limited STEM access are strongly encouraged to apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the MITE page. Questions: cseoutreach@utexas.edu.
notes: Selective. The page does not list a financial-aid policy; ask cseoutreach@utexas.edu if the $200 is a barrier.

name: DYNAMC (Discover Yourself In Accounting Majors and Careers)
org: McCombs School of Business, The University of Texas at Austin
grades: Current Texas high school sophomores and juniors
pay_detail: Free. The page says educational, food and boarding costs are covered. Students pay their own travel to and from campus.
duration: June 20 to 25, 2027 on the UT Austin campus, with on campus living
deadline_text: The page lists program dates in June 2027, an application deadline of Feb 1, 2027 and supplemental materials by Feb 8, 2027, but it also says applications are closed. These do not match, so confirm with McCombs.
who_can_apply: Current Texas high school sophomores and juniors. Students who are in summer school on the program dates cannot take part. Chosen students usually have a strong school record and personal wins.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for a transcript, your activities and leadership, essays, a letter of support and a resume. The Apply link on the page was a placeholder. Email SummerPrograms@mccombs.utexas.edu or call 512-475-7340.
notes: Texas high school students only. Shared McCombs page for three programs. Decisions are released by mid April.

name: McCombs Future Executive Academy (MFEA)
org: McCombs School of Business, The University of Texas at Austin
grades: Current Texas high school sophomores and juniors
pay_detail: Free. The page says educational, food and boarding costs are covered. Students pay their own travel to and from campus.
duration: June 6 to 11, 2027 on the UT Austin campus, with on campus living
deadline_text: The page lists program dates in June 2027, an application deadline of Feb 1, 2027 and supplemental materials by Feb 8, 2027, but it also says applications are closed. These do not match, so confirm with McCombs.
who_can_apply: Current Texas high school sophomores and juniors. Students who are in summer school on the program dates cannot take part. Chosen students usually have a strong school record and personal wins.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for a transcript, your activities and leadership, essays, a letter of support and a resume. The Apply link on the page was a placeholder. Email SummerPrograms@mccombs.utexas.edu or call 512-475-7340.
notes: Texas high school students only. Shared McCombs page for three programs. Decisions are released by mid April.

name: Subiendo: The Academy for Rising Leaders
org: McCombs School of Business, The University of Texas at Austin
pay_detail: Free. The page says educational, food and boarding costs are covered. Travel is covered by the program.
duration: June 13 to 17, 2027 on the UT Austin campus, with on campus living
deadline_text: The page lists program dates in June 2027, an application deadline of Feb 1, 2027 and supplemental materials by Feb 8, 2027, but it also says applications are closed. These do not match, so confirm with McCombs.
who_can_apply: Texas high school juniors only. Students who are in summer school on the program dates cannot take part. Chosen students usually have a strong school record and personal wins.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It asks for a transcript, your activities and leadership, essays, a letter of support and a resume. The Apply link on the page was a placeholder. Email SummerPrograms@mccombs.utexas.edu or call 512-475-7340.
notes: Texas high school students only. Shared McCombs page for three programs. Decisions are released by mid April. More info: https://www.mccombs.utexas.edu/undergraduate/subiendo/

name: UVA Advance Pre-College Program
org: University of Virginia Summer and Special Academic Programs
pay_detail: The FAQ says the maximum aid package covers full tuition and fees for Virginia residents, which is $7,097 for 2026. The cost for other students and the full breakdown were not read. Small number of need-based aid packages.
duration: 4 weeks (2026: July 11 to August 7), residential
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: application opened December 1; deadline March 1, 2026; teacher recommendation March 4; decisions March 31; accept by April 15. No 2027 dates posted yet.
who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors in good standing with a minimum 3.5 GPA in a college prep curriculum, age 15 or older on the first day and 18 or younger on the last day.
how_to_apply: Online application with transcripts, one teacher or administrator recommendation uploaded by the recommender, and a 350 to 500 word essay. Financial aid materials are due by March 1.
notes: Residents live in an air-conditioned residence hall with a 10 pm curfew. Travel, books, laundry and spending money are not included. Questions: UVaAdvance@virginia.edu, 434-243-2241. The Cost and Payment page was not read.

name: UVA Health Junior Volunteer Summer Program
duration: 8 weeks (2026: June 8 to July 31); at least 50 hours, or one full weekday, with at least 6 weeks of service
deadline_text: 2026 cycle: interest form due February 20, 2026; info sessions February 25 and March 7, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.
